# dosags (Adventure Game Studio) — DOS port plan

See `.sdl-dos-ports/plans/SDL_DOS_PORTING_PROGRAM.md` sections 15-21 and
30-31 (gitignored, local to a hub checkout) for the full AGS-specific
playbook this plan follows -- compatibility profile, renderer strategy,
audio phases, memory strategy, the milestone ladder, and first-test-game
selection criteria. This file tracks this port's own progress against it.

> **Rename, 2026-09-17:** `tests/harness/run-rig.sh` is now
> `tests/harness/run-hw.sh`, and `run-probe-rig.sh` is
> `run-probe-hw.sh` (operator decision 2026-09-16: drop the word "rig"
> from this repo's own names and new prose -- "real hardware", "the
> target machine", "hw"). Dated entries below keep the name that was in
> use when they were written; read `run-rig.sh` there as `run-hw.sh`.
> The vcctrl input-lock owner names the scripts generate changed with
> it (`run-rig-<TAG>` -> `run-hw-<TAG>`). vcctrl's own vocabulary and the
> hub's skill names (`dos-rig-operations`) are theirs and unchanged.

**`patches/ags/` now has 19 real, build-verified patches (0001-0019)**,
each generated via `git format-patch` against the pinned SHA, applied
via `apply-patches.sh`, and confirmed against the real DJGPP toolchain
after every single one (not just after Phase A finished). All of Phase A
(0001-0008, CMake configure gates) and Phase B (0009, `platform.h`) are
landed. `make configure-ags` succeeds completely (`Configuring done`,
`Generating done`) -- the first time any AGS CMake configure has
succeeded under DJGPP.

**Pushing on to an actual build (`make build-ags`) found four more real,
narrow DJGPP-specific gaps `PATCH-SEQUENCE.md`'s original CMake-only
research could not see**, each fixed as its own patch and confirmed by a
standalone reproduction against the real toolchain before being landed
(not just reasoned about) -- see `PATCH-SEQUENCE.md`'s new "Phase B2"
section for full detail on each:

- **0010**: FreeType's own vendored copy assumes "all non-Windows is
  Unix" and picks a `mmap()`-based file-I/O backend DJGPP can't provide;
  switched to FreeType's own portable ANSI-stdio implementation instead.
- **0011**: twelve targets compile in strict-ANSI mode
  (`C_EXTENSIONS NO`), which sets `__STRICT_ANSI__` -- and DJGPP's own
  libc headers hide real declarations (e.g. `struct stat` itself) behind
  `#ifndef __STRICT_ANSI__`. Fixed globally, once, for the whole tree.
- **0012**: DJGPP's libstdc++ doesn't export C99 `<cmath>` additions into
  `std::` at all, and GLM (used throughout Engine/Common, not just the
  disabled hardware renderer) calls `std::log2`/`round`/`trunc`/`fma`/
  `asinh`/`acosh`/`atanh` directly. New `Common/platform/dos_compat.h`,
  force-included into every C++ translation unit. Took two real
  iterations -- a first `using ::round;`-style attempt looked reasonable
  but failed a real build (GLM's function-pointer-typed dispatch needs
  three properly disambiguated overloads per function, not DJGPP's
  single double-only global) -- corrected before landing, per this repo's
  own "never silently" convention.
- **0013**: DJGPP is ILP32 with `int32_t` typedef'd to `long int`,
  distinct from `int` in C++'s type system even though both are 4 bytes
  here (unlike a 64-bit Linux dev host, where they're the same type) --
  a real, narrow divergence, not a systemic one: checked breadth first
  (8 candidate call sites), only 4 needed a cast.

third-party library (Allegro, FreeType, miniz, GLM all compile and link
clean) and fails on AGS's own `Engine/ac/sys_events.h:21`,

C/D/E/F patch numbers are renumbered (0014-0026) to make room for the
four Phase B2 patches.

**Patch 0014 (Phase C, `std::mutex`/`std::condition_variable` DOS shim)
is now also landed and build-verified** -- see `PATCH-SEQUENCE.md`'s
updated row for the full diagnosis. One correction to that row's
original plan, found by a standalone probe before writing the patch (not
assumed): `std::lock_guard<T>`/`std::unique_lock<T>` already exist as
generic templates under DJGPP even without `_GLIBCXX_HAS_GTHREADS` (they
only require `T` to provide `lock()`/`unlock()`), so only
`std::mutex`/`std::condition_variable`/`std::cv_status` -- concrete types
DJGPP's headers never declare -- needed shimming, and `dos_compat.h`'s
extension needed no changes to `debugmanager.h`/`.cpp` or

gracefully catching that DJGPP's `ld` has no LTO linker plugin
(`-- Interprocedural optimisation (IPO/LTO) not supported: <...>`,
followed by `Configuring done`/`Generating done`), not a fatal configure
error. A future session seeing this text in build output should not
mistake it for a new blocker needing investigation.

**One real correction found while writing 0015, not previously known**:
`PATCH-SEQUENCE.md`'s original plan for 0015 assumed `sys_main.cpp` is
where `SDL_HINT_DOS_MAX_BPP` gets set from the game's color depth.
Reading `Engine/main/engine.cpp` directly shows `sys_main_init()` runs
from `engine_init_backend()`, well before any game package is loaded --
the game's real color depth isn't known yet at that point in AGS's own
call order. Since the hint must precede `SDL_InitSubSystem(SDL_INIT_VIDEO)`
itself (BOOTSTRAP-0 probe 3), and that call already happened by the time
0021's window/surface code would run, this is a genuine unresolved
sequencing gap -- not solved by 0015, and not yet solved anywhere in the
sequence. `PATCH-SEQUENCE.md`'s 0021 row now carries this finding so it
isn't rediscovered; a real design decision (re-init the video subsystem
once depth is known, or a fixed DOS depth policy independent of the
loaded game) is needed before 0021 can be written for real.

## Current state (2026-09-10, third build session -- patches 0029-0036, COMPILES reached)

Picked up exactly where the second session left off: both this repo and
the hub had `HEAD == origin/main` in both repos before any work started
here, per this session's own first-thing check.

**Patches 0029-0031 (the `ali3dsw.cpp` window-surface rewrite, split into
three concerns as the prior session's own note suggested it might need
to be) landed and build-verified**:

- **0029**: the present-step rewrite itself. `SDL_GetWindowSurface` +
  `SDL_BlitSurfaceScaled` + `SDL_UpdateWindowSurface` replaces
  `SDL_CreateRenderer`/`SDL_CreateTexture`/`SDL_RenderCopyEx`;
  `IsModeSupported()`/`GetDisplayDepthForNativeDepth()` accept/return the
  game's own native depth (8 or 16) instead of a hardcoded 32; the
  virtual screen's own pixel buffer is wrapped directly as an
  `SDL_Surface` (`_vscreenSurface`) with no intermediate texture at all,
  since native-depth presentation means no conversion step is needed.
  **Resolves the `SDL_HINT_DOS_MAX_BPP` sequencing gap patch 0015 found**:
  the hint must precede `SDL_InitSubSystem(SDL_INIT_VIDEO)`, but that call
  already happened (from `sys_main_init()`, before any game package
  loads) by the time the real depth is known -- fixed by re-initializing
  the video subsystem once, right before creating the one window this
  backend ever creates (quit `SDL_INIT_VIDEO`, set the hint, re-init),
  confirmed safe by reading `DOSVESA_VideoInit()`/`VideoQuit()` directly
  (no static across-reinit guard). Traced `GetDisplayDepthForNativeDepth()`'s
  callers (`graphics_mode.cpp`) per the prior session's own open item:
  no 32-bit assumptions found needing a fix. Also fixed a real gap this
  rewrite would otherwise have introduced (no equivalent in the original
  `PATCH-SEQUENCE.md` row): the old `SDL_RenderClear()` every frame kept
  any letterbox border clean; a plain blit doesn't, so an explicit
  conditional black-fill was added. Screen-shake/mirror-display
  (`play.shake_screen_yoff`/`play.screen_flipped`) is honored via a
  lazily-allocated scratch surface, not dropped.
- **0030**: 8-bit palette sync. Every AGS call site that sets the palette
  (17 in `Engine/ac`/`media`/`plugin`/`main`, plus one in the
  never-compiled-for-DOS `apeg` video-decode library -- located by a
  tree-wide grep, per the prior session's own open item) calls Allegro's
  `set_palette()`/`set_palette_range()` directly; none need to change.
  Instead, `_vscreenSurface` is made to share the exact same `SDL_Palette`
  object as the window surface (confirmed via reading `SDL_pixels.c`'s
  `SDL_MapSurface()`/`Map1to1()` directly that two INDEX8 surfaces with
  merely equal-content-but-distinct palette objects are not guaranteed
  SDL's fast identity blit path), synced from Allegro's global palette
  once per present, only when it's actually changed (a 256-entry
  `memcmp` against a cached copy).
- **0031**: the two `gfxfilter_*_sdl_renderer` filters collapse to the
  one this driver's now-fixed-scale blit actually offers (`GetScaleMode()`/
  `InitSDLHint()` were already dead after 0029, not just simplified) --
  `gfxfilter_aa_sdl_renderer.h`/`.cpp` deleted outright. **A full**
  `cmake --build build/ags -j$(nproc) -- -k` **pass compiled
  `ali3dsw.cpp.obj`/`gfxfilter_sdl_renderer.cpp.obj` clean against the
  real (unstubbed) headers together for the first time** -- but then
  failed inside `Common/` on five files, a genuinely new discovery (see
  below), not a regression from this patch.

**Real, previously-latent discovery: `Common/` had 23 of its 91 `.cpp`

build**, confirmed by comparing `.obj` count (68) against `.cpp` count

one concern (five more instances of the by-now-familiar DJGPP
`int32_t`/`uint32_t`-vs-`int`/`unsigned int` divergence, matching

`tra_file.cpp`'s `std::max(0, ReadInt32())` sites, `allegrobitmap.h`'s
`RotateBlt` declarations (said `int angle`, real definitions already
used `fixed_t`), `image_png.cpp`'s `palette_colors` (a *pointer-type*

(said `int outline_color`, matching neither its own definition nor its
sibling `wouttext_outline`'s declaration one line above).

**A genuinely different DJGPP gap surfaced next, fixed as patch 0033**:
`wcslen` is *absent* under DJGPP, not merely undeclared -- DJGPP's own
`<wchar.h>` is documented in its own text as a "Bare bones header to
satisfy SGI STL's `basic_string<>`" and declares no wide-string
functions at all. Found via `Common/util/string_utils.cpp`'s one C++
call site, but the real fix needed a second half: `Common/libsrc/
alfont-2.0.9/alfont.c` (a plain C file, 13 call sites) never sees
`dos_compat.h`'s force-include (CXX-only), and even where the shim *is*
visible, a header-only `inline` function has no obligation to produce a
real externally-linkable symbol at all -- fixed with a new companion
`Common/platform/dos_compat.cpp` giving `wcslen` a real, non-inline,
`extern "C"` definition. **Worth recording plainly: the first grep for
alfont.c's own call sites came back empty** -- the shell's default
`grep` here is `ugrep`, which gave a false negative on this specific
file; re-running with `/usr/bin/grep` explicitly found all 13 sites
immediately. Re-verified every other "grepped the whole tree" claim
made earlier in this same session with `/usr/bin/grep` as a result
(found one more undercount, in patch 0030's own commit message: 18 real
`set_palette`/`set_palette_range` call sites exist, not 17 -- the design
conclusion is unaffected, since the 18th lives in never-compiled-for-DOS
`apeg` code, but the earlier count was wrong and is corrected here
rather than silently left standing).

`video.cpp`'s `AGS_NO_VIDEO_PLAYER`-disabled stub branch, which defined

outside that branch (only `video_single_pause()`/`video_single_resume()`/

nothing callable, and `video_single_stop()` was simply missing outright

branch patch 0025 already found issues in). **0035** defined
`is_sdl_mod_key()`/`make_sdl_mod_flag()` in `sys_events.cpp` -- patch
0017's own comment on their declarations already said "defined in
sys_events.cpp", but the actual bodies were never written; ported

94e271df9:Engine/ac/sys_events.h`), not guessed.

**Real tooling finding, worth recording plainly: `dosbox-run.sh
--merge-stderr` does more than fail to merge under DOSBox-X's shell -- it
corrupts the invoked program's own argv.** The existing tooling doc
(`.sdl-dos-ports/shared/skills/dos-emulator-workflow/references/tooling.md`)
already warns that DOSBox-X's shell parses `2>&1` as a redirect to a file
literally named `&1`, not a merge. What this session found in addition:
the RUN.BAT line `AGS.EXE  > STDOUT.TXT 2>&1` also leaves a stray bare `2`
token in the command line DJGPP's own argv-parsing sees, which AGS then
treated as a real command-line argument (a game-data path of literally
"2"), changing which of `define_gamedata_location_checkall()`'s two error
branches fired (the "provided path is not valid" branch instead of the
real "no compatible game data found" search-failure branch) -- a real
behavior change caused by the test harness, not by AGS itself. Re-ran
without `--merge-stderr`; AGS's own `Debug::Printf`/`WriteStdOut` already
default to stdout (confirmed by reading `agsplatformdriver.cpp`'s
`_writeStdOut` default and `--log-file`-only `_logToStdErr` override), so
nothing was lost by dropping it. **Practical rule for this repo: never
pass `--merge-stderr` to `dosbox-run.sh`/`dosbox-launch.sh` for this
engine** -- plain stdout capture already gets everything.

## Current state (2026-09-10, fifth session -- TITLE_SCREEN reached)

Picked up exactly where the fourth session left off: both this repo and the
hub had `HEAD == origin/main` before any work started here, per this

**Root-caused and fixed the "cosmetic" `c:/c:/` doubling bug STARTS left
open.** Per the fourth session's own instruction, wrote a real
`getcwd()` probe (`tests/probes/getcwd-probe/`) before touching anything
else -- raw DJGPP `getcwd()` is clean (`"c:/"` at root, `"c:/build/ags"`
from that subdir), ruling out DJGPP and the DOS mount immediately. Traced
the real cause to vendored Allegro's `canonicalize_filename()`
(`libsrc/allegro/src/file.c`): patch 0002's `__DJGPP__`/`ALLEGRO_UNIX`
branch left `DEVICE_SEPARATOR` as `'\0'` (the driveless-Unix default),
so an already drive-qualified absolute path (what DJGPP hands back as
`argv[0]`) falls into the "make relative path absolute" branch and gets
the current drive+cwd prepended a second time. **Not merely cosmetic**:
`define_gamedata_location_checkall()` calls `MakeAbsolutePath()` on a
*successfully resolved* game-data path too (engine.cpp:969), not just
the no-game-data error message -- an unpatched build would have silently
corrupted the very first real game-data path this port ever tried to
open. Fixed as patch 0037 (restores `DEVICE_SEPARATOR ':'`, adds a
DJGPP `_al_getdrive()` to `unix/ufile.c`), confirmed via a standalone
`canonicalize_filename()` harness linked against this tree's own
`liballeg.a`, before and after, from two real cwds -- and confirmed
STARTS still passes clean afterward.

**Built a minimal synthetic game package from first principles**
(`tests/fixtures/minimal-game-package/build_fixture.py`) to get past
`engine_init_gamedata()` -- a hand-crafted CLIB v6 container (one
`game28.dta` asset, one `agsfnt0.wfn` font asset) at `GameDataVersion=18`
(`kGameVersion_250`, the floor `OpenMainGameFileBase()` accepts). Two
subagents independently traced the CLIB format, the `game28.dta` header,
the `GameSetupStructBase` field layout, and the full `engine_init_gamedata()`
-> `SDL_CreateWindow` call chain (citing file:line throughout); their
reports were **not blindly trusted** -- one claim (`read_savegame_info`'s
version gate) was independently re-verified against the real
`GameDataVersion` enum values and found wrong, which mattered for the
final byte layout. The fixture needed, in order: `numfonts>=1` with one
real loadable `.wfn` font asset (`InitGameState()` hard-fails at
`numfonts==0` before any graphics code runs), `numcharacters=1` with one
real `CharacterInfo` record (`view`/`defview`/etc. explicitly `-1`, or
`engine_init_game_settings()` null-derefs `playerchar->view` at
engine.cpp:676), one legacy-format `Interaction` record per character,
a minimal valid `ccScript` (SCOM-format) global script (a global script
is not optional -- `InitGameState()` hard-fails without one), and a
minimal `GUI::ReadGUI()` header. `kGameResolution_320x240` was chosen
deliberately over `kGameResolution_Default` (which resolves to 320x200
for an 8-bit game, a resolution this DOSBox-X setup has no VESA mode for)
to isolate the window-surface code from that already-understood, separate
fallback path -- 320x200 is a deliberate follow-up, not forgotten.

**Found and fixed one real, subtle bug in the fixture itself, the hard
way.** A byte-complete fixture built through this reasoning still
crashed silently (no error text, no diagnostic) deep inside
`ReadGameData()`. Chased it through an extensive, disciplined elimination
campaign before finding the real cause -- worth recording so the next
investigation doesn't repeat it: isolated `ccScript::Read()` alone (safe,
both via `MemoryStream` and via the real `AssetManager`+`Seek()`), isolated
`Interaction::CreateFromStream()` alone (safe, same two ways), an inline
line-by-line replica of `Interaction::CreateFromStream()`'s own body
reading from the real stream at the real offset (safe), ruled out
optimization level (`-O3` vs `-O0` recompiles of `interactions.cpp`, no
difference) and stale objects (full clean rebuild, no difference), before
finally re-reading `GameSetupStruct::read_interaction_scripts()`
(`Common/ac/gamesetupstruct.cpp:130-178`) all the way to its actual last
line and finding an easy-to-miss **unconditional trailing
`numIntrVars = in->ReadInt32()`** (line 173) in the legacy 2.x branch,
regardless of `numcharacters`/`numinvitems` -- a field this fixture had
never supplied. The missing 4 bytes made that read consume the fixture's
own next real bytes (the following asset's `"SCOM"` signature) as a
garbage `numIntrVars` (~1.3 billion), driving `intrVars[i].Read()`
catastrophically out of bounds. A real, DJGPP-toolchain-agnostic fixture
bug, not an engine or toolchain bug -- the isolated probes that ruled out
every other hypothesis were not wasted effort, but the lesson is to read
a function to its actual last line, not to where the loops "look done."
Fixed by adding the missing `numIntrVars=0` field; documented in
`build_fixture.py`'s own comments. No engine-side patch was needed for
this finding.

**`TITLE_SCREEN` confirmed for both color depths.** With the fixed
fixture and `--user-data-dir c:\` (this staged DOSBox-X environment has

gracefully without it -- not a bug, a real environment requirement), a

load failure -> `quit()`) is well under a second, even at DOSBox-X's
parity-conf cycle count, defeated ordinary polled screenshot capture

cleared surface across every extracted frame -- correct for a game with
no sprites/rooms to draw, not a capture artifact. See README.md's

include/runmanifest.h`'s `runmanifest_emit()` is now called once at
`Engine/main/quit.cpp`'s `quit()`, right after its own `"***** ENGINE HAS

`SDL_DOS_AUDIO_SB_SKIP_DETECTION`, `SDL_INVALID_PARAM_CHECKS`) was read

and `.sdl-dos-ports/shared/tools/dosbox-x*.conf`'s `[autoexec]` blocks,
not guessed.

**A real macro collision, found and fixed.** Including `runmanifest.h`
in `quit.cpp` (which already includes `<allegro.h>`) broke the build:
vendored Allegro's `alconfig.h` unconditionally `#define`s `_farsetsel`/
`_farnspokeb`/`_farnspeekb`/etc as generic plain-pointer macros for its
own DOS backend (`libsrc/allegro/include/allegro/internal/alconfig.h:
389-395`), with no `#ifndef` guard. `runmanifest.h`'s DJGPP environment-
detection code (its 86Box BIOS-string scan) includes DJGPP's own real
`<sys/farptr.h>`, which declares real functions of those same names --
with `alconfig.h`'s macros already active by the time that header is
parsed, its real declarations get textually mangled (`"void
_farsetsel(unsigned short);"` becomes `"void ;"`), a real, confirmed
compile break (`error: declaration does not declare anything
[-fpermissive]`, then a cascade of `expected ')' before '*' token` errors
from `alconfig.h`'s own macro-definition lines). This collision was
latent until now -- no prior file in this port included both
`<allegro.h>` and `runmanifest.h`. Fixed by reordering `quit.cpp`'s own
includes so `runmanifest.h` comes first, letting DJGPP's real
declarations parse before `alconfig.h`'s macros exist; confirmed by a
real build failure before the reorder and a clean build after.

**The engine-stage build now has an include path into `shared/include`**
for the first time -- `Makefile`'s `AGS_CMAKE_FLAGS` gained
`-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$(NOSIMD_FLAGS) -I$(HUB_DIR)/shared/include"`. Had to
restate `NOSIMD_FLAGS` in the same `-D`, not just add the new `-I`:
`CMAKE_COMMON` (from `sdl3-dos.mk`) already passes `-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=
"$(NOSIMD_FLAGS)"`, and cmake's `-D` command-line processing takes the
LAST value for a given cache variable -- an override that didn't restate
it would have silently dropped the hard "no SIMD unless NOSIMD_FLAGS-
gated" constraint for this stage. Confirmed via `build/ags/CMakeCache.txt`
after reconfigure: both the SIMD-disable defines and the new `-I` are
present together.

on Makefile variables; this port's CMake-driven build has no equivalent
"flags changed forces a relink" guarantee established yet, and building
one wasn't in this session's scope. A real, honest empty value (the
schema's own documented "field present, empty" convention), not a
placeholder -- a real follow-up, not silently missing.

`AGS_BUILD_SHA12` (both vendor trees post-patch, this stage's own CMake
flags, the hub build fragment, compiler version -- dossage's own
`BUILD_SHA12`/`GAME_CXXFLAGS` ordering pattern, read directly and adapted
for CMake) threaded through `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS`. Landing it found and fixed
a real, previously-unknown quoting gap: two nested shell layers (this
Makefile's own recipe invoking `cmake`, then cmake's generated
`build.make` invoking the compiler from its own separate recipe) each
strip one level of backslash-quote escaping, so a single `\"` never
reaches the compiler as a real quote -- `\\\"` is needed. Also
empirically confirms (the task's own explicit ask, not assumed) that a
`CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS` change DOES force a real recompile+relink for this
CMake-driven stage (each object's own `build.make` depends on
`flags.make`) -- no stale-object hazard here, unlike dossage's plain-
Makefile-pattern-rule case. Confirmed end-to-end by a real DOSBox-X run
producing `binary_sha12=20a84a45bd83` in `RUNMANI.LOG`, matching `make
build-sha12`'s own output exactly. See Measured Constants for the full
diagnosis, including a real false lead (a static byte-grep of the
compiled `.obj`/`.exe` for the hex string finds nothing -- an `-O3`
inline-immediate-store artifact, not a bug; the runtime output is what
actually confirms it).

**New tooling finding: `AGSEditor.exe /compile` needs an absolute Windows
path, not a relative one, for reliable non-interactive use.** Invoking it
with a bare relative `Game.agf` argument from the matching host working
directory failed both times it was tried (once via the GUI's own file-open,
once via `/compile`): "Unable to load the game 'Game.agf' because it does
not exist". An absolute `Z:\tmp\...\Game.agf` path (Wine's default host
drive mapping) resolved reliably every time after that. Last session's own
recipe apparently worked with a relative path or a different invocation
shape not recorded in enough detail to reproduce exactly -- treat the
absolute-path form as the reliable one going forward, not the relative one.

**New AGS finding: a room's color depth is baked into its own `.crm` file
independently of the project's `<ColorDepth>` setting -- flipping the
project setting does NOT retroactively convert already-authored room
content, unlike a room authored fresh at the target depth.** AGSQuest ships
`<ColorDepth>TrueColor</ColorDepth>` (32-bit, outside this port's supported
8/16-bit range) and a custom `640x360` resolution. Following last session's
own "flip to Palette, recompile" recipe (which worked because that
session's own room was authored fresh at 8-bit) produced a REAL but
misleading result this time: `Compilation successful!`, but with four real
warnings, one per room -- "This room is hi-color, but your game is
currently 256-colour. You will not be able to use this room in this game."
AGSQuest's rooms are natively hi-color (unlike last session's from-scratch
template room), so the project-level downgrade to `Palette` silently
produced a package whose actual room content would not work, accepted by
the compiler as a warning rather than an error. **Fix: `HighColor` (16-bit)
instead of `Palette` (8-bit)** -- matches the rooms' own native format
exactly, and is fully within this port's already-supported range (16-bit
`SDL_PIXELFORMAT_RGB565`, confirmed working since `TITLE_SCREEN`).
Recompiling at `HighColor` produced a clean `Compilation successful!` with
zero warnings.

**Tooling findings, both real, worth keeping:**
- `tools/dosbox-run.sh --interactive` (and `dosbox-launch.sh`) set their
  OWN `DISPLAY` from a `DOSBOX_DISPLAY` env var (default `:0`), not the
  caller's exported `DISPLAY` -- already documented in
  `.sdl-dos-ports/shared/skills/dos-emulator-workflow/references/tooling.md`
  (the `DOSBOX_DISPLAY=:88` pattern used there), but this session re-learned
  it the hard way by not reading that reference first: a plain `DISPLAY=:210`
  export before calling the script silently has no effect on where the
  window actually opens, costing real time hunting for a window that was
  never going to appear on the display being searched.
- `dosbox-run.sh`'s headless mode has no internal timeout and hangs
  indefinitely if the DOS program never self-exits -- expected for any real
  game that reaches its own interactive main loop (as AGSQuest's title
  screen does). Wrap the whole invocation in an external `timeout N` and
  pass `--keep-stage` to inspect the staged `STDOUT.TXT` directly afterward
  (the script's own final "copy stdout out" step only runs if the wrapped
  program exits on its own); use `--interactive` under a private Xvfb
  instead when an actual screenshot is needed.

**Two real engine-behavior findings, neither anticipated by the eighth
session's own "Engine facts" research, both found by running the actual
DOSBox-X loop to a wrong-but-not-crashing result and reading the real
trace rather than guessing -- this is the kind of thing this project's
own "run-diagnose-fix-rerun, not delegable" rule exists for:**
1. `Hotspot`/`Object.RunInteraction()` is itself **deferred**, not
   synchronous -- `Engine/script/script.cpp`'s `run_interaction_script()`
   calls `QueueScriptFunction()` rather than the target function
   directly (the same mechanism `on_event`/room-change dispatch already
   use). A `player.HasInventory()`/`.Graphic` check placed immediately
   after `RunInteraction()` reads state from *before* the interaction
   actually ran -- confirmed by watching a `key`/`unlock` phase log
   "fail" immediately, then watching the *actual* successful interaction
   activity (real engine log lines matching the exact expected
   key-granting/door-unlocking code paths) show up several phases
   later, once the interpreter got around to draining the queue. Fixed
   by converting every phase that isn't itself waiting on a real
   `eEventEnterRoomAfterFadein`/`eEventGameSaved`/`eEventRestoreGame`
   event into an explicit poll (checked every `repeatedly_execute`
   frame, with a generous tick timeout) for its actual side effect,
   never an immediate check.
2. `player.ActiveInventory` must stay set **until the deferred
   interaction that reads it has actually run** -- `oDoor1_AnyClick`/
   `hTable_AnyClick` both read it directly, and clearing it right after
   issuing the (queued, not immediate) `RunObject`/`RunHotspot` call
   cleared it before the handler ever saw it, silently taking the
   "not using an item" branch instead. The engine's own diagnostic line
   for this was unambiguous once looked at directly:
   `SetActiveInventory: character doesn't have any of that inventory`.

Also found and fixed along the way, smaller but real: AGS's compiler
rejects chaining a method call directly onto another call's return value
(`Hotspot.GetByName("x").RunInteraction(m)` fails with "structure
required on left side of '.'" -- an intermediate local is required);
module-local functions must be defined above their first call site (no
bare-prototype forward declaration support for non-imported functions);
and the CWSDPMI env-var-override gotcha already documented for doskutsu
(`~/.claude` memory `reference_sibling_repos_and_rig_config.md`) applies
to dosags too -- `dosbox-run.sh`'s own CWSDPMI auto-include resolves
relative to the *script's* location (`.sdl-dos-ports/shared/tools/`),
never a per-port `vendor/cwsdpmi/`, so `run-dosbox.sh` sets `CWSDPMI`
explicitly rather than relying on the auto-include.

**The patch-series stamp trap (`~/.claude` memory
`reference_patch_series_stamp_trap.md`) was hit for real, not just
theoretically, while landing patch 0042**: `make build-ags` refused with
`verify-patches-applied`'s "SERIES CHANGED SINCE IT WAS APPLIED" once
patch 0041 had landed without an intervening `make patches` refresh.
Fixed the documented safe way -- commit the dirty vendor-tree edits into
the series first (turning them into patch 0042 itself), then run `make
patches`, never `APPLY_PATCHES_FORCE=1` or any other reset of a dirty
tree.

own vcctrl-collect pairing (`<TAG>.LOG`/`<TAG>SDL.LOG`) implies it might
on that port. Both are set to the same tag value in `RUN.BAT`.

## Current state (2026-09-11, eleventh session -- slice 7, `dialog`
phase + input-latency instrumentation)

Picked up where the tenth session left off: this repo, the hub, and
vcctrl were all confirmed clean/pushed before any work started (per the
handoff prompt's own instructions). The vcctrl-harness-migration thread
mentioned in the tenth session's write-up above had already completed
the same day it was written, fully pushed, nothing to resume -- unrelated
to this session's own work.

**The actual task: work order item 7, the `dialog` phase and its
input-latency approximation.** Both remain explicitly optional/fragile
per this document's own design decisions -- neither gates `PLAYABLE`.
Confirmed the next-free patch slot (`ls patches/ags/ | sort | tail`):
0045, as expected.

**The obvious design (call `dRedMage.Start()`, then click) does not
work, for real, non-obvious reasons -- not a coordinate mistake.**
Getting from "the click misses" to "the click lands and the dialog
completes" took four separate rounds of empirical investigation, each
producing a real, otherwise-undocumented engine fact (all recorded in
the Measured Constants table under 2026-09-11, and referenced from
`AutoPilot.asc`'s own `StartDialogPhase()`/`STEP_DIALOG_SETTLE` comments
-- read those directly for the full mechanism, this is a summary):

1. **`Character.RunInteraction(mode)` doesn't set `Mouse.Mode`.** The
   obvious first attempt -- simulate a real player's own click path via
   `cRedMage.RunInteraction(eModeTalkto)` (routes through
   GlobalScript.asc's `cRedMage_AnyClick()`, the same handler a real
   click reaches) -- silently no-op'd. `RunInteraction()`'s own `mood`
   argument only selects which interaction-table slot to run;
   `cRedMage_AnyClick()` branches on the GLOBAL `Mouse.Mode`, which
   nothing had set. Found by adding a temporary diagnostic `System.Log`
   directly into a locally-cloned `GlobalScript.asc` (not committed --
   `build-package.sh` re-clones fresh every run, so this kind of
   upstream-file diagnostic never persists) and confirming `mode=0` at
   entry.
2. **A script-set value needs a full tick before dependent per-tick
   logic sees it -- twice.** `Mouse.Mode` is set by this room's own
   per-tick `GetLocationType(mouse.x,mouse.y)` check, which reads a
   SEPARATE `mousex`/`mousey` pair that `Mouse.SetPosition()` does not
   update directly (it updates `sys_mouse_x`/`sys_mouse_y` immediately;
   `mousex`/`mousey` only catch up via `Mouse::Poll()`, once per tick).
   The exact same gap turned out to apply to `DialogOptions::Run()`'s
   OWN hover-detection, which reads the identical `mousex`/`mousey`
   pair. Both need at least one tick's wait between `SetPosition()` and
   whatever depends on the new position.
3. **`Dialog.Start()` (`dRedMage.Start()`), called from script, is
   itself deferred, not blocking.** `Engine/ac/global_dialog.cpp`'s
   `RunDialogOption()` queues a `PostScriptAction` rather than running
   the real conversation immediately, since script is always
   `inside_script`. Confirmed by a live DOSBox-X capture showing the
   options screen still up, "Leave" correctly highlighted, tens of
   seconds after this module had already logged "dialog ok" -- Start()
   had merely been queued, not actually finished. Worse: `RunDialog()`
   always runs the dialog's own `@S` entry point (an ordinary Say()-
   equivalent intro line) BEFORE the options screen exists at all, and
   that Say()'s own per-frame housekeeping drains any already-queued
   `Mouse.Click()` regardless of `Game.IgnoreUserInputAfterTextTimeoutMs`
   (a real, separate 500ms WALL-CLOCK debounce this session also found
   and disabled -- `Engine/main/game_run.cpp`'s `RunControls()` pops the
   queued event unconditionally, the debounce only gates whether the
   result is ACTED on). And once the real, deferred conversation
   finally starts, `Game.TickCounter` freezes and `repeatedly_execute()`
   stops being invoked at all for its whole real-world duration --
   confirmed with a temporary heartbeat `WriteLog()` -- which rules out
   any script-side poll-for-completion design (e.g. watching
   `DialogOptions.AreDisplayed`): there is no tick where both "the
   dialog is showing" and "this module's own script is running" are
   true at once.
4. **`Dialog.DisplayOptions()` is the actual fix.**
   `Engine/ac/dialog.cpp`'s `Dialog_DisplayOptions()` calls
   `show_dialog_options()` DIRECTLY -- no `inside_script`/`QueueAction`
   detour, no `@S` intro text, genuinely synchronous like
   `player.Walk(...,eBlock)`. It hands the chosen option's ID straight
   back to script without running that option's own topic script
   (irrelevant here -- this phase only needs to confirm the click
   reached the right row). Switching to it, combined with facts 1-2
   above, finally worked: `chosen=14` ("Leave"), reproduced across
   several independent real DOSBox-X runs, with every phase after
   `dialog` (save/restore/exit/gem/audio/shots/quit) completing
   normally afterward too.

**"Leave"'s own screen coordinates were read off a live capture, not
computed.** The default (no custom GUI) dialog-options renderer's exact
pixel layout depends on font metrics (`write_dialog_options()`/
`CalcOptionsHeight()`, `Engine/ac/dialog.cpp`) that would have taken
real risk to hand-derive correctly for the TTF font this port's own
`game_start()` sets as the dialog font. Instead: a temporary debug build
that reached the options screen and then deliberately hung there (no
click queued) was captured live via `xwd`/`import` under a private
Xvfb, calibrated against a room screenshot's own known-native
coordinates (the room's static art, e.g. the chandelier, gave a precise
window-pixel-to-game-coordinate offset), and the resulting `DIALOG_
LEAVE_X`/`DIALOG_LEAVE_Y` constants read directly off that capture.

**A real x11/xdotool click at the same screen position, sent from
outside the game, ALSO failed to register** during this investigation --
this did NOT indicate the coordinates were wrong; it was a
`dosbox-run-tooling-traps`-class red herring (no window focus was ever
established for the xdotool click in that private, WM-less Xvfb) and
was set aside once fact 3 above (Start()'s own deferred/frozen-tick
behavior) turned out to be the actual explanation for everything
observed, xdotool test included.

**`patches/ags/0045`** (`/sdldos:review`ed, same real-run-before-landing
discipline as 0041-0044): paired `DOS-PORT input_latency t_ms=<ms>
event=<inject|processed>` log lines, `uclock()`-based like patch 0042's
room-transition timestamps -- `event=inject` in
`ags_simulate_mouseclick()` (the moment `Mouse.Click()` queues the
synthetic SDL event), `event=processed` in `on_sdl_mouse_down()` (the
moment it's actually drained and acted on, gated on
`SDL_TOUCH_MOUSEID` so a real input device never pollutes the metric).
Real deltas across several runs: 11-24ms.

**`tests/harness/parse-results.py` gained `OPTIONAL_PHASES`** (currently
just `["dialog"]`) -- shown in the rendered `.md` record when present,
but never required and never affects the pass/fail gate, matching this
slice's own "optional/fragile, kept separate" design decision exactly.

**Everything from this session's DOSBox-X-confirmed work is committed
and pushed**: two commits in this repo (`patches/ags/0045` + `vendor/ags`
commit `355eaae9f`; `AutoPilot.asc`'s `dialog` phase + `parse-results.py`'s
`OPTIONAL_PHASES`), plus a docs write-up commit, all pushed with the
operator's explicit go-ahead. A real-hardware confirmation run was THEN
attempted and, after real infrastructure work, succeeded -- see the next
section for the full account and `results/
HW-486-66-2026-09-11-agsquest-slice7.md` for the record itself.

### Real-hardware confirmation for slice 7 (same session, after pushing)

**Confirmed working, first try that got a clean end-to-end result:**
`dialog` phase reports `ok`, `chosen=14` ("Leave"), all 16 pre-existing
phases plus all three screenshot hashes pass unchanged, real
`fps_p50=9.62`/`fps_p95=10.09` (identical to slice 6's own HW1 reading,
same hardware, same stress scene), `memory_min_free_kb=144704`. **First
real-hardware input-latency datum**: 223ms (vs. DOSBox-X's own 11-24ms
under `--fast` -- real 486DX2-66 hardware takes roughly an order of
magnitude longer to process a simulated click, exactly the kind of gap
this approximation exists to surface). Full record: `tests/harness/
results/HW-486-66-2026-09-11-agsquest-slice7.md`.

**Getting there took a real, multi-part infrastructure investigation on
the shared vcctrl rig (gateway2000/g2k-lab, the same physical HW-486-66
machine slice 6 used) -- none of it a dosags/AGS defect, all found and
fixed live by a peer `vcctrl` session over several attempts (tags
HW2-HW8):**
1. Stale FTP credentials baked into the card's `VCCHK.BAT`/`VCGET.BAT`/
   `VCLIST.BAT` (both resolving to the literal string "dos", not a real
   password) -- root-caused to two separate FTP servers on this rig
   (the vcctrl daemon's own, and a separate control-host recovery
   server) having been pointed at the same credential during an earlier
   public-release-prep session, when they were never meant to share
   one. Fixed by separating the two credentials and re-provisioning the
   card through the (now-working) recovery path.
2. A genuine boot-menu keystroke-retry bug in `vcctrld`'s own
   `_enter_net()`: it blindly typed "5<Enter>" up to 7 times to select
   the NET boot option, with no check for whether an earlier attempt
   had already landed and no keyboard-buffer drain before the next real
   command -- so the extra keystrokes executed as bogus commands at a
   live DOS prompt right after boot. Fixed and deployed
   (`vcctrl` commit `1f6f825`, 193+1 regression tests).
3. A real hard hang requiring a physical power cycle to recover --
   confirmed via an independent room camera (not just the rig's own
   capture stick) showing a genuinely wedged display, distinct from a
   video-mode-restore false alarm. Cause not conclusively identified;
   ruled out this session's own `uclock()` usage specifically (PIT-based
   on this DJGPP toolchain, not RDTSC, and already proven safe here via
   patch 0042's own successful HW1 run) as the likely mechanism, though
   something else in AGS/Allegro's own code remains a possibility if it
   recurs.
4. A `run-rig.sh` bug on this repo's own side: its cleanup trap deleted
   its own results directory before the very first fully-successful run
   (tag HW7) could be parsed -- the script prints that path specifically
   so `parse-results.py $(...)` can chain onto it, matching
   `run-dosbox.sh`'s own convention, but the trap raced ahead of any
   caller reading it. Fixed by moving the output directory outside the
   trap's scope; confirmed by a second full run (tag HW8) whose results
   were the ones actually kept and committed. Also hardened both of the
   script's polling loops (a bare `vc file-status | python3 -c ...`
   one-liner with no error tolerance had aborted the whole script twice
   under `set -e` on a transient hiccup in the check itself, not the
   underlying job) with a shared, retry-tolerant `wait_for_job_done()`
   helper.

None of 1-3 are dosags-repo changes (they live in the shared vcctrl
rig/daemon, tracked in vcctrl's own repo and docs); 4 is committed here.
Every real-hardware action in this whole investigation had the
operator's own explicit go-ahead at each step, per
`dos-hardware-validation`'s discipline -- including staying hands-off
of the daemon/rig-side fixes themselves and leaving those to the peer
session that owns that code.

`Object.GetByName("oChandelier")`, same room-local access pattern
already established for `hBench`/`oDoor1`/etc. Rather than trust
`Object.Animating` (`IsObjectAnimating()`) alone -- a flag that
wouldn't catch a stuck-but-still-"cycling" bug -- `anim` samples
`Object.Frame` once, waits, then checks it actually changed value
(`Engine/ac/object.cpp`'s `Object_GetFrame()`/`Object_GetAnimating()`
both read the same per-game-loop animation state the engine's own
update sets every tick, confirmed by reading the source, not assumed).
Placed right after the existing `interior` phase completes (both of
its own completion branches now call the new `StartAnimPhase()` instead
of jumping straight to `StartDialogPhase()`) -- still room 4, before
`dialog` begins, so nothing else in the sequence had to move.

## Current state (2026-09-11, thirteenth session -- S0, fixed timestep, DOSBox-X side done)

Picked up the Sound plan's own work order: **S0 lands first, before any
Sound-milestone fps measurement, because it changes what every later fps
number means.** Followed the section's own first instruction --
`shared/patches/nxengine-evo/0152-0153` (doskutsu's own wave-56 tick/
render split and wave-57 fixed-timestep accumulator) read in full, plus
this engine's own `WaitForNextFrame()`/`UpdateGameOnce()`/`render_graphics()`
-- before designing anything.

**Landed as three patches (`patches/ags/0046-0048`, each `/sdldos:review`ed,
confirmed on DOSBox-X):**

- **`0046`** -- a prerequisite refactor: a new `GameTimer.RenderCounter`,
  separate from `LoopCounter` (`Game.TickCounter`). Before this, the two
  were the same value by construction (one render per logic tick); the
  whole point of S0 is to break that equivalence, so `get_real_fps()`/
  `fps_p50`/`fps_p95` needed their own counter or they would silently
  become a second copy of the logic-tick rate instead of a real
  rendered-smoothness measurement. Audited every `render_graphics()`/
  `render_to_screen()` call site in the engine; only `UpdateGameOnce`'s
  own and `ShakeScreen::Run()`'s (`global_screen.cpp`, the one other site
  with its own render loop outside `UpdateGameOnce`) touched the loop
  counter before this patch, so both get a matching `RenderCounter`
  increment -- every other render site (Display()/dialog-options/
  screen.cpp's fades) never counted toward fps before and still doesn't,
  unchanged. Confirmed behavior-preserving via a full DOSBox-X harness
  run (all 18 phases, 3/3 screenshot hashes unchanged).
- **`0047`** -- the actual catch-up loop. `UpdateGameOnce` gained a
  `skip_render_and_wait` parameter (default false, so every existing
  caller is unaffected) that suppresses `render_graphics()`/
  `WaitForNextFrame()` while still running every logic step -- the same
  guard shape `play.fast_forward`'s cutscene-skip already uses, not a
  restructure. `GameTick()` now dispatches to `dos_run_tick_fixed()` under
  `DOSAGS_FIXED_TIMESTEP=1` (env-cached like `dos_auto_exit_check()`,
  default off): runs logic-only ticks for however many are owed at the
  game's current `frames_per_second` (read fresh every call, honors a
  mid-game `SetGameSpeed()`), then always one more normal tick that
  renders. `MAX_CATCHUP=5` mirrors doskutsu's own clamp.
  **A real design bug was caught and fixed in the same session, before
  landing**: the first version tracked backlog as a private wall-clock
  delta, which double-counted whenever a script reached a blocking modal
  AGS feature with its own internal update loop bypassing `GameTick()`
  entirely -- found via `DialogOptions::Run()` (dialog.cpp's own comment:
  "Run() can be called in a loop"), which calls `UpdateGameOnce()`
  directly from mid-script. Fixed by anchoring "how much is owed" to the
  authoritative `get_loop_counter()` (ticks expected by wall-clock since
  an epoch, minus ticks that actually exist) instead of a private clock,
  so a nested loop's own real ticks net out to zero owed instead of being
  double-counted. Same lesson this port's own `dos_auto_exit_check()` and
  doskutsu's own TAS accumulator fixes (`0280`/`0281`, read directly, not
  assumed from titles) already encode.
- **`0048`** -- RUNMANIFEST instrumentation: `DOS-PORT tick_rate=<hz>
  frames_skipped=<n>`, own line after the standard block (no schema
  field, same rationale as `memory_min_free_kb`). `tick_rate` is a
  whole-run average (`get_loop_counter()`/`get_runtime_ms()`), not yet
  windowed to exclude boot/loading time -- S7's own eventual KPI claim
  picks the real measurement window; this patch only wires the raw
  numbers through. Found and fixed one more real bug while validating
  this: `set_loop_counter()` (room.cpp's first-room-setup reset,
  savegame restore) reset `LoopCounter` without resyncing `RenderCounter`,
  permanently skewing `frames_skipped` by however many renders happened
  before the first reset -- fixed by resyncing both together.

**Verification method for the mechanism itself** (not just "it builds"):
a temporary, never-committed, env-gated sleep inside `UpdateGameOnce`'s
own render call simulated a 50ms-per-render stall (~20 fps ceiling).
`DOSAGS_FIXED_TIMESTEP=0` under the stall: the whole AGS Quest autopilot
sequence (boot..quit, ~3200 ticks) took ~193s at `fps_p50=18.27` --
render cost directly became game-speed cost, exactly the bug S0 exists
to fix. `DOSAGS_FIXED_TIMESTEP=1`, same stall, after the design fix:
~73-98s (matching this package's own un-stalled baseline duration) at
the SAME `fps_p50~18` -- rendered fps still honestly reports the
degraded smoothness, but game speed no longer inherits the stall.
`tick_rate` stayed consistent (~32-33, matching the un-stalled baseline)
regardless of whether render was stalled to ~18 fps or running at native
~40 fps -- the core property this milestone exists to deliver. All 18
phases stayed `ok` in every configuration tested (flag off, flag on
without a stall, flag on with the stall), including `dialog`'s own
`chosen=14` ("Leave") result, unchanged throughout.

## Current state (2026-09-12, fourteenth session -- S1, PCM on DOSBox-X, done)

Picked up the Sound plan's own work order at S1, per its own instruction
to read `Engine/media/audio/audioplayer.h`, `soundclip.cpp:133-175`,
today's stub patches (0016/0022/0023/0005-0007), the `ScriptAudioClip`
64-byte record, and the shared SDL3-DOS audio primitives directly before
designing anything -- all read fresh from the pinned sources, not
recalled from the plan's own paraphrase of them.

**Landed as three patches (`patches/ags/0049-0051`, each `/sdldos:review`ed,
confirmed on DOSBox-X):**

- **`0049`** -- a standalone 8-voice (3 reserved + 5) fixed-voice PCM
  mixer (`platform/dos/dos_audio_mixer.h/.cpp`) on one SDL3 audio stream
  at Tier-2 (11025 Hz mono S16), matching doskutsu/dossage's own
  established default. Target-depth pump plus `SDL_DOSAudioPump()`, an
  underrun counter, and the `audio_vital_status` string builder. Inert
  until wired in.
- **`0050`** -- a standalone RIFF WAV + Creative VOC loader
  (`platform/dos/dos_audio_decode.h/.cpp`) that sniffs the actual file
  header ("RIFF"/"WAVE" or "Creative Voice File") regardless of the
  clip's own extension or `fileType` hint -- PLAN.md's own requirement,
  since `v361_objnames` games can carry an unreliable fileName/fileType
  pairing. Handles WAV PCM 8/16-bit and VOC codec 0 plus type-9 16-bit,
  silence/continuation/extended blocks. Converts once at load to the
  mixer's device format (dossage's own `0039` lesson -- convert once, not
  per-chunk -- verified against that patch's actual text before citing
  it, not assumed from its title).
- **`0051`** -- the actual wiring: real `SDLDecoder`/`OpenAlSource` DOS
  implementations (`sdldecoder.cpp`/`openalsource.cpp`, keeping each
  interface's real public contract per 0022's/0023's own stubs), a real
  `sys_audio_init()`/`shutdown()` (`sys_main.cpp`, replacing 0016's
  always-false stub), the mixdown/pump call site in
  `audio_core_entry_poll()`, a second pump call narrowly scoped to
  `UpdateGameOnce`'s own fast-forward/`skip_render_and_wait` early-return
  (`game_run.cpp` -- see the bug below for why this is NOT routed through
  the shared `update_polled_stuff()`), and `audio_vital_status` wired into
  RUNMANIFEST (`quit.cpp`, sourced from a snapshot taken at device-shutdown
  time since the manifest is only built afterward).

**Two real bugs found and fixed before landing, not after:**
1. `SDL_InitSubSystem()` returns `bool`/true-on-success in SDL3, not
   SDL2's `0`-on-success `int` -- the first version of `sys_audio_init()`
   inverted this and silently treated success as failure (`Failed to init
   SDL audio subsystem: ` logged with an empty `SDL_GetError()`, since
   nothing had actually failed). A real SDL2->SDL3 migration trap worth
   remembering for any future `SDL_Init*` call written against
   half-remembered SDL2 conventions.
2. Routing the mixer pump through the shared `update_polled_stuff()` --
   a literal reading of the plan's own "the fast-forward path needs the
   pump too" -- caused a real, measured ~35% duration regression (110s
   -> 160s, `fps_p50` 34.6 -> 23.8) on the DOSBox-X harness, because that
   function has 17 other, much-more-frequent call sites (fades, dialog,
   GUI, room loading) that don't need an audio-mixdown pump on every
   visit. Fixed by placing the pump narrowly at the actual
   `play.fast_forward`/`skip_render_and_wait` early-return inside
   `UpdateGameOnce` instead, which reproduced the exact pre-change
   baseline duration. Generalizable lesson: "needs the pump too" meant
   the fast-forward CODE PATH specifically, not every function that
   happens to sit on it.

## Current state (2026-09-13 -- S5, WaveBlaster hub hoist + DOSBox-X validation, done; real hardware/GUS not started)

**WaveBlaster's hub hoist, dosags wiring, and DOSBox-X validation are
DONE.** Scope: exactly the WaveBlaster half of S5's own work-order line --
NOT the rig's PicoGUS check, NOT real-hardware validation, NOT the
operator listen, and NOT GUS (a separate future slice; nothing scaffolded
for it here).

**Hub (`shared/audio/waveblaster_sink.{c,h}`, commit `dc6ac74`)**: a
plain-C rebase of doskutsu's `MidiBackendWaveBlaster` (`patches/
nxengine-evo/0102`) onto `midi_sched_sink`, calling the shared MPU-401
primitives (SDL patches 0037/0047/0080-0101) directly. Unlike `opl3_sink`,
this module owns no GM mapping or voice allocation -- a real (or emulated)
WaveBlaster/MPU-401 synth voices GM itself, so every callback is a
near-direct MIDI byte pass-through. **A real, load-bearing difference from
opl3_sink, discovered by reading the CURRENT (not the patch-0102-commit-
message) `SDL_DOSMpu401Init` implementation, not assumed**: its default
cold-init sequence must run on a COLD ISA bus, strictly BEFORE the SB16
PCM device opens (`SDL_DOSAudioSB_IsDeviceHot()` becoming true makes it
decline unconditionally, by design -- a real hot-bus status read is
documented, in `SDL_dos_audio_synth.c`'s own W22-WB-D history, to stall
the bus indefinitely on at least one real card). `opl3_sink_open()` has no
such constraint and can open lazily, per clip; `waveblaster_sink_open()`
cannot. This also means a naive close()/reopen cycle between songs (S4's
own pattern for opl3, since `opl3_sink` has no partial silence-without-
close primitive) cannot apply to wb -- the module splits
`waveblaster_sink_silence()` (mute only, port stays alive) from
`waveblaster_sink_close()` (real teardown, session-end only).

**Hub validation probe (`shared/tests/probes/wbsinkmd.c`/`.bat`, commit
`2c9b09a`)**: the wb analog of `opl3midi.c`, plus a stronger witness
`opl3midi.c` doesn't need -- `SDL_dos_audio_synth.h`'s own
`dos_port_mpu_write_count`, read before/after, proving MIDI bytes reached
the real `SDL_DOSMpu401WriteByte()`, not just this probe's own dispatch
wrapper. **This answers the handoff's own open question -- can DOSBox-X
exercise an MPU-401/WaveBlaster path at all?** The probe sets
`SDL_HINT_DOS_AUDIO_PROBE_MPU401=1` in-process (DOSBox-X-only diagnostic
use; the default blind cold-init cannot answer this either way since it
always reports success). Real result, cross-compiled and linked against
dosags's own already-built `libSDL3.a`, run under real DOSBox-X/CWSDPMI:
`event_count=9 division=240`, `dispatched=7 tempo_us=400000
us_per_tick_x1000=1666667` (all exact matches to the pre-registered
expectation), sink wrapper counts exact (`note_on=3 note_off=3
program_change=1`), `dos_port_mpu_write_count` delta `=20` (the exact
expected byte count for those 7 events) -- `[wbsinkmidi VERDICT=PASS]`,
`[wbsinkmidi MPU401_EMULATION=ACKED]`. **Finding: DOSBox-X's MPU-401
emulation at the default port (0x330) DOES ACK a real reset sequence** --
the direct-port path is genuinely exercisable under DOSBox-X.

**dosags wiring (`patches/ags/0055`, vendor commit `698777be3`)**: reading
patches 0052-0054 directly found the existing `SDL_HINT_DOS_AUDIO_BACKEND=
wb` dispatch (`dos_midi_backend_open()`) was NOT sufficient as-is -- it is
only ever called lazily, per type-5 clip, well after `sys_audio_init()`
has already opened the PCM device at engine startup, which is always too
late for wb's one-shot cold-init (every such call would see a hot bus and
fail, hardware present or not). This needed real engine-side surgery, not
just wiring an existing seam:
- A new `dos_midi_backend_cold_init()`, called from `sys_audio_init()`
  strictly before `SDL_InitSubSystem(SDL_INIT_AUDIO)`/
  `dos_audio_mixer_init()` -- no-op, touching no WaveBlaster-related SDL
  call at all, unless the hint is actually `wb`, so every other backend/
  session is unaffected.
- `dos_midi_backend`'s handle type generalized from a concrete
  `opl3_sink*` to an opaque `void*` (its own S4 comment had already
  anticipated this: "once S5 gives them different failure kinds") --
  `AudioPlayer` no longer touches a backend-specific sink type anywhere.
- A new `dos_midi_backend_end_song()` makes Stop()/the destructor
  backend-aware: opl3 gets a real close+null (unchanged S4 behavior); wb
  gets `waveblaster_sink_silence()` only, handle left alive and reused
  directly on the next `Play()` -- no reopen, because a second cold-init
  after the bus is hot would fail. A new `dos_midi_backend_shutdown()`
  (called from `sys_audio_shutdown()`) does wb's one real, whole-session
  teardown.
- `CMakeLists.txt` gained `waveblaster_sink.c` in the same
  `DOS_PORT_SHARED_AUDIO_DIR` target_sources block `midi_sched.c`/
  `opl3_sink.c` already use.

## Known graphical glitch: black boxes around sprites -- reported 2026-09-12, ROOT-CAUSED 2026-09-16

**Resolved as a harness package-data defect, not a port bug -- see
"Black-box sprite glitch -- root cause, fix plan, test plan" (2026-09-16)
for the evidence and the fix.** Short version: the AGS Quest overlay
recompiles a TrueColor-authored game at HighColor, the Editor drops
sprite alpha for a HighColor game, and the source PNGs are RGB-black
under their transparent pixels -- so the package itself contains opaque
black where transparency should be, and AGS's official Linux engine
renders the identical frame (sha256-identical captures). The
doskutsu-derived SDL colorkey lead below does not apply to this engine
(no `SDL_ConvertSurface`/`SDL_SetSurfaceColorKey` anywhere on the
sprite path). The text below is kept as the original task entry.

**Reported by the operator (2026-09-12, fourteenth session)**: visible
graphical glitches -- black boxes around characters, items, and other
sprites. Not yet reproduced/pinned down by a session (no screenshot
diff or root cause identified yet) -- this section is the task entry,
not a fix. Not gating any current milestone or work order item; slot
this in as its own investigation before or alongside S2 onward, per
operator priority when picked up.

**Doskutsu had the same class of bug, fixed, and it is a real lead, not
just a vague precedent -- read `patches/nxengine-evo/0078-perf-wave-16-
fix-colorkey-magenta-bleed.patch` in `~/git/doskutsu` in full before
touching anything here.** Its symptom was solid-magenta boxes rather
than black ones, but the mechanism generalizes to any color a renderer's
mask/colorkey convention resolves to, and is worth checking against
first because it is a genuinely easy trap to fall into on this exact
software stack:

1. **A palette-remap/lookup cache keyed by a path format that didn't
   match what callers actually passed** (relative `"Title.pbm"` vs.
   `ResourceManager::getPath()`'s `"data/Title.pbm"`) -- every lookup
   missed, silently routing every sprite through the slow truecolor
   fallback path instead of the fast indexed-LUT path.
2. **SDL3's `SDL_ConvertSurface` bakes a source surface's colorkey into
   alpha=0 when the destination format has alpha**
   (`SDL_ConvertColorkeyToAlpha`, `vendor/SDL/src/video/SDL_surface.c`)
   -- a real SDL2->SDL3 behavior change, not an AGS/nxengine-specific
   bug. That fallback path hit exactly this: it converted a colorkeyed
   surface to RGBA32, alpha-flattened every "transparent" pixel to 0,
   remapped alpha==0 to the wrong master-palette index, and the result
   then failed the renderer's colorkey-skip test at blit time -- so
   "transparent" pixels were drawn as a solid block instead of skipped.

**AGS's own transparency model is NOT the same code as nxengine's
`Renderer.cpp`/`Surface.cpp`, so the exact fix will differ, but the
failure class to check for first is identical.** A first look
(fourteenth session) found AGS's own convention is `MASK_COLOR_8/16/32`
(`vendor/ags/Engine/gfx/gfxdriverbase.cpp`'s `is_color_mask`), not
necessarily SDL's own colorkey mechanism directly -- **not yet
confirmed** whether the DOS software renderer path (`ali3dsw.cpp`,
patches `0029`/`0030`) or any DOS-specific surface conversion in this
port's own patches ever calls `SDL_SetSurfaceColorKey`/
`SDL_ConvertSurface` on a mask-colored sprite surface, which is exactly
where doskutsu's trap lived. That is the first thing to check, by
reading source, not by assuming the mechanism transfers unchanged.

**First steps for whoever picks this up:**
1. Reproduce and capture: get an actual screenshot showing the glitch
   (DOSBox-X is fine for this -- correctness bug, not a performance
   question) and identify exactly which sprites/rooms show it, so there
   is a concrete before/after to diff against, the same discipline the
   harness's own screenshot-hash regression already uses.
2. Read `ali3dsw.cpp` and any patch touching it (`0029`/`0030`) plus
   AGS's own sprite-drawing/mask-color path (`gfxdriverbase.cpp` and
   whatever calls `is_color_mask`) end to end before touching anything --
   never guess about upstream AGS code, per this repo's own standing
   rule.
3. Check specifically for any `SDL_ConvertSurface` call (in this port's
   own patches or in the vendored SDL3-DOS backend) operating on a
   surface that has an SDL colorkey set, converting to a format with
   alpha -- doskutsu's own fix (strip the colorkey before the convert
   call, then rely on RGB-value matching instead of the colorkey-as-
   alpha side effect) is a directly reusable pattern if this is the same
   trap.
4. If the root cause turns out to be in the shared SDL3-DOS backend
   itself (not AGS-specific), the fix belongs in the hub's `shared/`
   patches, not `patches/ags/` -- ask "would every port want this" per
   `.sdl-dos-ports/CLAUDE.md`'s own rule before deciding where it lands.
5. `/sdldos:review` before landing, same as any vendor patch; DOSBox-X
   screenshot-hash regression confirms the fix without breaking anything
   else, before any real-hardware confirmation is needed.

## The SDL2->SDL3 strategy decision (do this first, it gates everything else)

Three options (full detail: porting-program doc section 18):

- **Strategy A -- port AGS's SDL2 calls directly to SDL3.** Preferred if
  the surface `SDL-SURFACE.md` finds is manageable: reuses the existing
  proven DOS backend directly, no second platform layer to maintain.
- **Strategy B -- a separate SDL2 DOS backend.** Avoid unless absolutely
  necessary -- duplicates all of doskutsu's proven platform work and
  splits maintenance permanently.
- **Strategy C -- a thin SDL2 compatibility shim over SDL3.** Fallback if
  AGS's SDL2 usage turns out broad but shallow (many calls, few distinct
  semantics).

Do not guess which one applies -- `SDL-SURFACE.md` (every SDL symbol AGS's
engine calls, grouped by video/audio/input/timer/thread/filesystem, each
flagged for whether it needs semantic changes or just a rename) is what
decides this. **Done 2026-09-10**: `SDL-SURFACE.md` recommends Strategy A
-- AGS's own engine code funnels almost all of its SDL2 usage through two
wrapper files, and most of the video/window surface is rename-only. Two
findings from that inventory could still change this conclusion (see its
tl;dr and "Open questions" below) before it's treated as settled.
**Review 2026-09-10: Strategy A is settled.** The renderer contingency is
resolved by decision (window-surface presentation from the start,
`PATCH-SEQUENCE.md` 0017 -- the `SDL_Renderer` probe is moot), and
mojoAL's fate affects the audio milestone's scope, not the strategy.
