## Performance KPIs (written down in advance, 2026-09-10)

Per the hub's `benchmark` skill and `docs/optimization.md`'s "Setting a
performance KPI" checklist, and following dossage's own precedent
(`docs/BENCHMARK-PLAN.md`) -- but this port has zero AGS-specific compute
data yet (no `COMPILES` build exists), so the numeric bar below is
deliberately deferred rather than guessed. Guessing a number now would be
exactly the confident-but-ungrounded mistake `docs/timing.md`'s
self-lying-metric entry warns against; AGS is also a heavier engine than
Passage/Cave Story (interpreted script VM, alfont/FreeType text, a real
sprite-cache abstraction), so neither sibling port's number transfers by
analogy.

### Primary KPI: sustained fps

- **Hardware tier carrying the pass/fail bar: 486DX2-66 only**, matching
  `README.md`'s own stated minimum target. `HARDWARE.md`'s other four
  tiers (486DX2-50, Pentium OverDrive 83, Am5x86-133, Pentium 75) stay
  informational/exploratory until there's a specific reason to expand --
  mirroring dossage's initial single-tier scope, not its eventual mature
  5-card x 4-CPU matrix.
- **The numeric fps floor is not set yet, by decision.** The first real
  486DX2-66 datum -- taken at the `TITLE_SCREEN` milestone (a near-idle
  scene: window surface open, palette set, no game logic running yet) --
  is **exploratory, not pass/fail**, the same treatment dossage gave
  Mach64's first-ever run ("no established figure ... first run is
  exploratory and cannot pass or fail against a band that does not
  exist"). Write the actual PASS/FAIL band down immediately after that
  datum lands, before any optimization work starts -- then refine it
  again once a real game room (not just an idle title screen) is
  rendering, since that's a meaningfully heavier scene.
  **Update 2026-09-11 (tenth session): a real HW-486-66 fps datum now
  exists (`fps_p50=9.62`/`fps_p95=10.09`, see Measured constants below
  and `tests/harness/results/HW-486-66-2026-09-11-agsquest.md`), but it
  is NOT the datum this bullet means** -- it was measured against AGS
  Quest's full `settle` scene (640x360x16, decision 4's stress/coverage
  workload), not the near-idle `TITLE_SCREEN` fixture this bullet
  specifically calls for. The `TITLE_SCREEN`-scene real-hardware datum
  this section is waiting on still does not exist. Do not set the
  PASS/FAIL band from the AGS Quest number.
- Once set, the number follows the hub's standard well-formed-KPI shape:
  real-hardware only (DOSBox-X is a correctness instrument here, never a
  performance proxy), `fps_p50`/`fps_p95` (or an explicit "no window
  below X" floor) via `.sdl-dos-ports/shared/include/runmanifest.h`,
  attributed to a specific `build_sha12`, falsifiable in advance (what
  counts as FAIL decided before the run, not after).
- **AGS's own game loop is not decoupled like Cave Story's**, unlike the
  framing `HARDWARE.md`'s doskutsu section uses -- read directly in
  `Engine/ac/timer.cpp`: `WaitForNextFrame()` ties one script/animation
  tick to one render pass at a single configurable rate
  (`frames_per_second`, default 40, set by the game's own script via
  `SetGameSpeed()`). Falling behind does not desync or skip logic (the
  pacer just stops sleeping and the loop free-runs slower --
  `MAXIMUM_FALL_BEHIND` only bounds how far the deadline-tracking is
  allowed to drift, it does not skip frames), but unlike Cave Story, a
  low achieved fps is not "still playable, just less smooth" -- it is
  the actual speed the game plays and animates at. Since we author the
  first test game ourselves, its `SetGameSpeed()` target is a free
  variable we control -- **do not lock the shipped test game's own
  target rate before the real 486DX2-66 ceiling is measured.**
- **Amended 2026-09-11 (twelfth session, operator decision) -- see
  "Fixed timestep and the fps KPI" below.** The coupling described in
  the previous bullet is now something this port CHANGES rather than
  works around: game logic gets pinned at AGS's native 40 ticks/s
  wall-clock with frame skipping, so *game speed* becomes a separate,
  hard PASS/FAIL KPI (40 ticks/s +/- 2% on the in-profile package on
  HW-486-66, from a new `tick_rate` line) and *rendered fps* becomes the
  tracked smoothness KPI with 40 (= native) as its target, "as close as
  the hardware allows" per tier, its HW-486-66 PASS band still set from
  the first in-profile datum exactly as this section already says. The
  HW10 run is the evidence the amendment rests on: tick-counted phase
  durations matched DOSBox-X exactly while wall-clock diverged ~10x,
  i.e. the 486 was running the game at whatever speed it could render.
  Every fps number taken before the fixed-timestep slice lands
  (HW1/HW8/HW10) is a "coupled" number and is labelled as such when
  compared against later ones.

### Secondary KPIs (decided 2026-09-10, all four in scope for v0.1; tracked once there's something to measure)

- **Room-transition / load latency.** Time from a room-exit trigger to
  the new room's first presented frame -- an adventure-specific UX cost
  the fps KPI alone doesn't capture. AGS's sprite-cache/compression path
  (128MB desktop defaults vs. patch 0022's DOS-tuned 4-8MB cache) makes
  this a real risk on a 16-32MB machine, not just a nice-to-have metric.
  Measurable starting at the "Game package parses, reaches initial room
  setup" milestone, once the chosen test game has more than one room.
- **Peak memory footprint vs. the 16MB minimum / 32MB recommended
  target** (`README.md`'s own stated RAM targets). Checked once patch
  0022's DOS cache-size tuning lands; the number that matters is headroom
  left after sprite/sound cache + engine + the DPMI host, not just
  whether it boots at all.
- **Audio glitch-free-ness.** Same present/no-dropout/no-corruption
  framing doskutsu and dossage already use for audio (not a numeric
  target) -- applies once real MIDI/WAV output replaces the
  `COMPILES`-stage stubs (patches 0012/0016/0018), at the Sound
  milestone.
- **Input-to-response latency.** Click-to-cursor-reaction time, tracked
  separately from the frame-rate KPI. AGS polls input once per game loop
  (`Engine/ac/sys_events.cpp`), so this is coupled to but not identical
  to achieved fps -- worth its own explicit measurement since an
  adventure game's moment-to-moment feel rides on hotspot/cursor
  responsiveness more directly than raw fps the way an action game does.

## Test harness (AGS Quest) -- decided 2026-09-10, eighth session follow-up

Now that `ags.exe` runs a real game under DOSBox-X, the port gets a
standing, automated test harness built around AGS Quest
(`adventuregamestudio/ags-demo-game`) that every later milestone --
"First room renders", `PLAYABLE`, Sound, `OPTIMIZING` -- is accepted
against, on DOSBox-X (correctness gate) and on real hardware (the only
source of benchmark numbers). It exists so fps, load times, room
transitions, memory, and audio are measured the same way every time and
comparable across builds and across the `HARDWARE.md` matrix, instead of
re-derived ad hoc per session.

### Decisions (operator, 2026-09-10)

1. **Everything that drives the game is scripted inside AGS itself** --
   an autopilot script module compiled into the package -- not external
   input injection (`xdotool` on DOSBox-X, `vcctrl mouse` on the rig,
   which `~/git/vcctrl/docs/BOARD-IDENTITY.md` documents as never
   exercised). Same package, same walkthrough, same log lines on both
   environments; coordinates never leak into the harness. (Operator's
   explicit preference: "if we can script all of this out using features
   of AGS, I absolutely prefer that.")
2. **The Wine rebuild script is the canonical package source.** Only our
   own code and assets are committed; the 16-bit AGS Quest package is
   rebuilt from a pinned upstream SHA by a script and lives in a
   gitignored directory. AGS Quest's art is CC BY-NC-ND (verified from
   its own `LICENSE.md` this session): it is never committed, never
   redistributed, and **no screenshot of it is committed either** -- the
   harness stores screenshot *hashes* for regression, not images.
   Reproducible from the repo alone at the cost of a one-time Wine setup
   on a fresh machine (~30-40 min, automated by a setup script).
3. **The overlay adds our own WAV + MIDI clips and one OFL TrueType
   font.** Stock AGS Quest has OGG-only audio and WFN-only bitmap fonts
   (feature inventory below), so as shipped it would never touch the
   port's real audio targets (Sound Blaster PCM, MIDI) or the
   alfont/FreeType text path this document already flags as a risk. Our
   additions are our own committable content (CC0/OFL, license files read
   and recorded), wired into the autopilot.
4. **AGS Quest is the feature-coverage and upper-bound stress workload,
   not the KPI datum.** At 640x360x16 it pushes ~7x the per-frame pixel
   data of the v0.1 target profile (320x200/240x8). Its real-hardware
   numbers are benchmarked and tracked over time, but the primary fps
   PASS/FAIL floor in "Performance KPIs" above is still set on an
   in-profile package once one exists (the self-authored spec game, whose
   authoring path -- Wine GUI first, Windows VM as fallback -- is the
   other decided next-session track). The harness is therefore
   **package-agnostic**: AGS Quest is the first package, not the only one.
5. **Generalize the hub's rig scripts before the first dosags rig run.**
   `vcctrl-sweep`/`vcctrl-cell`/`vcctrl-collect` are still hardcoded to
   doskutsu (`C:\DOSKUTSU\LOGS`, `DOSKUTSU_*` env names). That is hub
   (`shared/`) work, done first, so the rig flow is port-agnostic for
   every port rather than a second one-off. First rig tier: HW-486-66
   (the KPI tier), others exploratory.

### What AGS Quest actually exercises (inventory, read from its scripts)

Read directly from `Game.agf`, `GlobalScript.asc`, `room1-4.asc` (the
clone at `/tmp/wine-ags-test/dl/ags-demo-game`, pinned SHA
`064a14dfe171c6c0045aac8b46b221d7db17cce2`, tag `v0.1.0.0`):

- 4 rooms: 1 "AGS Logo" (auto-advances after `WaitMouseKey(2s)` in
  `room_AfterFadeIn` -> room 2); 2 "Main Menu" (`gTitleMenu`, PLAY ->
  `btnPlay_OnClick` -> `player.ChangeRoom(3, 389, 150)`); 3 "Forest with
  Treehouse" (main gameplay; `room_FirstLoad` runs a skippable cutscene
  with a blocking walk and three `Say`s); 4 "Treehouse Interior"
  (`cRedMage` lives here; looping chandelier animation). Transitions 3<->4
  through door/balcony hotspots, `RoomTransition=FadeOutAndIn`.
- Characters: `cBlueMage` (player, real walk view "MageBlue"), `cRedMage`.
  One-click interface: `repeatedly_execute` sets cursor mode from
  `GetLocationType()`; every hotspot/object handler is `*_AnyClick` and
  branches on `Mouse.Mode`/`player.ActiveInventory`.
- Room 3 interactions: `hBench` (blocking walk + `AddInventory(iKey)`),
  `oDoor1` (locked; `iKey` unlocks, `LoseInventory`), `oGem` on the
  balcony (`AddInventory(iGem)`), `oFrog` (animates), `hForest` (ending if
  `HasInventory(iGem)` -> `gCredits`), plus `hPond`/`hFlowers`/`hShrine`/
  `hToadstools`/`hWindow`/`hTreehouse`/`hEntrance`/`hBackDoorway`.
  Room 4: `hWashBasin` (`AddInventory(iGem2)`), `hTable` (use `iBlueCup`
  -> `oCupOnTable.Visible`), exits, furniture hotspots.
- Inventory: `iKey`, `iGem`, `iGem2`, `iBlueCup` (starts in inventory),
  shown in `InventoryWindow1` on `gInGameMenu`.
- One dialog, `dRedMage` (14 entries, option toggling, inventory-gated
  branch).
- GUIs (all `PopupStyle Normal`, 640x360 coords): title menu, in-game
  menu with **Save/Load buttons** (`SaveGameSlot(1)`/`RestoreGameSlot(1)`,
  a single custom slot -- no F5/F7), quit confirm, options (`sldVolume`
  -> `System.Volume`), credits, `@OVERHOTSPOT@` descriptions, text window.
- Audio: five OGG SFX only (door, frog, pickup sounds), no music, no
  MIDI/WAV, no `speech.vox`. Fonts: three WFN bitmap fonts, no TTF.
- `DebugMode=True` is on: Ctrl-X teleport-to-room (`Debug(3,0)`), Ctrl-S
  give-all-inventory, F9 `RestartGame()`, F12 `SaveScreenShot`.
- Not from any official template (custom assets, Apollo palette); its
  GUI defaults match "Empty Game", not Sierra-style. One script module
  entry (`GlobalScript`) in `<Scripts>`; a new module is one more
  `<ScriptAndHeader>` block with a fresh `<Key>` plus `.ash`/`.asc`
  files, inserted BEFORE `GlobalScript` (modules run in list order).

### Engine facts the autopilot design rests on (read from the pinned engine)

- **Script -> stdout logging exists**: `System.Log(eLogInfo, ...)`
  (`Engine/ac/system.cpp:540-544`) goes through `Debug::Printf` with the
  `script` group -- which is NOT on stdout by default (`debug.cpp:333-337`
  enables only `main/sdl/plugin`). `--log-stdout=+mgs:all` (option parsed
  `main.cpp:378-386`; one-letter groups `debug.cpp:228`) puts `main`,
  `game`, and `script` on stdout, which `dosbox-run.sh` already captures
  to `STDOUT.TXT`. Engine-generated script warnings go to `game` with a
  `(room:N) [script:line]` prefix (`debug.cpp:392-402`).
- **Script file writing**: `File.Open("$SAVEGAMEDIR$/AUTOPLT.LOG",
  eFileWrite)` resolves to `get_save_game_directory()` (`file.cpp:634-637`),
  i.e. exactly what `--user-data-dir c:\` sets -- so the same log lands as
  a plain file in `C:\` for the rig's `get-file` path, independent of
  stdout redirection. Names must be 8.3 by construction.
- **Blocking rules are hard `quit()`s, not warnings**: any blocking call
  in `game_start` -> `quit("!A blocking function was called before the
  first room has been loaded")` (`game_run.cpp:224-227`); any in
  `repeatedly_execute_always` -> quit (`game_run.cpp:235-237`). Blocking
  is allowed in `repeatedly_execute` (non-`always`) and room
  `AfterFadeIn`. **The autopilot is a phase state machine driven from
  `repeatedly_execute` + `on_event`, never from `game_start`.**
- **Click simulation without moving the mouse**: `Button.Click(eMouseLeft)`
  (`button.cpp:414-417`), `GUI.ProcessClick(x,y,btn)` (`gui.cpp:521-530`),
  `Hotspot/Object/Character/InventoryItem.RunInteraction(mode)`
  (`hotspot.cpp:317`, `object.cpp:1359`, `character.cpp:4373`,
  `inventoryitem.cpp:324`), `Room.ProcessClick(x,y,mode)`
  (`room.cpp:1461`). `Mouse.Click(eMouseLeft)` (`mouse.cpp:754` ->
  `ags_simulate_mouseclick`, `sys_events.cpp:640-646`) injects a real SDL
  down+up at the current pointer -- the one path that exercises the full
  input pipeline, paired with `Mouse.SetPosition`.
- **Timing available to script is coarse**: `Game.TickCounter` (one per
  game loop at `GetGameSpeed()` fps, `game.cpp:917-922`) and
  `DateTime.RawTime` (seconds). No ms clock in script -- **ms-resolution
  timings come from engine-side instrumentation (patches below), the
  autopilot only marks phase boundaries.**
- **Save/load are deferred**: `SaveGameSlot`/`RestoreGameSlot` queue a
  `PostScriptAction` that runs after the current script returns
  (`global_game.cpp:135-174`); completion is `on_event(eEventRestoreGame,
  slot)` (`game.cpp:1469`). Module globals are part of the save
  (`savegame_components.cpp:1377-1410`), so the autopilot's phase variable
  is restored too -- advance it *before* queuing the save so the restored
  copy resumes at the correct step. `--loadsavedgame <slot>`
  (`main.cpp:268-272`) restores at startup, skipping `start_game`.
- **Clean exit**: `QuitGame(0)` -> `quit("|You have exited.")`
  (`global_game.cpp:523-532`, `'|'` = normal exit) -> the same `quit()`
  tail that emits RUNMANIFEST (patch 0038) and `exit(EXIT_NORMAL)`.
- **CLI switches that matter**: `--test` sets `play.debug_mode`
  (`main.cpp:367`), readable from script as `game.debug_mode` -- **the
  autopilot arms only when this is set**, so the same package plays
  normally otherwise; `--startr N` overrides the start room
  (`main.cpp:255-258`); `--no-message-box`; `--nosound`/`--nomusic`;
  `--fps`. No config-file autoplay key exists (`config.cpp:490-500`).
- Text that would block on input: set `Speech.SkipStyle`/`SetSkipSpeech`
  (`speech.cpp:499`) and `Game.TextReadingSpeed`/`MinimumTextDisplayTimeMs`
  from the autopilot's first phase so `Say`/`Display` auto-advance.
- `System.GetEngineInteger(ENGINE_VALUE_I_SPRCACHE_*)`
  (`system.cpp:237-262`) exposes sprite-cache sizes in KB from script --
  one input to the memory KPI line.
- RUNMANIFEST (`.sdl-dos-ports/shared/include/runmanifest.h`) allows
  extra `key=value` lines inside the block; `fps_p50`/`fps_p95`,
  `audio_vital_status`, `scene`, banner counts are all still NA in this
  port (patch 0038/0040 fill only identity/env/timing/exit). AGS already
  keeps real-fps accounting (`game_loop_update_fps()`/`get_real_fps()`,
  `Engine/main/game_run.cpp:1154-1182`) that nothing samples yet.

### Architecture

Everything lives in **this repo, `tests/harness/`** (AGS-specific; the
hub's "would every port want this?" rule keeps it out of `shared/`), and
reuses the hub's existing pieces rather than duplicating them:
`dosbox-run.sh`/`dosbox-launch.sh`, `runmanifest.h`, the `benchmark` and
`dos-hardware-validation` skills' ABBA/threshold discipline,
`templates/BENCHMARK.md`'s record format, `profiles/dosags.yaml`.

```
tests/harness/
  README.md              what this is, how to run, what is/isn't committed
  setup-wine.sh          one-time: WINEPREFIX + winetricks dotnet46 + Editor zip
  build-package.sh       <package>: clone at pinned SHA, apply overlay, Wine
                         /compile (absolute Z:\ path), place in games/<pkg>/
  packages/agsquest/
    PIN                  upstream URL + SHA + Editor version
    overlay/             our code/assets only:
      Game.agf.patch     ColorDepth->HighColor, AutoPilot module entry,
                         our audio clips + TTF font slot
      AutoPilot.ash/.asc the autopilot module
      assets/            CC0 WAV clips, generated MIDI, OFL .ttf + licenses
    LICENSE-NOTES.md     what upstream content is used and why it is never
                         committed; our additions' licenses
  games/                 GITIGNORED build output (AGSQUEST.AGS, etc.)
  run-dosbox.sh          stage + run under DOSBox-X (private Xvfb, external
                         timeout, --keep-stage), collect STDOUT.TXT/
                         RUNMANI.LOG/AUTOPLT.LOG/screenshots
  run-rig.sh             the vcctrl flow (after the hub scripts are
                         generalized -- decision 5)
  parse-results.py       logs -> one JSON + one BENCHMARK.md-format record
  results/               committed records (numbers + hashes, never images)
  expected/              screenshot hashes per phase per environment
```

Makefile targets to add: `harness-setup`, `harness-build PKG=agsquest`,
`harness-dosbox PKG=agsquest`, `harness-rig PKG=agsquest HW=HW-486-66`,
`harness-report`.

**Autopilot module (`AutoPilot.asc`)**, armed only when `game.debug_mode`
is true (`--test`). A phase state machine in `repeatedly_execute`, with
`on_event` for room-load and restore completion. Every phase boundary
emits one line in a fixed grammar to BOTH `System.Log` (-> stdout via
`--log-stdout=+mgs:all`) and `$SAVEGAMEDIR$/AUTOPLT.LOG`:

```
AUTOPILOT phase=<name> status=<begin|ok|fail> tick=<TickCounter> room=<n> [k=v ...]
```

Phases, in order (names are the stable identifiers the parser and the
`expected/` hashes key on):

| Phase | Drives | Exercises |
|---|---|---|
| `boot` | engine start -> room 1 `AfterFadeIn` | package parse, sprite init, first present (load-time metric) |
| `splash` | room 1's own 2 s `WaitMouseKey` (left as-is) | title-room render, timed wait |
| `menu` | `btnPlay.Click(eMouseLeft)` in room 2 | GUI button path, `ChangeRoom` -> room 3 |
| `intro` | `SkipCutscene()` (verify name at implementation) + auto-advancing text settings | cutscene skip, `Say`/`Display` text rendering (TTF font slot after overlay) |
| `settle` | hold N ticks in room 3 with `oFrog` animating, nothing else | **the sustained-fps sample window** (`scene=forest-idle`) |
| `key` | `hBench.RunInteraction(eModeInteract)` | blocking walk, hotspot handler, `AddInventory` |
| `unlock` | `player.ActiveInventory=iKey; oDoor1.RunInteraction(eModeUseinv)` | use-inventory-on-object, `LoseInventory`, object state |
| `enter` | `hEntrance.RunInteraction` -> room 4 | **room-transition latency sample** (fade-out/in) |
| `interior` | `hWashBasin`, `hTable` with `iBlueCup` | more hotspots, object visibility toggle, chandelier animation |
| `save` | advance phase var, then `SaveGameSlot(1)` | save path, deferred action |
| `restore` | `RestoreGameSlot(1)`; `on_event(eEventRestoreGame)` confirms | restore path, module-global round-trip (phase var must resume correctly) |
| `exit` | `hFrontExit.RunInteraction` -> room 3 | second room transition (reverse direction) |
| `gem` | balcony route, `oGem.RunInteraction` | last inventory pickup |
| `audio` | play our overlay WAV clip, then MIDI clip (`.Play()`), hold M ticks | SB PCM + MIDI paths (no-op until the Sound milestone; package must still parse them) |
| `shots` | `SaveScreenShot("PH<nn>.BMP")` at fixed points above | engine-framebuffer captures, identical mechanism on both environments |
| `quit` | `QuitGame(0)` | clean shutdown, RUNMANIFEST emission |

Optional/fragile, kept separate: `dialog` (`Mouse.SetPosition`+
`Mouse.Click` on an option, then `Dialog.DisplayOptions()` -- the only
script path to choose a dialog option is coordinate-coupled; landed
2026-09-11, eleventh session, using `DisplayOptions()` rather than this
paragraph's original `dRedMage.Start()` design -- see the Measured
Constants table's 2026-09-11 rows and work order item 7 for why) and an
input-latency approximation via `Mouse.Click` injection timestamps
(`patches/ags/0045`).

Pass/fail on DOSBox-X (the correctness gate; never a performance number):
every phase reports `ok`; engine log contains the witness lines
(`Graphics mode set: 640 x 480 (16-bit)`, `Initialize sprites`,
`Initialize path finder`); a RUNMANIFEST block is present with
`exit_code=0`; each phase screenshot's hash matches `expected/` (hash
only -- a mismatch is a diff to eyeball locally, not a committed image).

**Engine-side instrumentation (patches, `patches/ags/` next free slots --
confirm with `ls patches/ags/ | sort | tail`, 0041 was free at the end of
the eighth session)**, all DOS-guarded and reviewed with `/sdldos:review`
before landing, following this document's own "instrument before
optimizing" rule:

- fps sampler: sample `get_real_fps()` once per second into a fixed ring
  buffer, compute p50/p95 at `quit()`, fill RUNMANIFEST `fps_p50`/
  `fps_p95`; per-phase percentiles as extra `key=value` lines (the
  `settle` window is the number that matters).
- ms timestamps: DJGPP `uclock()`-based `[t=<ms>]` prefix on stdout lines
  and dedicated lines at room-change start and first presented frame after
  fade-in -> room-transition latency and boot-to-first-frame load time,
  keyed to the autopilot's phase markers.
- memory: DPMI free-memory (`__dpmi_get_free_memory_information`) minimum
  across the run + sprite-cache KB at each phase -> peak-footprint KPI.
- run identity: honor `DOSAGS_LOG_TAG` / `DOSAGS_SCENE` / an auto-exit
  tick env (the placeholders `profiles/dosags.yaml` already declares as
  "not yet implemented") and write `RUNMANI.LOG` per tag instead of
  appending to one fixed file across runs (a real collision today).

**Real hardware** (after decision 5's hub work): per
`docs/hardware-testing.md` -- `vcctrl stage-file` + `send-file --return`
for `AGS.EXE`, `CWSDPMI.EXE`, `AGSQUEST.AGS` (single files, 8.3-safe --
no DOS-side unzip exists yet), a `RUN.BAT` that sets the env allowlist
vars and runs `AGS.EXE --test --log-stdout=+mgs:all --user-data-dir
C:\DOSAGS > LOGS\<tag>.LOG`; `expect_log` witnesses use early engine
lines (`Graphics mode set: 640 x 480 (16-bit)`, `Initialize sprites`),
never a RUNMANIFEST field; results back via `file-refresh`/`get-file`
(`<tag>.LOG`, `RUNMANI.LOG`, `AUTOPLT.LOG`, `PH*.BMP`); audio phase judged
with `vcctrl_audio_verdict`/`audio_match` against our own WAV/MIDI
reference. ABBA blocks with pre-registered thresholds per the
`dos-hardware-validation` skill for any A/B comparison; one
`results/<hw>-<date>-<sha12>.md` per run in `templates/BENCHMARK.md`'s
format, every self-reported fps paired with an independent wall-clock
bracket.

### Milestone mapping

- "First room renders": `boot`..`settle` green on DOSBox-X with a matching
  `expected/` hash for the room-3 screenshot, plus one real-hardware run
  showing the same room (its screenshot inspected, its hash recorded).
- `PLAYABLE`: the full phase list through `quit` green on DOSBox-X and on
  HW-486-66 -- room transitions, inventory, dialog (optional phase),
  save/load, GUI, animation all exercised by the same script.
- Sound: `audio` phase produces a real `audio_vital_status` and a passing
  rig audio verdict.
- `OPTIMIZING`: `settle`-window `fps_p50`/`fps_p95` and the secondary
  KPIs from `results/` are the before/after numbers; AGS Quest is the
  stress workload, the in-profile package carries the PASS/FAIL floor
  (decision 4).

### Risks and known constraints

- Wine/winetricks/download drift can break `setup-wine.sh` on a fresh
  machine; the existing prefix at `/tmp/wine-ags-test` is not durable.
  `build-package.sh` must use the absolute `Z:\` path form (relative
  paths fail -- Measured Constants).
- Upstream AGS Quest is pinned by SHA; a bump is a deliberate re-verify,
  never automatic.
- 640x360x16 on real VESA cards is untested (`HARDWARE.md`'s Mach64/ViRGE
  mode quirks; the engine picks 640x480 fullscreen-desktop under DOSBox-X
  -- a real card may differ). The first rig run is exploratory.
- 16 MB minimum-RAM target vs. 16-bit 640x360 backgrounds and sprites:
  unknown until measured -- which is the point of the memory KPI line,
  not a reason to pre-judge.
- Blocking-call restrictions (above) are `quit()`s: an autopilot bug
  looks like an engine crash. The phase log's last `begin` line localizes
  it.
- `RUNMANI.LOG` appends across runs until the run-identity patch lands;
  the parser must take the last block until then.
- Dialog option selection has no coordinate-free script path -- kept
  optional.
- NC-ND: images from AGS Quest never enter git history, in either repo;
  `results/` and `expected/` hold numbers and hashes only. README
  screenshots stay on synthetic fixtures or on our own future in-profile
  game.

## Sound milestone plan -- decided 2026-09-11, twelfth session follow-up

Planned before any Sound patch was written, the same way the test harness
was: operator decisions first, then the engine and shared-layer facts the
design rests on (read from the pinned sources and from doskutsu's/
dossage's own measurements, not recalled), then a slice work order. The
"Game porting framework" and "Fixed timestep" sections that follow were
decided in the same sitting and are cross-referenced from the work order
below; the fixed-timestep change lands BEFORE the Sound fps measurements
because it changes what every later fps number means.

### Decisions (operator, 2026-09-11)

1. **The sound-on fps bar applies to the in-profile package (320x200/
   240x8) on HW-486-66, the KPI tier.** AGS Quest (640x360x16, ~10 fps on
   that machine with audio stubbed) stays the stress/tracking workload;
   its sound-on/off delta is recorded, not gated. HW-486-50 stays the
   exploratory "torture" tier per `HARDWARE.md`.
2. **OGG/MP3 are pre-converted on the host, automatically -- never
   decoded on DOS.** A host-side tool rewrites a game's compressed clips
   to WAV at the device tier (11025 Hz mono, see below); the DOS engine
   plays WAV/VOC + MIDI (+ tracker, pending decision 5). No per-game hand
   work: the tool is one stage of the porting framework (next section).
   Rationale: DevilutionX measured ~4.5 fps for MP3 decode on DOS (hub
   `docs/audio.md`); Vorbis is not cheaper.
3. **Engine generically, guided by AGS-era conventions** -- no named
   target list at the engine level. Separately, five golden-reference
   games (below) exercise the format cross-section and become the
   porting framework's first inputs and regression fixtures.
4. **The host tool targets compiled games** (repack the CLIB pack, patch
   each clip's type byte), not just Editor source projects -- games in
   the wild are binaries.
5. **Tracker music (MOD/XM/S3M/IT): profile one real file on the rig
   before deciding** native decode vs. pre-rendering to WAV by the same
   host tool. Unmeasured cost, deliberately not guessed.
6. **doskutsu's GM MIDI sinks are hoisted into the hub's `shared/`**, one
   copy every port consumes, dosags the first consumer; order OPL3 ->
   WaveBlaster/MPU-401 -> GUS. doskutsu keeps its own copy until it bumps
   its subtree pin.
7. **Verification is by the rig's audio capture, not by the operator
   listening.** The operator will not be present; ask them to listen
   only with strong automated evidence in hand, and attach the capture
   so they can listen asynchronously. (Recorded as a standing rule in
   this session's memory too.)
8. **A repeatable game-porting framework is its own phase** (next
   section), used for the five golden references rather than converting
   titles by hand.

### What AGS actually does with audio at this pin (read from source)

- **Decode** is SDL2_sound: `Engine/media/audio/sdldecoder.cpp/.h`
  (`Sound_NewSample`/`Sound_NewSampleFromMem` with an extension hint,
  `Sound_Decode` in 64 KB chunks -- patch 0022 lines 113/218), plus an
  `SDLResampler` on SDL2's `SDL_BuildAudioCVT`. AGS forces the MIDI
  decoder on (`CMake/FetchSDL_Sound.cmake:17`, `SDLSOUND_DECODER_MIDI`):
  **MIDI is decoded to PCM by SDL2_sound's software TiMidity**, needing a
  patch set. There is no native or hardware MIDI path anywhere in 3.6.3.
  Engine-side MIDI is vestigial: `soundclip.cpp:91,105` return 0 for
  position<->ms ("TODO: reimplement"); `audio.cpp:997,1079` exclude
  MIDI/MOD from crossfading; the legacy `SeekMIDIPosition`/
  `GetMIDIPosition`/`PlaySilentMIDI` script API routes through the
  generic channel (`global_audio.cpp:173-191,392-414`).
- **Mix/output** is OpenAL via vendored mojoAL (`libsrc/mojoAL/mojoal.c`,
  4,923 lines of float 3D mixing). `MAX_GAME_CHANNELS 32` + a crossfade
  channel (`audiodefines.h:53-56`); reserved speech 0 / ambient 1 /
  music 2, normal 3+ (`:63-66`); two queued buffers per source
  (`MaxQueue = 2`, patch 0023). AGS expresses no sample-rate preference;
  the rate follows each clip.
- **Clip types the game data can carry**: `eAudioFileOGG=1, MP3=2, WAV=3,
  VOC=4, MIDI=5, MOD=6` (`Common/ac/dynobj/scriptaudioclip.h:27-36`; MOD
  covers `.mod/.xm/.s3m/.it`, `.cpp:32-33`). A clip whose decoder is
  missing fails gracefully per clip: `load_sound_clip` returns null
  (`sound.cpp:104-153`) -> `AudioClip.Play: unable to load sound file`
  (`audio.cpp:397`) -- exactly what dosags logs today for AGS Quest's OGG.
- **Threads are already off on DOS**: patch 0001's CMake branch defines
  `AGS_DISABLE_THREADS=1` (`CMakeLists.txt:101-109`), so
  `audio_core_init()` skips the mixer thread (`audio_core.cpp:61-69`)
  and `audio_core_entry_poll()` runs from `WaitForNextFrame()`
  (`Engine/ac/timer.cpp:73-75`). The slot map + poll
  (`audio_core.cpp:154-165`) are already main-loop-driven.
- **One hook covers every wait path.** `WaitForNextFrame()` (`timer.cpp:
  71`) is reached by `UpdateGameOnce` (`game_run.cpp:1449`),
  `UpdateGameAudioOnly` (`:1459`), fades/shake (`global_screen.cpp:107,
  115`, `screen.cpp:124`), `Display()`/Say (`display.cpp:103`), dialog
  options (`dialog.cpp:1296`), the inventory window (`invwindow.cpp:
  425`); every blocking `GameLoopUntil*` wait runs `GameTick()` ->
  `UpdateGameOnce(true)` (`game_run.cpp:1524-1548`). One exception:
  `play.fast_forward` (skipped cutscenes) returns before the wait
  (`game_run.cpp:1442-1446`) -- `update_polled_stuff()` (`:1628`, called
  on every path) needs the pump too.
- **The pump hook must be explicit.** The frame sleep is `std::this_
  thread::sleep_for` (`timer.cpp:98`), as are `platform->Delay()`/
  `YieldCPU()` (`agsplatformdriver.cpp:263-283,129-134`); `SDL_Delay`
  appears nowhere in Engine for DOS. Under this DJGPP libstdc++
  `_GLIBCXX_USE_NANOSLEEP` and `_GLIBCXX_HAS_GTHREADS` are both undefined
  (`c++config.h:1691,1820`) -- the generic `__sleep_for` fallback, i.e.
  exactly the "a sleep that bypasses `SDL_Delay` gets total silence"
  trap the hub's `docs/audio.md:88-100` documents and dossage hit.
- **Clip loading and memory**: assets <= `MaxLoadAtOnce` (1 MB default,
  `sound.h:26`, `[sound] stream_threshold`) are read whole into
  `SoundCache` (2 MB on DOS via patch 0039) and decoded from memory;
  larger ones stream from the asset `Stream`. The cache holds RAW FILE
  BYTES -- a WAV already at the device format costs zero conversion.
- **The replacement seam is small**: `AudioPlayer` (`audioplayer.h:36-
  74`: `Play/Pause/Stop/Seek(ms)/Poll/GetPositionMs/GetDurationMs/
  GetFrequency/SetVolume/SetSpeed/SetPanning/GetPlayStateNormal`) is the
  whole contract `SoundClip::update()` drives (`soundclip.cpp:133-175`).
  Today's stubs: 0016 (`sys_audio_init()` returns false -> `engine_init_
  audio()` sets `usetup.AudioEnabled=false`, `engine.cpp:394-419`), 0022
  (`SDLDecoder::Open()` always fails), 0023 (`audio_core_*` no-ops,
  `OpenAlSource` interface kept), 0005/0006/0007 (CMake gates for mojoAL,
  SDL2_sound, Cda).
- **Script-API minimums**: every hard `quit()` in the audio API is
  argument validation, never backend state (`global_audio.cpp:55,98,327,
  336,338,354,419`; `audiochannel.cpp:203,213`; `PlaySilentMIDI` only
  quits if MIDI is already playing, `:394`); channel ops are `if (ch)`-
  guarded. A MIDI sink returning 0/NOP for seek/position is upstream-
  equivalent (upstream already returns 0). Speed/panning may be no-ops
  on a mono mixer.
- **Where clips live**: `audio.vox` if present (`GetAudioVOXName()`,
  `gamesetupstructbase.h:200`; lookup `engine.cpp:320-372`), else the
  main pack (`AddLibrary(GamePak, ",audio")`, `:353`); path via
  `AssetPath(fileName,"audio")` (`file.cpp:904-913`). The compiled AGS
  Quest has no `audio.vox`: 18 assets in `AGSQuest.ags` (CLIB v30):
  `au00000C-10.ogg`, `au000011.wav`, `au000012.mid`, `game28.dta`, rooms,
  fonts, sprites.
- **The clip record the host tool patches**: `ScriptAudioClip::
  ReadFromFile` (`scriptaudioclip.cpp:59-73`) is a fixed 64-byte record
  -- id(4) + scriptName(30) + fileName(15) + bundlingType@49 + type@50 +
  **fileType@51** + repeat + pad + priority(2) + volume(2) + pad(2) +
  reserved(4) -- read by `read_audio` (`gamesetupstruct.cpp:299-316`)
  after the variable-length plugin/custom-property sections
  (`main_game_file.cpp:1171-1179`) inside `game28.dta`. The 15-byte
  `fileName` is a unique anchor for in-place patching. The decoder hint
  is the asset name's extension if present, else `GetExtFromAudioFile
  Type(fileType)` (`sound.cpp:121-122`); legacy `MUS_*` behaviour
  derives from that extension (`sound.cpp:31-45`). 3.6.1+ games carry
  `v361_objnames`, which overrides `clip.fileName` from a variable-
  length string (`main_game_file.cpp:952-957`) -- so the tool keeps
  names, swaps only the bytes, and our loader sniffs RIFF regardless of
  extension.
- **CLIB v30 has a writer in-tree**: `Common/data/multifilelib.cpp`
  `ReadV30` (`:380-397`) and `WriteHeader/WriteV30/WriteEnder` (`:399-
  441`); TOC = reserved int32, lib-name cstrings, per asset cstring +
  libUid(1) + offset(8) + size(8), payloads after. Trivial to mirror in
  Python. `tests/fixtures/minimal-game-package/build_fixture.py:64-86`
  writes only the v6 single-lib format -- not reusable as-is.
- **Minimum loadable data version**: `main_game_file.cpp:174` rejects
  `DataVersion < kGameVersion_250` (`= 18`, `game_version.h:154`; "can
  only run games made with AGS 2.5 or later", `:64`); current is
  `kGameVersion_363_10` (`:201`). AGS 2.0x-2.4x games (2000-2001, e.g.
  Rob Blanc) cannot load without an Editor re-save.

### What the shared layer provides, and what it measured

- **SB PCM (DMA)** is the only SDL streaming device (`vendor/SDL/src/
  audio/dos/SDL_dosaudio_sb.c`): 44100 floor by default, dropped per
  port via `SDL_DOSAudioSetDeviceFrameRate(hz)` (`SDL/0090`,
  `SDL_dosaudio_devicerate.h`; dossage: 11025, `patches/passage/0009`);
  the 8-bit DMA path defaults to U8 mono (`SDL/0107`, hints
  `SDL_HINT_DOS_AUDIO_SB_FORCE_8BIT`/`_SB_8BIT_STEREO`), SB16 negotiates
  S16 stereo; ring `SDL_HINT_DOS_AUDIO_RING_CHUNKS` default 16
  (`SDL/0023`); `SDL_DOSAudioPump()` (`SDL/0067`, `SDL_dosaudio_pump.h`)
  is the mandatory per-frame service call.
- **Hardware MIDI primitives** are in shared: OPL3/OPL2 register
  transport, detect, 18-voice offsets, note on/off (`SDL/0037`,
  `SDL_dos_audio_synth.h`); a PIT/INT8 pump for SB-less AdLib (`SDL/
  0110`); MPU-401/WaveBlaster init, byte write, DRR polling (`0037`,
  `0047`, `0080-0101`); a native GUS/GF1 backend (`SDL/0112-0114`,
  `SDL_dosgus.h`; `SDL_HINT_DOS_GUS_VOICES` 20, `_GUS_SFX_VOICES` 4).
  `shared/audio/midi_sched.{c,h}` is the SMF parser + tick scheduler:
  plain C, a 4-callback sink (`note_on/note_off/control_change/
  program_change`), main-loop tick, no ISR -- doskutsu's `0101`
  MidiScheduler already ported.
- **NOT in shared -- the actual GM sinks and backend selection**, all in
  doskutsu's engine patches (`~/git/doskutsu/patches/nxengine-evo/`):
  `0102` WaveBlaster passthrough (170+82 lines); `0103` OPL3 (549+130:
  GM program -> OPL3 patch, fnum/block, drums) with fixes `0106`
  (hanging note), `0141` (bank loader), `0142` (reg 0xBD clear), `0171`
  (release rate), `0232` (transpose byte, 8.3 bank name); `0235` OPL2/
  AdLib (451+119); `0238` GUS (607+139, GM `.pat` loader) with fixes
  `0243-0245`, `0248-0249`, `0254-0255`, `0261` (drum clamp). Every sink
  subclasses a C++ `MidiBackend` (`MidiScheduler.h`) and uses nxengine's
  `Logger.h`; the shared scheduler is C with the 4-callback sink. **The
  hoist is a re-base of ~2,000 lines onto `midi_sched_sink` plus a log
  shim, not a file move** (WB ~250, OPL3 ~900, OPL2 ~570, GUS ~800).
  Backend selection (`auto/organya/wb/opl3/adlib/gus/none`) lives in
  `vendor/nxengine-evo/src/sound/AudioBackend.cpp:27-203`; its auto
  chain is OPL3 -> Organya, and WaveBlaster is deliberately NOT auto-
  probed (doskutsu `0217`: an MPU-401 status read can stall the ISA
  bus). Shared `SDL/0071`/`0075` only read the hint.
- **Assets and licensing for `shared/`**: `opl3bank.dat` is 1,548 bytes,
  generated by doskutsu's `scripts/gen-opl3-bank.py` from DMXOPL's
  `GENMIDI.op2` (github.com/sneakernets/DMXOPL). doskutsu's `THIRD-
  PARTY.md:50-70` records the repo LICENSE as MIT while DoomWiki says
  CC BY-SA 4.0 -- per the hub's licensing rule the LICENSE at a pinned
  SHA gets re-read before the bank enters `shared/`, and the generator
  moves with it. GUS `.pat` sets ship nothing: loaded at runtime from
  the user's `%ULTRADIR%\MIDI` (doskutsu `docs/SOUND.md:118-160`) -- no
  `shared/` exposure.
- **Measured, real hardware** (doskutsu `docs/SOUND.md` "Performance",
  `docs/CONFIG.md`, `qa-results/MATRIX-POD83.md`, `docs/TAS-
  BENCHMARKING.md:169`, `PLAN.md:569`; dossage `PLAN.md:15-60,118-140`,
  `patches/passage/0009,0039,0041`): doskutsu's default Tier-2 is 11025
  Hz mono (`SDL_HINT_DOS_AUDIO_TIER2=1`); 22050 stereo cost ~11 fps in
  music-heavy scenes; the SB16 IRQ alone cost ~13.5 ms/flip with an
  idle callback until the rate was halved; the Organya software synth
  cost ~9 fps vs hardware MIDI; OPL3/AdLib FM music runs within ~1 fps
  of music-off and SFX cost ~0.3 fps; GUS runs ~4 fps lower, entirely
  `.pat` upload stalls at song boundaries. dossage on the 486DX2-50:
  22050 stereo ~10 fps vs 11025 mono 14.79 -- audio CONVERSION was 43%
  of every frame until `0039` converted the song once to the negotiated
  device format at load, after which both tiers ran 14.97-15.02; the
  silence-detect throttle cost 0.08-0.18 fps.
- **Hub `docs/audio.md` rules this plan follows**: phase order PCM ->
  MIDI -> compressed only if profiled -> game-specific formats; hardware
  MIDI first on a 486; `SDL_DOSAudioPump()` every frame with a target-
  depth top-up, not run-to-cap; every sleep path must reach `SDL_Delay`;
  `SDL_Delay(0)` mid-loop below ~20-22 fps; a ~21-25 fps wall-clock
  floor for any in-callback synthesis (the reason there is none here);
  A/B `SDL_HINT_DOS_SILENCE_DETECT` per port; never PIT channel 0 for a
  pump (`SDL/0122`); never GF1 diagnostic reads on PicoGUS; avoid 28 GUS
  voices; clamp drum notes; test on the slowest CPU.
- **The rig audio verdict, as it exists today** (`~/git/vcctrl/agent/
  vcctrl_mcp.py:945-1010`, `bin/vcctrl-audio`, hub `docs/hardware-
  testing.md:155-180`): the g2k's line-out feeds the capture stick's
  ALSA device (`capabilities.audio.settings.device`, default `hw:1,0`),
  read non-invasively from the daemon's PCM ring. `vcctrl_audio_verdict
  (ms)` -> NO_SIGNAL / SILENT / AUDIO_PRESENT + `tone_like`, from level
  plus 8 octave bands (100 Hz-12.8 kHz, `common/audio_bands.verdict()`);
  reference points -30.8 dB mean for working audio vs -65.6 dB floor,
  ~-91 dB disconnected; absolute levels are not comparable across
  sessions (a volume knob is in the path). `vcctrl_audio_match(file, ms)`
  decodes a LOCAL reference via ffmpeg to the same 8 bands and reports
  Jaccard overlap 0-1 -- **no calibrated threshold exists yet**. Our
  `autopilot_chime.wav` works as that reference as-is; `autopilot_tune.
  mid` does not (ffmpeg cannot render MIDI). RUNMANIFEST's
  `audio_vital_status` (`runmanifest.h:132`) is a free-form string with
  no vocabulary defined anywhere -- doskutsu (0138/0293) and dossage
  (0034) all emit `NA` -- so dosags defines the first real one.

### Architecture (what the measurements settle)

- **Replace, don't port.** mojoAL and SDL2_sound stay gated out (0005/
  0006 already do). A DOS `AudioPlayer` implementation + a small fixed-
  voice mixer feeds one SDL3 audio stream at the negotiated device
  format -- Tier-2 (11025 Hz mono) by default, hint-overridable; voice
  cap ~8 (3 reserved + 5), also a hint; every clip converted ONCE at
  load to that format (dossage's `0039` lesson), so the per-chunk mix is
  add-and-clip. The loader is a tiny RIFF WAV + Creative VOC parser that
  sniffs the header regardless of extension. No resampler on DOS: the
  host tool emits clips at the device tier.
- **MIDI clips (type 5) never reach the mixer**: `midi_sched` + a hoisted
  sink, ticked from the same main-loop hook; the music channel's
  `AudioPlayer` becomes a thin adapter (volume, stop, repeat; seek/
  position 0, upstream-equivalent). Backend selection reuses doskutsu's
  `SDL_HINT_DOS_AUDIO_BACKEND` semantics (`auto/opl3/wb/adlib/gus/none`);
  auto = OPL3 -> none, WaveBlaster never auto-probed (doskutsu `0217`).
- **Pump placement**: `SDL_DOSAudioPump()` + the MIDI tick beside
  `audio_core_entry_poll()` in `WaitForNextFrame()`, and again in
  `update_polled_stuff()` for the fast-forward path. Verified by the
  harness, not assumed: room 3's intro cutscene (blocking walk + three
  `Say`s) and the `dialog` phase both run under blocking waits.
- **`audio_vital_status` vocabulary (dosags defines it)**: a compact
  `pcm=<device>@<rate><ch><bits>,voices=<n>,underruns=<n>;midi=<backend>,
  events=<n>` string, e.g. `pcm=sb16@11025m8,voices=8,underruns=0;midi=
  opl3,events=1412`; `NA` only when no device opened. Underruns and
  event counts are what make a silent-but-"working" run detectable
  without ears.
- **Tracker music**: undecided until profiled (decision 5). The
  profiling slice's first question is which decoder to measure with --
  SDL2_sound is gone, so it is a new dependency either way (libxmp-lite
  vs libmodplug; licenses read before either is vendored, hub rule 6
  "no new dependencies casually"). If the cost is anywhere near the
  softsynth numbers above, the answer is pre-render.

**The five picks** (freeware, local-testing-only, never committed --
same rule as AGS Quest; only hashes, logs, and manifests enter git):

1. **5 Days a Stranger** (2003, 320x200x16, ~1 MB) -- the canonical
   MIDI-era freeware hit; a 1 MB download is almost certainly MIDI (or
   tiny MOD) + small SFX, i.e. the native hardware-MIDI path. One pass
   covers Yahtzee's whole Chzo run (7 Days, Trilby's Notes, 6 Days).
   In-profile depth. Loadability very likely, verify.
2. **Trilby's Notes** (2006, 320x200x8, ~2 MB) -- the only loadable
   top-20 title at the v0.1 in-profile 8-bit depth; 2.7x data, the last
   pre-3.0 format. **Doubles as the in-profile sound-on/off fps
   workload** until the self-authored game exists (decision 1).
3. **Maniac Mansion Deluxe** (2004, 320x200x16, 5.8 MB, still #2 by
   monthly downloads) -- the most-played remake; 5.8 MB at 16-bit
   suggests MIDI/tracker music plus WAV/OGG SFX, a good "does the host
   converter find anything" probe. Loadability likely, verify.
4. **A Tale of Two Kingdoms** (2007, 320x200x32, 95 MB, "75 minutes of
   music") -- the compressed-audio era at 320x200, the host converter's
   primary stress case. Off-profile (32-bit) and the original build may
   be unobtainable; fallbacks for the same slot: Duty and Beyond (2006,
   320x200x32, 4.3 MB) or Heroine's Quest (2013, 320x200x32, 400 MB).
5. **Nelly Cootalot: Spoonbeaks Ahoy!** (2007, 640x480x32, Best Game
   2007) -- hi-res + 32-bit + mid-era data; out of the v0.1 profile on
   both axes and almost certainly too slow on a 486. The compatibility-
   sweep ceiling case, not a Sound target. Alternative: A Second Face.

Only picks 1-3 are in-profile for the 486 target and the Sound
milestone; 4-5 need the 32-bit path (not in v0.1) and belong to the
compatibility sweep. First job of the porting framework's `inspect`
stage on each: the real `DataVersion` and the real clip-type mix.

Not determinable from the web, settled by `inspect` on a local copy:
data version for all but Shards of God/Strangeland; plugin lists; music
and speech formats (OGG vs MP3 vs MIDI); whether KQ1/KQ2+'s hosted
builds are the post-2.5 re-releases.

**The 32-bit display path is therefore a real, named slice**, added to
the Milestones list. Its first question is design, not scheduling:
either a genuine 32-bit VESA/LFB present path in the shared SDL3-DOS
backend (4 bytes per pixel, the Mach64's 2 MB VRAM fits 320x200x32 and
640x480x32), or running 32-bit games on the existing 16-bit path by
converting sprites/rooms to 16-bit at load (cheaper per frame, alpha
blending degraded -- AGS's own `Engine/ac/draw.cpp`/gfx conversion
routines decide whether that is even coherent). Read both before
choosing; do not schedule it ahead of Sound without the operator.

### Acceptance gate (refines the harness Milestone mapping's "Sound")

1. **DOSBox-X**: the harness's `audio` phase reports `ok` AND RUNMANIFEST
   carries a real `audio_vital_status` with `underruns=0` and a non-zero
   MIDI event count, against DOSBox-X's SB16 + OPL emulation. Correctness
   gate only; no fps claim.
2. **Real hardware, PCM**: `vcctrl_audio_verdict` reads SILENT before the
   `audio` phase and AUDIO_PRESENT during it (a differential, so a
   permanently-noisy line cannot pass), and `vcctrl_audio_match` against
   `autopilot_chime.wav` clears a threshold set by ONE calibration run
   and recorded in `results/` before it gates anything.
3. **Real hardware, MIDI**: `autopilot_tune.mid` is generated by
   `overlay/assets/generate_assets.py`, so its note sequence and timing
   are known in advance -- a small analysis script pitch-tracks the
   capture and matches fundamentals + onsets against that list (timbre
   differs per OPL3/WaveBlaster/GUS, so melody and tempo are compared,
   never the waveform). Passing that is the "strong assumption" bar of
   decision 7: the first real capture is then sent to the operator once,
   as a file, for a golden-reference listen.
4. **fps**: sound-on vs sound-off ABBA per `dos-hardware-validation`, on
   the in-profile workload (Trilby's Notes, or the self-authored game
   once it exists) on HW-486-66, AFTER the fixed-timestep change below
   has landed. Pre-registered bar, from doskutsu's own numbers: OPL3
   music + Tier-2 SFX costs <= 1.5 fps against sound-off. AGS Quest's
   delta is recorded alongside as a tracking number.
   **WAIVED for OPL3/WaveBlaster, 2026-09-15 (operator decision)**: a
   full real-hardware investigation (PLAN.md's chronological "S7 --"
   entries, eighteen-plus real-hardware cells) found this bar
   unreachable on this rig's current PGSB-profile hardware config for a
   source-verified, non-software reason -- see "S7 -- acceptance gate
   decision" below. **Re-targeted at GUS instead** -- **PASS, 2026-09-15**:
   real-hardware ABBA (tags `SGA1`/`SGB1`/`SGB2`/`SGA2`) measured a
   -0.05 fps cost (noise, not a real cost) against the <= 1.5 fps bar,
   all invalidity checks clean. See "S7-GUS -- acceptance gate item 4
   ABBA" below.
5. The milestone is claimed with operator sign-off, as PLAYABLE was.
   **Claimed 2026-09-15.**

      and 5, re-targeted at GUS. Real hardware (2026-09-14, tag `GUST1`,
      `tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/S7-gus-midi-realhw-2026-09-14.md`)
      confirmed GUS mode (no concurrent SB16 emulation) escapes the
      OPL3/WaveBlaster tax entirely -- catch-up ticks cost the same as
      the sound-off baseline. The originally-suspected `reap_finished_
      voices()`/`SDL_DOSGusGetState()` voice-mask-scan cost turned out to
      be a red herring once measured directly (exonerated as cheap,
      `S7-gus-getstate-cost-realhw-2026-09-15.md`) -- the real ~6.89s
      outlier was `gus_sink_prepare_song()`'s `.pat` upload PIO cost
      (root-caused, fixed via default GUS DRAM auto-increment,
      `patches/ags/0074`), and a separate session-level confound
      (`SDL_HINT_DOS_GUS_DIAG`'s own synchronous logging) explained an
      unrelated tick_rate anomaly along the way -- see the chronological
      "S7-GUS --" entries for the full path. **Real-hardware ABBA
      (2026-09-15, tags `SGA1`/`SGB1`/`SGB2`/`SGA2`): PASS** -- GUS
      sound-on costs -0.05 fps against sound-off (noise, not a real
      cost) against the pre-registered <= 1.5 fps bar, all invalidity
      checks clean (A-to-A and B-to-B spread both 0.00).
      `tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/
      S7-gus-acceptance-abba-realhw-2026-09-15.md`. **Operator sign-off
      2026-09-15: acceptance gate items 4 and 5 met, Sound milestone
      claimed.**

The porting framework (next section) proceeds in parallel: its `inspect`
and `convert` stages are host-side Python with no engine dependency, and
S2/S7 want its output (a converted golden reference) as a workload.

### S5 GUS architecture -- decided 2026-09-13, sixteenth session

Written before any GUS code, same discipline as the Sound milestone plan
itself: read the pinned sources first, then decide. WaveBlaster's own
scope (MIDI byte pass-through, PCM untouched) does NOT generalize to GUS
-- two real architectural gaps surfaced this session that WaveBlaster
never hit, both confirmed from source/rig docs, not assumed, and both
resolved by the operator as explicit scope decisions before any line of
GUS code was written:

**Gap 1 -- GUS has no simultaneous SB PCM device on this rig.** The
rig's `PGGUS` boot profile (`~/git/g2k/README.TXT` SOUND section) sets
only `ULTRASND`, no `BLASTER` string -- a genuine firmware-mode swap, not
an add-on alongside SB emulation. `dosags`'s own `dos_audio_mixer_init()`
(`platform/dos/dos_audio_mixer.cpp`) unconditionally opens an SDL
SB-PCM stream; under GUS that open will fail, and `sys_audio_init()`
(`platform/base/sys_main.cpp:242`) currently treats that failure as fatal
to the WHOLE audio subsystem (`SDL_QuitSubSystem(SDL_INIT_AUDIO)`, returns
false) -- which would silence MIDI too, not just PCM SFX. doskutsu's own
`docs/internal/GUS-NATIVE-DESIGN.md` hit this exact fork for GUS (and
AdLib before it) and resolved it as **model B, out-of-band**: when that
backend is selected, the SB16 + SDL3_mixer PCM device bring-up is skipped
entirely (`SoundManager.cpp`'s `_gus_path`/`_adlib_path` gates,
`patches/nxengine-evo/0238`) -- this rig's own `PGADLIB` profile already
ships that exact tradeoff as correct, documented behavior ("a real AdLib
has no DAC, so there are no digital sound effects in this profile, and
that is correct behaviour, not a fault," `g2k/README.TXT`).
**Operator decision: build a native GF1 PCM path too**, rather than
shipping GUS as MIDI-only like AdLib -- see Gap 2 for what that requires.

**Gap 2 -- GF1 hardware voices are not a streaming target.** AGS's own
WAV/VOC clip delivery (`OpenAlSource::PutData()`,
`media/audio/openalsource.cpp:51`) is fed chunk-by-chunk every poll
(`AudioPlayer::Poll()`, `media/audio/audioplayer.cpp:114-122`) into a
bounded ring -- exactly what the SB-DMA path expects, and the same model
`dos_audio_mixer.cpp`'s own 8-voice ring mixer already assumes. A GF1
voice plays from ONE static, already-uploaded DRAM sample (one-shot or
looped); there is no "feed me more bytes as you go" primitive
(`SDL3/SDL_dosgus.h`'s own header: "DMA = upload, NOT streaming").
doskutsu's own precedent for PCM-on-GF1, **`patches/nxengine-evo/0239`
+ fixes 0241/0242/0246/0247/0249/0256-0260 (Pixtone SFX on GF1 voices,
real and shipped, found this session -- the original GUS handoff did not
know about this series)**, sidesteps the mismatch entirely: Cave Story's
117 `.pxt` SFX are a small, fixed, fully-known-at-compile-time set,
uploaded ONCE at boot and played as simple one-shot voices. AGS's own
`audio.vox`/CLIB clips are dynamic, arbitrary-length, arbitrary-count --
never that shape. **Operator decision: build true streaming**, not a
bounded-resident-clip approximation.

**What true streaming can actually be built from, given the exposed
primitives (checked, not assumed):** `SDL3/SDL_dosgus.h` exposes
`voice_active_mask` (per-voice active/inactive, in `SDL_DOSGusState`) but
NO per-voice live playback-position read, and `SDL_DOSGUS_IRQ` is
explicitly a documented no-op ("the IRQ-independent driver never enables
wave-end IRQs -- poll `voice_active_mask` instead"). True register-level
ping-pong (loop a voice, rewrite the far half while the near half plays,
timed off a live position register) is NOT buildable against the current
shared SDL3-DOS GF1 export surface without a new low-level export (a
separate, larger hub `shared/` change, not undertaken here). What IS
buildable from what already exists: **alternating one-shot half-buffers,
swapped on reap.** Play buffer A as a one-shot voice; while it plays,
decode/accumulate the next chunk into buffer B and upload it; poll
`voice_active_mask` every pump cycle (the same cadence
`dos_audio_mixer_pump()`/`SDL_DOSAudioPump()` already run at); the instant
A's bit clears, immediately start B (already uploaded) and begin
refilling A. This is genuinely gapless only if the poll cadence stays
ahead of playback -- unlike a hardware DMA ring, a slow frame can miss the
swap window and produce an audible click/underrun. This is a real,
measured risk, not something to solve preemptively with more complexity
(no wave-end IRQ path exists to remove the polling dependency) --
DOSBox-X + real-hardware validation must characterize it, matching this
project's own "measure, don't assume" discipline
(`docs/optimization.md`).

**Voice/DRAM sharing with GUS MIDI (already solved at the shared layer,
not something to build):** the hub's vendored SDL3-DOS already carries
`SDL_DOSGusAllocVoiceSfx()` (`shared/patches/sdl3-dos/0114`, a reserved
top-slice partition of the voice pool, sized by
`SDL_HINT_DOS_GUS_SFX_VOICES`) -- doskutsu's own Pixtone-on-GF1 path
(`patches/nxengine-evo/0259`) already uses exactly this to keep SFX from
stealing music's voices. The new PCM-streaming module allocates from this
SAME reserved partition, so GUS MIDI's own note-voice pool
(`SDL_DOSGusAllocVoice()`, hub `shared/audio/gus_sink.c`, below) is
untouched by construction -- no new voice-arbitration code needed. DRAM
is the remaining shared resource: GUS MIDI's own per-song `.pat`
residency (lazy, bounded by the card's <=1MB DRAM) and the PCM module's
own upload buffers both live in the same DRAM space. doskutsu's own
`RESERVE_FOR_MUSIC` split (`patches/nxengine-evo/0239`/`0260`, tuned
320KB -> 384KB from real g2k data) is the precedent to adapt, not
re-derive from scratch -- exact split is a DOSBox-X/real-hardware tuning
question, not a design one.

**Work order for this sub-slice (each independently buildable/committed,
per this project's own narrow-slice rule):**
1. **Hub hoist, `shared/audio/gus_sink.{c,h}`**: `MidiBackendGus`
   (`patches/nxengine-evo/0238`) + fixes `0243`-`0245`/`0248`-`0249`/
   `0254`-`0255`/`0261` rebased onto `midi_sched_sink`, same pattern as
   `opl3_sink.c`/`waveblaster_sink.c`. GM `.pat` files stay user-supplied
   (`%ULTRADIR%`) -- no licensing work, matching the Sound milestone
   plan's own decision. A standalone DOSBox-X probe (`gussinkmd.c`,
   mirroring `wbsinkmd.c`/`opl3midi.c`) validates it in isolation.
2. **Hub, `shared/audio/gus_pcm_stream.{c,h}` (new -- no doskutsu
   patch to rebase; this project's own design)**: the alternating
   one-shot half-buffer streaming primitive described above, allocating
   from `SDL_DOSGusAllocVoiceSfx()`. Generic (any port could want GUS PCM
   streaming), so it lives in `shared/`, not `dosags/patches/ags/`.
3. **dosags wiring**: `dos_audio_mixer` gains a GUS-backed
   implementation (using step 2's module instead of the SDL SB stream)
   selected the same way `dos_midi_backend` already selects a MIDI
   backend; `sys_audio_init()` restructured so GUS skips the SB/
   `SDL_INIT_AUDIO` bring-up entirely (doskutsu's own model B) rather
   than attempting-and-failing it; `audio_vital_status` gains a
   `pcm=gus@...` form.
4. **DOSBox-X validation** of the whole stack together (does DOSBox-X's
   GUS emulation support `voice_active_mask` polling well enough to
   validate the swap-on-reap logic at all -- an open question, check
   before trusting any DOSBox-X streaming result as more than a
   correctness smoke test, per `dosbox_not_proxy`).
5. **Real-hardware validation** on the rig's PicoGUS under `PGGUS`
   (`pgusinit` mode-check only, never a GF1 diagnostic read) -- needs the
   operator's own fresh go-ahead before any rig action, same standing
   rule as every other real-hardware step this project has taken.

### Real-hardware finding, 2026-09-13: DMA upload does NOT share PIO's wedge risk

Item 1 (`gus_sink.{c,h}`) landed and was DOSBox-X-validated this same
session -- `feaa0c9`. Before starting item 2, the open safety question
above (can ANY upload happen while a voice plays, without wedging the
real PicoGUS) was tested directly on HW-486-66, PGGUS, with the
operator's own fresh go-ahead for the specific hang risk. A new
standalone probe, `shared/tests/probes/gusdmawedge.c` (`4fa9c1f`,
DOSBox-X-unvalidatable -- see its own doc for a separate, pre-existing
DOSBox-X/CWSDPMI `disable()`/`enable()` incompatibility affecting this
whole probe family, not this probe specifically), brought up the GF1,
started voice 0 looping, and attempted a DMA-based upload of a second
sample to a different DRAM region while voice 0 kept sounding --
mirroring `SDL_dosaudio_gus.c`'s own `gus_upload_dma()` register sequence
byte-for-byte.

**Result: `DMATEST=1 REPEAT=3` completed cleanly.** All 3 attempts
returned `poll_ok=1` (no hang), the post-hoc DRAM verify showed 0/64
mismatches (correct data, not just "didn't crash"), and the machine
returned to a normal prompt. Full log: `GUSDMAWE.LOG`, reproduced in
`shared/tests/probes/GUSDMAWEDGE.md`'s revision history. This is one
clean pass at one configuration (single voice, 4096-byte chunk, 3 reps)
-- not proof for every condition (more voices, bigger chunks, longer
runs still worth trying during item 5's own real-hardware validation) --
but it is real evidence, from the actual failure-prone hardware, that
**DMA-based upload is the mechanism item 2 should build on**, not the
PIO path gus-3's wedge was found on.

**Consequence for item 2's design, made concrete:**
- `SDL_DOSGusUploadSample()` (already exported, already vendored) already
  contains this exact DMA path -- it silently uses it when
  `SDL_HINT_DOS_GUS_DMA_UPLOAD=1` AND the upload is
  `>= GUS_DMA_UPLOAD_MIN` (4096 bytes, `SDL_dosaudio_gus.c`). Item 2 does
  NOT reimplement DMA upload (that would duplicate untested code the
  probe didn't exercise) -- it calls the existing export, and sets the
  hint itself at stream-open time (documented why: this session's own
  finding, not assumed safe by default) if not already set.
- **Half-buffer `chunk_bytes` MUST be >= `GUS_DMA_UPLOAD_MIN` (4096
  bytes)** or an upload silently falls back to the wedge-vulnerable PIO
  path with no error -- a real footgun to guard against (an assert or a
  runtime clamp-up in `gus_pcm_stream_open()`, not just a doc comment).
  At Tier-2 (11025 Hz mono S16), 4096 bytes is ~186 ms per half -- close
  to `dos_audio_mixer.cpp`'s own existing `TARGET_QUEUED_BYTES` (~186 ms)
  by coincidence, not by design; keep them independently tunable.
- **No new arbitration needed for the single shared playback-DMA
  channel.** `SDL_DOSGusUploadSample()`'s DMA path is synchronous (it
  blocks until that transfer's own completion poll returns, per
  `gus_upload_dma()`), and DOS has no real concurrency -- every
  `gus_pcm_stream_pump()` call across every open stream runs on the same
  single thread, so two DMA transfers physically cannot overlap. A pump
  call that needs a refill will briefly block for the transfer's
  duration (matching the existing accepted cost of the MIDI `.pat`
  PIO-burst uploads) -- not a new kind of cost, just a new site of it.

### Correction, same day: DMA validation only covers 8-bit uploads -- GUS PCM is 8-bit, not S16

The item-2 implementation fork caught this before writing any code (good
catch, reported rather than guessed past): `SDL_DOSGusUploadSample()`'s
DMA path has a THIRD, unstated gate the API sketch below originally
missed -- `SDL_dosaudio_gus.c:1213`, `want_dma = (g_gus_dma_upload &&
!is16bit && len >= GUS_DMA_UPLOAD_MIN)`. **16-bit uploads always take
PIO**, deliberately (`SDL_dosaudio_gus.c:1204`'s own comment: "16-bit
always takes PIO (sidesteps the 16-bit DMA dest quirk)" -- an
unimplemented 16-bit DMA destination-addressing difference noted in
`GUS-NATIVE-DESIGN.md`'s own register map, sec 2.3's 16-bit address
shift). `gusdmawedge.c`'s real-hardware pass uploaded an 8-bit payload
(`is16bit=0`) -- it validated 8-bit DMA specifically, saying nothing
about 16-bit. `dos_audio_mixer`'s existing device format
(`DOS_AUDIO_MIXER_FORMAT`) is `SDL_AUDIO_S16` -- built as originally
sketched, `gus_pcm_stream` would silently take 16-bit PIO for every real
upload, inheriting the wedge risk this whole design exists to avoid,
while looking safe because the hint is set.

**Operator decision: GUS PCM streaming is 8-bit unsigned, not 16-bit.**
Stays entirely on the validated-safe DMA path; no new real-hardware wedge
research needed (the alternative -- fixing the shared driver's 16-bit DMA
addressing quirk -- is a real, separate hub `shared/` project needing its
own fresh wedge/correctness validation, not undertaken here). This also
roughly matches what this exact rig's own SB path already delivers in
practice: `PGSB` is a PicoGUS-in-SB-2.0-mode profile, 8-bit-DMA hardware
regardless of the mixer's logical S16 request (`g2k/README.TXT`'s own
"T3 rather than T6... matches the card's 8-bit-DMA reality"). Consequence
for item 3: `dos_audio_mixer`'s device format becomes backend-dependent
(S16 for SB, U8 for GUS) rather than the single compile-time
`DOS_AUDIO_MIXER_FORMAT` constant it is today -- a real structural change
to that header, not just a new branch, since whatever currently reads
that constant (the mixdown loop, `sdldecoder.cpp`'s convert-once-at-load
step, the status-string bit-width report) needs to ask the active
backend rather than assume one format hub-wide. `gus_pcm_stream_open()`
below no longer takes a `bits` parameter -- it IS 8-bit unsigned, always;
leaving a parameter that could be misset back to 16 and silently
reintroduce the wedge risk is exactly the footgun this correction exists
to close.

### Correction #2, same day: `SDL_DOSGusUploadSample()` is a bump allocator -- streaming needs a new export

The item-2 fork caught this too, before writing code: `gus_dram_alloc()`
(`SDL_dosaudio_gus.c:626-651`) permanently advances a bump pointer on
every call and always returns a NEW address -- there is no exported
primitive to overwrite an already-allocated DRAM region. The only
reclaim mechanism, `SDL_DOSGusResetDram(keep_bytes)`, rewinds the entire
allocator to one global point and invalidates everything above it
(`gus_sink.c`'s own per-song `.pat` swap already uses exactly this, with
every voice stopped first). The "alternating half-buffers, refill the
one that just finished" design assumed the two half-buffer addresses
could be refilled in place across the stream's whole lifetime --
`SDL_DOSGusUploadSample()` cannot do that; each refill would mint a
brand-new region instead, permanently consuming ~11KB/sec of the shared
<=1MB DRAM budget for as long as any one stream plays. Not a tuning
question -- a hard ceiling reached in around two minutes for even a
single voice.

**Operator decision: extend the shared driver with a new export**,
`SDL_DOSGusOverwriteSample()`, rather than reverting to bounded resident
clips. Design (to add as a new `shared/patches/sdl3-dos/` patch,
`docs/patch-conventions.md` numbering/provenance discipline applies):

```c
/**
 * Upload a sample block to a CALLER-CHOSEN DRAM address, overwriting
 * whatever was there -- unlike SDL_DOSGusUploadSample, this does NOT
 * bump-allocate; the caller owns the address (from an earlier
 * UploadSample call, or its own bookkeeping) and its validity (< the
 * card's dram_size). Mirrors UploadSample's transfer mechanics EXACTLY
 * (same 8-bit-DMA-only + >=GUS_DMA_UPLOAD_MIN gate; 16-bit always PIO,
 * matching Correction #1 above) -- this export changes only WHERE the
 * data lands, nothing about HOW it gets there, so it inherits
 * gusdmawedge.c's own wedge-safety finding by construction rather than
 * needing a new wedge investigation from scratch (the wedge mechanism is
 * bus contention during the transfer itself, which does not know or
 * care whether the destination address was freshly bump-allocated or
 * reused).
 *
 * SAFETY (caller's responsibility, not enforced here): never overwrite a
 * region a CURRENTLY ACTIVE voice is reading. gus_pcm_stream only ever
 * targets the half NOT presently playing, confirmed via
 * voice_active_mask before every overwrite -- see gus_pcm_stream_pump().
 *
 * \returns true on success, false on failure (address >= dram_size).
 * \since sdl3-dos patch NNNN (assign at land time).
 */
extern SDL_DECLSPEC bool SDLCALL
SDL_DOSGusOverwriteSample(Uint32 dram_addr, const void *data, Uint32 len, int is16bit);
```

Implementation shape: factor `SDL_DOSGusUploadSample()`'s existing
transfer logic (the PIO/DMA dispatch, `gus_upload_dma()`/the PIO burst
loop) out from its `gus_dram_alloc()` call into an internal
`gus_upload_to(Uint32 dest, ...)` helper; `UploadSample` becomes
`gus_upload_to(gus_dram_alloc(len, is16bit), ...)`, and the new
`OverwriteSample` becomes `gus_upload_to(caller_addr, ...)` after a
bounds check. **Still needs its own confirming real-hardware pass before
`gus_pcm_stream` depends on it** (this project's own "measure, don't
assume" discipline, `docs/optimization.md`) -- the reasoning above that
it inherits the existing wedge finding is an inference, not yet a
measurement; a small extension to `gusdmawedge.c` (or a new probe) that
overwrites an already-once-written address while a different voice plays
is the cheap way to confirm it before trusting it in the real mixer path.

**`gus_pcm_stream.h` API (hub `shared/audio/`, to write in item 2; revised again)**:

```c
typedef struct gus_pcm_stream gus_pcm_stream;

// Allocates one voice from the reserved SFX partition
// (SDL_DOSGusAllocVoiceSfx) + two FIXED DRAM half-buffer regions of
// chunk_bytes each, allocated ONCE via SDL_DOSGusUploadSample (silence)
// at open time and refilled in place thereafter via
// SDL_DOSGusOverwriteSample (Correction #2) -- never re-allocated, so
// DRAM use is bounded and constant for the stream's whole lifetime, not
// proportional to how long it plays. Clamps chunk_bytes up to
// GUS_DMA_UPLOAD_MIN if given smaller. Sets SDL_HINT_DOS_GUS_DMA_UPLOAD=1
// if unset. Stream data is ALWAYS 8-bit unsigned PCM -- no bits/format
// parameter, by design (Correction #1: a 16-bit option would silently
// take the wedge-vulnerable PIO upload path with no error). NULL on
// failure (no voice, no DRAM) -- same graceful-degradation contract as
// the rest of this mixer.
gus_pcm_stream *gus_pcm_stream_open(unsigned rate, unsigned channels,
                                     size_t chunk_bytes);

// Appends already-device-format PCM into the pending host-side fill
// buffer. Returns bytes accepted (0 = full, caller retries next pump).
size_t gus_pcm_stream_write(gus_pcm_stream *s, const void *data, size_t bytes);
size_t gus_pcm_stream_queued(const gus_pcm_stream *s);
void   gus_pcm_stream_set_active(gus_pcm_stream *s, bool active);
void   gus_pcm_stream_stop(gus_pcm_stream *s);   // drop pending data, silence
void   gus_pcm_stream_set_volume(gus_pcm_stream *s, float volume);

// Call every pump cycle (same cadence as dos_audio_mixer_pump()). If the
// currently-playing half's voice has gone inactive (voice_active_mask)
// and the OTHER half already has a full chunk staged, retrigger onto it
// immediately (StartVoice) and begin overwriting the half that just
// finished (SDL_DOSGusOverwriteSample, DMA, its FIXED address from
// open()) with the next pending chunk.
void gus_pcm_stream_pump(gus_pcm_stream *s);

int  gus_pcm_stream_underrun_count(const gus_pcm_stream *s);  // swap missed its window
void gus_pcm_stream_close(gus_pcm_stream *s);
```

**Voice-budget tension, flagged not solved**: `dos_audio_mixer`'s
existing 8-voice budget (3 reserved + 5 normal) assumes the SB path's
ordinary voice pool. `SDL_DOSGusAllocVoiceSfx()`'s reserved partition is
clamped to `<= num_voices/4` at GF1 device-open -- e.g. 20 active voices
(doskutsu's own best-sounding default, avoiding the 28-voice PicoGUS
firmware dead-zone) caps the SFX/PCM partition at 5, not 8. dosags has no
separate Pixtone-style engine SFX system competing for that partition
the way doskutsu does, so the whole reserve is available for PCM
streaming voices alone -- but 5 < 8 still means the GUS path may need a
smaller effective voice cap than the SB path's, or a larger
`SDL_HINT_DOS_GUS_SFX_VOICES`/`GUS_VOICES` pairing than doskutsu's own
tuned default. Not resolved here -- a real-hardware tuning question for
item 5, not a design blocker for item 2.

### Real-hardware finding, 2026-09-13: first combined GUS MIDI+PCM run was ~2-3x slower than every prior baseline

First real-hardware run of AGS Quest under `PGGUS` (GUS MIDI via
`gus_sink` + GUS PCM via `gus_pcm_stream` together, tag GUSQ1) looked
hung mid-run (About screen static 74+s, `verify-input: false`) and was
recovered with a power cycle. Reading back `STDOUT.TXT`/`AUTOPLT.LOG`
afterward complicated that read: the log shows every scripted phase
completing (`status=ok` through `audio`), `DosMidiBackend: native GF1
(Gravis Ultrasound) backend active`, and a genuine `***** ENGINE HAS
SHUTDOWN` -- engine-level shutdown really did complete. No `GUSQ1.LOG`
(RUNMANIFEST) was ever written; `quit.cpp` shows RUNMANIFEST emission
runs strictly *after* that print, and nothing in that path (file I/O +
two counter reads) does live GF1 access, so whether the apparent late
hang was real (something in DOS-level exit after engine shutdown) or a
stale-frame artifact of the `vcctrl` primary-capture daemon bug fixed
this same session (commit `60469ad`, independent of `verify-input`) is
**still unresolved** and needs a clean re-test to settle -- not chased
further this round in favor of the regression below, which is
unambiguous and didn't need that resolved first.

**The regression itself is real and fully isolated to GUS**, confirmed
by comparing `t_ms` room-transition timestamps against four independent
prior real-hardware baselines that all land within ~1-2% of each other
regardless of MIDI backend:

| run | audio config | duration_s | fps_p50 | tick_rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S2 (2026-09-12) | SB PCM, no MIDI | 577 | 8.65 | 6.02 |
| S4MIDI1 (2026-09-12) | SB PCM + OPL3 MIDI | 609 | 8.57 | 5.90 |
| S5WB1/S5WB2 (2026-09-13) | SB PCM + WaveBlaster MIDI | 608 | 8.57 | 5.91 |
| GUSQ1 (2026-09-13) | GUS PCM + GUS MIDI | not completed -- `t_ms=753098` (~753s) reached at a room transition the *entire* S2 baseline run, start to finish, completes by `t_ms` ~577000 | -- | -- |

Any MIDI backend at all costs nothing (OPL3/WaveBlaster match the
no-MIDI baseline within noise) -- this is GUS-specific, not a general
MIDI-scheduling cost.

**Root cause (static analysis, not yet the subject of its own
real-hardware profiling run -- see below)**: `gus_pcm_stream_pump()`
called `SDL_DOSGusGetState()` every single call (i.e. every rendered
frame, for as long as any half-buffer is sounding) purely to learn
whether its OWN one voice was still running. `SDL_DOSGusGetState()`
scans EVERY busy GF1 voice on the card (cli/sti-wrapped register reads
each) to build a full mask -- correct for `gus_sink`'s `reap_finished_
voices()` (which genuinely needs to know about every voice, and is only
called on note-on, not every frame), wasteful for a caller that only
ever asks about one voice it already owns, every single frame. No
analogous per-frame full-hardware-scan exists anywhere in the SB/OPL3/
WaveBlaster paths (`SDL_DOSAudioPump()` is a memory-only ISR/ring-buffer
check) -- this is the one piece of new S5 GUS code that is both
GUS-exclusive and runs continuously for as long as any ambient/SFX PCM
clip plays, which for an adventure game is most of a run. Two other
hypotheses were checked and ruled out before landing on this one:
`DOS_SchedulerInit()` (thread subsystem, not audio-subsystem-gated, so
GUS's Model B skipping `SDL_INIT_AUDIO` doesn't affect it) and the
"external PIT pump (SDL/0110)" `SDL_dosaudio_gus.c` mentions for its
music clock (owned by the software OPL2/SB-synth path in
`SDL_dosaudio_sb.c`/`SDL_dos_audio_synth.c`, never engaged by `gus_sink`/
`gus_pcm_stream` on this real-hardware config where real OPL2/GF1
hardware exists, so it cannot be reprogramming anything here).

**Fix landed (hub commit, this session)**: new SDL export
`SDL_DOSGusVoiceActive(int voice)` (sdl3-dos patch 0140) -- the same
per-voice hardware read + start-race grace-window logic
`SDL_DOSGusGetState()` already used (factored into a shared static
`gus_voice_check_running()` so the two never diverge on that quirk
workaround), for exactly one voice, in its own short cli/sti section,
no full-mask scan. `gus_pcm_stream_pump()` now calls this instead of
`SDL_DOSGusGetState()`. `gus_sink.c`'s `reap_finished_voices()` is
unchanged -- it legitimately needs the full mask and is note-driven, not
frame-driven, so it was never the flagged hot path.

**Still needed before calling this done**: build + DOSBox-X validation
(this session), then a fresh real-hardware go-ahead for one more GUSQ1-
style run to (a) confirm the fix actually recovers baseline-comparable
`tick_rate`/`fps_p50`/duration, and (b) get a clean, complete
`GUSQ1.LOG` RUNMANIFEST this time, which would also settle the still-
unresolved late-hang-vs-capture-artifact question above as a side
effect of the run actually finishing at a normal speed.
