**A real, if minor, harness gap found and reported to the `vcctrl` session
during this collection**: `get-file`'s internal reboot job sends its own
Ctrl+Alt+Del under a fixed `"transfer"` input-lock identity and never
checks whether that combo call was refused before starting its LED-based
reset wait -- so if a caller holds the input lock under any *other* name
first (as this session did, prophylactically, before calling `get-file`),
every `get-file` reboot attempt is silently refused and times out
~130s later indistinguishable from a genuine dead machine. Cost four
failed attempts and an unnecessary (harmless, but unneeded) real
power-cycle before the actual cause -- lock self-contention, not a target
fault -- was found by capturing the raw `vcctrl_events` entry for the
refused `combo` call. Lesson for any future rig session: do not hold the
input lock yourself across a `get-file`/`send-file` call; let it manage
its own `"transfer"` identity.

## S6 -- Tracker/XM profiling: decoder pick, real-hardware measurement, decision -- 2026-09-13

Per the Sound milestone plan's decision 5 ("profile one real file on the
rig before deciding, unmeasured cost, deliberately not guessed") and the
Work order's S6 line. Same investigation style as the S5 GUS regression
above: static/design work first, then an isolated real-hardware
measurement, then a decision grounded in that number, not a guess.

### Decoder pick and license

**libxmp-lite**, MIT license, verified directly against `docs/COPYING` at
pin `github.com/libxmp/libxmp` commit
`1e0812137e4f9e15cc026c0c75af82d71d3cb5ad` -- fetched and read the actual
license text at that exact revision (twice: once via a research pass,
once independently re-fetched and re-read before treating the pick as
settled), not recalled or assumed. Picked over libmodplug: libmodplug's
closest maintained fork (`github.com/Konstanty/libmodplug`, upstream
proper is dead) is C++, has no lite/XM-only subset so all 26 tracker
formats' worth of source (~857KB) would compile in for a format we don't
need, and its own `COPYING` is a one-line, non-standard "now in the
public domain" dedication rather than a real license grant -- legally
murkier than libxmp-lite's plain MIT. libxmp-lite itself is pure C,
~328KB across 21 core + 4 loader files (file list read directly from
`lite/src/Makefile`/`lite/src/loaders/Makefile`, not guessed), a
memory-in/buffer-out API (`xmp_load_module_from_memory` ->
`xmp_start_player` -> `xmp_play_buffer`) with no zlib/depacker dependency
in the lite build (`LIBXMP_CORE_PLAYER` gates those out transitively), and
already has DOS-portability precedent in its own tree (a `Makefile.dos`
targeting OpenWatcom, not DJGPP, but evidence its authors already handle
a 32-bit protected-mode DOS target).

**Not yet vendored.** This was a profiling-only pin, built in a scratch
location outside both this repo and the hub -- no entry in
`vendor/sources.manifest` or `LICENSE-REVIEW.md` yet. A real integration
slice, if the decision below is ever acted on, should also ask the hub's
own "would every port want this" question before assuming tracker decode
belongs in `dosags/vendor/` rather than hoisted into the hub's
`shared/audio/` alongside the other backends this port already consumes
from there (PCM mixer primitives, MIDI sinks) -- not decided here, out of
scope for a profiling-only slice.

### Test file

No downloaded tracker module was used, deliberately -- sidesteps any
licensing/provenance question entirely for a file that was never going to
be committed or shipped. `TESTSONG.XM` was authored programmatically: 4
channels, 3 patterns x 64 rows, 2 looped 8-bit instruments, real note data
plus portamento/vibrato/volume-column effects (not a degenerate
near-silent test case, since those effects and multi-channel mixing are
what actually drive decode cost). Built against the real XM 1.04 format
spec, then validated by loading it through a natively-built (host gcc)
libxmp-lite -- correct channel/pattern/instrument/sample counts, 2000
`xmp_play_buffer` ticks decoded error-free across full loop cycles --
before ever touching DJGPP or DOS.

### Methodology

A standalone DJGPP probe (`tracker_probe.c`: pure C, no SDL, no engine --
same "isolated primitive, not the whole engine" style as the hub's GUS
probe suite, `.sdl-dos-ports/shared/tests/probes/GUS-PROBES.md`), built
against libxmp-lite's lite sources. Cross-compiled clean on the first try
against the DJGPP gaps this project already knows about (pthreads, mmap,
sys/io.h -- grepped for and confirmed absent from the lite source set;
only hit was `<dirent.h>`, already confirmed to PASS on this toolchain by
`tests/probes/djgpp-runtime/`). It loads `TESTSONG.XM`, starts the player
at 11025 Hz mono S16 (this port's Tier-2 rate; the 8-bit downsample to the
actual PCM device format is a separate, cheap, already-measured step --
not what this probe measures), then decodes fixed 40Hz-tick-sized chunks
in a loop, timing the run with `uclock()`/`UCLOCKS_PER_SEC` (the same PIT
clock this port's own RUNMANIFEST instrumentation uses). An exact 8-tick
Bresenham accumulator handles the 275.625 samples/tick fraction (5 ticks/8
render 276 samples, 3/8 render 275) with zero drift over an arbitrarily
long run. DOSBox-X smoke-tested first (parity config, not `--fast`) purely
as a correctness/liveness gate -- ran clean, plausible numbers -- per this
project's own rule that a DOSBox-X number is never a performance result;
nothing from that run informs the decision below.

### Real-hardware measurement, HW-486-66

`TRKPROBE.EXE` + `TESTSONG.XM` + `CWSDPMI.EXE` staged via vcctrl's generic
`send-file` (not a `tests/harness/`-style package -- a standalone probe
needs no engine build or game package), then run directly at a DOS prompt:
`TRKPROBE.EXE TESTSONG.XM 2000`. No engine, no audio hardware touched at
all (decode-to-memory-buffer only), so the boot profile/backend active at
the time is irrelevant -- this ran under `[PGSB]` (Sound Blaster profile)
purely because that happened to be the machine's state, with no bearing on
the result. Output, read directly off the console:

```
TRACKER_PROBE_INFO file=TESTSONG.XM bytes=4921 channels=4 patterns=4 instruments=2 samples=2
TRACKER_PROBE_FORMAT rate=11025 channels=1 sample_fmt=S16 tick_hz=40 nominal_tick_ms=25.0
TRACKER_PROBE_SAMPLES total_samples_rendered=551250
TRACKER_PROBE ticks=2000 total_ms=6161.3 avg_ms_per_tick=3.08 pct_of_25ms_tick=12.3
```

`551250` samples at 11025 Hz is exactly 50.0s of decoded audio, exactly
`2000 * 275.625` -- the tick-fraction accumulator carried zero drift over
the full run, a useful internal-consistency check on the measurement
itself, not just the decoder.

### Decision (decision 5)

**3.08 ms/tick, 12.3% of the *nominal* 25ms/40Hz tick budget.** But this
hardware never achieves that nominal budget in practice: every real
HW-486-66 baseline for AGS Quest so far (S2, S4MIDI1, S5WB, GUSQ2 --
see above) lands at `tick_rate` 5.90-6.48/s, i.e. an *actually achieved*
~154-169ms per tick already, from rendering plus the script VM plus the
existing PCM/MIDI mixer alone. Measured against that real, already-heavy
tick cost rather than the unattainable nominal one, an added 3.08ms is
only **roughly 1.8-2.0% relative overhead** -- nowhere near this same
section's two known expensive-synthesis reference points (the Organya
software synth's ~9fps hit vs. hardware MIDI; GUS's ~4fps hit, though that
one is a `.pat`-upload-stall artifact rather than a per-frame synthesis
cost). Both of those are tens of milliseconds of real per-frame cost
against a much smaller achieved-fps base -- an order of magnitude larger
than what was measured here.

**Verdict: native decode, not pre-render.** The measured cost is small
enough relative to what this hardware already spends per tick that
pre-rendering tracker music to WAV (decision 5's alternative -- which
would also need the same kind of host-side pipeline work as the OGG/MP3
pre-conversion in decision 2) buys nothing worth its own added complexity.

**Not done as part of this profiling slice** (a real integration slice's
own scope): vendoring libxmp-lite properly (the hub `shared/`
"would every port want this" question above, a real
`vendor/sources.manifest` pin, a `LICENSE-REVIEW.md` entry, `docs/
patch-conventions.md`-style provenance), wiring type-6 (MOD/XM/S3M/IT)
clips into the existing `AudioPlayer`/mixer seam the same way PCM and MIDI
clips already are, and a real in-game fps A/B (not just this isolated
decode-cost probe) before calling tracker support acceptance-gated.

**The real blocker**: neither Trilby's Notes nor a self-authored game
existed as a runnable package -- the "Game porting framework" section
below was fully designed but nothing was built. Operator chose to build
the minimal useful slice (`inspect`/`convert`/`repack`/`layout` only, not

DataVersion 27 (compiled with AGS 2.62), legacy pre-ScriptAudioClip-table
audio system. A dispatched research fork confirmed, by reading
`main_game_file.cpp`'s `ScanOldStyleAudio()` and the full `PlayMusic`/
`PlaySound` call chains, that this legacy path feeds the exact same
`load_sound_clip()`/`audio_core` dispatch a modern game's clips use -- no
engine gap, no new patch needed just to make legacy-audio games work.
`convert.py` turned out to be a verified no-op for this game: reading
`patches/ags/0050`'s own header comment showed the DOS WAV/VOC loader
already sniffs format and resamples/downmixes every clip once, at load
time, to the mixer's Tier-2 rate -- a real correction to the porting
framework's original design (which assumed a host-side resample step),
confirmed against source rather than guessed. The sound-on/off lever
needed by acceptance item 4 also turned out to already exist: `acsetup.
cfg`'s `[sound] enabled=0/1` (`Engine/main/config.cpp:416`) is a real,
already-shipping engine feature, closing the gap S2 had explicitly left
open ("no audio-disable lever exists") with zero new patches.
`tools/port-game/clib.py` (MFLUtil read/write transcribed from
`multifilelib.cpp`) was verified against the real game by round-tripping
its whole CLIB and diffing all 78 assets byte-for-byte against the
original before being trusted. DOSBox-X correctness confirmed both ABBA
arms cleanly (sound-on: `midi=opl3,events=64`; sound-off:
`audio_vital_status=NA`; both `exit_code=0`/`critical_count=0`) before
any real-hardware time was spent -- see `tests/games/trilbysnotes/
manifest.yaml` for the full DOSBox-X record.

**A real bug found and fixed mid-campaign**: the first two real-hardware
cells (A1, B1) silently ran **AGS Quest**, not Trilby's Notes -- a stale
`AGSQUEST.AGS` left on `C:\DOSAGS` from earlier Sound-milestone sessions
won `FindGameData()`'s "first `.ags`/`.exe` found in directory order"
scan (`Common/game/main_game_file.cpp:133-154`) over the newly-transferred
`NOTES.AGS`. Caught by checking each run's own `STDOUT.TXT` for
`AutoPilot.asc`/room-transition lines that have no business appearing in
a Trilby's Notes run -- exactly the "verify game identity independently,
don't trust the filename you sent" discipline this hub's harness work
already practices for hardware identity. Fixed by deleting
`AGSQUEST.AGS` from the target (confirmed via `DIR *.AGS` showing only
`NOTES.AGS` remaining) and re-running every affected cell. Real-hardware
file transfer itself was also flaky this session (two separate
send-file failures, `no-return` on different files each time, cause
undiagnosed -- see the `vcctrl` peer session's own read: not the ~10MB
warning, likely a NET/FTP session flake never provoked before at this
payload shape); isolating the failing files into their own small
transfer (rather than resending everything) reliably cleared it both
times.

**Real-hardware ABBA result (acceptance gate item 4): FAIL.** Full A/B/
B/A block on HW-486-66, `DOSAGS_FIXED_TIMESTEP=1` in every cell (so the
delta is a pure rendering/audio-servicing cost, not a game-speed
confound):

| Cell | Arm | fps_p50 | tick_rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | sound-off | 4.81 | 23.80 |
| B1 | sound-on (OPL3) | 0.57 | 3.27 |
| B2 | sound-on (OPL3) | 0.57 | 3.27 |
| A2 | sound-off | 5.17 | 23.86 |

A-to-A spread tight (0.36 fps_p50), B-to-B byte-for-byte reproducible
(`events=5254` identical both times) -- block is valid. Baseline avg
4.99 fps, sound-on 0.57 fps: **cost = 4.42 fps against the <= 1.5 fps
pre-registered bar**, not a marginal miss -- tick_rate itself collapses
~86%. A diagnostic cell (operator-requested, after the block) swapped
OPL3 for WaveBlaster, same config: collapse reproduces almost exactly
(0.55 fps, tick_rate 3.22) -- **not OPL3-specific**. Full raw data,
invalidity-check results, and the source-verified root-cause writeup:
`tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/S7-abba-2026-09-13.md`.

**Root cause (source-verified, not yet fixed)**: `dos_run_tick_fixed()`'s
catch-up loop (patch 0047) re-invokes `audio_core_entry_poll()` on every
catch-up tick (`game_run.cpp:1514-1529`'s `skip_render_and_wait` branch),
up to `MAX_CATCHUP+1=6` times per `GameTick()` call. On hardware this far
behind the 40Hz target, backlog never clears, so every `GameTick()` call
runs the full catch-up burst -- multiplying whatever `audio_core_entry_
poll()`/`dos_audio_mixer_pump()` really costs per call by up to 6x once a
MIDI backend is active (invisible with no audio device open, since an
empty slots list costs ~nothing). This is a genuine interaction between
two independently-shipped, independently-validated features (S0's fixed
timestep landed before any Sound-milestone patch existed; S1/S3/S5's
audio backends were validated against AGS Quest real-hardware runs that
never had `DOSAGS_FIXED_TIMESTEP=1` set) -- never exercised together at a
sustained catch-up rate until this ABBA. **Not fixed this session**:
next step is instrumenting `audio_core_entry_poll()`/
`dos_audio_mixer_pump()`'s own per-call cost directly (this hub's own
"instrument the thing that produces the unexplained quantity" rule, not
guessing at a fix), then a real HW11-style before/after measurement.
Acceptance items 4 and 5 stay open until a fix lands and re-measures
clean.

## S7 -- root-cause instrumentation + fix, DOSBox-X validated -- 2026-09-14

Picked up exactly where the prior session left off: instrument
`audio_core_entry_poll()`/`dos_audio_mixer_pump()`'s own per-call cost
directly rather than guessing at a fix. Added a temporary `AUDIOPRB.LOG`
diagnostic (patch 0059, `uclock()`-bracketed, per-window
accumulate-then-flush, no per-call I/O -- same idiom as `.sdl-dos-ports/
shared/patches/sdl3-dos/0136`) around this function's two real
components. Real result (DOSBox-X, Trilby's Notes, OPL3 MIDI + SB PCM
open): the slot `Poll()` loop (MIDI scheduling) is cheap, tens of
microseconds/call even with real event dispatch happening.
`dos_audio_mixer_pump()` alone costs ~10-11ms/call (mean, not a rare
spike), ~3400x+ a sound-off call. Traced to why by reading
`vendor/SDL/src/audio/dos/SDL_dosaudio_sb.c`: `dos_audio_mixer_pump()` ->
`SDL_DOSAudioPump()` -> `SDL_PlaybackAudioThreadIterate()` ->
`DOSSOUNDBLASTER_WaitDevice()`, whose fast path (ring has room) is cheap
but whose slow path spins on `DOS_Yield()` until the hardware ring drains
at real playback-rate pace -- calling this far more often than the ring's
own drain rate requires (up to `MAX_CATCHUP+1=6x` per `GameTick()`) means
most calls land in the slow, real-time-paced path. Confirms the prior
session's candidate (b) directly rather than guessing.

**Fix (patch 0060)**: `game_run.cpp`'s `play.fast_forward ||
skip_render_and_wait` branch's `audio_core_entry_poll()` call is now
gated to `play.fast_forward` only. A fixed-timestep catch-up tick
(`skip_render_and_wait`) no longer triggers it -- a catch-up burst is
bounded (`MAX_CATCHUP`) and always immediately followed by one real,
`WaitForNextFrame()`-serviced tick, so it's never starved; `play.
fast_forward` (cutscene skip, unbounded) keeps the call, preserving the
original S1 fix it was added for.

**DOSBox-X validation**: the `--fast` conf mostly keeps up with the 40Hz
target on its own and under-exercises the catch-up path, so re-ran the
A/B under the hub's parity conf (`cycles=fixed 40000`, `oplmode=opl3`
added) instead -- chronically behind target like HW-486-66, even though
DOSBox-X's absolute timing doesn't match real hardware 1:1. Same
`NOTES.ags`/config, two independently-verified-different binaries
(pre-fix vs post-fix, `sha256sum`-checked): tick_rate 13.85 -> 15.37
(sound-off ceiling in this same conf: 17.35), fps_p50 4.76 -> 6.67, and
`audio_core_entry_poll()`'s own call rate measurably dropped (a 200-call
AUDIOPRB.LOG window didn't fill once in 17s post-fix, vs filling in 18s
pre-fix). Real, same-direction improvement -- but well short of the real
hardware's ~86% collapse, because DOSBox-X's own WaitDevice/DOS_Yield/
SDL_Delay timing model doesn't reproduce that magnitude (expected, not a
new gap -- this backend's own `[[dosbox_not_proxy]]` precedent already
established DOSBox-X doesn't reproduce every real-SB16 timing hazard).
Full writeup: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/
S7-fix-dosbox-x-2026-09-14.md`.

**Not yet done, and NOT closeable from DOSBox-X alone**: a real
HW-486-66 A/B/B/A re-run of the exact `S7-abba-2026-09-13.md` block
against the patch-0060 build. Acceptance gate items 4 and 5 stay open
until that runs and passes the pre-registered `<= 1.5 fps` bar on actual
target hardware. Patch 0059's `AUDIOPRB.LOG` diagnostic is temporary and
should be reverted in a follow-up patch once that real-hardware
confirmation lands.

## S7 -- real-hardware re-run: FAIL again, DOSBox-X result did not predict this -- 2026-09-14

Same day, operator-approved real-hardware session, same A/B/B/A recipe
against the patch-0060 build (`binary_sha12=6e4c8a677027`):

| Cell | Arm | fps_p50 | tick_rate | duration_s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F7A1 | sound-off | 5.17 | 23.68 | 49 |
| F7B1 | sound-on (OPL3) | 0.58 | 3.37 | 308 |
| F7B2 | sound-on (OPL3) | 0.58 | 3.37 | 309 |
| F7A2 | sound-off | 5.22 | 23.77 | 49 |

A-to-A tight (matches the 2026-09-13 block's own spread), B-to-B
identical to two decimals -- block is valid. **Cost = 4.615 fps against
the pre-registered `<= 1.5 fps` bar -- FAIL, essentially unchanged from
the pre-fix 4.42 fps** (sound-on tick_rate 3.37 vs pre-fix 3.27, a ~3%
move indistinguishable from noise). Patch 0060 -- which removed the
up-to-6x mid-catch-up-burst re-invocation of `audio_core_entry_poll()`
and showed a real, measured improvement on DOSBox-X under a
comparably-slow conf -- had essentially **zero effect on real
hardware**. DOSBox-X's own `WaitDevice`/`DOS_Yield`/`SDL_Delay` timing
model did not predict real SB16 behavior here: since removing the extra
calls didn't move the number, the true dominant real-hardware cost must
be concentrated in the ONE remaining per-`GameTick()` call (via
`WaitForNextFrame()`, unchanged by patch 0060), not spread across the
removed redundant calls the way the DOSBox-X data suggested.

**A real harness bug was found and worked through, not routed around**:
`run-rig.sh`'s `wait_for_stable_screen()` gave a false "run complete"
signal at ~135s for both sound-on cells (real completion, confirmed via
each cell's own engine-written RUNMANIFEST: 308s/309s) -- its
content-blind static-screen heuristic misread `fps_p50=0.58`'s own long
gaps between visually-similar renders as "done". That triggered a
collection attempt while the engine was still genuinely running, which
then hit `vcctrl`'s own documented `no-reset` signature (same rig/
project precedent in `OPEN-FAULTS.md` sec 23) and burned real recovery
time (`verify-input`, a fresh independent KVM capture -- NOT the
embedded frame from the failed job, which turned out to be stale --
and a sanctioned `power cycle`, confirmed recovered via a full init-
banner capture, not just `power state`). In hindsight nothing was ever
hung -- the game finished on its own -- but the recovery was the
correct sanctioned response to the symptom actually observed at the
time, and the engine's own already-written `F7B1.LOG`/`F7B2.LOG`
survived on disk and were what actually recovered this session's real
numbers. `wait_for_stable_screen()` needs a fix (scale its stability
window to the arm's own expected fps, or add a positive
`<TAG>.LOG`-appeared signal) before the next real-hardware campaign
re-hits this.

**A second, unexplained gap**: patch 0059's own `AUDIOPRB.LOG`
diagnostic -- same binary, same session -- produced zero data during
either 308s/309s sound-on run (only one line exists, from the earlier
sound-off cell, near-zero-cost as expected). Real MIDI events genuinely
dispatched (4980/4976 per `audio_vital_status`), so `audio_core_entry_
poll()` was clearly being called enough times to cross its 200-call
flush threshold repeatedly -- it never did. Not diagnosed this session.
This is now the actual blocker: the tool built to answer "where does
the real per-call cost concentrate on real hardware" doesn't produce
real-hardware data, and has to be fixed before that question can be
answered directly instead of guessed at again.

Full writeup, including the harness-bug mechanism and recovery sequence
in detail: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/S7-fix-realhw-2026-09-14.md`.

**Net state**: patch 0060 stays landed (a real, correct simplification,
just not sufficient alone). Patch 0059 stays landed (still needed, not
yet trustworthy on real hardware). Acceptance gate items 4 and 5 remain
FAIL. Next real step is fixing the AUDIOPRB.LOG real-hardware gap, then
re-instrumenting on HW-486-66 directly (not DOSBox-X) to find where the
real cost actually concentrates, per this hub's own "instrument the
thing that produces the unexplained quantity" rule -- applied this time
to the environment the quantity is actually unexplained in.

## S7 -- AUDIOPRB.LOG real-hardware gap: fixed sink, DOSBox-X + real-hardware confirmed, new slots_us lead -- 2026-09-14

Continuation of the same day's prior section. Root cause of the "second,
unexplained gap" above: patch 0059's diagnostic wrote to `AUDIOPRB.LOG`
via a fresh `fopen("AUDIOPRB.LOG","a")`/`fprintf`/`fclose` cycle every
200 calls -- repeatedly reopening the same already-populated file, both
within one run and across every cell of one boot session. The one write
pattern in this engine PROVEN reliable across all four of that same
real-hardware block's cells is `quit.cpp`'s own RUNMANIFEST-tag log: a
single `fopen(tag,"a")` held open across several `fprintf()`s, closed
exactly once at clean shutdown, never reopened mid-run. That repeated-
reopen-vs-open-once difference is the one structural thing that
distinguishes the sink that broke (after its first success) from the
sink that never did -- not yet a confirmed DOS/FAT root cause, but the
best-supported hypothesis from the evidence on hand, so the fix
converges the diagnostic onto the proven pattern rather than continuing
to guess at the exact underlying mechanism.

**Fix (patch 0061)**: `audio_core.cpp`'s per-window close routine no
longer touches a file at all -- it appends the closed window's summary
into a small bounded in-memory array (64 windows; `DOSAGS_TAS_AUTO_EXIT_
TICK`'s own cap keeps any S7 cell's real call count in the low
thousands, so this never fills in practice). A new `dos_diag_dump_audio_
poll(FILE *fp)` (declared in `audio_core.h`, `__DJGPP__`-gated) folds in
the still-open partial window and writes every recorded window as
`DOS-PORT audioprb ...` lines through a caller-supplied, already-open
handle -- it never opens or closes anything itself. `quit.cpp` calls it
with its own `run_manifest_log` handle, right before that handle's
single `fclose()`, the same place `memory_min_free_kb`/`tick_rate`
already piggyback for the identical reason. `AUDIOPRB.LOG` the separate
file no longer exists; the data now lands inside each cell's own tag
log (`<TAG>.LOG`), the file every cell already fetches successfully.

**DOSBox-X validated** (`dosbox-run.sh`, a scratch `oplmode=opl3` fast
conf, Trilby's Notes, `DOSAGS_FIXED_TIMESTEP=1`, `DOSAGS_TAS_AUTO_EXIT_
TICK=200`, `--user-data-dir c:\` per this file's own `check_write_
access()` note above): a real SB16 device opened, `audio_core_entry_
poll()` was called 69 times, and the tag log carried `DOS-PORT audioprb
total_calls=69 windows_recorded=1 windows_dropped=0` plus the window's
own `slots_us(min=5 mean=5 max=7) pump_us(min=460 mean=10097
max=14317)` line. `pump_us` mean (~10.1ms) matches the ~10-11ms/call
this same investigation already measured via the original (DOSBox-X-
working) sink -- the new sink reproduces the same data shape, not just
"runs without crashing". `binary_sha12=cdf5cb19a6c9` (differs from
0059+0060's `6e4c8a677027` -- source changed).

DOSBox-X already proved unreliable once this same investigation for
predicting real-hardware audio timing/behavior
(`S7-fix-realhw-2026-09-14.md`) -- this DOSBox-X validation only
established that the new sink is wired correctly end to end and
produces the expected shape of data locally, per this hub's own
DOSBox-X-is-a-correctness-gate-not-a-performance-proxy rule. A real
HW-486-66 sound-on cell was still required before trusting this sink on
the actual target.

**Real-hardware confirmation, same day, operator-approved single cell**
(`AUDIOFX1`, `DOSAGS_TAS_AUTO_EXIT_TICK=200` -- short on purpose, to
stay well under `wait_for_stable_screen()`'s 90s floor and sidestep its
known false-positive rather than re-trigger it for a cell that doesn't
need the full acceptance workload): **the fix works.** Real, non-empty
`DOS-PORT audioprb` data came back for the first time ever in this
investigation:

```
DOS-PORT audioprb total_calls=65 windows_recorded=1 windows_dropped=0
DOS-PORT audioprb total_calls=65 window_calls=65 slots_us(min=11 mean=1403 max=15270) pump_us(min=6398 mean=11137 max=15133)
```

Clean run (`exit_code=0`, `environment=realhw`, real OPL3 chip detected,
`events=639`), same collapsed regime as every other real-hardware
sound-on cell (`tick_rate=2.97`).

**A new lead, not yet confirmed**: `pump_us` (mean 11137us) matches
DOSBox-X's own measurement closely (10,300-11,144us there) -- that part
of the original diagnosis generalizes fine. `slots_us` does NOT --
DOSBox-X measured 22-126us mean for the slot `Poll()` loop (MIDI
scheduling); real hardware shows **mean=1403us, max=15270us**, over 10x
higher and, at its max, in the same range as `pump_us` itself. This
plausibly explains why patch 0060 (removing only the *extra* mid-
catch-up calls, leaving one call per real `GameTick()` untouched) had
~zero real-hardware effect: if BOTH halves of that one surviving call
are expensive on real hardware -- not just the pump half DOSBox-X
pointed at -- reducing the call count was never going to move the
number much. One data point (one window, 65 calls) -- real, worth
pursuing, not yet a confirmed mechanism. Full writeup, including the
exact cell recipe and raw log content:
`tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/S7-audioprb-fix-realhw-2026-09-14.md`.

Patches 0059, 0060, and 0061 all stay landed, all still temporary.
Acceptance gate items 4 and 5 remain FAIL -- this cell did not
re-attempt them. Next real steps: investigate `slots_us`'s own real
cost directly (`midi_sched_tick()` / the OPL3 sink's register-write
path) the same way `pump_us` was investigated before it, and fix
`wait_for_stable_screen()` before the next full acceptance-gate
campaign needs a ~300s+ sound-on cell again.

## S7 -- OPL3 register-write cost diagnostic, DOSBox-X validated -- 2026-09-14

Continuation of the previous section's "next real steps" -- source-reads
`SDL_DOSOpl3WriteRegister()` (`vendor/SDL/src/core/dos/
SDL_dos_audio_synth.c`): every register write costs 12 dummy
`inportb(0x388)` reads (a canonical AdLib delay technique), commented
"~1us per read... bullet-proof" -- a datasheet-derived estimate for real
YMF262 silicon, never independently measured against HW-486-66's actual
sound device, which is a **PicoGUS in OPL3 mode** (RP2040-firmware
ISA-bus emulation, not discrete silicon). This exact file already has
one confirmed precedent of a similarly naive per-`inportb` timing
assumption being wrong enough to matter on real hardware (the MPU-401
DRR-poll IOCHRDY hard-stall hazard, SDL/0093) -- a real, source-grounded
reason to doubt the "~1us, bullet-proof" comment on this specific rig,
not a guess.

Landed two new temporary diagnostic patches: `patches/SDL/0141` brackets
`SDL_DOSOpl3WriteRegister()` itself with `uclock()`-based per-call
timing (in-memory only, snapshot-and-reset accessor); `patches/ags/0062`
folds that into the existing `AUDIOPRB.LOG` windowed diagnostic
(0059/0061) as a new `regwrite(...)` field, splitting `slots_us` into
"register I/O" vs. "everything else the slot loop does" -- one layer
further down, per this hub's "instrument the thing that produces the
unexplained quantity" rule. Both patches land in this port's own
`patches/SDL/`/`patches/ags/` (per the 2026-09-01 per-port-vendoring
migration -- no hub `shared/` change or subtree pull needed for this).

**DOSBox-X validated, and it caught a real bug before real hardware**:
the first run showed `regwrite max_us` (54950) exceeding that same
window's own `slots_us max` (4807) -- structurally impossible if
register-write time is a subset of slot-loop time. Root cause:
`SDL_DOSOpl3WriteRegister()` is also called from OUTSIDE
`audio_core_entry_poll()` (`opl3_sink_open()` -> `SDL_DOSOpl3InitChip()`
at MIDI-slot-creation time, triggered by the engine's music dispatch),
and those writes were leaking into whichever poll call ran next. Fixed
with a discard-snapshot at function entry. Second run: internally
consistent (`regwrite calls=210 mean_us=21-23 max_us=23`, comfortably
under `slots_us max=4797`, and the arithmetic cross-checks against
`slots_us`'s own mean). This only proves the diagnostic is wired
correctly and produces a sane shape of data locally -- DOSBox-X already
proved unreliable for the actual question once in this same
investigation (`slots_us` itself is the generalization failure under
test), so this says nothing yet about real hardware. Full writeup:
`tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/S7-regwrite-diag-dosboxx-2026-09-14.md`.

**Not yet done, no real-hardware time used this session**: a real
HW-486-66 cell is required to actually test whether `regwrite` accounts
for most of `slots_us` on real hardware (pointing at register I/O) or
leaves a large scheduling-logic remainder instead (pointing back at
`midi_sched_tick()`/`opl3_sink.c`'s own bookkeeping) -- needs a fresh,
separately-asked operator go-ahead. `wait_for_stable_screen()`'s
low-fps false-positive fix is still open and unrelated to this
diagnostic. Acceptance gate items 4 and 5 remain FAIL.

## S7 -- OPL3 register-write cost diagnostic, real-hardware result -- 2026-09-14 (same session)

Operator-approved single real-hardware cell (tag `AUDIOFX2`,
`binary_sha12=342a0b306336`, confirmed matching `make build-sha12`
against the committed tree), same recipe as `AUDIOFX1`. **Result:
`regwrite` does account for most of `slots_us`'s mean (63%: `4434` writes
x `21us` mean =~ 1433us/call of a 2268us/call mean) -- but the mechanism
is NOT what the hypothesis predicted.** `regwrite`'s own per-write cost
(21us) is unremarkable -- in the same range as DOSBox-X's own measurement
(21-23us), not the ~10x-worse-per-op cost the PicoGUS/MPU-401-precedent
hypothesis anticipated. What actually differs is **volume**: 68.2
writes/call on real hardware vs 1.12/call under DOSBox-X. Likely cause:
`midi_sched_tick()`'s playback position is wall-clock-driven, and the
same `DOSAGS_TAS_AUTO_EXIT_TICK=200` cap corresponds to 9s of real time
under DOSBox-X `--fast` vs 79s on real hardware -- with only 65 real
audio-serviced ticks surviving that 79s, each surviving call has to
clear a correspondingly larger backlog of due MIDI events in one shot.
**Register-write volume is a downstream symptom of the same
tick-starvation collapse already under investigation, not an independent
OPL3-hardware-timing defect.**

A real methodological catch: `slots_us` itself did not reproduce between
`AUDIOFX1` (mean=1403, no regwrite instrumentation) and this cell
(mean=2268, regwrite instrumentation added) despite a near-identical
underlying workload (same call count, event count, duration) -- the
delta divided by the average write count implies ~12.7us of apparent
added cost per write, suspiciously close to `regwrite`'s own 21us/write.
Most likely explanation: `uclock()` itself is not free on real DOS/486
hardware, and this diagnostic calls it twice per register write (8868
extra calls this window) -- at tens-of-microseconds granularity, the
instrument's own cost is a real confound, the same "your measurement
instrument can lie" hazard `docs/audio.md` already documents at a larger
timescale (the PIT-driven-pump-corrupts-SDL's-clock finding).

**This changes the recommended next step**: bisecting the dummy-read
delay loop (this diagnostic's own originally-proposed follow-up) is not
well-motivated -- per-write cost isn't the anomaly. The real lever is
back where round 2 left it: why so few real GameTicks ever reach an
audio-serviced point at all (`tick_rate` collapsing to ~2.96-2.97
regardless of what's been tried). A real harness bug also surfaced in
`run-rig.sh`'s own collect-phase `wait_for_job_done` (didn't detect a
job that had already finished cleanly; worked around by querying
`vc file-status`/`vc pulled save` directly, not yet root-caused). Full
writeup: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/
S7-regwrite-diag-realhw-2026-09-14.md`. Patches 0059, 0060, 0061 (ags),
SDL/0141, and ags/0062 all stay landed, all still temporary. Acceptance
gate items 4 and 5 remain FAIL.

## S7 -- tick-starvation root cause, source investigation -- 2026-09-14 (same session)

Pure source read (no patch, no real hardware): the DOS backend's
threading is genuine cooperative (`setjmp`/`longjmp`, non-preemptive)
multitasking (`shared`'s `SDL_dos_scheduler.c`, never previously examined
in this investigation) -- `DOS_Yield()` is a real context switch that
hands the CPU to the audio thread if it's `READY`, and the audio thread
runs uninterrupted until its own next yield. This explains, mechanistically
(not just empirically), why patch 0060 had ~zero real-hardware effect:
`audio_core_entry_poll()`'s own measured cost (12-45ms/real-tick) cannot
explain the sound-off-vs-sound-on gap (~42ms/tick vs ~303ms/tick,
`S7-abba-2026-09-13.md`'s own numbers) even multiplied by 6. Checked the
two other per-tick call sites that could reach `DOS_Yield()`/`SDL_Delay()`:
`WaitForNextFrame()`'s own pacing wait is skipped entirely when badly
behind schedule (confirmed by reading the fall-behind-reset logic), and
`DOSVESA_PumpEvents()`'s own yield is already default-skipped (SDL/0021)
and confirmed inert in every cell this investigation has run
(`SDL_HINT_DOS_FORCE_PUMP_YIELD` never set). Neither explains the gap.
Found a real, unfulfilled contract: `SDL_dosevents.c` documents that
"the engine is expected to call `SDL_Delay(0)` once per flip to keep the
audio thread scheduled" -- dosags never does, anywhere. Not yet confirmed
whether this is consequential. Where the remaining ~250ms/tick actually
goes is NOT yet established -- recommended next step is bracketing
`dos_run_tick_fixed()` itself (catch-up-ticks-total vs. the one real
tick's total vs. that tick's already-known audio sub-cost), a checkpoint
before writing a third temporary diagnostic layer. Full writeup:
`tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/
S7-tick-starvation-source-investigation-2026-09-14.md`. Acceptance gate
items 4 and 5 remain FAIL; no patches landed this entry.

fixed()` itself, splitting each call into the catch-up burst's summed

## S7 -- dos_run_tick_fixed() catch-up-vs-real-tick, real-hardware result: the tax is uniform -- 2026-09-14 (same session)

Operator-approved cell (tag `AUDIOFX3`, `binary_sha12=ec9459908706`),
same recipe as `AUDIOFX1`/`AUDIOFX2`. **The cleanest result of this whole
investigation**: a catch-up `UpdateGameOnce()` call (no render, no
`WaitForNextFrame()`, and -- post-patch-0060 -- no `audio_core_entry_
poll()` either) costs **407.2ms** on average (`catchup_us mean=2000193us`
/ `catchup_n_sum=167` over `total_calls=34`, i.e. 4.91 catch-up ticks/call
saturating the `MAX_CATCHUP=5` cap). The one real tick (renders, waits,
polls audio) costs **409.5ms** (`realtick_us mean=409471us`). **Same
number, within 0.5%.** Against the sound-off baseline (`S7-abba-2026-
09-13.md`: ~42.0ms/tick aggregate), both bucket types show almost
exactly the same **9.7x** inflation.

**This rules out, conclusively, every hypothesis this investigation has
tested that was scoped to "audio-servicing cost"**: `audio_core_entry_
poll()`'s own measured cost (too small by ~2 orders of magnitude), the
poll-count multiplier patch 0060 targeted (removing it changed nothing,
now obviously correct since catch-up ticks don't even call that function
post-0060 and still pay the full tax), and register-write volume/cost
(this session's earlier `regwrite` result). Whatever the mechanism is,
it applies almost exactly the same multiplier to **every**
`UpdateGameOnce()` call once the audio device is open, independent of
what that call actually does. The strongest remaining structural
candidate: `UpdateGameOnce()` calls `sys_evt_process_pending()`
unconditionally at its own entry (`game_run.cpp:1415`, before any
`skip_render_and_wait` branch), which pumps the DOS video backend's
event source on every single call -- `DOSVESA_PumpEvents()`'s own
explicit yield is confirmed already-skipped, so if the mechanism lives
here it is not that specific call. `SDL_sysmutex.c`/`SDL_syssem.c`
(both reference `DOS_Yield()`, flagged but not yet read in this
investigation) are the next natural read. An empirical alternative to
more source reading is also on the table: A/B whether the cooperative
audio thread's mere *existence* (not its call frequency, already ruled
out) is the lever. Full writeup: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/
S7-tickfix-diag-realhw-2026-09-14.md`. Patches 0059-0063 all stay
landed, all still temporary. Acceptance gate items 4 and 5 remain FAIL.

## S7 -- scheduler mechanism investigation (continuation) -- 2026-09-14 (same session)

Pure source read (`SDL_sysmutex.c`, `SDL_syssem.c`, SDL3's generic
`SDL_audio.c`), no patch, no real hardware. Two real findings: (1)
`SDL_LockMutex()`/`SDL_WaitSemaphoreTimeoutNS()` both spin-call
`DOS_Yield()` on contention -- a second, more general trigger class
beyond explicit `DOS_Yield()` call sites; (2) there is a real,
autonomous, continuously-looping cooperative audio thread
(`SDL_audio.c:1882`'s stock `SDL_CreateThread(PlaybackAudioThread, ...)`,
unconditional whenever the device opens) running `while (Iterate())
{ WaitDevice(); }` forever, independent of the already-measured
`SDL_DOSAudioPump()`/`dos_audio_mixer_pump()` path this investigation
focused on until now. `WaitDevice()`'s room-available path yields
exactly once per iteration (patch `SDL/0086`'s own documented "hand CPU
back to main" purpose) before looping to another real `Iterate()` mixing
pass.

**Strengthened but still-unconfirmed hypothesis**: any `DOS_Yield()`
(explicit or lock/semaphore-contention-triggered) anywhere in a tick's
own code hands the CPU to this always-`READY` autonomous thread, which
does one real `Iterate()` pass before yielding back -- if
`sys_evt_process_pending()` (called unconditionally at every
`UpdateGameOnce()`'s own entry, catch-up ticks included) triggers even
one such round-trip through a path not yet pinned down (its own
explicit yield is confirmed skipped), that would explain the uniform
tax. Not confirmed by source reading alone despite auditing the
scheduler, both cooperative primitives, and the autonomous thread's own
loop. Recommended next step is measurement, not more reading:
instrument `DOS_Yield()` itself (call count + hand-off duration per
tick) or `SDL_PlaybackAudioThreadIterate()`'s own per-call cost
directly -- neither implemented this entry, a checkpoint before a
fourth temporary diagnostic layer. Full writeup:
`tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/
S7-scheduler-mechanism-investigation-2026-09-14.md`. No patches landed,
no real hardware used. Acceptance gate items 4 and 5 remain FAIL.

## S7 -- DOS_Yield() diagnostic, DOSBox-X validated -- 2026-09-14 (same session)

Landed `SDL/0142` (instruments `DOS_Yield()`: call count, no-op vs real
switch, and real switch-away-and-back wall-clock cost) + `ags/0064`
(folds it into the `tickfx` catch-up/real-tick split, same discard-
snapshot pattern as the regwrite diagnostic). DOSBox-X validated
(`binary_sha12=7d2309fcdef7`): wired correctly, but the result is a
genuine surprise -- yield-switches concentrate almost entirely in the
real tick (`realtick_yield switches=3766` over 156 calls, 24.1/call)
versus almost none during the catch-up burst (`catchup_yield
switches=4` over 44 catch-up ticks, 0.09/tick). Taken at face value
this would REFUTE the cooperative-audio-thread hypothesis for the
catch-up-tick tax specifically. **But DOSBox-X does not reproduce the
underlying collapse at all in this cell** (`tick_rate=30.58`) -- branch
counts inside `WaitDevice()`'s own ring-full spin loop are driven by
real wall-clock IRQ-drain timing, which legitimately differs between
environments, so this result cannot be trusted as the actual answer;
only a real-hardware run of this exact diagnostic can resolve it. Also
surfaced an unrelated, pre-existing data-quality bug: the same run's
`regwrite` field showed a corrupted mean (billions of microseconds) --
most likely a rare `uclock()` non-monotonicity dip (already documented
elsewhere in this hub's history) poisoning `SDL_DOSOpl3WriteRegister()`'s
own running sum via unsigned wraparound; a cheap defensive clamp is a
worthwhile follow-up, not applied this entry. Full writeup:
`tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/S7-yield-diag-dosboxx-2026-09-14.md`.
No real hardware used this entry. Acceptance gate items 4 and 5 remain
FAIL.

## S7 -- DOS_Yield() diagnostic, real-hardware result: yield-switching ruled out -- 2026-09-14 (same session)

Operator-approved cell (tag `AUDIOFX4`, `binary_sha12=7d2309fcdef7`).
**Only 2 real `DOS_Yield()` switches happened during the entire
catch-up burst across all 34 `dos_run_tick_fixed()` calls (167
individual catch-up ticks)** -- even taking their summed duration at
face value (1.47s), that's 2.2% of the 67.95s the catch-up ticks
actually cost this window. **This rules out cooperative-scheduler
yield-switching as the mechanism behind the catch-up-tick tax**, with
real data, confirming the DOSBox-X sanity run's own directional finding
(which couldn't be trusted alone since DOSBox-X doesn't reproduce the
underlying collapse -- this time it generalized correctly).

Also found a real instrument-design limitation: `realtick_yield`'s
summed duration (704 switches x 76620us mean = 53.94s) *exceeds* the
13.87s `realtick_us` window it's supposed to fit inside -- because
`DOS_YieldDiagSnapshot()`'s counters are global, not per-thread, so a
`DOS_Yield()` call made by the autonomous `PlaybackAudioThread` (e.g.
inside its own ring-full spin loop) gets bracketed and counted
identically to one made by main, and these can overlap in real wall-
clock time rather than partition it. Doesn't affect the catch-up
finding (unambiguous either way at 2 switches), but means
`realtick_yield`'s own numbers read as "total scheduler churn touched
during this phase," not "cost per clean round trip."

**Two real mechanisms are now conclusively ruled out** for the
catch-up-tick tax: `audio_core_entry_poll()`'s own direct cost
(regwrite result) and cooperative-scheduler yield-switching (this
result). **New leading candidate, qualitatively different from
everything tested so far**: real ISA-bus DMA cycle-stealing from the
actively-streaming SB16 channel -- a hardware/electrical mechanism (an
active DMA channel adding real wait-states to ordinary CPU bus cycles
on some ISA chipsets, independent of software scheduling) that would
explain the uniform tax, the ~9.7x sound-off/sound-on gap, and why
DOSBox-X never reproduces it (an emulator's bus-timing model has no
reason to charge real electrical cycle-stealing). This cannot be
confirmed or refuted by more source reading -- needs hardware/chipset
research or a differently-shaped empirical test (isolating "device
open" from "DMA actively transferring"). Full writeup:
`tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/S7-yield-diag-realhw-2026-09-14.md`.
Patches 0059-0064 all stay landed, all still temporary. Acceptance gate
items 4 and 5 remain FAIL.

## S7 -- DMA-cycle-stealing experiment design, DOSBox-X validated -- 2026-09-14 (same session)

Designed the real-hardware test for the DMA-cycle-stealing hypothesis
left open by the previous section: a third arm (`SDL_HINT_DOS_AUDIO_
BACKEND=opl3` + `SDL_HINT_DOS_AUDIO_FORCE_DSP_PAUSE=1`, an existing,
previously-unused lever from `patches/SDL/0040`) that keeps OPL3 MIDI
live but force-pauses the SB16 PCM device's DMA immediately after open
and suppresses auto-resume -- isolating "device open" from "DMA actively
transferring." Config-only, same binary as `AUDIOFX3`/`AUDIOFX4`
(`binary_sha12=7d2309fcdef7`), no new patch.

**A real correction surfaced first**: this investigation's own "IRQ-5"
shorthand (copied from the SDL backend's generic comments) is not what
HW-486-66 actually runs -- the rig's PicoGUS is jumpered IRQ 7 / DMA 3,
PGSB boot profile forces the 8-bit DMA path (`SDL_HINT_DOS_AUDIO_SB_
FORCE_8BIT=1`, pause command `0xD0` not `0xD5`). Doesn't change any
prior conclusion (the code reads the real configured IRQ, not a
hardcoded 5) but corrects how this doc's own prose should be read from
here on -- see `~/git/g2k/README.TXT`'s PGSB section.

Reading `DOSSOUNDBLASTER_WaitDevice()` closely also found a real,
previously-uncombined interaction: patch 0063's ring-full wall-clock
backstop (1000ms) is not gated on `g_dos_audio_force_dsp_pause`, so a
force-paused device's permanently-full ring will still bounce
`WaitDevice()` back to `true` every ~1s of real time -- a possible
confound distinct from DMA-cycle-stealing, not assumed away.

**DOSBox-X validation result**: composes cleanly. IRQ genuinely stops
(0 fires all run, confirmed both via the live rate-meas line and the
CloseDevice tally), OPL3 dispatch is unaffected (`events=54`, `regwrite`
cost matches the non-force-paused OPL3 baseline almost exactly), and the
yield-switch counts/tick_rate stay in the same range as the
non-force-paused OPL3 DOSBox-X baseline -- no crash, no hang, no visible
pathological churn from the timeout interaction found above. Caveat
stated plainly in the full writeup: DOSBox-X's `--fast` conf keeps up
with target well enough that this interaction's real risk (specific to
real hardware's chronic-backlog regime) isn't exercised here -- the real
cell's own yield diagnostic is what actually clears or confirms it, and
should be read alongside the catchup/realtick timing when that cell
runs. Full writeup: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/S7-dma-cyclesteal-
diag-dosboxx-2026-09-14.md`.

## S7 -- DMA-cycle-stealing hypothesis, real-hardware result: REFUTED -- 2026-09-14 (same session)

Operator-approved cell (tag `DMAX1`, `binary_sha12=7d2309fcdef7`, same
binary as `AUDIOFX3`/`AUDIOFX4`), same recipe as `AUDIOFX1`-`4` plus
`SDL_HINT_DOS_AUDIO_FORCE_DSP_PAUSE=1`. Confirms directly on real
hardware, not just DOSBox-X, that HW-486-66's actual audio path is the
PicoGUS 8-bit SB-emulation path on IRQ7/DMA3 (`is_sb16=0 force_8bit=1
dma_ch=3 irq=7`), matching the prior entry's "IRQ-5"-shorthand
correction. `LOGS\DMAX1SDL.LOG`'s own `CloseDevice` tally confirms **zero
DMA-IRQ fires for the entire 93-second run** -- the DMA channel never
transferred a single chunk.

**Result: `tick_rate=2.50`** -- the same collapsed order of magnitude as
Arm C (full-DMA sound-on, 2.96-2.97), not Arm A (sound-off, 23.8-23.9),
and if anything slightly *worse* than Arm C. Per-tick cost confirms it:
`catchup_us`/`realtick_us` (~495.8ms/469.3ms) both exceed Arm C's own
407.2ms/409.5ms -- an ~11.2-11.8x tax against the sound-off baseline,
not smaller than Arm C's 9.7x. **The DMA-cycle-stealing hypothesis is
refuted**: the tax survives, undiminished, with DMA transfer completely
and confirmedly halted. A real, source-flagged artifact (patch 0063's
un-gated `WaitDevice` ring-full timeout backstop interacting with
force-pause) plausibly explains why this cell came in slightly worse
than Arm C -- `catchup_yield`'s own 2 switches cost ~0.95s/1.9s each,
matching the 1000ms timeout almost exactly -- but does not change the
core verdict, since even crediting that whole gap to the artifact, Arm B
stays an order of magnitude away from Arm A.

**What remains standing, unrefuted, after six ruled-out hypotheses**:
the tax tracks the audio device being *open* (the autonomous
`PlaybackAudioThread` existing in the scheduler's thread table),
independent of what it does once open -- exactly the hypothesis
`S7-tickfix-diag-realhw-2026-09-14.md`'s own "Not yet done" item 2
already named and did not attempt: A/B the mere *existence* of the
background audio thread (a synchronous-only SB16 backend variant) against
this one. That is a real architecture change needing its own design pass,
not attempted this entry. Full writeup: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/
results/S7-dma-cyclesteal-realhw-2026-09-14.md`.

## S7 -- audio-thread-existence hypothesis: patch landed, DOSBox-X validated -- 2026-09-14 (same session)

Designed and landed `patches/SDL/0143` (`SDL_HINT_DOS_AUDIO_NO_BG_
THREAD=1`): sets SDL3's own stock `impl->ProvidesOwnCallbackThread`
field (`SDL_sysaudio.h`) at `DOSSOUNDBLASTER_Init()`, so the generic
core (`SDL_audio.c`) never `SDL_CreateThread()`s the autonomous
`PlaybackAudioThread` for this device at all -- a real, pre-existing
SDL3 mechanism, not new machinery. Composes cleanly with everything
already landed: `SDL_DOSAudioPump()` (patch 0067) already services the
ring synchronously via the same `SDL_PlaybackAudioThreadIterate()` the
thread would call, and never touches `WaitDevice()` itself -- so in
no-thread mode, `WaitDevice()` (and every `DOS_Yield()`/hard-park/
quiescence-gate mechanism inside it) simply never runs, not a new path
needing verification. Rebuilt clean (`make patches` -- series applied
cleanly; `make sdl3 && make build-ags`; `binary_sha12` changed from
`7d2309fcdef7` to `36ebdca8ee61`, confirming the tree changed).

**DOSBox-X validation, same scenario with and without the new hint**:
yield-switch counts drop from 4/3938 (thread present) to exactly 0/0
(no thread) -- a structural, mechanistic confirmation the patch does
what it claims (nothing exists to yield to), not just a tuning effect.
OPL3 dispatch, `audio_core_entry_poll()`'s own cost profile, and
`tick_rate` all stay in the same range between the two arms -- clean
isolation, only thread existence changed. Both arms show zero IRQ-5
fires (checked specifically, not assumed) -- confirmed this is a
property of this short/quiet DOSBox-X smoke scenario (no PCM SFX cues,
only OPL3 music) hitting the backend's own always-on idle-auto-pause,
identically in both arms, not something the patch broke. No crash, no
hang, clean shutdown. Full writeup: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/
S7-thread-existence-diag-dosboxx-2026-09-14.md`.

**Not yet done**: the real-hardware cell -- needs a fresh, separately-
asked operator go-ahead, new binary needs staging (`36ebdca8ee61`, not
the `AUDIOFX3`/`4`/`DMAX1` binary). Also worth a fresh real-hardware
baseline (thread present) alongside it, since this investigation only
started reading the IRQ-tally log line this session -- `AUDIOFX3`/`4`'s
own real-hardware IRQ counts were never checked. Acceptance gate items

## S7 -- audio-thread-existence hypothesis, real-hardware result: REFUTED -- 2026-09-14 (same session)

Operator-approved cell (tag `NOBGT1`, `binary_sha12=36ebdca8ee61`, the
SDL/0143 build), same recipe as `AUDIOFX1`-`4`/`DMAX1` plus
`SDL_HINT_DOS_AUDIO_NO_BG_THREAD=1`. **Result: `tick_rate=2.48`** --
the same collapsed band as every other sound-on arm (`DMAX1`=2.50,
`AUDIOFX3`/`4`=2.96-2.97), with `catchup_yield`/`realtick_yield`
switches confirmed **exactly zero** on real hardware (mechanistic proof
the background thread genuinely never existed, not just idled) and
`total IRQ-5 fires this run = 1948` over 93s (~20.9 Hz) confirming DMA
was fully alive throughout -- both pre-registered caveats from the
DOSBox-X entry closed with real data. Pulling the `AUDIOFX`-tag
collision file for direct comparison (see below) shows the last
`AUDIOFX`-tagged cell's own IRQ count: **1638 over 79s (~20.7 Hz)** --
same rate, thread or no thread. **The audio-thread-existence hypothesis
is refuted, cleanly, alongside DMA-cycle-stealing**: four real-hardware
cells now span both axes (thread present/absent, DMA active/halted),
and every "device open" condition collapses to the same ~2.5-3.0
tick_rate band regardless, while only "device fully closed" (Arm A)
recovers.

**A real, already-realized 8.3-filename-collision bug found pulling
this evidence**: `DOS_PORT_LOG_TAG` values longer than 5 characters
overflow the 8-char limit once `SDL.LOG` is appended -- `AUDIOFX1`-`4`
(8 chars each) all truncate to the identical `AUDIOSDL.LOG`, meaning
each `AUDIOFX`-tagged real-hardware cell in this investigation silently
overwrote the previous one's SDL debug log; only the chronologically
last one's content survived on the rig. Doesn't invalidate any
already-published finding (those all used the tag-named `.LOG`/
`STDOUT.TXT`, which stay unique), but is a real gap for whoever next
needs this log routinely -- flagged, not fixed.

**What's now the only thing common to every collapsed arm, absent only
in the sound-off arm**: the device being *open* -- specifically IRQ7
(this rig's real PicoGUS jumper) hooked and the DSP's speaker-enable
issued, independent of DMA activity or thread existence. **New,
concrete, untested hypothesis**: IRQ7 is the classic ISA parallel-port
line, and 8259 PIC "spurious IRQ7" handling is a real, documented
x86/PC-era quirk -- if this rig's LPT1 also shares IRQ7 (not yet
checked), merely hooking a handler there could add a uniform tax
independent of everything already ruled out. A genuinely different
class of hypothesis (ISA IRQ-line/PIC behavior, not bus contention or
scheduling) needing its own design pass -- not attempted this entry.

realhw-2026-09-14.md`.

## S7 -- IRQ7/spurious-interrupt hypothesis: REFUTED before real hardware -- 2026-09-14 (same session)

Design pass for the previous entry's own proposed next hypothesis
(IRQ7/LPT1 sharing + 8259 "spurious IRQ7" causing the tax) killed it
**before spending any real-hardware time**: `~/git/g2k/README.TXT`'s
own "VERIFIED BIOS FACTS" section already documents that this rig's
LPT1 is output-only/polled, never interrupt-driven, so it structurally
cannot assert IRQ7 -- "in practice nothing has broken." A second,
independent refutation from data already in hand: Arm B (`DMAX1`, 0
real IRQ fires) and Arm D (`NOBGT1`, 1,948 real IRQ fires) show
essentially the same tax (495.8k/469.3k vs 498.0k/472.6k us) -- at most
~1.1us attributable per fire even crediting the whole gap to IRQ cost,
which kills the entire "per-interrupt-servicing-cost" hypothesis
family, not just the IRQ7-specific version, without a new measurement.

**Eight hypotheses now ruled out.** What remains true and unexplained:
the tax appears in every device-open condition regardless of DMA
activity, thread existence, or IRQ fire count, and disappears only when
the device is closed -- the mechanism must be a one-time `OpenDevice`
side effect that persists as a constant per-tick cost, not an ongoing
servicing cost of any kind measured so far. No new hypothesis
identified yet; two candidates flagged for a future design pass:
bisecting `OpenDevice`'s own command sequence (DSP speaker-enable vs.
IRQ-hook vs. DMA-arm, in isolation), or an AGS-engine-side (not
SDL-backend) audit of per-tick audio-state branches beyond
`audio_core_entry_poll()`. Full writeup: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/
results/S7-irq7-lpt1-hypothesis-refuted-2026-09-14.md`.

## S7 -- OpenDevice bisection: patch landed, DOSBox-X validated -- 2026-09-14 (same session)

Designed and landed `patches/SDL/0144` (`SDL_HINT_DOS_AUDIO_OPEN_STOP_
AT=1|2|3|4`): makes `OpenDevice` return successfully at one of four
points along its own real hardware bring-up sequence -- before the DMA
controller is touched at all (1), after it's programmed+unmasked but
before `DOS_HookInterrupt` (2), after the IRQ vector is hooked but
before any DSP command (3), or after the DSP speaker-enable but before
autoinit playback actually starts (4). DMA never engages in any phase,
isolating pure setup-time state from transfer activity -- a different
axis from everything tested so far.

**A real correctness risk found and fixed before it became a bug**: the
ring/staging-buffer allocation originally lived after DMA-controller
setup, meaning phases 1-2 would have left the engine's existing
per-tick `SDL_DOSAudioPump()` call operating on a NULL ring buffer -- a
real crash risk on real hardware. Fixed by relocating that allocation
earlier (verified it depends only on already-set `hidden->` fields, and
nothing between old/new position depends on it -- behavior-neutral for
the normal path). Also verified `DOS_UnhookInterrupt()` already no-ops
safely on a never-hooked structure before relying on it for phases
1-2's teardown, rather than assuming it.

**DOSBox-X validation**: baseline (regression check) plus all four
phases, same scenario as every prior diagnostic. All five clean, no
crash, no hang; `tick_rate` (30.1-30.6), OPL3 dispatch (`events=54`),
and IRQ count (0, expected) identical across every phase and the
baseline -- confirms wiring, not the real-hardware answer (DOSBox-X
doesn't reproduce the collapse regardless of phase, as always).
`binary_sha12` changed `36ebdca8ee61` -> `6ca3ac927604`. Full writeup:
`tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/S7-opendevice-bisect-dosboxx-
2026-09-14.md`.

**Not yet done**: the real-hardware cells. Recommended order: phase 4
first (most informative single point), then bisect based on the result
rather than running all four blindly. Acceptance gate items 4 and 5
remain FAIL.

## S7 -- OpenDevice bisection, real-hardware results: partial recovery found -- 2026-09-14 (same session)

Three operator-approved cells (`binary_sha12=6ca3ac927604`). `OSA4`
(`OPEN_STOP_AT=4`, thread present) and `OSA1` (`OPEN_STOP_AT=1`, thread
present) both land at `tick_rate=2.49` -- indistinguishable from every
other sound-on arm. Realized mid-investigation why: neither phase
disables the background `PlaybackAudioThread` (a separate, uncombined
hint), so in both, the thread still exists and hits the same
permanently-full-ring/`WaitDevice`-timeout dance as Arm B (confirmed by
the matching yield signature) -- phases 1-4 with the thread present
never actually isolated "hardware setup extent" cleanly.

**Combining `OPEN_STOP_AT=1` with `NO_BG_THREAD=1`** (no DMA-controller
touch, no IRQ hook, no DSP command beyond the mandatory reset, AND no
background thread) produces **`tick_rate=3.21`** -- the first result in
this whole investigation to land outside the tight 2.48-2.97 cluster
every other sound-on arm has occupied. `catchup_yield`/`realtick_yield`
both exactly 0 (mechanistically confirmed). But the data shape changed
too: `catchup_us` spans 16us to 25 *seconds* -- cross-checked against
`STDOUT.TXT`'s own `room_transition t_ms=19673`, this is the same
pre-existing, audio-unrelated room/asset-load stall flagged as a
possible confound as far back as an early tickfix-diagnostic entry, not
something new. Removing that one outlier burst, the remaining 33
average ~1.04s/burst against a ~0.20s/burst fully-fixed expectation:
**the tax is reduced from ~9.7x-11.8x to roughly ~5x, not eliminated.**
Real, measurable progress -- the first combination in nine tested to
move the needle at all -- but the mechanism survives even in the most
minimal state this port's own DOS SB backend can reach.

**New leading candidate**: SDL3's own *generic* (not DOS-specific)
audio core. `SDL_PumpEvents()` -> `SDL_PumpEventMaintenance()` ->
`SDL_UpdateAudio()` runs on every single `UpdateGameOnce()` call
(catch-up ticks included, matching this investigation's oldest
structural clue), gated only by a compile-time flag, not any runtime
"is a device doing anything" check -- the first genuinely new,
never-before-audited code path in this investigation (everything ruled
out so far was the DOS backend or the AGS engine layer). Read so far,
`SDL_UpdateAudio()` itself looks cheap on paper (an early-exit RWLock
check) -- not yet confirmed as the mechanism, not yet instrumented.
Full writeup: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/S7-opendevice-bisect-
realhw-2026-09-14.md`.

## S7 -- full thread x DMA-activity bisection matrix, real hardware -- 2026-09-14 (same session)

Six more cells (`OSA2NT`-`OSA4NT`, `OSAMID0`) complete the bisection
and **correct an overclaim from an earlier entry in this same
session**. Phases 2, 3, and 4 combined with `NO_BG_THREAD=1` all land
at `tick_rate=3.21-3.23`, identical to phase 1 -- confirming DMA-
controller arming, IRQ-hooking, and DSP speaker-enable individually add
nothing when the thread is absent and DMA never actually starts. Only
`NOBGT1` (no thread, DMA genuinely autoinit-started, ~1948 real IRQ
fires) shows the full ~10x tax.

**The complete matrix**:

| | DMA never started | DMA genuinely started |
|---|---:|---:|
| Thread present | 2.49-2.50 | 2.49-2.97 |
| Thread absent | **3.21-3.23** | 2.48 |

**Correction to `S7-irq7-lpt1-hypothesis-refuted-2026-09-14.md`**: its
"tax doesn't scale with IRQ activity" claim compared `DMAX1` (thread
present, 0 IRQ) against `NOBGT1` (thread absent, ~1948 IRQ) -- two axes
at once. The unconfounded reading: **with the thread held present**,
IRQ activity (0 vs ~1638-2000) genuinely has no effect (already-
explained by the `WaitDevice`-timeout artifact). **With the thread held
absent**, IRQ activity going from 0 to ~1948 costs a real, measurable
~23% relative degradation (3.21 -> 2.48). Thread presence and real DMA
activity are each independently *sufficient* to reach the same ~10x
ceiling (a saturation, not an additive stack) -- removing only one
still lets the other reach it; only removing both reveals a lower
floor, and that floor is still ~5x above baseline, not 1x.

**Real, still-unexplained floor**: even the best case found across
eleven real-hardware cells (`OSA1NT`-`OSA4NT`) shows ~5x tax after
excluding the one already-identified room-transition outlier common to
all of them -- present in the single most minimal state this port's
DOS backend can reach (no thread, nothing hardware-touched beyond a
mandatory DSP reset). This is now the single most important open
question: what causes it, since it's the *only* thing present in every
sound-on configuration tested so far.

**Dormant feature found**: `SDL_DOSAudioSetIdlePauseEnabled()` (a real,
already-built SB16 auto-idle-pause API) is never called anywhere in
`vendor/ags/`/`patches/ags/` -- this port's idle-pause stays
permanently disabled, which is why autoinit DMA, once started, never
voluntarily quiets down even during genuine silence (Tier-2 SFX never
fires in this scene; only OPL3 MIDI plays, which doesn't use this
ring). Explains `NOBGT1`'s own self-sustained ~1948 real IRQ fires with
no thread ever touching the device after open. Worth its own
correctness review before enabling (changes real playback behavior),
but doesn't by itself explain the ~5x floor (present even when DMA
never started at all).

**`SDL_HINT_DOS_MIDI_ISR_TICK=0` tested and refuted**: normal full
open, thread present, real DMA active, MIDI tick reverted to the
engine's own main-loop path -- `tick_rate=2.49`, no different from
baseline. The ISR's own per-fire MIDI-tick callback cost is not a
meaningful contributor either.

**Twelve mechanisms now checked and refuted as the full explanation.**
The next genuinely unexplored territory: SDL3's *generic* audio core
beyond `SDL_UpdateAudio()` (e.g. `SDL_CreateAudioStream`'s own
resampler/format-conversion setup), or `SDL_InitSubSystem(SDL_INIT_
AUDIO)` itself as a once-per-process cost distinct from any specific
device -- neither audited yet. Full writeup: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/
results/S7-full-bisection-matrix-realhw-2026-09-14.md`.

Acceptance gate items 4 and 5 remain FAIL. Patches 0059-0064, 0141,
0143-0144 all stay landed, all still temporary. Paused here at operator
request -- to be picked back up.

## S7 -- generic SDL core + SDL_INIT_AUDIO-subsystem-axis source audit -- 2026-09-14 (new session)

Picked back up per the "not yet found" list above. Pure source read, no
patch, no DOSBox-X, no real hardware. **Candidate 1 (SDL3's generic
audio core beyond `SDL_UpdateAudio()`) is dead**: `SDL_CreateAudioStream`/
`SDL_OpenAudioDevice`'s own bookkeeping is one-time (open-time only),
structurally unable to explain a per-tick cost paid on every
`UpdateGameOnce()` call; and a fresh read of `sys_evt_process_pending()`'s
actual call depth (`SDL_PollEvent` -> `SDL_WaitEventTimeoutNS(event, 0)`)
shows the zero-timeout path never reaches the joystick/sensor/tray
polling-interval machinery at all, and `SDL_PumpEventMaintenance()`'s
other callees are each gated on their own unrelated subsystem, none
audio-conditioned. Also closed a real gap in the per-tick call-graph
audit not named in the handoff: `update_audio_system_on_game_loop()`
(`game_run.cpp:1475`) runs unconditionally on every tick, catch-up
included, and was never previously read -- traced its full chain
(`sync_audio_playback`, `SoundClip::update`, `AudioPlayer::
GetPositionMs`/`GetPlayStateNormal`, the DJGPP `std::mutex` shim) and
found it entirely cheap (MIDI-mode accessors early-out, the mutex shim's
`lock()`/`unlock()` are true empty inline no-ops per patch 0014's own
commit message).

**Candidate 2 (`SDL_InitSubSystem(SDL_INIT_AUDIO)` as its own axis) is
confirmed genuinely untested and now concretely designed**, not just
named: `engine_init_audio()` only calls `sys_audio_init()` when
`usetup.AudioEnabled`, and inside it the non-GUS path always bundles
`SDL_InitSubSystem(SDL_INIT_AUDIO)` immediately with `dos_audio_mixer_
init()` (which reaches `OpenDevice`) -- every real-hardware cell in this
investigation, including `OSA1NT`'s earliest-possible-return phase, has
had BOTH; none has ever tested "subsystem initialized, zero devices ever
opened." Confirmed this is buildable as a real (not degenerate-silent)
test: `dos_midi_backend_open()`'s OPL3 path (`opl3_sink_open()`) talks
to the OPL3 chip directly via port I/O with no dependency on an
`SDL_AudioDeviceID` at all -- the same structural pattern GUS's existing
"Model B, out-of-band" path already uses. A new arm skipping only the
device-open call would still play real MIDI, giving a genuine
apples-to-apples `tick_rate` comparison.

**A new class of hypothesis named, not yet designed as a patch**: given
essentially the entire reachable per-tick call graph (AGS engine side and
SDL3 generic core) is now either measured or read and found cheap, and
the ~5x floor survives the single most minimal software state this port
can reach, the remaining mechanism may not be software at all -- a real
ISA-bus/electrical wait-state effect from the PicoGUS leaving a fully-idle
firmware state (distinct from the already-refuted DMA-cycle-stealing;
this would tax *all* bus traffic, not just DMA-competing traffic) would
explain the uniform tax, the floor's survival under every software axis,
and why DOSBox-X never reproduces any of this investigation's findings.
Would need a synthetic CPU-bound probe independent of any audio call,
not a source-reading pass. Full writeup: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/
results/S7-generic-core-and-subsystem-audit-2026-09-14.md`.

investigation spent eleven real-hardware cells testing inside `SDL_
dosaudio_sb.c` (thread existence, DMA activity, IRQ hooking,
`OpenDevice`'s own bring-up extent), is now proven unnecessary for the
tax** -- the mechanism cannot live there, since this run proves that code
never ran at all here.

**What remains, narrowed to exactly two untested-in-isolation
candidates**: (1) `SDL_InitSubSystem(SDL_INIT_AUDIO)`'s own generic-core
bookkeeping with zero devices ever opened, and (2) the OPL3 MIDI backend/
`midi_sched` path itself, entirely independent of SDL audio (structurally
possible -- `opl3_sink_open()` never touches an `SDL_AudioDeviceID` --
but never isolated from (1) until a follow-up test exists, since
`sys_audio_init()`'s current structure always calls `SDL_InitSubSystem(
SDL_INIT_AUDIO)` before `engine_init_audio()` ever reaches `audio_core_
init()`). Neither was previously suspected as the PRIMARY mechanism --
MIDI's own per-write cost was checked and refuted long ago, but never
whether an active MIDI backend *at all*, independent of SDL audio, is
sufficient by itself. Full writeup: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/
S7-audio-subsystem-only-realhw-2026-09-14.md`.

**Next, decisive step**: extend patch 0065 (or add a new value) so
`sys_audio_init()` can return success without ever calling `SDL_
InitSubSystem(SDL_INIT_AUDIO)`, while `engine_init_audio()` still
proceeds to `audio_core_init()` and OPL3 still plays for real --
isolating "MIDI active, SDL audio subsystem never touched" as its own
condition for the first time. If the tax survives there too, the entire
mechanism is inside the OPL3 MIDI backend/`midi_sched` path, not SDL's
audio subsystem at all. Acceptance gate items 4 and 5 remain FAIL.
Patches 0059-0065, 0141, 0143-0144 all stay landed, all still temporary.

## S7 -- SDL_INIT_AUDIO-never-touched, real-hardware result: the entire mechanism is outside SDL's audio subsystem -- 2026-09-14 (new session, continued)

Operator-approved cell (tag `SUBSY2`, `binary_sha12=406c63249f6b`).
**Result: `tick_rate=2.53`** -- essentially identical to `SUBSY1`'s own
2.52, and **`regwrite calls=6079` is the exact same count as `SUBSY1`**,
not just similar order of magnitude: `SDL_InitSubSystem(SDL_INIT_AUDIO)`
being called or not makes zero observable difference to anything, since
nothing downstream ever reads that state once the OPL3 MIDI backend is
what actually drives playback.

**Conclusion, decisive**: combined with `SUBSY1`'s own finding, the
entire ~10-12x tax mechanism lives **entirely outside `vendor/SDL/src/
audio/`** -- not `SDL_dosaudio_sb.c`, not SDL3's generic `SDL_audio.c`
core, not `SDL_InitSubSystem` itself. Fifteen real-hardware cells across
this whole investigation (`AUDIOFX1`-`4`, `DMAX1`, `NOBGT1`, `OSA1`-`4`,
`OSA1NT`-`4NT`, `SUBSY1`, `SUBSY2`) were exploring code that, while real
and worth ruling out, was never where the mechanism could have been.

**A promising lead chased and correctly killed**: `SDL_dos_audio_synth.c`
exports `SDL_DOSOplTimerPumpStart()`, which reprograms PIT ch0 (IRQ-0,
the system timer) via `DOS_HookInterruptReplace` and drives the MIDI
tick directly from interrupt context -- exactly the shape of thing that
could explain a uniform, system-wide tax, and its own guard (refuses
when the SB device is "hot") means it would have been refused in every
one of the fifteen prior cells but newly eligible in `SUBSY1`/`SUBSY2`
(which never open the SB device at all). **Re-verified with `/usr/bin/
grep` rather than trusting the first Bash-builtin search** (per this
session's own standing note on that tool's real false-negative
history): no caller of `SDL_DOSOplTimerPumpStart` exists anywhere in
this codebase -- `opl3_sink_open()` calls only `SDL_DOSOpl3InitChip()`
(register writes only, confirmed by reading its body, no interrupt
hooking). This port never wires the OPL timer pump in. A correctly
avoided false lead.

**What remains**: catch-up ticks call neither `audio_core_entry_poll()`
nor any MIDI function at all (gated to `play.fast_forward` only since
patch 0060) yet pay the identical ~495ms/tick tax as real ticks in every
cell measured -- ruling out, by construction, any "MIDI software work
costs X per tick" hypothesis. The only mechanism class left standing
that can explain a cost paid by ticks that call zero audio-related code:
a real, continuous hardware/electrical effect from the OPL3 chip (this
rig's PicoGUS in OPL3-emulation mode) actively synthesizing audio,
independent of DOS-side polling -- structurally the same shape as the
already-refuted DMA-cycle-stealing hypothesis, but attributed to OPL3
synthesis firmware rather than SB16 DMA, never previously testable since
nothing before this session isolated OPL3 activity from the SB16
device's own concurrent state. Full writeup: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/
results/S7-audio-subsystem-only-v2-realhw-2026-09-14.md`.

**The search space is now dramatically and correctly narrowed** for the
first time in this investigation: from "somewhere in SDL3-DOS's audio
backend or generic core" to "the OPL3 chip's own real-time synthesis
activity, or something inside `shared/audio/opl3_sink.c`/`midi_sched.c`
never yet suspected as a primary mechanism." Acceptance gate items 4 and
5 remain FAIL. Patches 0059-0066, 0141, 0143-0144 all stay landed, all
still temporary. Next: a silence-vs-sounding OPL3 test (does the tax
appear at chip-init time or only once a note is actually key-on/
synthesizing) -- needs a new diagnostic, DOSBox-X validation, then real
hardware.

## S7 -- no-MIDI-backend-at-all, real-hardware result: MIDI touch is the necessary trigger, and it corrects the earlier bisection matrix -- 2026-09-14 (new session, continued)

Operator-approved cell (tag `NOBK1`, `binary_sha12=433340f66668`), a
COMPLETELY NORMAL SB16 open (thread present, default autoinit DMA,
nothing about the SB16 backend restricted) plus `DOSAGS_MIDI_NO_
BACKEND=1`. **Result: `tick_rate=3.20`** -- matching `OSA1NT`'s own
3.21 almost exactly, the ~5x floor, **not** the full ~10-12x tax every
other "SB16 fully open, thread present" cell in this investigation has
shown. `audio_vital_status` confirms `midi=none,events=0` -- `dos_midi_
backend_open()` genuinely never ran.

**This is the first cell in the entire investigation to test "SB16
open completely normally AND zero MIDI backend touched" -- and it
corrects the earlier bisection matrix's own conclusion.** Every prior
"SB16 fully open, thread present" cell also had a real, dispatching
OPL3 MIDI backend active; `S7-full-bisection-matrix-realhw-2026-09-14.md`'s
own "thread presence and DMA/IRQ activity are each independently
sufficient to reach the ~10x ceiling" claim was never actually isolated
from MIDI state, because no cell before `NOBK1` broke that correlation.
**`NOBK1` shows a fully-normal SB16 open, with MIDI never touched, lands
at the same ~5x floor as the maximally-minimal SB16 state** -- thread/
DMA state was a proxy for "MIDI is also active," not an independent
booster.

**The corrected, now fully coherent two-factor model** (combining all
eighteen real-hardware cells in this investigation): (1) the SB16
device merely being open, in any configuration, costs a real ~5x tax
against the sound-off baseline; (2) a MIDI backend being touched at
all -- even chip-init-only with zero dispatch (`SILNT1`), even with the
SB16 device never opened at all (`SUBSY1`/`SUBSY2`) -- is independently
*sufficient* to reach the full ~10-12x ceiling by itself, regardless of
SB16/thread/DMA/IRQ state. Neither factor's earlier attribution
survives untouched; what actually carries the full tax in every cell is
MIDI activity, however minimal, not thread or DMA state.

**What remains**: the only action `SILNT1` (full tax) has that `NOBK1`
(floor) lacks is `dos_midi_backend_open()` itself succeeding -- for
OPL3, `SDL_DOSOpl3InitChip()`'s ~20 register writes, already measured
cheap in isolation and structurally unable to explain a tax persisting
for the rest of a 75-95s run by cost alone. Since `TNWB1` (WaveBlaster/
MPU-401, a completely different chip and I/O port range, touched even
earlier at session cold-init) shows the identical collapse, the
mechanism generalizes across both MIDI hardware paths -- pointing at a
persistent hardware/electrical side effect of activating a second
legacy interface (OPL3 or MPU-401) alongside the SB16 emulation on this
rig's PicoGUS card, not a register-write cost or any software
mechanism this investigation's tools (source reading, DOSBox-X) can
resolve further. Full writeup: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/
S7-midi-no-backend-realhw-2026-09-14.md`.

**Practical implication for the 40fps goal**: on this specific rig, a
title using both PCM SFX and real MIDI music pays close to the full
~10-12x tax essentially unavoidably in software once a MIDI backend is
touched at all -- this looks like a real hardware-level constant of this
PicoGUS-based rig configuration, not a software inefficiency this
port's own code can fix, and (per this hub's "never contribute
upstream" policy) not something to chase into PicoGUS's own firmware
either. The pre-registered `<= 1.5 fps` acceptance bar was assuming a
fixable software cost; re-scoping it given this finding is an operator
decision, not made here. Acceptance gate items 4 and 5 remain FAIL.
