## S7 -- GUS MIDI escape-hatch, real-hardware result: GUS avoids the tax entirely -- 2026-09-14 (new session, continued)

Operator-approved cell (tag `GUST1`, same unmodified binary as `NOBK1`).
**A real harness gap hit first**: `run-rig.sh --boot-profile 3` failed
twice (`select_boot_profile -> None`), both times landing safely back
on the default `PGSB` profile (confirmed via independent screenshot,
no corruption) -- the first time this dosags harness path has ever
exercised `vcctrl`'s blind LED-timed menu selection for this port.
Worked around, not routed around: manually drove the same protocol
(reboot, poll `vc leds` directly for the real capslock POST-edge at
t+24.9s, fire four `3`+`enter` keys in a single ~0.58s burst well under
the CONFIG.SYS menu's 5s timeout, poll for the scrolllock RDYPULSE
signal) -- landed on `PGGUS` cleanly on the first manual attempt. A
separate `wait_for_job_done` false-negative (waited the full 1800s even
though the underlying transfer had already finished within 5 minutes,
confirmed via direct `vc file-status`) was the same already-documented,
low-severity `vcctrl` quirk this investigation has hit before -- flagged
`vcctrl`'s own boot-profile-selection timing as worth a closer look for
whoever next needs `--boot-profile` on this rig, not fixed this entry.

**Result: `tick_rate=9.39`** -- 2.4x-3.8x better than every OPL3/
WaveBlaster sound-on cell in this whole investigation (2.48-3.23),
real dispatch confirmed (`midi=gus,events=70`, zero underruns). Per-tick
breakdown is the cleanest confirmation this investigation has produced:
**catch-up ticks (which touch zero audio-related code by construction)
cost ~37ms/tick -- statistically indistinguishable from the ~42ms/tick
sound-off baseline.** The systemic, everything-pays-it tax this whole
S7 arc chased is **absent** under GUS. The remaining elevated cost
(`realtick_us` mean 383.7ms) is fully explained by a real, already-
precedented, scoped inefficiency: `gus_sink.c`'s `reap_finished_
voices()` (called on every note-on) triggers `SDL_DOSGusGetState()`, a
full GF1 voice-mask hardware scan -- the exact same class of cost the
S5 GUS architecture work already found and fixed for the PCM path
(`SDL_DOSGusVoiceActive()`, patch 0140) but explicitly left unfixed for
MIDI's own reap path at the time ("note-driven... never the flagged hot
path" -- true for that session's PCM-focused workload, never actually
measured under real sustained MIDI note-on traffic until now). `slots_us`
max of 6.9 SECONDS for one scan suggests either register-read volume or
a genuine GF1-communication stall worth its own follow-up.

**Practical implication for 40fps**: switching this rig's target profile
from `PGSB` to `PGGUS` sidesteps the entire ~10-12x systemic tax this
whole session characterized -- a real, working alternative path to music
at much better performance, with a concrete, scoped, already-precedented
fix available for the remaining cost (port `SDL_DOSGusVoiceActive`'s
per-voice pattern to `gus_sink.c`'s own reap path). This is exactly the
kind of information the pending acceptance-gate re-scoping decision
needs. Full writeup: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/
S7-gus-midi-realhw-2026-09-14.md`.

Operator-approved cell (tag `GUSD1`, `binary_sha12=c6d6f6626df8`). Hit

completed independently of the local process, recovered by polling
`file-status` directly instead of re-invoking the full script.

**Result: `gusscan(calls=28 min_us=27 mean_us=109 max_us=170)`** --
only 28 calls total, each 27-170us, ~3ms total. **`SDL_DOSGusGetState()`
is completely exonerated** -- it cannot explain any part of `slots_us`'s
101ms mean or 6.9s max. The prior entry's own handoff-inherited fix
idea (port `SDL_DOSGusVoiceActive`'s pattern to `reap_finished_voices()`)
would have targeted a function that isn't slow at all, on top of
already being architecturally mismatched.

**The real finding, checked precisely rather than trusting the
aggregate mean**: in both `GUST1` and `GUSD1`, ONE single call accounts
for ~99.8% of the total `slots_us` sum -- the other 66-67 calls average
only 120-162us each (cheap, unremarkable). **The outlier itself is
nearly identical across the two independent runs on two different
binaries: 6,890,560us vs 6,890,385us, a difference of only 175
microseconds out of 6.89 seconds** -- far too precise to be
environmental/disk-I/O jitter (the room-transition timestamps
themselves differ by ~220ms between the same two runs). This points at
a deterministic mechanism tied to the song/scene content itself, not a
general GUS dispatch inefficiency. Not yet identified -- candidates
include `midi_sched_tick()`'s own `delta_ms > 10000` catch-up clamp
combined with this specific song's event density, or an unmeasured
per-call cost in `SDL_DOSGusSetVoiceFreq/Vol/Pan`/`SDL_
DOSGusStartVoice` (read this entry, look like plain register writes,
not yet individually instrumented). Full writeup: `tests/games/
trilbysnotes/results/S7-gus-getstate-cost-realhw-2026-09-15.md`.

**Encouraging reframing**: GUS's own typical per-call MIDI dispatch
cost (~120-160us) is cheap, nothing like the OPL3/WaveBlaster systemic
tax. The gap between GUS's `tick_rate` (~9.36-9.39) and the sound-off
baseline may be dominated by this one narrow, reproducible,
not-yet-explained event rather than a general inefficiency -- if so, a
real fix could recover much closer to baseline than the raw number
currently suggests, but this needs the next diagnostic pass to confirm,
not assumed. Patches SDL/0145 and ags/0069 stay landed (the diagnostic
is sound); no `gus_sink.c` fix landed -- correctly not landed, since
the originally-planned one would have been wrong. Acceptance gate items
4 and 5 remain open.

## S7-GUS -- GUS voice-setup call + midi_sched_tick() call-site cost, real-hardware result: all six exonerated, new source-verified candidate found -- 2026-09-15 (new session, continued)

Operator-approved cell (tag `GUSV1`, `binary_sha12=760ec38b22ea`). The
manual LED-edge boot-profile workaround, which landed on `PGGUS` first-
try in both `GUST1` and `GUSD1`, did NOT transfer cleanly this session
-- two attempts using the previously-recorded ~25s timing both landed on
the wrong profile (`PGSB`). Recovered by recording a boot on video and
extracting frames via `ffmpeg` (the CONFIG.SYS menu never produces a
stable capturable frame on this rig -- a real VGA sync-loss during that
mode), which found the menu actually resolves ~35.5s after `ctrl+alt+
delete`, not ~25s. A fifth attempt fired the keystroke burst at that
corrected window and landed cleanly. **This is new information**: the
manual workaround's timing is not as session-independent as the prior
two "worked first-try" cells suggested -- a third real, reproducible
timing-sensitivity finding for this exact rig/profile combination
(`vcctrl`'s own `select_boot_profile()` remains flagged, not fixed).

**Result**: `slots_us` max=6,891,495us -- a THIRD independent
confirmation of the same outlier, within 1110us of `GUST1`'s 6,890,560
and `GUSD1`'s 6,890,385 (a 1-in-~6000 relative spread across three
runs on two binaries). **All five voice-setup calls (`voicefreq`/
`voicevol`/`voicepan`/`voicestart`/`voicestop`) and `miditick` itself
are all exonerated** -- `miditick` max=3,602us, three orders of
magnitude short of the outlier, conclusively ruling out
`midi_sched_tick()` as a whole (dispatch loop, tempo math, every GUS
call it makes) as the mechanism.

**New candidate, source-verified this entry**: `miditick`'s own call
count (20) is less than `audioprb`'s `total_calls` (68) in the same
window, and `AudioPlayer::MidiPoll()`'s own structure calls `Init()`
(NOT bracketed by `miditick`, which starts only at the `midi_sched_
tick()` call after it) before ever reaching the bracket. `Init()` ->
`MidiInit()` -> `dos_midi_backend_prepare_song()` -> (GUS backend)
`gus_sink_prepare_song()` (`shared/audio/gus_sink.c`) loops every
melodic/drum program the song uses, uploading each resident subsample
via `SDL_DOSGusUploadSample()`. Read directly this entry: the default
upload path, `gus_upload_pio()` (`vendor/SDL/src/audio/dos/
SDL_dosaudio_gus.c`), is a byte-wise PIO transfer loop, and
`g_gus_pio_autoinc` defaults to `false` -- meaning the DEFAULT path
re-selects the full DRAM address before EVERY byte (the function's own
comment: "~6 outportb/byte" vs ~1 with autoinc on). For a real GM
instrument set (multiple subsamples per instrument, up to 2MB per
sample per `gus_sink.c`'s own cap), this is exactly the kind of
deterministic, per-song, one-shot, multi-second real-hardware cost this
whole investigation has been chasing -- and it runs on the SAME `Poll()`
call `slots_us` times, one call before `midi_sched_tick()` (and
`miditick`'s bracket) ever starts. Strong and well-supported, but NOT
yet directly measured -- per this hub's own discipline, and per this
exact sub-investigation's own prior history of two wrong assumptions
(`reap_finished_voices()`'s architecture mismatch, `SDL_DOSGusGetState()`
assumed-slow), the next pass instruments this directly rather than
trusting the source read. Full writeup: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/
results/S7-gus-voicecalls-miditick-realhw-2026-09-15.md`.

**Not yet done**: bracket `SDL_DOSGusUploadSample()`/`gus_upload_pio()`
(or `gus_sink_prepare_song()` as a whole) directly and re-run. If
confirmed, `SDL_HINT_DOS_GUS_PIO_AUTOINC=1` (an existing hint, never
enabled by default) could plausibly cut the cost ~6x with zero new
code -- a real, likely-fixable software cost, unlike the OPL3/
WaveBlaster hardware constant. Acceptance gate items 4 and 5
(re-targeted at GUS) remain open.

## S7-GUS -- default GUS DRAM upload to auto-increment mode: patch landed, DOSBox-X validated -- 2026-09-15 (new session, continued)

**Important, unresolved by this entry**: autoinc was originally written
(SDL patch SDL/0112) as the fix for a documented real CPU-freeze hazard
on real GF1 hardware (a PicoGUS RP2040 asserting IOCHRDY under the
per-byte path's port-op flood, stalling the ISA bus indefinitely with
interrupts disabled) -- left off by default "until g2k confirms autoinc
reaches gameplay, then flip to ON," a confirmation this hub's history
shows never happened. **Autoinc mode has never been exercised on real
GF1 hardware before this patch.**

**DOSBox-X validation** (`binary_sha12=54d51604e8d8`): build succeeds
cleanly, no regression to the OPL3 path (`miditick`/`regwrite` both
real and consistent with prior sessions), GUS-backend run hits the same
already-documented GF1-detection gap as every prior pass. **This
validates compilation and no-regression only -- it cannot and does not
validate autoinc's real-hardware safety**, since DOSBox-X's `[gus]`
emulation never presents as real GF1 hardware. Full writeup: `tests/
games/trilbysnotes/results/S7-gus-autoinc-fix-dosboxx-2026-09-15.md`.

**Not yet done**: the real, carefully-supervised real-hardware
validation -- autoinc's first-ever real GF1 exposure, treated as a
first-time validation of previously-unexercised code, not a routine
re-measure. Needs its own fresh, separately-asked operator go-ahead. If
a hang/instability is observed, `patches/ags/0074` must be reverted and
the observation recorded as confirmation of the original #41 hazard
persisting on this rig's current PicoGUS firmware.

## S7-GUS -- default GUS PIO autoinc, real-hardware result: NO FREEZE, but an unexplained regression elsewhere -- 2026-09-15 (new session, continued)

Operator-approved cell (tag `GUSA1`, `binary_sha12=54d51604e8d8`),
`SDL_HINT_DOS_GUS_DIAG=1` set and the run actively monitored throughout
as the pre-planned safety measure. **No freeze, no hang -- the
specific documented hazard did not materialize.**

**But the fix underperformed badly, and something unrelated broke.**
`prepsong` (6,274,811us) is only ~9% faster than `GUSU1`'s non-autoinc
baseline (6,891,245us) -- nowhere near the ~6x hypothesized.
`uploadpio`'s own per-call cost for the IDENTICAL 712,114 bytes is only
~13% better. Meanwhile: `tick_rate` collapsed from `GUSU1`'s 9.34 to
**2.31**; `duration_s` grew from 28 to **100** for the same fixed
auto-exit tick target; total MIDI events dispatched grew from 76 to
**1083**; and `SDL_DOSGusGetState()` -- untouched by this patch,
already exonerated as cheap (~106-170us/call) in three prior real-
hardware cells -- ballooned to **22,623us mean per call** (~213x) across
530 calls (~19x), a cumulative ~12 real SECONDS just in `gusscan` cost
alone (vs ~3ms in `GUSU1`).

**Two competing explanations, NOT distinguished by this single cell**:
(1) a real correctness/interaction defect in autoinc mode leaving the
GF1's voice-tracking state confused for the rest of the session
(`gusscan` reads `voice_active_mask` directly, so this would explain
its cost/frequency blowup specifically); or (2) a downstream confound
where something unrelated slowed real-time pacing, letting `midi_sched_
tick()`'s own catch-up clamp advance further per call and dispatch more
events (explaining the event-count jump, though less obviously the
per-call `gusscan` cost). The `gusscan` per-call cost increase has no
obvious confound-only explanation and is the strongest reason to
suspect (1), not pure noise -- but this is not confirmed.

**Recommendation: given the net real-hardware effect is a large
regression (tick_rate 9.34 -> 2.31), `patches/ags/0074` should not
remain this port's shipped default while this anomaly is unexplained**,
even though the specific freeze hazard tested for did not occur. Full
writeup: `tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/
S7-gus-autoinc-fix-realhw-2026-09-15.md`.

**Not yet done**: decide revert-vs-investigate-further (a same-session
autoinc-on/autoinc-off A/B, back to back, would directly distinguish
the two explanations above -- this single cell cannot). Acceptance gate
items 4 and 5 remain open, further from closeable than before this
cell given the net regression. Boot-profile workaround now
characterized more precisely (a ~1.2s real interactive window,
capture-blind during it) but still unresolved (1 automated success / 4
failures across five sessions).

## S7-GUS -- tick_rate/gusscan confound ROOT-CAUSED: SDL_HINT_DOS_GUS_DIAG's own synchronous logging -- 2026-09-15 (new session, source analysis)

Not a session-to-session hardware/rig effect. Grepping every S7-GUS
result doc for the diag hint gives a 100% clean split: `GUST1`/`GUSD1`/
`GUSV1`/`GUSU1` (tick_rate 9.34-9.39, `gusscan` calls=28, mean_us
106-109) never set `SDL_HINT_DOS_GUS_DIAG`; `GUSA1`/`GUSAB0`/`GUSAB1`
(tick_rate 2.31-3.32, `gusscan` calls 283-530, mean_us 18640-26008) all
set `SDL_HINT_DOS_GUS_DIAG=1` as the (reasonable, intentional)
freeze-hazard safety net for the autoinc real-hardware tests.

**Mechanism, source-confirmed in `SDL_dosaudio_gus.c`**: `dos_port_dbg_
log` (line ~189) is `fprintf` + a per-line `fsync` (patch 0036) --
real, synchronous disk I/O. `SDL_DOSGusGetState()` (line 1224, called
from `reap_finished_voices()` on every note-on) calls `gus_diag_
flush()` (line 241) only when `g_gus_diag` is true, draining a queued
ring of voice-state records with one fsync'd log line each -- with diag
off this is a pure register scan (~106-170us, exactly the clean
baseline); with diag on it's disk I/O per call. `gus_upload_pio()`
(line ~745-752) is gated the same way, logging progress roughly every
1KB during the upload -- for 712,114 bytes that's ~695 extra fsync'd
writes injected into one `prepsong` call, explaining `GUSAB0`'s 11.27s
vs `GUSU1`'s clean 6.89s for the identical byte count. The `gusscan`
call-count blowup (28 -> 283-530) is a feedback loop on top of this, not
a separate cause: once each tick is I/O-bound, `midi_sched_tick()`'s
`delta_ms>10000` catch-up clamp has more real time to advance through
per call, dispatching more events, allocating/reaping more voices, each
reap flushing more queued diag records. One mechanism explains every
symptom across both the read-side scan and the write-side upload loop,
which is why it read as a broad "something about this session" effect
rather than a narrow, specific bug.

**Does not reopen the autoinc decision** -- autoinc never regressed
anything even in the diag-contaminated `GUSAB0`/`GUSAB1` A/B. It does
mean autoinc's true benefit is understated: that A/B's ~2x prepsong
improvement was measured with BOTH arms paying the diag tax; a clean
diag-off comparison would likely land much closer to the original ~6x
hypothesis.

**Proposed next cell (NOT yet run, needs a fresh operator go-ahead)**:
single cell, `PGGUS`, `SDL_HINT_DOS_GUS_DIAG` left unset (not `0` --
just don't set it), autoinc=1 (current shipped default), same song/
settings as `GUSU1`/`GUSAB1`. Predicts `tick_rate` back near 9.3,
`gusscan` calls back near 28 at ~100-170us mean, `prepsong` well under
`GUSU1`'s 6.89s baseline. Cheapest cell in this whole sub-investigation
-- no new instrumentation needed, just the existing hint turned off --
and would close the confound question with a real-hardware confirmation
plus give the first clean read of autoinc's actual benefit. Acceptance
gate items 4/5 can likely close on this result if it lands as predicted.

(best of the whole sub-investigation), `gusscan` calls=28 at 106us
mean -- byte-for-byte `GUSU1`'s clean baseline -- and `midi events=76`
(matches `GUSU1`'s 76, not the 580-1083 seen in every diag-on cell).
**Confirms the confound was entirely `SDL_HINT_DOS_GUS_DIAG`'s own
synchronous fsync'd logging, not a GF1/autoinc interaction.**

**True autoinc benefit, now uncontaminated**: `uploadpio` mean_us=53071
vs `GUSU1`'s 274,958us (autoinc off, diag off) -- a **5.18x reduction**
for the identical 712,114 bytes, landing close to the original "~6
outportb/byte -> ~1 outportb/byte" hypothesis this sub-investigation set
out to test (the ~2x measured in the earlier diag-contaminated
`GUSAB0`/`GUSAB1` A/B understated it). `prepsong` max_us=2,009,752
(~2.01s) vs `GUSU1`'s 6,891,245us (~6.89s), a 3.43x reduction.

**Both questions this sub-investigation opened are now closed**:
`patches/ags/0074` delivers a real, large, now-quantified improvement
with no freeze/hang across three real-hardware exposures (`GUSA1`,
`GUSAB1`, `GUSN1`); the tick_rate/gusscan anomaly was the diagnostic
hint's own cost, not an autoinc defect. Acceptance gate items 4/5
(re-targeted at GUS) look closeable on this result. Full detail:
`tests/games/trilbysnotes/results/S7-gus-diag-off-confirmation-realhw-2026-09-15.md`.

Also worth recording: `vcctrl`'s `select_boot_profile()` timing hazard
this sub-investigation kept hitting has been fixed upstream in
`~/git/vcctrl` (commit `d645faa`, same-day turnaround from the precise
LED-sequence report this investigation produced) -- not yet deployed to
the live daemon, no action needed here, will apply automatically once
it is.

## 32-bit display path -- design comparison, 2026-09-15 (design session, following Sound claim)

Same discipline as "S5 GUS architecture" above: read the pinned sources
first (AGS's own `Engine/gfx/ali3dsw.cpp`/`.h`, `Engine/ac/draw.cpp`,
`Common/gfx/bitmap.cpp`, `Common/ac/gamesetupstructbase.h`; the shared
SDL3-DOS backend's `SDL_dosmodes.c`/`SDL_dosframebuffer.c`), then decide
-- no implementation code written against this yet. Scheduling is
resolved (Sound claimed 2026-09-15, see above); **the design choice
itself is not** -- this section lays out both options with real numbers
and leaves the choice to the operator, per this milestone's own PLAN.md
entry ("Read both before choosing; do not schedule it ahead of Sound
without the operator").

### What is actually blocked today, and where

The failure the operator saw ("Failed to init gfx mode. Error: Display
colour depth not supported: 32") comes from exactly one line:
`ali3dsw.cpp:65-68`'s `IsModeSupported()`, which rejects any
`mode.ColorDepth` other than 8 or 16. This is a narrower gate than it
first looks, and the scope of each option below depends on how narrow:

- **The rest of the software-rendering pipeline is already 32-bit-capable
  today, unconditionally, on every platform including this one.**
  `GetCompatibleBitmapFormat()` (`ali3dsw.cpp:294-297`) is a pure
  identity passthrough -- it does not clamp to 8/16. Sprite/DDB creation
  (`CreateDDB`, `CreateDDBFromBitmap`, `ALSoftwareBitmap`), the sprite
  depth-conversion pipeline (`Engine/ac/draw.cpp`'s
  `PrepareSpriteForUseImpl`, see below), and per-pixel alpha blending
  (`Engine/gfx/gfx_util.cpp`) all operate generically on whatever depth a
  `Bitmap` reports, 8/16/32 alike -- this is stock upstream AGS behavior,
  not something DOS-specific was ever added or removed for. **Only two
  places in `ali3dsw.cpp` hard-code 8-or-16: `IsModeSupported()` and
  `CreateVirtualScreen()`'s `vscreen_fmt` ternary** (`ali3dsw.cpp:214`,
  `INDEX8` or `RGB565`, no third branch). This was a deliberate choice,
  not an oversight: the file's own header comment and patch 0029's commit
  message record that the *previous* version of this driver went the
  other way -- it hard-required a 32-bit display via `SDL_Renderer` +
  an `SDL_Texture` conversion step (`ali3dsw.h`'s DOS-PORT comment,
  `SDL-SURFACE.md:95-101`), which patch 0029 ripped out specifically
  because it cost three full-frame passes at 4 bytes/pixel for an 8-bit
  game and depended on a 320x200x32 VESA mode that 486-era cards often
  do not expose. **That old path is not what Option 1 below would
  rebuild** -- it presented via a texture/renderer at a hardcoded 32,
  never at the game's own native depth; a new 32-bit branch on the
  *current* native-depth `SDL_GetWindowSurface`/`SDL_BlitSurfaceScaled`
  architecture is a materially smaller, different change from the thing
  that was removed.

- **The shared SDL3-DOS backend's VESA/LFB layer is already mostly
  bpp-generic, and already enumerates 32-bit modes -- it has just never
  been exercised at 32bpp end to end.** `SDL_dosmodes.c`'s mode
  enumeration (`GetVESAModeInfo`/`DOSVESA_video_addr...` loop,
  `SDL_dosmodes.c:721-748`) already maps VBE `bpp == 32` to
  `SDL_PIXELFORMAT_XRGB8888` alongside the existing 8/16/24 cases -- this
  is not new code to write, it already runs today and already produces
  32bpp `SDL_DisplayMode` entries on hardware that has them (currently
  simply never picked, because nothing above it ever asks for one).
  `SDL_dosframebuffer.c`'s framebuffer creation and flush path
  (`CreateNormalFramebuffer`, `populate_fb_state_for_direct_fb`,
  `BankedDosmemput`, `SDL_DOSVesaDirectPresentFull`) derives its byte
  math from `SDL_BYTESPERPIXEL(mode->format)` throughout -- no
  8/16-specific branch exists in the mode-set, bank-switch, or LFB
  nearptr write paths. **None of this has ever run at 32bpp on this
  hub's hardware or in DOSBox-X** -- the mode-enumeration/framebuffer-flush
  code being generic "by construction" is not the same as "validated at
  this depth," and the DMA-upload/16-bit-PIO surprise the S5 GUS work hit
  (`SDL_DOSGusUploadSample()`'s undocumented third gate) is a live
  reminder that "reads as generic" and "confirmed correct at a depth
  nothing has ever asked for" are different claims. One generic helper
  in this same file, `GetConvertedCursorSurface()`
  (`SDL_dosframebuffer.c:504-580`), *is* hard-limited to a paletted
  (`SDL_GetSurfacePalette(dst)` non-null, i.e. 8-bit) destination -- but
  checked and ruled out as relevant: AGS never calls `SDL_SetCursor`/
  `SDL_CreateCursor` (`grep -rn SDL_SetCursor vendor/ags/Engine/` finds
  only an unrelated `SDL_ShowCursor()` in `sys_main.cpp:480`), it draws
  its own mouse pointer as an ordinary sprite through the same DDB
  pipeline as everything else. This helper is dead code for this port at
  every depth, not a new 32-bit-specific gap.

### Option 1: a real 32-bit VESA/LFB present path

**What actually has to change, given the above:** `ali3dsw.cpp`'s
`IsModeSupported()` gains a third accepted depth; `CreateVirtualScreen()`
gains a third `vscreen_fmt` branch (`SDL_PIXELFORMAT_XRGB8888` -- AGS's
32-bit `Bitmap` format is BGRA-ordered with an alpha byte AGS treats as
opaque/masked per `Common/gfx/bitmap.cpp`'s `makeacol32`/`MASK_COLOR_32`
convention, matching what `_trans_alpha_blender32` in this same file
already assumes, so `XRGB8888` -- alpha ignored, not `ARGB8888` -- is the
right target format for the *presented* surface even though sprites
carry real alpha internally); `Present()`'s existing
`SDL_BlitSurfaceScaled()` call needs no change, it already converts
whatever `_vscreenSurface`'s format is to whatever the window surface's
format is generically. That is a small, narrow, dosags-local (`ali3dsw.cpp`
is this port's own patched copy, not shared/) change -- the S0-class
"narrow buildable slice" this project's own workflow rule asks for.

**What is NOT narrow: validating the shared backend at a depth it has
never run at.** Per the "would every port want this" test in the hub's
own `CLAUDE.md`, any real bug found while exercising 32bpp mode-set,
bank-switch math, or LFB nearptr writes for the first time belongs in
`.sdl-dos-ports/shared/`, fixed there, then pulled back via the subtree
pin -- not patched around locally in dosags. This is the same shape of
work S5 GUS's items 4-5 called out (DOSBox-X validation first, asking
whether the emulator's own VESA/GUS emulation is even a fair proxy at
this depth, before trusting it as more than a correctness smoke test;
real-hardware validation on the Mach64 needing its own fresh
operator go-ahead) -- expect a comparable, non-trivial validation pass
before this is "done," not just the `ali3dsw.cpp` patch.

**Per-frame cost, checked against real numbers, not assumed:** at 4
bytes/pixel, 320x200x32 (the depth every 486-tier requested title
actually needs -- see the "Requested titles" table above; none of them
are 640x480 at the 486 KPI tier) is 256,000 bytes/frame -- exactly 2x
today's 320x200x16 in-profile ceiling (128,000 bytes/frame) and 4x
320x200x8 (64,000 bytes/frame, the number `SDL_dosmodes.c`'s own
`SDL_HINT_DOS_MAX_BPP` comment already uses as its baseline). Whether
that 2x is affordable on HW-486-66 is an open, real-hardware question,
not answerable from source alone -- but it is a much smaller ask than
`SDL_dosmodes.c:612-618`'s wave-16 finding that dropping 640x480 from
24 to 16bpp was worth ~1.5x by itself, i.e. bpp-doubling costs on this
class of hardware are real and roughly linear, not negligible, and
should be measured (DOSBox-X first, then real hardware) rather than
assumed survivable just because the byte count "only" doubles.
**640x480x32 VRAM math** (the rig's ATI Mach64, 2 MB per
`HARDWARE.md`): a single 640x480x32 page is 1,228,800 bytes, which fits
comfortably; a double-buffered pair would need 2,457,600 bytes, which
does NOT fit in 2 MB. This driver already runs single-buffered only
(`SDL_dosframebuffer.c`'s patch-0014 comment: page-flipping was
force-disabled project-wide because real Cirrus/Mach64 hardware could
not reliably swap the displayed page) -- so "fits in 2 MB" is true in
practice, but only because that trade-off was already made for other
reasons, not because 640x480x32 has real headroom to spare. This matters
only for the compatibility-sweep ceiling case (Nelly Cootalot); no
requested 486-tier title needs it.

**Shared vs. dosags-local split:** the `ali3dsw.cpp` depth-gate change is
dosags-local (this file is AGS-specific, already project-owned, not
shared/). Any shared/ work this option turns up is exactly the kind of
change every port would want (a correctly-validated 32bpp present path
benefits any future 32-bit-native port, not just AGS), so it belongs in
`.sdl-dos-ports/shared/`, per that repo's own "would every port want
this" rule -- not written as a dosags-specific patch.

### Option 2: convert 32-bit assets to 16-bit at load, run the existing path

**AGS already ships the depth-conversion machinery this would reuse --
this is not new engineering, it is wiring up an existing upstream
feature.** `Engine/ac/draw.cpp`'s `PrepareSpriteForUseImpl()`
(`draw.cpp:491-549`) already converts any sprite whose stored depth
(`bmp_col_depth`) differs from `game.GetColorDepth()`
(`game_col_depth`) via `GfxUtil::ConvertBitmap()`, unconditionally, on
every load -- this is how upstream AGS has always handled a sprite
imported at a different depth than the game's own configured depth, on
every platform. `game.color_depth` (bytes-per-pixel: 1/2/4) is a plain
public field on `GameSetupStructBase`
(`Common/ac/gamesetupstructbase.h:56`), read once via `ReadInt32()` at
game-data deserialization (`gamesetupstructbase.cpp:115`) -- structurally
nothing stops a DOS-specific hook from overriding it immediately after
load, before any sprite is first touched, forcing every 32-bit sprite
through the existing downgrade path as if the game had been authored at
16-bit.

**Alpha coherence, checked against the actual conversion code, not
assumed free:** two genuinely different features are both called
"alpha" in AGS and they are NOT equally affected.
- **Whole-object constant-alpha transparency** (`Object.Transparency`/
  `Character.Transparency`, screen fades) is untouched by this option.
  `Engine/gfx/gfx_util.cpp`'s `DrawSpriteWithTransparency()`
  (`gfx_util.cpp:105-133`) uses Allegro's `set_trans_blender()` +
  `TransBlendBlt()` whenever `surface_depth > 8` -- not gated on 32 at
  all. This is the same mechanism 16-bit-only AGS games have used since
  long before 32-bit PNG import existed; it survives the downgrade
  completely.
- **Genuine per-pixel alpha channel art** (soft/anti-aliased sprite
  edges baked into a 32-bit PNG import, the common modern-AGS authoring
  workflow) is real-alpha-blended only when `ds->GetColorDepth() == 32 &&
  sprite->GetColorDepth() == 32` (`gfx_util.cpp:92-93`) -- exactly the
  case this option removes. Before downgrading such a sprite,
  `PrepareSpriteForUseImpl` calls
  `BitmapHelper::ReplaceHalfAlphaWithRGBMask()` (`draw.cpp:513-517`),
  which is `ReplaceAlphaWithRGBMask(bmp, 127)`
  (`Common/gfx/bitmap.cpp:182-196`): every pixel with alpha <= 127
  becomes fully transparent (`MASK_COLOR_32`), every pixel with alpha >
  127 becomes fully opaque at its own RGB. **This is a hard binary cutoff
  at the 50% mark, not a soft degrade** -- a genuinely translucent
  50%-alpha overlay effect sits right at the threshold and becomes
  visually incoherent (flickers between fully-there and fully-gone
  depending on which side of 127 individual pixels land), while ordinary
  anti-aliased sprite/character edges just become hard-edged/jagged --
  a real, visible cosmetic regression, but a survivable one for content
  whose alpha use is edge AA rather than deliberate translucency effects.
  Which of the 10 requested 32-bit titles lean on which is not knowable
  from the web survey already in this document -- it is exactly what
  `inspect` (the porting-framework tool) would need to sample per-title
  once a copy exists, same "not determinable from the web" caveat the
  "Requested titles" section already recorded for data version and clip
  mix.

**Room backgrounds are the real gap in "convert at load," and this
document already has direct evidence for it.** `PrepareSpriteForUseImpl`
converts *sprites* (via the sprite cache); it is not in the room-load
path. `Common/game/roomstruct.cpp:129`'s `FixBitmap()` (called for every
`room->BgImages[i]` at `roomstruct.cpp:142`) only fixes width/height, not
color depth. This document's own "Measured constants" table already has
a directly relevant, previously-recorded finding: **"each `.crm` room
file bakes in its own native color depth at authoring time; changing the
project's `<ColorDepth>` does NOT retroactively convert already-authored
room content"** (2026-09-10 entry, verified via a real Wine `/compile`
against AGSQuest with `<ColorDepth>` flipped). Forcing `game.color_depth`
post-load reproduces exactly that mismatch at runtime instead of at
compile time -- the engine will not crash (room backgrounds are drawn
through `recycle_ddb_bitmap`/`gfxDriver->DrawSprite`, which shares the
same generic cross-depth `ConvertBitmap`/`Blit` machinery
`DrawSpriteWithTransparency` uses, confirmed by reading
`Engine/ac/draw.cpp:2354-2368` and `Engine/gfx/gfx_util.cpp` together),
but a background left at its native 32-bit depth would pay a live
32-to-16 conversion cost on every dirty-background redraw through that
generic fallback, rather than the one-time load-time cost sprites get.
**Option 2, if chosen, needs its own explicit room-background
conversion-at-load hook** (mirroring what `PrepareSpriteForUseImpl`
already does for sprites) to actually be "cheap per frame" as advertised
-- not just the one `game.color_depth` field flip. GUI element
backgrounds (`draw.cpp:2660-2666`'s `repair_alpha_channel` call) were
not traced this session and are a real, named open item for whichever
implementation session takes this on.

**Shared vs. dosags-local split:** entirely dosags-local. Nothing here
touches `.sdl-dos-ports/shared/` -- the DOS backend keeps presenting at
16-bit exactly as it does today; the only new code is an AGS-specific
load-time hook, squarely inside "this game's engine," per this repo's
own `CLAUDE.md` split.

### Comparison

| | Option 1: real 32-bit VESA/LFB path | Option 2: convert to 16-bit at load |
|---|---|---|
| Per-frame bytes at 320x200 | 256,000 (2x today's 16-bit ceiling) | 128,000 (unchanged, today's number) |
| Code surface | Small dosags patch (`ali3dsw.cpp`) + validation of an untested shared/ code path | Small dosags-local load hook + a new room-background conversion step |
| shared/ touched? | Only if the untested 32bpp path has real bugs (expected, not certain) -- hub work, benefits every future port | No |
| Real-hardware validation needed | Yes -- new depth, new byte counts, DOSBox-X first per `dosbox_not_proxy`, then Mach64 | Yes, but lower-risk -- same present path already proven at 16-bit; only the conversion step and fps of the (unchanged) 16-bit present path need checking |
| Per-pixel alpha art (AA edges, glows) | Preserved exactly as authored | Hard binary cutoff at 50% alpha (`ReplaceAlphaWithRGBMask(..., 127)`) -- visible but survivable degradation for edge-AA use; incoherent for deliberate translucency effects |
| Whole-object transparency (fades, `Object.Transparency`) | Unaffected either way | Unaffected either way -- already depth-independent above 8bpp |
| Memory (sprite cache, RAM-constrained 486) | 2x per 32-bit sprite vs. 16-bit | Baseline (converted sprites are the same size as any other 16-bit game's) |
| Resolutions it actually unlocks at 486 tier | All 10 blocked requested titles (all 320x200x32) | Same 10, same resolution -- the depth is what changes, not what's on screen |

### Recommendation (advisory only -- NOT decided; needs operator sign-off)

Given everything read this session, Option 1 looks cheaper on the
*dosags-local* code-surface axis than it first appeared (the engine-wide
32-bit pipeline and the shared backend's mode-enumeration/present-byte
math already exist and are not being built from scratch), but it carries
a real, currently-unquantified real-hardware performance risk (2x bytes/
frame, unmeasured) and a validation obligation in shared/ that Option 2
entirely avoids. Option 2 is cheaper to validate (reuses an
already-proven 16-bit present path) and entirely dosags-local, but
trades away real per-pixel alpha fidelity for an as-yet-unknown subset of
the 10 gated titles, and needs its own new room-background conversion
step to actually deliver the "cheap per frame" property it is chosen
for. Neither option is free, and the alpha-usage question genuinely
cannot be settled from the web survey already in this document -- it
needs `inspect` run against a real copy of at least one representative
32-bit title (Shards of God or If On A Winter's Night, both free, both
already flagged in "Requested titles" as needing only the 32-bit path)
before the alpha-coherence risk in Option 2 can be called anything but
theoretical. **This is a real architectural fork for the operator to
decide, not something to default on** -- left unset here, per this
milestone's own instruction not to schedule or choose unilaterally.

**Operator decision, 2026-09-15: Option 1 -- a real 32-bit VESA/LFB
present path in the shared SDL3-DOS backend.** Not yet implemented.
Before writing code: real-hardware validation of 32bpp VESA modes on
this rig's ATI Mach64 (never exercised at this depth end to end,
per the risk noted above) should land early in the slice, not at the
end, given the shared/ blast radius -- every port pulling a future
subtree bump inherits this change. `inspect` against a real copy of
at least one free 32-bit title (Shards of God or If On A Winter's
Night, both already flagged as needing only this path) is the other
early step, to get a first real read on how much this milestone
actually unblocks.

### Real-hardware results, 2026-09-15

Implementation landed same-day as the operator decision above
(`patches/ags/0075` opens `ali3dsw.cpp`'s `IsModeSupported()`/
`CreateVirtualScreen()` gate for 32-bit; `patches/ags/0076` adds
`DOSAGS_FORCE_COLOR_DEPTH`, a DJGPP-only load-time override used only
for this benchmarking campaign, not a player-facing feature).
Validated on DOSBox-X first (`tests/probes/window-surface-smoke/`,
then a full Shards of God boot-to-title), then real hardware.

**Test games**: two real, free/NYOP 32-bit AGS titles were sourced from
itch.io for this (never guessed URLs -- see each game's own `PIN` file
for the verified source/hash/license read): *Shards of God* (Honza
Vavra/PacoDiago) and *If On A Winter's Night, Four Travelers*
(IOAWN4T). Both kept local-only (never committed -- no per-game
content license offered on either page). IOAWN4T's real-hardware run
was explicitly descoped by the operator: its package (~988MB) exceeds
what this rig's transfer link can move in a reasonable campaign, so it
has DOSBox-X-only mechanism numbers, no real-hardware entry.

**The 8/16/32-bit comparison actually run** (all sound-disabled,
fixed-timestep, `DOSAGS_TAS_AUTO_EXIT_TICK`-driven, per each game's
`manifest.yaml`):

| Game | Depth | Environment | fps_p50 | fps_p95 | tick_rate | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shards of God | 32 (native) | DOSBox-X | 40.00 | 40.38 | 37.85 | mechanism only |
| Shards of God | 16 (forced, patch 0076) | DOSBox-X | 32.69 | 35.24 | 37.62 | mechanism only |
| Shards of God | 32 (native) | **HW-486-66** | **0.05** | **0.05** | 0.32 | **real KPI datum** |
| Trilby's Notes | 8 (native) | **HW-486-66** | **4.99** (avg) | -- | -- | **real KPI datum**, different game/content |
| If On A Winter's Night | 32 (native) | DOSBox-X | see `tests/games/iowna/manifest.yaml` | -- | -- | mechanism only; real HW out of scope |
| If On A Winter's Night | 16 (forced) | DOSBox-X | see manifest | -- | -- | mechanism only; room15 script-error caveat noted in manifest |

This is **not** a strict same-content three-depth real-hardware
comparison -- no real-hardware 16-bit-forced measurement for Shards of
God was taken (not yet attempted; see "40fps push" below), and the
8-bit real datum comes from a different game (Trilby's Notes; no 8-bit
variant of either 32-bit game exists to test directly, and building
one was explicitly narrowed to "for benchmarking only," see git
history around 2026-09-15 for the operator's scope call). Treat the
~100x figure as a real, measured, order-of-magnitude finding about
native 32-bit rendering cost at this content complexity on this
hardware tier -- not as a precise per-depth multiplier.

**Headline finding**: DOSBox-X is mechanism-confirmation only, never a
performance proxy -- this campaign is the most dramatic evidence this
port has produced for that hub-wide rule. DOSBox-X showed native
32-bit only ~18% slower than 16-bit-forced on identical content
(40.00 vs 32.69 `fps_p50`). Real hardware showed native 32-bit at
`fps_p50=0.05` against native-8-bit's 4.99 -- roughly two orders of
magnitude apart, a gap direction and magnitude nothing in the DOSBox-X
numbers hinted at. Anyone tempted to size a 486-tier optimization
target off local emulator numbers alone should read this section
first.

**Real blockers found and fixed while getting this datum** (full
account in `tests/games/shards/manifest.yaml`'s `validated:` entry;
condensed here since it directly informs "40fps push" below):

1. vcctrl `REFUSE_BYTES` (64MB) too low for the ~126MB Shards package
   -- raised to 150MB for this transfer specifically (vcctrl's own
   fix, not a blanket policy change).
2. vcctrl `TRANSFER_TIMEOUT_S` was a flat 180s that never scaled to
   file size -- `SHARDS.AGS`'s real round trip needed ~221-255s. Fixed
   properly by vcctrl (scales with file size), not worked around.
3. `run-rig.sh`'s `wait_for_job_done()` masked a real send-file
   failure as `UNKNOWN` (a `pipefail` bug), turning a fast failure into
   a 30-minute hang. Fixed (dosags commit b60745f).
4. `run-rig.sh` measured the **wrong game** once (a stale
   `NOTES.AGS` sorted before `SHARDS.AGS` in AGS's own
   directory-scan game lookup, since `RUN.BAT` invoked `AGS.EXE` with
   no explicit gamefile argument). Fixed by passing the package name
   explicitly (dosags commit d4082dc) -- a real, general correctness
   gap for any campaign that stages more than one game in the same
   target directory, not specific to this one incident.
5. A real PS/2 hard-hang occurred once mid-campaign (confirmed via
   vcctrl's own `verify-input`, matching `docs/lab/OPEN-FAULTS.md`
   sec. 23's known signature) -- resolved by an operator-authorized
   power-cycle; root cause not identified, filed as open, not chased
   further since a clean retry was the more useful next step.
6. A newly-added `run-rig.sh` safety check (`vc verify-input` after
   the wait, before collecting -- added in direct response to #5,
   commit 7848182) has its own bug: it's called without
   `--as "run-rig-$TAG"`, so it collides with the script's own
   held lock and falsely refuses every time, independent of real
   hardware state. **Fixed in commit 79c88d0** (the `--as` argument
   added to that one call, with a comment citing this incident) -- this
   item read "not yet fixed" until 2026-09-16 although the fix had
   landed alongside it. Unexercised on the rig until the next session's
   first cell completes its collection step.
7. Real-input-mechanics finding, needed to get a clean quit (and
   therefore a real RUNMANIFEST) out of an extraordinarily-low-tick-
   rate game: an instantaneous `mouse click` (press+release) can fall
   entirely between two of the game's own widely-spaced input polls
   and never be observed -- a discrete button *edge* needs to overlap
   an actual poll to register, unlike cursor *position*, which is
   always current whenever the game does poll. `mouse down` held for
   a full poll interval, then `mouse up` (the release edge is what
   AGS's GUI click handling reacted to), reliably registered. This is
   a generally useful technique for any future sub-1-fps real-hardware
   cell, not specific to this game.
8. vcctrl's analog capture (`vcctrl_shot`) got stuck on a stale frame
   during the active 32-bit VESA mode -- cross-verified via
   `vcctrl_camera_shot` (physical webcam), which confirmed the game
   was genuinely responding. Filed by vcctrl as `docs/lab/
   OPEN-FAULTS.md` sec. 28 -- confirmed anomalous, not yet diagnosed.

## 40fps push -- forward plan, opened 2026-09-15

**Context**: the operator's stated goal, once the 8/16/32-bit KPI
comparison above landed, is driving this port's real-hardware fps
toward the 40fps native target (see "Fixed timestep and the fps KPI"
below for why 40 is the right target number). This section is the
concrete starting point for that push, written down before any
optimization work begins so later work has pre-registered numbers to
aim at rather than a vague "make it faster."

**What the KPI campaign actually established**:

- Native 8-bit on the 486 KPI tier (HW-486-66) is the only depth with
  a real-hardware number anywhere close to workable for a 40fps target
  today: Trilby's Notes averages `fps_p50=4.99` -- still ~8x short of
  40, but the right order of magnitude to attack with a normal
  profiling-driven optimization pass (dirty rectangles, reduced
  surface conversions, fixed-point where justified -- see the
  "OPTIMIZING" milestone above).
- Native 32-bit on the same tier (`fps_p50=0.05`) is not a "needs
  optimization" gap to 40fps, it is a ~800x gap. Nothing in this
  port's existing optimization backlog (dirty rectangles, cache
  sizing, etc.) plausibly closes three orders of magnitude on 486-class
  hardware. Treat native 32-bit at this content complexity as
  **out of reach for the 40fps KPI on the 486 tier** until proven
  otherwise by real measurement, not assumption.
- The DOSBox-X-vs-real-hardware divergence measured here (18% vs
  ~100x) means **no future depth/format/path decision for this port
  may be sized off DOSBox-X numbers alone** -- this is now the
  concrete cited precedent for that hub-wide rule, not just a
  restated policy.

**Immediate next steps, in priority order**:

1. **Fix the `run-rig.sh` `verify-input` lock bug** (item 6 above --
   add `--as "run-rig-$TAG"` to the call added in commit 7848182).
   **DONE** -- it landed in commit 79c88d0, the same commit that opened
   this section (this text and item 6 above said "not yet fixed" until
   2026-09-16; the committed script has carried the fix since). Not yet
   exercised on the rig: the first cell of the next rig session
   confirms it by simply completing its collection step.
2. **Get a real-hardware 16-bit-forced Shards of God datum** to make
   the three-depth comparison same-content (today the 8-bit and 32-bit
   real numbers come from two different games). This is the cheapest
   remaining way to sharpen the "roughly 100x" figure into a real
   same-content curve across all three depths, using the same
   `DOSAGS_FORCE_COLOR_DEPTH=16` lever already built and validated
   under DOSBox-X (patch 0076).
3. **Decide the depth-gating question for the 40fps push**: given
   native 32-bit's real cost, does this port (a) hardware-tier-gate
   the native 32-bit path (offer it only on a faster real-hardware
   tier than HW-486-66, once one exists in this port's matrix), (b)
   revisit Option 2 (convert-32-bit-to-16-bit-at-load) specifically
   for the 486 tier now that real numbers exist to size it against
   (Option 2's whole pitch was "same proven 16-bit present path, half

   not just "more bytes to push"). This decision needs operator

4. **Start the native 8-bit optimization pass** (Trilby's Notes,
   4.99 -> closer to 40) in parallel -- it does not depend on the

   already, and is the more tractable of the two live gaps.
5. Once (3) is decided, fold whichever native-32-bit path survives
   into the same optimization-pass discipline as (4), with its own

**Step 2 result, 2026-09-16 (rig session): datum NOT obtained --
real, informative finding instead.** Operator authorized powering the
rig back on for exactly this cell. Boot verified through its full
normal sequence (PicoGUS banner, MSCDEX, `[PGSB] ready`) via screenshot
before touching anything.

A real harness bug surfaced on the first attempt (tag S16FRC1,
`--timeout 300`, matching the DOSBox-X-validated arm's own budget): the
run never returned to a DOS prompt within the wait window, and
`run-rig.sh` REFUSED to collect ("input verification failed... may be
wedged"). Investigation (screenshot, not assumption) showed a clean,
correctly-rendered Shards of God title screen, not a wedge or garbage
frame -- the run-rig.sh poll's own log showed `changing` through ~t+75s
(boot + load + transition into the title room) then `static` from
~t+90s on, consistent with a genuinely-reached, idling title screen
whose loop-counter-driven auto-exit (tick 1000) simply hadn't fired
yet, not a crash. **A second, distinct real bug**: this REFUSED path
left the run's own input lock held (`run-rig.sh` exits before its own
lock-release line), which then blocked a retry's reboot chord even
after one manual release, until released again with the exact matching
`--as` name. **Fixed** (commit 48f3948): the lock release now lives in
the script's existing cleanup trap, firing on every exit path.

With the lock fixed, the original title screen was left running (no
new reboot needed, no sunk progress lost) and observed periodically
via read-only screenshots rather than idle rig-lock time: two shots
~2 minutes apart were byte-size-identical (43561 vs 43572 bytes, mean
brightness 35.888 vs 35.913) -- no visible change, and the total
elapsed real time since the original launch passed ~20 minutes with no
return to a DOS prompt. Rather than continue an open-ended wait, the
rig was powered off cleanly (lock free, `vcctrl_power off` confirmed)
rather than left running an unbounded, unmonitored cell.

**Why this is surprising, source-checked, not assumed:** patch 0076's
own commit message says `DOSAGS_FORCE_COLOR_DEPTH` converts sprites
and room backgrounds to the target depth ONCE, at load time
(`PrepareSpriteForUseImpl`/`load_new_room`'s existing per-load
conversion path, not new per-frame work) -- so 16-bit-forced Shards
should be paying the same PER-FRAME depth-conversion cost as any
natively-16-bit game (i.e., none), not the native-32-bit path's own
cost. If the DOSVESA backend's present "fast path" is gated at <=16bpp
(unconfirmed this session -- see the flip-instrumentation note below),
16-bit-forced should also be eligible for it, unlike native 32-bit.
Under that reasoning, 16-bit-forced "should" perform far closer to
Trilby's Notes' `fps_p50=4.99` than to native 32-bit's `fps_p50=0.05`.
Twenty real minutes without even reaching one full drive window is
inconsistent with that expectation, and is itself the interesting
result: **either the fast-path gate does not actually include this
game/mode the way source review predicted, or some other per-frame
cost scales with something other than bytes-per-pixel** (sprite/object
count, room complexity, an unrelated per-tick cost specific to this
game's own content). Not resolved this session -- named here as the
concrete next question, not guessed at.

**Recommendation for the next rig round** (operator decision, not
defaulted): either (a) budget a single cell at several multiples of
the DOSBox-X-sized timeout (e.g. 30-45 real minutes) and let it run
unattended to get the raw number regardless of how slow, or (b) first
enable `SDL_HINT_DOS_FLIP_INSTR=1` (see "Step 4" investigation below --
already-built, currently-unused per-flip timing instrumentation
inherited from doskutsu) on a short, bounded cell to check whether
16-bit-forced Shards is even taking the fast present path before
spending real rig time on a long unattended wait for a number that a
mis-routed present path would make meaningless anyway.

**Step 2 CLOSED, 2026-09-16: real datum obtained, tag S16FRC5.** Fixed
