## 8-bit optimization pass, DPMI/interrupt investigation: THE GAP IS CLOSED -- Present() is the answer (2026-09-16)

**Operator instruction, following the clean inline-code audit:**
investigate real-mode callback frequency and cost (CWSDPMI's own
real-mode-switch mechanism, keyboard/mouse polling via INT 16h/33h,
anything that makes a BIOS/DOS INT call per tick), and build a
counter of real-mode-callback invocations correlated with the gap
size, even without a precise cost-per-call number, before assuming
it's unmeasurable.

**Confirmed real DPMI activity exists**, by reading source, not
assuming: `sys_evt_process_pending()` (bracketed as `input_poll`) goes
through SDL's own event pump to `DOSVESA_PumpEvents()`
(`vendor/SDL/src/video/dos/SDL_dosevents.c`), which issues
`__dpmi_int(0x33, ...)` (a real protected-to-real-mode DPMI switch) for
mouse polling on every call, unconditionally. A broader source-wide
grep found six DOS-backend files making real-mode switches
(`SDL_sysjoystick.c`, `SDL_dosmouse.c`, `SDL_dosframebuffer.c`,
`SDL_dosevents.c`, `SDL_dosmodes.c`, `SDL_dosvideo.c`) -- the most
promising per-tick candidate: `SDL_dosframebuffer.c`'s `SwitchBank()`
(VESA bank-switch via `__dpmi_int(0x10, ax=0x4F05)` or a fast real-mode
callback), reached from the actual VRAM flush during `Present()`, on
every real render tick.

**Read `render_graphics()` (ac/draw.cpp) fully to check this** and
found something more fundamental: after the `scene_construct`-bracketed
block, it calls `render_to_screen()` -- completely unbracketed by any
prior patch in this whole investigation. `render_to_screen()` calls
`gfxDriver->Render(xoff,yoff,flip)`, which calls `RenderToBackBuffer()`
(already bracketed as `render_backbuffer` since patch 0079) **then
`Present()`** (`ali3dsw.cpp`) -- and `Present()`'s own cost (a format-
converting blit at a fixed `SDL_SCALEMODE_NEAREST`, per that file's own
comment, plus `SDL_UpdateWindowSurface()`, which reaches the DOS
framebuffer driver's flush mechanism) had **never been measured by
anything**, this whole investigation.

**Bracketed as `render_to_screen`** (patch 0085, whole function).
**Also added real-mode-callback visibility per the operator's own
suggestion**: `SDL_DOSVideoIsBankedMode()` (the resolved LFB-vs-banked
flush decision) and a new `SDL_DOSVideoGetBankSwitchCount()` accessor
(SDL patch 0148, exposing an existing-but-unexposed wave-16 counter),
logged to RUNMANIFEST as `video_banked_mode`/`bank_switches` -- this
answers "does this hardware/mode even take the banked path at all"
empirically instead of by inference.

**DOSBox-X sanity (tag not recorded, quick 200-tick check):**
immediately promising -- `render_to_screen` mean_ms=19.36 vs
`render_backbuffer`'s mean_ms=0.02, a ~1000x difference even on a fast
host.

**Real-hardware result, tag TNP85A** (established recipe): `exit_code=0`,
`duration_s=49`, `tick_rate=23.86`. `render_to_screen`: `calls=210
total_ms=25486 mean_ms=121.37` vs `render_backbuffer`'s `total_ms=65`.
**`video_banked_mode=0 bank_switches=0`** -- this hardware/mode uses
the LFB flush path, not banked VESA. **DPMI real-mode bank-switching is
cleanly ruled out as the mechanism** (zero switches occurred all run).

**A real accounting anomaly, investigated rather than glossed over:**
naively summing `render_to_screen`'s whole total into the established
formula gives **43835ms, exceeding `update_game_once_total`'s own
39649ms** -- impossible for a true subset. Root cause, found by
grepping every `render_to_screen()` call site across the engine: it
has MANY callers beyond `render_graphics()`'s own per-tick one --
`ac/screen.cpp`'s fade-transition state machine (a `Draw()`/`RunImpl()`
pair that calls `render_to_screen()` once per fade STEP, driven by its
own `_alpha` accumulator, exercised by this exact game's one-time
room-transition fade at startup -- `Game : (room:1) Transition-in in
room 1` in STDOUT.TXT), plus `global_screen.cpp`, `media/video/video.cpp`,
and `main/engine.cpp`. `render_to_screen`'s own bracket is a
whole-PROCESS accumulator summing every call site, including calls
made during the one-time startup transition (before the 1000-tick
benchmark loop even begins) -- not a pure subset of
`update_game_once_total`'s own per-tick-loop total.

**Fix (patch 0086): isolate the per-tick call site specifically.** A
second bracket, `render_to_screen_pertick`, wraps ONLY the
`render_to_screen()` call inside `render_graphics()` (the one call site
actually reached from `UpdateGameOnce()`'s own per-tick render step),
cleanly comparable against `update_game_once_total` without
cross-call-site contamination. DOSBox-X sanity confirmed the isolation
works as expected: `render_to_screen_pertick` (128 calls) <
`render_to_screen` (161 calls) -- the difference is exactly the
fade-transition calls.

**Real-hardware result, tag TNP86A (the closing cell):** `exit_code=0`,
`duration_s=49`, `tick_rate=23.65` (matches trusted baseline).
`render_to_screen_pertick`: `calls=178 total_ms=21629 mean_ms=121.51`
-- `calls=178` matches `game_tick_outer`'s own 180 almost exactly,
confirming this is genuinely the clean per-tick slice.

**FULL, METHODOLOGICALLY CLEAN ACCOUNTING** (using
`render_to_screen_pertick`, not the contaminated whole-process total):
named phases sum to **40144ms**; `update_game_once_total=40388ms`;
**GAP = 244ms = only 0.6% of update_game_once_total.** 21567ms closed
versus TNP84A's own 21811ms gap (98.9%). **Cumulative: 25807ms of the
ORIGINAL 26051ms gap from the very start of this entire diagnostic
chain is now explained -- 99.1%.**

**Honest conclusion: the gap is effectively closed, and the mechanism
is NOT what the operator's own hypothesis proposed.** DPMI real-mode
switching was a reasonable, well-motivated thing to check (this
project's own track record made it worth investigating properly), and
real DPMI activity genuinely exists in the input-poll path -- but
`video_banked_mode=0`/`bank_switches=0` on both real-hardware cells
this round rules it out specifically as THIS game's dominant per-tick
cost. The actual answer is far more mundane and far more actionable:
**`Present()`'s own CPU-bound cost -- a format-converting scaled blit
plus the window-surface update -- was simply never measured**, and
turns out to be responsible for ~121ms of genuine per-tick work on
this 66MHz 486, roughly 300x `RenderToBackBuffer()`'s own cost. This is
now a real, source-grounded fix candidate for step C of the original
8-bit optimization mandate (`ali3dsw.cpp`'s `Present()`: eliminate or
cheapen the format-conversion/scaling blit, e.g. by matching the back
buffer's pixel format/resolution to what the window surface actually
needs, avoiding the generic per-pixel convert-and-scale path
`SDL_BlitSurfaceScaled` takes today) -- not yet implemented, reported
for operator direction on whether/how to pursue it next.

## 8-bit optimization pass, step C: Present() fast-path fix, ABBA pre-registration (2026-09-16)

**Design, read from source before picking a fix shape, per operator
instruction.** `SDLRendererGraphicsDriver::Present()` (`Engine/gfx/
ali3dsw.cpp`) calls `SDL_BlitSurfaceScaled(blit_src, nullptr,
win_surface, &dst, SDL_SCALEMODE_NEAREST)`. Two questions, both
answered by reading the actual code rather than assuming:

1. **Is a format conversion actually happening?** No. `CreateVirtualScreen()`
   (same file) sets `_vscreenSurface`'s format to `SDL_PIXELFORMAT_INDEX8`
   for an 8-bit game (`vscreen_fmt = (_srcColorDepth == 8) ?
   SDL_PIXELFORMAT_INDEX8 : ...`), and the window surface is ALSO
   `SDL_PIXELFORMAT_INDEX8` -- confirmed independently from a real
   STDOUT.TXT line: "Window surface pixel format:
   SDL_PIXELFORMAT_INDEX8". Source and destination share the same
   format; `SDL_BlitSurfaceScaled` is paying generic per-pixel
   conversion logic it never needs for this case.
2. **Is the scale factor really a fixed, clean integer ratio, not
   assumed from STATUS.md's "AGS auto-scales 2x" line?** Verified from
   a real STDOUT.TXT, not assumed: "Game native resolution: 320 x 240
   (8 bit)" and "Graphics mode set: 640 x 480 (8-bit) fullscreen
   desktop" -- 640/320 = 480/240 = exactly 2, a clean uniform integer
   ratio, on every real-hardware benchmark cell this whole session
   (TN8A1 through TNP86A all used this same default config).

**Fix (patch 0087):** `TryFastIntegerNearestBlit()` -- when source and
destination formats match, the destination fully covers the window
with no offset (no screen-shake, no letterbox/pillarbox border), and
the scale is an exact uniform integer ratio >1, replicate each source
pixel horizontally into a scratch row once per source row, then
`memcpy` that row vertically `scale_y` times. No per-pixel division or
multiply; the vertical replication is a handful of large,
cache-friendly `memcpy` calls instead of generic per-destination-pixel
math. Falls back to the existing, always-correct
`SDL_BlitSurfaceScaled()` for every other case (mismatched formats, a
border/offset, a non-integer or non-uniform scale, or 1x) --
arbitrary window sizes and gfxfilter options are untouched.

**Correctness validation on DOSBox-X, screenshot hash comparison (not
just "compiles and runs"), per operator instruction.** Captured the
SAME rendered frame (the title screen, since this benchmark recipe
injects no input) from the pre-patch binary and the patched binary,
via `run-dosbox.sh --interactive` + `import -window root` against the
private Xvfb display, same mechanism this project's own AGS Quest
title-screen capture used. **Result: byte-for-byte identical**
(`sha256sum` matches exactly: `03de57f79...`; ImageMagick `compare
-metric AE` reports 0 differing pixels). The fast path is pixel-perfect
for this real game's actual render. A full headless 1000-tick DOSBox-X
run also completed cleanly (`exit_code=0`, no crash) after the fix.
Note: DOSBox-X itself shows no measurable speed change from this
patch (`render_to_screen_pertick` mean_ms~=18.8, statistically the
same as pre-patch) -- expected, not a red flag: DOSBox-X presents via
a real X11/Xvfb window, where `SDL_UpdateWindowSurface()`'s own X-server
round-trip dominates that step's cost on a fast host, masking any
change in the blit computation itself. Real hardware's DOS backend
does a much more direct framebuffer update with no such round-trip,
which is exactly why this fix needs a real-hardware measurement, not a
DOSBox-X one, to show its effect -- DOSBox-X's role here is
correctness-only, as it always has been in this project.

**ABBA pre-registration, decided BEFORE collecting any real-hardware
data, per operator instruction:**

- **Design:** A/B/B/A, 4 cells, same established recipe as every prior
  TNP8x/TN8A cell (`DOSAGS_TAS_AUTO_EXIT_TICK=1000`,
  `DOSAGS_FIXED_TIMESTEP=1`, sound_off/`ACSETUP-OFF.CFG`,
  `HW-486-66`). A = the pre-patch-0087 binary (patches through 0086
  only). B = the patch-0087 binary.
- **Primary KPI:** `fps_p50`. **Threshold: an improvement of at least
  1.0 fps_p50 counts as a real win** -- comfortably more than 2x this
  exact game/hardware's own established A-to-A noise floor (0.36
  fps_p50, from the 2026-09-15 S7 campaign's TN8A1/TN8A2 pair), a
  clean, round, easily-defensible bar. Anything at or below the 0.36
  noise floor is noise, not a result. Anything strictly between 0.36
  and 1.0 is ambiguous -- reported honestly as inconclusive, not
  rounded either way.
- **Secondary KPI:** `tick_rate`, compared against the established
  Trilby's Notes baseline (`tick_rate=23.7-23.8`, TN8A1/TN8A2/TNP8x
  series). No separate pass/fail threshold pre-registered for this one
  (its own historical A-to-A spread, 0.06, is too tight relative to
  this fix's plausible effect size to set a meaningful bar the same
  way) -- reported as corroborating context for whatever `fps_p50`
  shows, not a second gate.
- **Invalidity conditions, checked BEFORE trusting any delta** (same
  discipline as the 2026-09-13 S7 ABBA campaign): both A cells must
  share one `binary_sha12`; both B cells must share a DIFFERENT one
  (confirming the right binary actually ran each arm); `env_block_sha`
  and `memory_min_free_kb` must match across all 4 cells (rules out an
  environment/memory-pressure confound); `exit_code=0` and
  `critical_count=0`/`warn_count=0` on every cell; game identity
  reconfirmed from each cell's own STDOUT.TXT ("Game title: 'Trilby's
  Notes'"); `frames_skipped` in the same ballpark as the established
  baseline (roughly 820/1000, not some qualitatively different
  execution shape). Any invalidity condition failing voids that cell's
  own contribution to the comparison, reported plainly rather than
  averaged in.

## 8-bit optimization pass, step C: ABBA result -- A REAL WIN (2026-09-17)

**Caught and fixed a real bug during bring-up, before collecting any
official ABBA data.** A quick real-hardware A/B pair with the FIRST
version of patch 0087 (tags TNP-ABBA-A1/B1, not otherwise recorded)
showed NO measurable improvement: `render_to_screen_pertick`
mean_ms=120.84 (A, baseline) vs 124.19 (B, patched) -- statistically
identical, if anything slightly worse. A one-shot diagnostic (`Debug::
Printf`, temporary, never landed) confirmed the fast path WAS engaging
correctly (`fast=1`, every precondition matched: `src_fmt==dst_fmt`,
`dst.x=0 dst.y=0`, `dst.w=640 dst.h=480` matching the window exactly,
`src.w=320 src.h=240`) -- ruling out "never runs" and pointing at the
loop body itself. Root cause: the horizontal-replication loop called
`std::memcpy()` once per REPLICATED BYTE -- for an 8-bit game, ~640
one-byte `memcpy()` calls per row x 240 rows = ~153600 tiny calls per
frame. A slow DJGPP libc's real per-call overhead for a 1-byte copy
swamped whatever the replication saved. Fixed by special-casing
`bpp==1` (every 8-bit game, this port's only real-hardware-tested
profile) with a direct byte-store loop (`*out++ = v`) -- no per-pixel
function call at all. Squashed into a single, clean patch 0087 before
landing (the broken intermediate version and the diagnostic were never
kept as separate commits) -- correctness re-validated the same way
(byte-for-byte identical screenshot against the pre-patch binary,
`sha256` match, `compare -metric AE` = 0 differing pixels) after the
fix.

**Real hardware, full A/B/B/A, exactly as pre-registered above.**

| TNFIXB1 | 8a2d3a032833 | 86414d38bb21 | 154944 | 0 | 0/0 | 7.27 | 7.69 | 27.84 | 780 |

| TNFIXA2 | 3ff4c2d741e5 | 86414d38bb21 | 154944 | 0 | 0/0 | 4.81 | 5.50 | 23.67 | 822 |

(Tags `ABBAA1`/`ABBAB1` were used for the bring-up pair above and

## 8-bit optimization pass, patch 0089: sub-phase breakdown of the remaining ~74-80ms (2026-09-17)

**Operator instruction: instrument before guessing a second fix, same
discipline that found patch 0087 itself.** Added fine-grained brackets
across every real step in `render_to_screen()`/`Present()`'s own call
chain (patch 0089): `screen_overlay_vsync` (plugin-hook check +
`construct_engine_overlay()` + vsync-set logic, before
`gfxDriver->Render()`), then inside `Present()`:
`present_get_win_surface`, `present_sync_palette`,
`present_flip_handling`, `present_blit`, `present_update_window`. Also
broke `present_blit` down further via manual microsecond accumulation
inside `TryFastIntegerNearestBlit()` (one record per `Present()` call,
not per source row, to avoid per-row RAII overhead across up to 240
rows/call): `fastblit_lock`, `fastblit_hreplicate`, `fastblit_vmemcpy`.

**A real methodological wrinkle, same class as patch 0086's own
finding, handled the same way:** these new brackets sit inside
`Present()`/`render_to_screen()`, which (per patch 0086) has call
sites beyond the per-tick one `render_to_screen_pertick` isolates --
so their raw `calls=`/`total_ms=` cannot be summed directly against
`render_to_screen_pertick`'s own total. Per-call MEANS are the correct
comparison instead (the per-call cost of a fixed-size 320x240
INDEX8->640x480 operation does not depend on which caller triggered
it): summing every sub-phase's own mean gives 82.91ms
(0.07+0.18+0.29+0.01+57.70+24.66), matching `render_to_screen_pertick`'s
own 80.92ms mean within noise -- confirms the breakdown is complete
and consistent, not missing a hidden cost.

**DOSBox-X sanity first**, confirming the mechanism works and produces
sane numbers (not a proportional match to real hardware -- DOSBox-X's
own `SDL_UpdateWindowSurface` cost is dominated by its X11/Xvfb
round-trip, a different bottleneck than real hardware's, as already
established when patch 0087 was validated). Screenshot-hash comparison
against the current baseline (patch 0087's already-validated binary):
byte-for-byte identical, confirming patch 0089's pure instrumentation
changed nothing about the rendered output.

**Real-hardware result, tag TNP89A** (established recipe):
`exit_code=0`, `tick_rate=26.74`. Full breakdown (mean_ms, 248 calls):

| sub-phase | mean_ms |
|---|---|
| `fastblit_hreplicate` | **45.86** (dominant) |
| `present_update_window` | 24.66 |
| `fastblit_vmemcpy` | 9.74 |
| `present_sync_palette` | 0.29 |
| `present_get_win_surface` | 0.18 |
| `screen_overlay_vsync` | 0.07 |
| `present_flip_handling` | 0.01 (confirms flip is inactive, as expected -- verified not assumed) |
| `fastblit_lock` | 0.01 |

**`fastblit_hreplicate` -- patch 0087's OWN horizontal-replication
loop -- is still the single largest remaining cost**, even after
removing the per-byte `memcpy()` call. Reading the loop again with
this data in hand: for `bpp==1`, `scale_x==2` (the only case this port
ever exercises in practice), the loop is `for (sx...) { v = src[sx];
for (r=0; r<scale_x; r++) *out++ = v; }` -- a nested loop where the
INNER loop's own overhead (increment, compare, branch) is paid twice
per source pixel for what is, in the by-far-most-common case, exactly
two identical byte writes. `present_update_window` (24.66ms,
`SDL_UpdateWindowSurface` itself) is real and substantial -- likely
the necessary system-RAM-to-VRAM copy for this LFB-backed surface (a
`SDL_GetWindowSurface()`-returned surface is system memory; getting it
onto the display requires copying it into video memory somewhere) --
flagged as a separate, not-yet-investigated candidate, not addressed
this round; today's fix targets `fastblit_hreplicate` specifically,
the clear largest and most directly fixable cost.

**Fix design (patch 0090):** special-case `scale_x==2` (confirmed the
only real case) with a branch-free 16-bit word store: replicate the
8-bit source value into both bytes of a `Uint16` via a multiply
(`v * 0x0101`, no branch) and write it in ONE store instead of two
separate byte stores in a loop -- half the store operations, and the
inner `for r` loop is eliminated entirely for this case. Falls back to
the existing generic per-byte loop for any other integer scale (kept
correct, just not specially fast).

**Correctness re-validated the same way as every prior round:**
byte-for-byte identical screenshot hash against the same original
baseline capture. A full headless DOSBox-X run also completed cleanly
(`exit_code=0`).

**Bring-up cell, tag TNP90A (not an official ABBA -- confirms the fix
works before designing a proper pre-registered comparison, same
discipline as patch 0087's own bring-up):** `exit_code=0`,
`fps_p50=8.57`, `tick_rate=31.50` (up from patch-0089-only's 26.74).
`fastblit_hreplicate` mean_ms=21.96 -- down from 45.86, **a real ~52%
reduction**, matching the fix's own design intent almost exactly (half
the store operations). `render_to_screen_pertick` mean_ms=56.43 --
down from ~74-80ms.

## 8-bit optimization pass, patch 0091: skip Present() when unchanged -- a massive win (2026-09-17)

**Operator instruction: investigate `SDL_UpdateWindowSurface`'s
~22-25ms/call cost properly before assuming it's an unfixable hardware
bandwidth limit.** Read the actual mechanism, source-grounded, before
concluding anything:

- **`SDL_UpdateWindowSurface()` (SDL_video.c) always copies the FULL
  window.** It is a thin wrapper: `SDL_UpdateWindowSurfaceRects(window,
  &full_rect, 1)` with one rect spanning the entire window -- confirmed
  by reading the function directly, not assumed from its name.
- **The DOS backend's LFB path already has dirty-rect dispatch logic**
  (`SDL_dosframebuffer.c`'s `DOSVESA_UpdateWindowFramebuffer`, from an
  earlier DOSKUTSU wave, patch 0033/"wave 17.4"): when given a rect
  list that does NOT cover the full framebuffer, it does a per-rect,
  per-row `SDL_memcpy` (the `nearptr path (LFB fallback)` branch,
  since `video_banked_mode=0` on this rig, confirmed earlier this
  session). But `_dos_port_is_full_fb_rect_list()` always sees the
  single full-window rect AGS's `SDL_UpdateWindowSurface()` call
  provides, so it always takes the OTHER branch: one
  `SDL_memcpy(fb_state.vram_ptr, fb_state.pixels, fb_state.fb_size)` --
  **307200 bytes moved every single call, regardless of whether
  anything actually changed.** The dirty-rect machinery exists and has
  since an earlier DOSKUTSU wave, but AGS's own present path never
  feeds it anything but "update everything."
- This is exactly the class of gap flagged all the way back in the
  first round of this whole investigation (`RenderToBackBuffer()` has
  no dirty-rect tracking) but never revisited once script/blit costs
  turned out to dominate instead.

**Fix design (patch 0091):** building full sub-window dirty-rect
tracking (making AGS's own renderer track which regions actually
changed and feed a real partial rect list all the way down) is a much
larger change. The simpler, still-real win: cache the last-presented
frame's raw pixel bytes and **skip the blit and
`SDL_UpdateWindowSurface()` entirely** when the new frame is
byte-identical to the cached one, the palette did not change
(`SyncPaletteIfNeeded()` now returns whether it actually changed
anything, instead of the caller having no way to know), and
xoff/yoff/flip match. Restricted to the case with no flip and no
border/offset (dst fills the whole window) -- anything else always
falls through to the normal path and invalidates the cache, so
arbitrary window configurations remain correct, just without this
specific speedup.

**DOSBox-X sanity first**, and the result was immediately striking:
`present_skip_unchanged` fired on **991 of 1014 present calls (97.7%)**
-- confirming this game/scene (room 1, no player input injected in
this TAS-style benchmark) is genuinely near-static almost the entire
run. `present_update_window` dropped from ~248-264 calls to just 23.
Screenshot-hash comparison against the SAME original baseline capture
this whole investigation has used throughout: byte-for-byte identical
-- the skip logic does not change what gets displayed, only how often
a genuinely-unchanged frame gets re-pushed. A full headless run also
completed cleanly (`exit_code=0`).

**Real-hardware result, tag TNP91A** (established recipe): `exit_code=0`,
`duration_s=37` (down from 43-49), **`fps_p50=22.12`** (up from
8.57 -- more than DOUBLE), `tick_rate=33.47` (up from ~31.7-32.0).
`present_skip_unchanged`: `calls=546` of `present_dirty_check`'s
`569` -- **95.9% skip rate on real hardware**, confirming the DOSBox-X
finding held up almost exactly. `present_update_window` calls=23 (down
from ~248-264). `render_to_screen_pertick` mean_ms=16.25 -- down from
~74-80ms before patch 0087, ~56ms after patch 0090.

**A real secondary finding, not chased this round:** the comparison
itself (`present_dirty_check`) costs mean_ms=14.69/call -- higher than
a rough bandwidth estimate for a 76800-byte `memcmp` would suggest
(~4-5ms at a naive few-cycles-per-byte rate), possibly a
non-word-optimized libc `memcmp` on this DJGPP target. Still vastly
cheaper than the ~34-52ms it replaces for the 546 skipped calls this
run, so the net win is enormous regardless -- flagged as a legitimate
further target for a future round, not pursued now (this round's own
scope was the skip mechanism itself).

**Fresh ABBA pre-registration, against the CURRENT baseline (patch
0090's own already-validated result), decided BEFORE collecting any

**Invalidity conditions -- one real, explained difference, otherwise
clean.** `binary_sha12` matches within each pair and differs between
them (A: `7762d0ac915e`, the SAME binary the prior ABBA validated as
B; B: `2baf55f31095`). `env_block_sha` identical across all 4 cells.
`exit_code=0`/`critical_count=0`/`warn_count=0` throughout.
`audio_vital_status=NA` throughout. **`memory_min_free_kb` differs
between A (154944) and B (154880) by exactly 64KB -- but is IDENTICAL
within each binary's own pair** (154944/154944 for A1/A2,
154880/154880 for B1/B2), confirming this is a real, deterministic
property of patch 0091's own code (the new `_lastPresentedPixels`
cache buffer, a persistent ~76800-byte allocation holding the last
presented frame), not environmental noise or an uncontrolled
confound. This is expected and correct for an A/B comparing two
genuinely different binaries -- the invalidity check that matters
(consistency WITHIN each pair) passes cleanly; a diff ACROSS the pair
is exactly what a real code change that allocates new persistent state
should produce. `frames_skipped` dropped from ~770-775 (A) to
~469-474 (B) -- fewer catch-up ticks needed now that real-render ticks
are dramatically cheaper, a real and expected consequence of the fix
working, not an anomaly (same class of observation as patch 0087's own

**Result:**

- **fps_p50: A avg = 8.570 (identical both times: 8.57, 8.57). B avg =
  21.045 (21.90, 20.19). DELTA = +12.475.** A-to-A spread: 0.00.
  B-to-B spread: 1.71 -- wider than prior rounds' own 0.31-0.41, likely
  because the skip mechanism's own hit rate depends on exactly how
  many real content changes occur in a given run (idle-animation/event
  timing can shift by a tick or two between otherwise-identical runs),
  giving it more inherent run-to-run variance than a smooth per-tick
  cost would have. **+12.475 clears the pre-registered >=1.0 threshold
  by an overwhelming margin -- 34.7x the historical 0.36 noise floor,
  and still ~7.3x this round's own (wider) B-to-B spread.** This is
  unambiguously a real, massive win, not a close call.
- **tick_rate: A avg = 31.70 (79.2% of the 40Hz target), B avg = 33.72
  (84.3% of target). Delta = +2.02.** Notably smaller, proportionally,
  than the `fps_p50` jump -- expected: `tick_rate` measures ALL 1000
  logic ticks (catch-up included), gated by whatever per-logic-tick
  costs remain untouched by this fix (script VM, event dispatch,
  etc.), while `fps_p50` measures the actual frame-presentation rate,
  which is exactly what patch 0091 targeted and dramatically cheapened.

**Honest conclusion: the largest single win of this entire
optimization pass, and a genuine confirmation of the operator's own
instinct not to assume a hardware ceiling without checking.** The
~22-25ms/call `SDL_UpdateWindowSurface` cost was not a bandwidth limit
at all -- it was pure, eliminable redundant work (copying an unchanged
307200-byte frame on 95-98% of present calls, for a game/scene that
turns out to be genuinely near-static across almost this entire
benchmark window). Trilby's Notes is now at 84.3% of the 40Hz target
(up from 59.2% at the start of step C, through 69.5% after patch 0087
and 79.7% after patch 0090). `present_dirty_check`'s own cost
(~14.69ms/call, flagged in the bring-up round) remains the next
identified candidate, along with whatever now dominates the
still-uncaptured tick-level budget outside `render_to_screen_pertick`
-- reported for operator direction on whether to continue this pass
or treat it as complete.

## 8-bit optimization pass, patch 0092: closing round -- word-sized frame comparison (2026-09-17)

**Operator instruction: optimize `present_dirty_check`'s own
~14.7ms/call cost, closing round for this pass regardless of outcome.
Same discipline -- read the actual comparison code first, don't assume
it needs a specific fix shape.**

**Read the actual code, not assumed:** patch 0091's unchanged-frame
check called `std::memcmp()`. Rather than assume it was slow or fast,
extracted and disassembled DJGPP's own `memcmp.o` from `libc.a`
directly (`i586-pc-msdosdjgpp-objdump -d`). Confirmed: a genuinely
naive byte-at-a-time loop -- load byte, load byte, compare, branch,
increment both pointers, decrement counter, loop. No `REP CMPSB`, no
word-at-a-time widening, no SIMD. ~8 instructions per byte is
consistent with TNP91A's own measured ~14.69ms for a 76800-byte
compare (roughly 12 cycles/byte on a 66MHz 486).

**Fix (patch 0092):** `FramesEqualFast()` compares in 32-bit words
instead of bytes -- a quarter as many loop iterations for the same
byte count, with a byte-wise tail loop for any remainder (the byte
count here, 320x240 at 1bpp, is already a multiple of 4, but the
function handles the general case correctly regardless). This is NOT
a hash/checksum shortcut or any kind of approximation -- a `Uint32` is
equal iff all 4 of its constituent bytes are equal, so word comparison
is semantically IDENTICAL to a byte-for-byte compare and cannot
produce a false "unchanged" the way a hash collision could. x86
tolerates unaligned reads (never a correctness issue, only a possible
speed one), so no alignment precondition was required.

**Correctness verified before touching the real engine, per the
operator's own explicit warning that a false "unchanged" would be a
real rendering bug:** wrote a standalone host-side test suite
(`g++ -O2`, not DJGPP -- the function is portable C++) covering
identical-content buffers at multiple lengths, a difference injected
at EVERY single byte position (including the non-word-aligned tail)
across multiple lengths, and 5000 random-fuzz iterations cross-checked
directly against libc's own `memcmp`. All passed before this landed in
the engine.

**DOSBox-X sanity, and a strong correctness signal beyond the byte
suite:** `present_skip_unchanged` (991) and `present_update_window`
(23) calls -- EXACTLY the same counts as patch 0091's own DOSBox-X run
-- confirming the new word-based check agrees with the old memcmp-based
one on every single call in this run, not just in isolated unit tests.
`present_dirty_check` mean_ms dropped from 2.67 to 0.60 (DOSBox-X).
Screenshot-hash comparison against the SAME original baseline this
whole investigation has used: byte-for-byte identical. A full headless
run completed cleanly.

**ABBA threshold, reasoned from this project's own established noise
floor rather than reusing the prior >=1.0 bar blindly, per operator
instruction:** the historical `fps_p50` B-to-B spreads across this
pass's three prior ABBAs are 0.35 (patch 0087), 0.31 (patch 0090), and
**1.71 (patch 0091)** -- that last one is the most relevant reference
here, since patch 0092 does not change WHICH frames get skipped
(confirmed identical skip/update counts above), only the COST of
deciding -- meaning the SAME skip-rate-driven run-to-run variance that
produced patch 0091's own 1.71 spread should carry forward largely
unchanged into this comparison too. A threshold of 1.0 (the prior bar)
would sit BELOW that most-relevant recent noise observation, unable to
reliably distinguish a real effect. **Threshold: an improvement of at
least 3.0
fps_p50 counts as a real win for this specific round** -- comfortably
above the 1.71 reference spread, while still achievable: 
`present_dirty_check` fired 569 times in TNP91A, and if each call
saves roughly the DOSBox-X-observed ~4x reduction (call it ~10ms/call
on real hardware, pessimistically), that is a plausible ~5.7 seconds
of raw processing time saved across the whole run -- a real, if
smaller, magnitude than patches 0087/0090/0091's own fixes. Anything
positive but below 3.0 is reported as real-but-statistically-ambiguous
against this round's own established variance, not rounded up to a
win.

- **Design:** A/B/B/A, 4 cells. A = the patch-0091 binary
  (`sha12=2baf55f31095`, the SAME binary the prior ABBA validated as
  B, reused not rebuilt). B = the patch-0092 binary.
- **Secondary KPI:** `tick_rate`, compared against the CURRENT
  baseline (patch-0091's own B average, 33.72 -- 84.3% of the 40Hz
  target).
- **Invalidity conditions:** same list as every prior round in this
  pass -- matching `binary_sha12` within each pair and differing
  between them, matching `env_block_sha` across all 4 cells,
  `exit_code=0`/`critical_count=0`/`warn_count=0` throughout, game
  identity reconfirmed, `frames_skipped` in a consistent ballpark.
  `memory_min_free_kb` is expected to match within each pair but MAY
  differ slightly between A and B (same class of real, explained
  difference as patch 0091's own ABBA, if patch 0092 adds any new
  static state -- it does not add a persistent buffer, so no
  difference is actually expected here, but this is noted in advance
  rather than treated as a surprise if it appears). Fresh,
  never-before-used tags for every cell.

## 8-bit optimization pass, patch 0092: ABBA result -- another massive win, closing this pass (2026-09-17)

**Real hardware, full A/B/B/A, exactly as pre-registered above.**

| cell | binary_sha12 | env_block_sha | mem_min_free_kb | exit_code | critical/warn | fps_p50 | fps_p95 | tick_rate | frames_skipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TNP4A1 | 2baf55f31095 | 86414d38bb21 | 154880 | 0 | 0/0 | 21.90 | -- | 33.72 | 464 |
| TNP4B1 | 123d6d53a911 | 86414d38bb21 | 154880 | 0 | 0/0 | 34.62 | -- | 33.77 | 166 |
| TNP4B2 | 123d6d53a911 | 86414d38bb21 | 154880 | 0 | 0/0 | 34.62 | -- | 33.78 | 152 |
| TNP4A2 | 2baf55f31095 | 86414d38bb21 | 154880 | 0 | 0/0 | 22.12 | 23.08 | 33.72 | 474 |

**Invalidity conditions, all clean, including the one predicted in
advance:** `binary_sha12` matches within each pair and differs between
them. `env_block_sha` identical across all 4 cells.
**`memory_min_free_kb` is IDENTICAL across all 4 cells (154880)** --
confirming the pre-registration's own prediction that patch 0092 (no
new persistent buffer, just a different comparison algorithm) would
not reproduce patch 0091's own A/B memory difference. `exit_code=0`/
`critical_count=0`/`warn_count=0` throughout. `audio_vital_status=NA`
throughout. `frames_skipped` dropped further, from ~464-474 (A) to
~152-166 (B) -- far fewer catch-up ticks needed now that the dirty
check itself is cheap, letting more real-render ticks succeed without
falling behind, the same class of expected consequence as every prior
round's own drop.

**Result:**

- **fps_p50: A avg = 22.010 (21.90, 22.12). B avg = 34.620 (34.62,
  34.62 -- identical). DELTA = +12.610.** A-to-A spread: 0.22. B-to-B
  spread: 0.00. **+12.610 clears the pre-registered >=3.0 threshold by
  more than 4x -- far larger than the conservative estimate behind
  that threshold predicted, and essentially tied with patch 0091's own
  +12.475 as the largest single win of this whole optimization pass.**
- **tick_rate: A avg = 33.72, B avg = 33.78. Delta = +0.06 -- flat.**
  This is the clearest confirmation yet that `tick_rate` and `fps_p50`
  are measuring genuinely different things at this point in the
  investigation: `tick_rate` (all 1000 logic ticks, catch-up included)
  was already close to saturated near whatever it's currently gated by
  (script VM, event dispatch, and the rest of the still-unoptimized
  per-tick budget), while `fps_p50` (real frame-presentation rate) was
  the metric patches 0091/0092 directly targeted, and it responded
  enormously. 84.3%/84.4% of the 40Hz target on `tick_rate` -- both
  arms essentially the same, as expected.

**Why the conservative pre-registered threshold undershot the real
effect so much, worth understanding rather than just noting:**
`present_dirty_check` fired on every "clean case" present call (real
update or skip alike) -- 569 of 1000 ticks in TNP91A -- and cutting
its own cost by ~4x freed up enough total per-tick CPU time that the
fixed-timestep engine could sustain dramatically MORE real-render
ticks per second before falling behind and resorting to a catch-up
tick, which is exactly what `frames_skipped`'s own halving-and-more
(464->166, roughly 2.8x fewer) shows directly. The threshold's own
back-of-envelope math (per-call savings x call count = total time
saved) correctly estimated the RAW time savings but did not account
for this feedback loop with the catch-up mechanism amplifying that
savings into a much larger real-render-rate gain -- a useful
methodological note for any future round in this same fixed-timestep
architecture: a per-call cost's real fps impact is not simply
proportional to the raw milliseconds saved once the catch-up
mechanism is actively compensating for a still-behind-target tick
rate.

**Closing summary for the 40fps push / 8-bit optimization pass, per
operator instruction that this is the intended closing round:**

| stage | fps_p50 | tick_rate | % of 40Hz target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pre-step-C baseline (patch 0087's own A) | 5.015 | 23.69 | 59.2% |
| After patch 0087 (fast integer blit) | 7.445 | 27.78 | 69.5% |
| After patch 0090 (branch-free word-store) | 8.415 | 31.88 | 79.7% |
| After patch 0091 (skip when unchanged) | 21.045 | 33.72 | 84.3% |
| **After patch 0092 (word-sized comparison)** | **34.62** | **33.78** | **84.4%** |

Trilby's Notes went from `fps_p50=5.015` to `fps_p50=34.62` across this
whole optimization pass -- **a 6.9x improvement**, achieved entirely
through source-grounded, instrument-then-fix, correctness-verified-
before-performance-claimed rounds, each validated by a real,
pre-registered ABBA on real hardware. `tick_rate` itself plateaued
around 84% of the 40Hz target once `fps_p50` caught up to what the
per-logic-tick budget (script VM, event dispatch, and everything else
outside `render_to_screen_pertick`) can currently sustain -- that
remaining ~16% gap is a different, not-yet-investigated part of the
per-tick cost, and a legitimate target for a future session, not
pursued further in this one.

**P0 item 1 -- anchor verdict (source-verified 2026-09-17, not
inferred from data):** `get_runtime_ms()` is `Clock::now() -
GameTimer.StartTime`; `StartTime` is set by `set_runtime_start()`,
called from `start_game()` (`main/game_start.cpp:77`). That call sits
AFTER `initialize_start_and_play_game()` logs "Engine initialization
complete" and BEFORE `RunScriptFunctionInModules("game_start")`,
`load_new_room()`, and `first_room_initialization()`; the first
`GameTick()` comes after all of those, from `RunGameUntilAborted()`.
`tick_rate` (`quit.cpp`) is `get_loop_counter()` / that runtime.

- **Finding 1's retraction stands, and source agrees with it on the
  point that matters:** engine init is NOT in the denominator.
  `total_to_first_frame_ms` was never subtractable from it. The
  "34.43" figure is not a real quantity.
- **Where source refines the wording above ("load time is NOT in the
  denominator") -- stated plainly rather than deferred to:** *part* of
  startup IS in it. `first_room_load_ms` is bracketed from
  `load_new_room()`'s entry (`ac/room.cpp`) to the `kRoomEvent_AfterFadein`
  event in `process_event()` (`ac/event.cpp`), and that event fires
  INSIDE tick 1's `processallevents()`. So it straddles the loop
  boundary, and all of it is post-anchor.
  ~~TNP4B2's own numbers close on this: runtime 29603 ms minus
  `game_tick_outer` 28475 ms leaves 1128 ms outside any `GameTick()`.~~
  **CORRECTED the same day, by the yardstick's own first rig cell
  (TNY94A) -- my arithmetic there was invalid, and so is the "~96% of
  runtime" argument in finding 1 above, for the same reason:**
  `game_tick_outer`, `update_game_once_total`, and
  `process_events_dispatch` are INCLUSIVE brackets, and tick 1's
  blocking fade-in RE-ENTERS the loop (nested `GameTick()`s via
  `GameLoopUntilEvent()`), so their totals double-count nested time
  and can exceed the wall span they cover. Patch 0093's exclusive
  (self-time) accounting measures it directly: **preloop 3130 ms
  (start_game() -> first tick: the placeholder room's fade-OUT, the
  `game_start` script, and the room load) + loop 26507 ms + ~200 ms
  shutdown = the 29.83 s runtime.** The source-verified anchor position
  is unaffected -- that was read, not derived -- but the DATA argument
  for it was weaker than it looked: the loop is 89% of the runtime,
  not 96%, and 10.5% of `tick_rate`'s denominator is pre-loop startup.
- **The tick-1 ~2.6 s stall is therefore identified (P1 item 4,
  answered early): it is the room's blocking fade-in transition.**
  `render_to_screen` fired 881 times against `render_to_screen_pertick`'s

  (8103 - 6295), i.e. the fade state machine's own `Draw()` loop
  (`ac/screen.cpp`), each step also paced by a frame wait (33 x ~25 ms
  = ~825 ms). 1808 + 825 = 2633 ms against the measured 2605 ms

  transition, not a defect -- correctly excluded from a steady-state
  figure and reported separately, which is exactly P0 item 3's job.
- **Consequence worth stating before P1 starts -- MEASURED, replacing
  my hand estimate of ~38.8 (which used the double-counting inclusive

**P1 item 1 -- the probe: result (HW-486-66, 2026-09-17).**
`tests/harness/results/clock-probe/clkprobe.cpp`, a synthetic DJGPP
program in the style of the instrumentation-overhead probe, run on the
rig through the new `tests/harness/run-probe-rig.sh` (a staged-batch
bare-exe runner -- the last probe was hand-driven and lost its working
directory to vcctrl's transfer reboots). It `#include`s the engine's own
`util/time_util.h`, so item (a) is the exact `Clock` type the engine
uses. Every loop is bounded by 10,000 iterations OR a 6 s budget.

Mechanism, read before measuring (disassembled `libc.a`, same method as
the `memcmp` check): this libstdc++ has `_GLIBCXX_USE_CLOCK_MONOTONIC`
undefined and `_GLIBCXX_USE_GETTIMEOFDAY` defined, so
`steady_clock::now()` is `gettimeofday()`; DJGPP's `gettimeofday()`
references `__dpmi_int` TWICE (DOS get-date + get-time) plus `mktime`
and `localtime`. `usleep()` spins on `clock()` with `__dpmi_yield`.

| primitive | per call, rig | note |
|---|---|---|
| (c) `uclock()` -- control | **4.9 us** | |
| (a) engine `Clock::now()` | **1324.6 us** | 272x `uclock()` |
| -- `gettimeofday()` | 1318.8 us | `Clock::now()` IS this, to within 0.5% |
| -- one `__dpmi_int(0x21, AH=2Ch)` | 171.2 us | x2 per `gettimeofday()` = ~342 us |
| -- `mktime()` | 723.7 us | the LARGEST component -- a calendar conversion, not a mode switch |
| (b) `__dpmi_int(0x33, AX=3)` mouse poll | **81.9 us** | |
| (d) `sleep_for(0)` | 0.4 us | libstdc++ short-circuits a zero duration |
| (d) `__dpmi_yield()` | 122.6 us | |
| (d) `sleep_for(1 ms)` / `(10 ms)` / `(25 ms)` | **54.9 / 54.8 / 54.8 ms** | ANY positive sleep rounds up to a whole BIOS tick |
| `Clock` resolution | **55 ms steps** | 36 steps in 2 s, min 50 ms |

Calls per 1000 idle logic ticks, counted from source, against TNP4B2's
own brackets (848 outer/render iterations in that run):

| call site | lands in | calls | x per-call = predicted | measured | explained |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `game_loop_update_fps()` + `dos_fps_sample_tick()` + `dos_memory_sample_tick()` -- one `Clock::now()` each, every tick | `end_of_tick` | 2997 | 3970 ms | 4106 ms | **96.7%** |
| `dos_run_tick_fixed()`'s `now_ns` | `game_tick_outer` minus `update_game_once_total` | 848 | 1123 ms | 1193 ms | **94%** |
| `WaitForNextFrame()`'s `now` | `wait_next_frame` beyond its requested sleeps | 880 | 1166 ms | 1428 ms | **82%** (93% adding its `audio_core_entry_poll()`) |
| **all `Clock::now()`** | | **4725** | **6259 ms = 6.3 ms/tick** | | **~28% of the ~22 ms/tick** |
| `__dpmi_int(0x33)`: one per `SDL_PumpEvents()`, and the idle tick pumps THREE times -- `UpdateGameOnce()`'s `input_poll`, `Mouse::Poll()` (via `ags_domouse()`), `GameUpdateCheckControls()` | `input_poll` + `input_handling` | 3001 | 246 ms = 0.25 ms/tick | 1518 ms | **16%** |

**Verdict -- the hypothesis is half right, reported as such:**

- **`Clock::now()`: CONFIRMED, and sharper than proposed.** It costs
  1.32 ms and the constant-cost brackets it was suspected in close on it
  to 94-97%. `end_of_tick`'s suspiciously constant 4.11 ms is exactly
  three clock reads. Uncomfortable detail worth stating: TWO of those
  three are this port's OWN samplers (`dos_fps_sample_tick`,
  `dos_memory_sample_tick`), each reading the clock every tick only to
  self-gate to once a second -- ~2.6 ms/tick of instrumentation overhead
  we added ourselves. The dominant cost inside is `mktime()` (724 us),
  not the real-mode switches (342 us): the "DPMI switch" framing was
  the wrong half of why it is slow.
- **The mouse poll: a CLEAN RULE-OUT as a significant cost.** 82 us,
  0.25 ms/tick even at three polls per tick -- 1.1% of the idle
  overhead, and only 16% of the input brackets it sits in. A pump costs
  ~0.47-0.53 ms and the DPMI call is 0.08 of it; the rest is SDL's own
  event machinery. Polling once per rendered frame instead of per tick
  (P1 item 2's second half) would save ~0.16 ms/tick. Not worth its own
  slice; the three-pumps-per-tick redundancy is the bigger lever there.
- **Not explained by this probe, and still P1 item 3's job:**
  `present_dirty_check` (5.5 ms/tick -- a 76,800-byte compare, memory
  work), `process_events_dispatch`'s 3.4 ms/tick of zero-work overhead,
  `rep_exec_wrapper` (3.3 ms/tick), `scene_construct` (2.8 ms/tick).
  Source shows no clock read or pump on any of those paths (`Clock`,
  `FastClock`, `time()` call sites all enumerated; `IsIgnoringInput()`'s
  clock read only fires on a real input event; `ccInstance::Run()`'s
  `FastClock::now()` is not reached -- `rep_exec_vm` totals 2 ms). "A
  shared cause" covers ~6.3 of the ~22 ms, not all of it.
  **[RETRACTED 2026-09-17 -- this was MY claim and it was wrong.
  `ccInstance::Run()`'s `FastClock::now()` IS reached, on every script
  function run; I argued it away from `rep_exec_vm` "totalling 2 ms",
  which was the unit bug (really ~2 s). So `rep_exec_wrapper`'s
  1.63 ms/call is one 1.32 ms `gettimeofday()` plus real script time,
  and part of `process_events_dispatch` is the same. The clock's share
  of the idle overhead was ~9 ms/tick, not 6.3. Fixed by folding
  `FastClock = Clock` into patch 0096.]**

**Two findings the probe surfaced that were not in the hypothesis, both
of which constrain P1 item 2's design:**

1. **The engine's clock has 55 ms resolution.** `dos_run_tick_fixed()`
   derives `expected_ticks` from it and `WaitForNextFrame()` schedules
   25 ms periods off it, so owed ticks arrive ~2.2 at a time per clock
   step rather than evenly. The run-average tick rate still comes out
   right (the accumulators are exact), but tick and frame CADENCE is
   quantized to 18.2 Hz steps. A `uclock()`-backed clock (0.84 us)
   fixes this as well as the cost -- a correctness-of-pacing argument
   for P1 item 2, independent of the speed one.
2. **Any positive `sleep_for` costs up to a whole 55 ms BIOS tick.** The
   pacer is currently harmless only BY ACCIDENT: the coarse clock makes
   it believe it is behind nearly always, so it rarely sleeps (56 sleeps
   in TNP4B2) and the loop free-runs. Give it a precise clock and it
   will correctly see it is ahead and sleep EVERY frame -- and each of
   those sleeps rounds up to the next 18.2 Hz boundary, capping rendered
   frames at ~18 fps while the catch-up loop holds ticks at 40. **A
   uclock-backed `Clock` on its own would make Gate 1's fps half
   unreachable.** P1 item 2 must replace the pacing wait in the same
   slice (a `uclock()`-deadline wait; `__dpmi_yield()` at 123 us is a
   fine enough grain to yield with), not as a follow-up.

**Does the 0087/0090 fast blit engage at bpp==2? NO -- and the reason

**P1 item 2 -- DESIGN, written before coding (2026-09-17): a
uclock-backed engine clock AND the pacing wait, one slice.**

*What `uclock()` really is, read from `libc.a`'s own `uclock.o`
(disassembled -- this toolchain ships no libc source or info pages):*

- Value = `(BIOS tick at 0040:006C << 16) | (65535 - PIT ch0 counter)`,
  minus a base captured on the first call; 1,193,180 units/s.
- **First call reprograms PIT channel 0** (`out 43h,34h`; reload FFFFh):
  mode 2 instead of the BIOS's mode 3, because mode 3 counts down by
  two. Side effect: a BIOS tick becomes 65535 counts instead of 65536
  (15 ppm, ~1.3 s/day) while `uclock` still accounts it as 65536.
  Negligible, and NOT new -- every tickstats bracket since patch 0079
  already calls `uclock()`, so the PIT has been in mode 2 on every cell
  this whole investigation.
- **First call also BLOCKS until the BIOS tick changes** (up to 55 ms,
  spinning on `__dpmi_yield`) to align to a tick edge. Already paid at
  startup today (`main_init()` calls `uclock()`).
- **Midnight: handled, one rollover per call pair.** If the BIOS tick
  read is below the previous one it subtracts exactly `1800B0h << 16`
  (one day of ticks) from its base. The engine calls it many times a
  second, so two missed midnights cannot happen.
- **It CAN step backwards, by ~55 ms -- a real hole, not a
  theoretical one.** Each read is tick / latch counter / tick-again,
  retried if the tick moved. Not covered: the counter has reloaded but
  IRQ0 has not been serviced yet, so BOTH tick reads are stale and the
  value lands one whole tick early. This project has already recorded
  it (`clamped_neg` in tickstats; the negative `gui_poll` total that
  prompted patch 0082's clamp). The error is always backward, always
  ~one tick, and self-heals on the next read after the ISR runs.
- It depends on IRQ0 actually being serviced. Mask interrupts for >55 ms
  and it silently loses a tick and runs slow -- exactly the hub's
  busy-wait precedent. Hence the cross-check below.

*The clock (`util/time_util.h`, `#ifdef __DJGPP__` only; every other
platform keeps upstream's alias byte-for-byte):* `DosUclockClock`,
meeting the std::chrono TrivialClock requirements. `duration` is
`std::chrono::nanoseconds` -- deliberately the SAME duration type
libstdc++'s `steady_clock` has, so no other line of engine code changes
type (`Clock::duration tick_duration`, `duration_cast<Clock::duration>`
in `dos_run_tick_fixed()`, `Delay()`'s `std::min<nanoseconds>` all
compile unchanged). Conversion is split (`secs*1e9 + rem*1e9/1193180`)
because the obvious `t*1e9/1193180` overflows int64 after ~2 hours.
**Monotonic guard:** a read below the last returned value returns the
last value instead -- time stalls for the IRQ latency window rather
than jumping back 55 ms. With the guard `is_steady = true` is honest;
without it it would not be. Epoch is the first `uclock()` call, which
is fine: nothing converts a `Clock::time_point` to calendar time --
verified by grep, every `to_time_t`/`from_time_t`/`time_since_epoch` in
the engine is on `ScriptDateTime::SystemClock` (`system_clock`), and
`FastClock` stays `system_clock`. The one `Clock::time_point` held in
game state (`GamePlayState::_ignoreUserInputUntilTime`) is not
serialized (4 uses, all in `gamestate.cpp`, none in save/restore).

*The pacer (`WaitForNextFrame()`, DOS only):* replace
`std::this_thread::sleep_for(frame_time_remaining)` -- measured at
54.8 ms for ANY positive duration -- with a spin on the new clock to the
deadline, calling `audio_core_entry_poll()` each iteration so a sound-on
run is pumped MORE often than today, not starved. **No `__dpmi_yield()`
in the wait**, despite its 123 us cost on the rig: the same probe
measured it at 54.6 ms per call under DOSBox-X (it halts to the next
timer interrupt there), which would rebuild the exact 18 fps cap this
slice exists to remove, on the emulator every correctness gate runs on.
**How this avoids the hub's busy-wait precedent** (a wait that starved
the BIOS timer and made a self-reported fps number go UP while real
speed collapsed): (1) interrupts stay ENABLED for the whole wait -- no
`cli`, no PIC mask write; the loop touches only PIT ports 43h/40h
(inside `uclock()`) and the audio poll. (2) The clock being polled
cannot run slow unnoticed: a starved IRQ0 shows up as `uclock` falling
behind an oscillator it shares nothing with. **Cross-check, in every
log when `DOSAGS_CLOCK_CROSSCHECK=1`:** sync to a CMOS RTC second edge
(INT 1Ah AH=02h -- its own 32.768 kHz crystal, independent of the PIT
and of IRQ0) before engine start and again at quit, and emit the
`uclock` span over the RTC span. 1.000 +/- 0.5% or the cell's
self-reported rates are void. Env-gated because the two edge syncs cost
up to 1 s each; the start sync runs BEFORE the engine's own start
timestamps are taken, so no startup KPI sees it.

*Other positive sleeps, all listed (grep: `sleep_for`, `->Delay(`,
`YieldCPU()`):*

| site | per-frame? | action |
|---|---|---|
| `timer.cpp` `WaitForNextFrame()` | YES -- and it is the ONLY pacer: fades (`screen.cpp`), `ShakeScreen` (`global_screen.cpp`), dialog options, inventory window, `Display()`, GUI push-buttons, csci dialogs all call it | **fixed here** |
| `video.cpp:414` `sleep_for(8 ms)` | yes, but only inside video playback | **left, flagged**: would cap video at ~18 fps; no fixture plays a video, so a change could not be validated this round |
| `agsplatformdriver.cpp` `Delay()` | no | left: callers are `engine.cpp:651` (one 500 ms splash hold at startup -- overshoots by <=55 ms once), `draw.cpp:1414` (fullscreen-lost recovery, unreachable on DOS), `debug.cpp` (editor debugger, unreachable) |
| `YieldCPU()` -> `Delay(1)` | no | left: only in `game_update_suspend` loops (switched-away, never on DOS) and the debugger |

*The samplers:* `end_of_tick`'s three clock reads become ONE, taken by
`game_loop_update_fps()` and handed to `dos_fps_sample_tick(now)` and
`dos_memory_sample_tick(now)`. Considered and rejected: gating them on
a tick count instead. `fps_p50` is a percentile over once-per-REAL-
second samples; sampling every N ticks would make it tick-weighted
(one sample per 3 s at 13 ticks/s) and break comparability with every
fps figure recorded so far. A shared read is as cheap and changes no
KPI's meaning.

**P1 item 2 -- what the DOSBox-X gate found, and the ABBA
PRE-REGISTRATION (written 2026-09-17 BEFORE any rig cell of this round;
the rig is powered off as this is committed).**

Implementation landed as two patches rather than one, deliberately:
**0095** is the RTC cross-check alone (behaviour-neutral, env-gated),
**0096** is the clock + pacer + samplers. Splitting them puts the
cross-check in BOTH ABBA arms, so it also says whether the OLD binary's
uclock numbers were honest -- at the price that arm A is "the current
binary plus an inert diagnostic" (sha12 `73d569d0be8c`) rather than
0094's `621d9a024f97` byte-for-byte. A's own figures against TNY94A
(same recipe, 0094) show whether that is as inert as claimed.

Two things the DOSBox-X gate changed in the design above:
- **The RTC is read through ports 70h/71h, not INT 1Ah AH=02h.** Under
  DOSBox-X the BIOS call returns a time frozen at emulator start
  (370,000 polls in 5 s, never advanced); the chip's own registers
  advance. Guarded per the datasheet (skip while UIP, re-check after,
  seconds read twice). `clkprobe2` item 5 asks the rig whether INT 1Ah
  advances THERE, for the record.
- **The in-wait audio poll uses an adaptive margin.** The first build
  polled whenever >2 ms remained; one `audio_core_entry_poll()` is
  ~1 ms on the rig but **11 ms under DOSBox-X**, and it ran through the
  deadline (max wait 32 ms). It now polls only when the remaining wait
  exceeds what recent polls cost + 1 ms: max wait 25 ms.

DOSBox-X results (binary `be452784ef30`): Trilby's Notes screenshot
byte-identical to the standing reference (sha256 `03de57f79303d68c...`);
AGS Quest AutoPilot every phase `ok`, exit 0, 0 critical / 0 warn; game
speed **not above 40** -- `fps_p50` 40.04, stall-free window 40.00
ticks/s (Trilby's) and 39.90 (AGS Quest). `clkprobe2` under DOSBox-X:
raw `uclock()` stepped BACKWARDS 64 times in 1.96 M reads (worst
54.9 ms) -- so the hole is real even on the emulator -- and the engine
`Clock` zero times, worst forward step 16 us.

**A yardstick finding that changes how "must not exceed 40" is
judged.** `tick_rate_steady` reads 40.4-40.5 on a run paced at exactly
40 -- before this patch too (TNY94A: 40.50). It removes stall ticks and
their time, but the fixed-timestep loop then REPAYS up to
`MAX_CATCHUP`=5 ticks after each stall, and those land in the numerator
with no time to match: ~+0.2 per stall over a 25 s cell. It is the
right figure for "what rate does the game hold outside stalls" and the
wrong one for "is the pacer letting the game run fast". So
`port_game.py` now also derives **`tick_rate_window`**: ticks over real
elapsed time from the first per-second row >= 200 ticks past the last
stall to the last row -- no stall, no repay, no post-stall fade inside
it. TNY94A re-parsed: steady 40.50, **window 40.00**.

*Cells (HW-486-66, Trilby's Notes idle, the TNY94A recipe + the
cross-check):* `run-hw.sh trilbysnotes --env
DOSAGS_TAS_AUTO_EXIT_TICK=1000 --env DOSAGS_CLOCK_CROSSCHECK=1
--extra-file games/trilbysnotes/ACSETUP-OFF.CFG:ACSETUP.CFG`, fixed
timestep on (the script's default). Order **A B B A**, fresh tags
`TNC96A1`, `TNC96B1`, `TNC96B2`, `TNC96A2`. A = `73d569d0be8c`
(patches through 0095), B = `be452784ef30` (through 0096), both saved
aside and swapped into `build/ags/ags.exe`.

*Predictions, from the probe table (4725 clock reads per 1000 ticks x
1.32 ms = 6.3 ms/tick = ~7.3 ms per OUTER iteration at TNY94A's
855 iterations):*

| figure | A expected (= TNY94A) | B predicted | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| per-outer-iteration work | ~26.2 ms (28.9 ms/iter less 2.7 ms mean wait) | **~18.9 ms** | -7.3 ms of clock reads; under the 25 ms budget, so the loop becomes PACER-bound |
| `fps_p50` (render passes/s; static screen, ~23 of ~890 presents real) | 34.6 | **40.0 (39.5-40.5)** | pacer-bound at the 25 ms grid |
| `frames_skipped` | ~145 | **< 35** | catch-up ticks only after the two startup stalls (<=5 each) and during the fade |
| `end_of_tick` mean | 4.04 ms | **<= 0.3 ms** | 3 x 1.32 ms of clock reads -> one 5 us read |
| `wait_next_frame` | mean 2.7 ms, max 57 ms, 55 sleeps | **mean 5-7 ms, max <= 26 ms, ~850 waits** | now waits every frame, never a 55 ms sleep |
| `tick_rate_steady` | 40.50 | **40.3-40.6** (unchanged) | already at 40 via catch-up; the +0.4-0.5 is the repay artifact above |
| `tick_rate_window` | 40.00 | **40.0 (39.8-40.2)** | ditto; this is the must-not-exceed figure |
| whole-run `tick_rate` | 33.52 | **33.4-34.0 (no real change)** | the steady state was ALREADY 40 Hz (the catch-up loop made up the ticks the slow clock cost, at the price of skipped renders); this slice touches neither the 3.1 s pre-loop nor the 1.9 s of stall ticks, which are what hold it at 33.5. At most the fade gets ~0.3 s cheaper (+0.35). |

So, said in advance: **this slice is predicted to move `fps` to its
gate and to leave both tick figures where they are** -- `steady`
already passes, whole-run will still FAIL 40 +/- 2% by a wide margin,
and that failure is the pre-loop + stall-tick work the operator's
both-figures decision made a Gate 1 item. If whole-run moves by more
than +0.5 my model of where that time goes is wrong and I will say so.

*Thresholds (pre-registered):*
- **Primary, `fps_p50`:** WIN if mean(B) - mean(A) >= **+3.0** AND both
  B cells exceed both A cells. Between +1.0 and +3.0 = real but the
  model over-predicted (report as such). < +1.0 = noise/loss.
- **Game speed (pass/fail on each B cell, not a delta):**
  `tick_rate_window` in **[39.2, 40.8]**, and `tick_rate_steady` <=
  **40.8**. Above either = the pacer lets the game run fast = the slice
  FAILS regardless of fps.
- **Whole-run `tick_rate`:** |mean(B) - mean(A)| < 0.5 = "no change, as
  predicted". >= +0.5 = a real gain I did not predict. <= -0.5 = a
  regression; the slice fails.
- **Independent wall-clock bracket, every cell, both arms:**
  `clock_crosscheck ratio` in **[0.995, 1.005]** (`port_game.py check`
  gates on it). Outside it, that cell's self-reported rates are VOID --
  and if it is the B cells only, the pacer is starving IRQ0 and the
  slice fails. Reported beside it: `ticks / rtc_s` for the whole
  RTC-edge-to-RTC-edge bracket (includes engine init and shutdown, so a
  floor, not the gate figure) for A vs B.
- *Invalidity (cell discarded and re-run under a fresh tag, never
  averaged in):* `binary_sha12` not the arm's; `exit_code` != 0 or any
  critical/warn; game title in STDOUT.TXT not Trilby's Notes; more than
  one `[RUNMANIFEST-BEGIN]` in the log; `env_block_sha` differing
  between cells; `memory_min_free_kb` off the others by > 5%;
  `presents_real` outside 20-30 (would mean the scene was not idle).

Before the ABBA, `clkprobe2` on the rig (not an ABBA cell): new clock's
cost, raw vs guarded backward steps, uclock vs RTC over 10 s, INT 1Ah
liveness, and 200 pacer deadlines bracketed by RTC edges. After it, one
AGS Quest cell on B (`AQ96N1`, same recipe as AQ94N1 + the cross-check)
as a datum. Prediction for that datum: `tick_rate_steady` 32.8 ->
**~38-40** (its steady ticks cost 30.5 ms each, of which 6.3 ms was
clock reads, so ~24 ms -- right at the 25 ms line, with repay pushing
the reported figure up), `fps_p50` 6.67 -> **~7.0-7.5** (a rendered
frame is ~95 ms of blit + flush the clock never touched; ~6 ms off
each), whole-run 13.2 -> **~13.5-14** (58% of its loop is stall ticks).

**P1 item 2 -- PRE-REGISTRATION AMENDMENT (2026-09-17, after the first
cell `TNC96A1` and BEFORE any further cell; thresholds and predictions
are UNCHANGED).** One arm-A cell has been run and is DISCARDED, for a
reason that is not a KPI: the rig booted with a bogus DOS date and ran
in the state described below. Stated here so the exclusion rule exists
in writing before the cells it will be applied to.

*What happened.* `TNC96A1` (arm A, `73d569d0be8c`): `tick_rate=4.03`,
`fps_p50=0.68`, `duration_s=264`, `started_utc=2059-04-13T13:34:12Z`.
CPU-bound brackets were NORMAL (`present_dirty_check` 6.09 ms vs 6.27;
blit and flush normal); every bracket that contains a
`gettimeofday()`-backed clock read was ~31x: `end_of_tick` 127.6 ms (3
reads) vs 4.04, `wait_next_frame` 42.9 ms (1 read) vs ~1.4 --
`Clock::now()` cost **~42 ms instead of 1.32 ms**. Its RTC cross-check
read `ratio=0.16657`, which is NOT a clock verdict: the harness's own
timeline bounds the run at under ~7 minutes, the RTC span it implies is
26, and the reader was then shown to be unreliable (next paragraph).

*This is a PRE-EXISTING rig condition, not this round's code.* Every
recorded real-hardware log was re-read for `started_utc`: **18 earlier
cells, back to 2026-09-13 -- before any RTC code existed -- carry a
bogus date (2059-04-12/-23, 2062-06-04, 2062-07-07, 2064-02-01,
2071-07-21), and all 18 are the catastrophically slow ones**
(`tick_rate` 0.24-3.29): TNB1B, TNB2, TNWB1, AUDIOFX1, DMAX1, NOBGT1,
OSA1-4 / OSA1NT-4NT, OSAMID0, S16FI1, S32FI1, TNFI1, S16TV1, TNP81A.
Every cell with a 2026-09 date ran at normal clock cost (`end_of_tick`
3.76-4.14 ms in all 27 that have the bracket). Four more (S4MIDI1,
S5WB1/2, GUSQ2) are dated 2026-11-27/28 -- also wrong -- at
`tick_rate` ~6. Today's and yesterday's bogus dates are the SAME offset
from the truth (+11896 days), and the state comes and goes between
reboots inside one power-on session (TNC96A1 bad; the five probe boots
after it good). **Mechanism NOT established.** Ruled out: `mktime()`
being slow for far-future years (measured under DOSBox-X: 2059 is
FASTER than 2026, 296 us vs 1041 us); RTC port access changing DOS's
get-time cost (clkprb3 on the rig: `gettimeofday` 1.30-1.35 ms and
INT 21h AH=2Ch/2Ah 183 us before and after every kind of port 70h/71h
access, index left at 00h/0Ah/0Ch/0Dh, NMI bit either way). What it
means for the record: those 18 cells measured a rig fault, not the
port, and any conclusion in this file that rests on one of them needs
re-reading -- flagged for the operator, not re-litigated here.

*And patch 0096 is not immune to it.* `FastClock` stays `system_clock`
(the script VM's timeout checks read it), which is why `TNC96A1`'s
`rep_exec_wrapper` was 22 ms and `process_events_dispatch` 63 ms per
call. That is also the strongest evidence yet for what the "zero-work
overhead" in those two phases IS on a good boot (P1 item 3, not
started): `gettimeofday()` reads.

*The RTC reader was wrong, and is fixed in both arms.* A read-only
probe on the rig (`rtcerr`): a CONSTANT CMOS register reads back as
another register's value about once in 60,000 index-write/data-read
pairs (8 of 622,047; 40 of 624,135 with an I/O delay between the two
port accesses -- more often the longer the gap, never with UIP set):
something on an interrupt moves the index register under us, and the
wrong values are plausible BCD seconds/minutes, i.e. something reads
the clock on a timer tick. The first reader double-checked only the
seconds register; a replica of the engine's exact start/end sequence
(`ordp`) returned hour 00 for 12 on its first run. It now reads the
whole h/m/s/regB set twice and requires exact agreement. Patch files
0095 and 0096 regenerated; **arm A is now `dfae69677424`, arm B
`39036f2a1d6e`** (B's DOSBox-X gate re-run: screenshot identical,
`fps_p50` 40.00, exit 0).

*Added invalidity condition (applies to every cell from here on, both
arms; re-run under a fresh tag, never averaged in):* **`started_utc`
not dated 2026-09-17** -- the rig booted in the bogus-date state, in
which a `gettimeofday()` costs ~31x. Cells continue `TNC96A3`,
`TNC96B1`, `TNC96B2`, `TNC96A4` (order still A B B A; `TNC96A1` is
burnt, `A2` is skipped so the two A tags stay visibly distinct from
the discarded one).

**P1 item 2 -- SECOND AMENDMENT (2026-09-17, after discarded cells
`TNC96A1` and `TNC96A3`, before any further cell): the "bogus-date rig
state" is NOT a rig state. It is a libc bug this port has been running
into since 2026-09-13, it is now fixed (patch 0097), and the fix goes
into BOTH arms.** Thresholds and predictions still unchanged.

`TNC96A3` (arm A rebuilt with the fixed RTC reader) came back the same:
`started_utc=2059-04-13`, `tick_rate=4.03`, `end_of_tick` 127.6 ms --
while every PROBE booted in between showed the right date. So it
follows the process, not the boot. The cross-check now worked
(`rtc_s=264 uclock_ms=263991 ratio=0.99997`): the run really took
264 s, the clock was honest, the engine really was that slow.

*Mechanism, measured on the rig (`envp`, `tzp`, read-only):* with `TZ`
unset, DJGPP's `tzset()` looks for a default zone file
(`/dev/env/DJDIR/etc/localtime`, then `zoneinfo/localtime`,
`posixrules`, `GMT`). With no DJGPP install every open fails (errno 22
on the rig) -- and what that failure path leaves behind there is not a
clean GMT. DOS reported 2026-09-17 13:25:05 while `time()` in the same
process said 2026-09-25: **`tm_gmtoff` = -675288 s**; the next process,
-1024 s; `localtime()` right both times. It behaves like uninitialised
state inside libc. In the engine the offset came out **+11896 days**
(hence 2059), and in that state every `gettimeofday()` -- which runs
`mktime()` through the broken zone state -- costs ~42 ms instead of
1.3 ms. After `setenv("TZ","UTC0")` the same process read `gmtoff=0`
and the right date. DOSBox-X never reproduces it (same binary, same
environment: 2026), which is why no gate caught it.

*Patch 0097:* `main_init()` sets `TZ=UTC0` when the user has not set
one (a set TZ is parsed, never loaded), calls `tzset()`, and re-anchors
the frame timestamps static initialisers took through the broken
state. `UTC0` is what the fallback was meant to be -- DOS local time
taken as-is -- so game-visible time does not move.

*What this does to the record (flagged for the operator, not
re-litigated here).* **Twenty real-hardware cells carry a 2059-2071
`started_utc`, and they are exactly the ones that ran 8-100x slow**
(the 18 listed in the first amendment + `TNC96A1` + `TNC96A3`). Whether
a cell was hit varied with the binary and the `SET` lines it ran under
-- the 0094 binary under the TNY94A recipe never was; the 0095 binary
with one more `SET` line was, twice, identically. So this was not
noise, it was a CONFOUND: e.g. `TNP81A` (hit, `tick_rate` 3.29) vs
`TNP81B` (not hit, 23.71) differed in what was being tested AND in
whether libc's clock was broken. Every conclusion resting on one of
those 20 cells -- including the `DOSAGS_FLIP_INSTR` "per-flip cost"
reading (S16FI1/S32FI1/TNFI1 were all hit) and the OSA*/DMAX1/NOBGT1
sound-milestone timings -- needs re-reading with that in mind. The four
cells dated 2026-11-27/28 (S4MIDI1, S5WB1/2, GUSQ2) show the same bug
with a smaller offset; their `tick_rate` ~6 may or may not have been
affected -- unknown. Every cell dated 2026-09 by its own log ran at
normal clock cost.

**Unit bug in the instrumentation (found by a read-only research fork,
verified in source by the coordinator and by me; patch 0098,
2026-09-17).** Patch 0083 changed `dos_port_tick_record()` from
milliseconds to microseconds and converted every call site but two --
`script/script.cpp`'s `script_vm` and `rep_exec_vm` brackets kept passing
`(uclock()-t0) * 1000 / UCLOCKS_PER_SEC`. **Every record from the 0083
build onward logs those two phases 1000x too small**: TNP83A-TNP86A,
TNFIX*, TNP89A-TNP92, TNP2*/3*/4*, TNY94A, AQ93N1/AQ94N1, and this
round's TNC96* cells before 0098. ONLY those two rows: fps, both tick
rates, stalls and every other phase stand (every other call site was
audited and is in microseconds). The tell sat in every log --
`script_vm max_ms=2` beside `process_events_dispatch max_ms=2605` for
the same blocking call -- and was read backwards, as wrappers costing
milliseconds around a VM doing nothing. Patch 0098 renames the function
`dos_port_tick_record_us()` (a stale caller no longer compiles) and
gives manual brackets one helper, `dos_port_tick_elapsed_us(t0)`. First
true numbers (DOSBox-X, 1000 idle ticks): `script_vm` 2318 ms (one
2284 ms blocking call), `rep_exec_vm` 169 ms.

**`clkprobe2` on the target machine (2026-09-17, before the ABBA; raw:
`tests/harness/results/clock-probe/HW-486-66-2026-09-17-clkprobe2-PRBOUT.TXT`).**
Engine `Clock::now()` **12.1 us** (uclock 4.6 us + two 64-bit divides)
vs 1324.6 us before -- 109x. Raw `uclock()` stepped BACKWARDS 46 times
in 1.72 M reads over 8 s (worst 373 us; 853 us on a second run) -- the
hole is real on this machine, smaller than under DOSBox-X (54.9 ms) --
and the guarded engine clock **zero** times in 636 k reads, worst
forward step 124 us. uclock vs the CMOS RTC over 10 s: **0.99997**
(-34 ppm, crystal tolerance). INT 1Ah AH=02h DOES advance here (it is
DOSBox-X that freezes it). 200 pacer deadlines on a 25 ms grid:
5000.02 ms by uclock, worst overshoot 63 us, RTC bracket consistent.

**P2 amendments from the presentation research
(`docs/design/p2-presentation-design.md`, every claim cited file:line;
its two biggest claims re-verified by the coordinator). RECORDED, not
started.**
- **Mode 13h has NO fixture today**, so candidate (a) leaves the P2.1
  bake-off until BENCH8 exists (being built in its own worktree,
  `~/git/dosags-bench8`, branch `bench8` -- not touched from here).
  Trilby's Notes is **320x240** to the engine (`letterbox-by-design`,
  AGS's compiled letterbox option), which is also WHY today's 2x fast
  blit engages at all; 5days/7days/mmd are 16-bit, shards/iowna 32-bit.
  Prior evidence the card runs Mode 13h: doskutsu
  `docs/internal/MACH64-TRIAGE.md:618-621`.
- **The backend's NORMAL LFB path -- the one dosags is on
  (`hint_direct_fb=0 hint_prefer_lfb=0`) -- never reads the rect list**;
  it copies the whole surface every call. So flush scoping (P2.2) and
  dirty rects (P2.4) do NOTHING until
  `SDL_HINT_DOS_ALLOW_DIRECT_FRAMEBUFFER` is on. **New first step, zero
  code:** the current binary with `SET SDL_DOS_ALLOW_DIRECT_FRAMEBUFFER=1`
  (then also `SDL_DOS_PREFER_LFB=1`) on Trilby 2x and AGS Quest with real
  presents forced -- what does the extra normal-path copy cost? Watch for
  tearing; confirm AGS really hides the SDL cursor (the direct path
  composites none). **P2.0's probe times both banked-dosmemput and
  nearptr-LFB writes, and a system-RAM-to-system-RAM memcpy as the
  control** (coordinator, earlier the same day).
- **Centring alone makes things SLOWER**: a bordered dst disables the
  skip-unchanged check AND the fast blit, and triggers the full-window
  `SDL_FillSurfaceRect` every present (`ali3dsw.cpp:1097-1098` -- AGS
  Quest's ~15 ms). So the **Present() 1x path comes FIRST**: clear
  margins once per (window surface, dst rect); at scale 1 with equal
  formats, row `memcpy` into the window surface at dst instead of the
  generic scaled blit; `SDL_UpdateWindowSurfaceRects(window, &dst, 1)`;
  relax `clean_case` to "dst inside the window and margins known
  clean"; shake/flip fall back to clear + full update. Validate under
  DOSBox-X with the hub's `shared/tools/dosbox-x-oversized.conf` (no
  low-res VESA modes -- doskutsu's stand-in for this card) via
  `dosbox-run.sh --conf`. That ONE slice is P2.2 and the enabler for
  the centred candidates.
- **The bake-off is then:** (d) today's 2x; (b) 512x384 centred --
  config only (`fullscreen=512x384`, `game_scale_fs=round`, optionally
  pinned with `SDL_HINT_DOS_FORCE_MODE_ID=0x01F3`; `0x01D4` for
  16-bit); (c) 640x480 centred 1x -- needs a small DOS-only max-scale
  cap where `get_game_frame_from_screen_size` is called with scale 0
  (`graphics_mode.cpp:579`). NEVER the `--windowed` route on this card
  (the note's section 3: the top-left-corner trap). For the operator's
  eventual choice: doskutsu retired 512x384 for a PRODUCT reason (it
  exists only in UniVBE's list), not a technical one; this target has
  UniVBE resident.
- **Palette-only present (a P1 stall item that depends on P2.3;
  `docs/design/p2-dirtyrect-and-idle-design.md` section 5 -- recorded,
  not built):** AGS already fades 8-bit by palette alone, but each of
  its 13 steps changes the palette, which defeats patch 0091's skip and
  forces a full ~76 ms blit + push + vblank wait for pixels that did
  not change -- that IS the 1132 ms stall tick, and ~1 s of the 3.1 s
  pre-loop is the same 13 presents fading out a placeholder room that
  shows nothing. Fix shape: when only the palette version changed, set
  the DAC and push no pixels; the full gain needs the direct-framebuffer
  path first. The 734 ms tick is not identified from source yet.

- **The clock is honest in both arms**: 0.99997 against the CMOS RTC in
  all four cells (-30 ppm, crystal tolerance) -- so the busy-wait pacer
  does not starve IRQ0, and every uclock-based figure recorded before
  today was on a sound time base too.
- **Where the model was wrong.** The two misses are the same mistake: I
  predicted `rep_exec_wrapper` and `process_events_dispatch` would
  collapse to almost nothing once `FastClock` stopped costing 1.3 ms,
  i.e. I still half-believed the "wrappers around an idle VM" picture.
  With true units (0098) the VM is NOT idle: `rep_exec_vm` is 1.71 s
  per 1000 ticks in B and `script_vm` 0.57 s outside its one blocking
  call -- **~2.3 ms of real script per idle tick on the 486**. The
  clock's share was 0.70 ms per `rep_exec` call and 1.2 ms/tick of
  event dispatch, and that part did go. The idle tick is now ~14 ms of
  work in a 25 ms budget: `present_dirty_check` ~6, script ~2.3,
  `scene_construct` ~3, the rest small.
- **`hw_guard`'s first runs against the real vcctrl** (8 witnesses over
  4 cells): every one fired on a HEALTHY reboot with 2 POST + 2 ready
  edges, within 1-2 s of the job ending, and no recovery was triggered.
  One thing to tidy: after a collection the OCR reads the screen as
  `other`, not `ready-prompt` (MODE12 graphics text) -- harmless, the
  rule is only "not the FTP log", but noted.

  rate goes from 32.8 to **39.6 -- at the 40 Hz line** -- and real

  the fps because I only counted the clock reads saved per TICK (~6 ms

  cheaper the catch-up loop needs fewer of them per rendered frame, so
  frames come round sooner. A rendered frame is still **~85 ms**

  means:** AGS Quest's self-reported whole-run rates read ~0.5% HIGH in

  if it fell inside stalls -- unknown); the A-vs-B comparison is

**Why real-hardware AGS Quest cells run with "Audio is disabled" (asked
by the operator watching AQ96N1; answered from the files, not from
memory): it is an ACCIDENT that happens to match the sound-off
convention.** `[sound] enabled=0` reaches the engine as
`usetup.AudioEnabled=false` (`Engine/main/engine.cpp:400-426`: no
"Initializing audio" line is printed at all, only "Audio is disabled"
-- both AQ94N1's and AQ96N1's STDOUT show exactly that, so it is config,
not a failed init). But nothing in the AGS Quest recipe sets it:
`tests/harness/games/agsquest/` holds only `AGSQuest.ags` -- no
`acsetup.cfg` -- and `run-hw.sh agsquest` stages no `--extra-file`. What
the engine reads is the `ACSETUP.CFG` that an earlier TRILBY'S NOTES
cell staged into the same `C:\DOSAGS` (`--extra-file
games/trilbysnotes/ACSETUP-OFF.CFG:ACSETUP.CFG`), which is never removed
-- vcctrl deletes nothing on the target and every package shares that
directory. Under DOSBox-X each run gets a fresh staging directory with
no such file, so the same package comes up with audio ("Initializing
audio" present in today's post-merge DOSBox-X run). That is round 3's
unnamed "genuine environment difference". **Every real-hardware AGS
Quest record since the Trilby sound-off cells began (AQ16N1, AQ32F1,
AQ93N1, AQ94N1, AQ96N1, AQ96A1) is therefore a sound-off cell** --
consistent with each other, and with the benchmark convention, but by
luck: a Trilby sound-ON cell run in between would silently flip AGS
Quest to sound-on. Fix (small, not done this round): give `agsquest` its
own `ACSETUP-OFF.CFG` and stage it explicitly, the way every other
package does.

tests/games/bench8/manifest.yaml --arm all` PASS on all seven arms
