  game.** `steady` drops stall ticks and their time but keeps the <=5
  ticks the fixed-timestep loop repays after each stall; over 25 s that
  is +0.2 per stall, over a ~1 s run it is +10%. `tick_rate_window` is
  the figure that answers "is the game running fast", and it is
  deliberately undefined for a run with fewer than 200 ticks after its
  last stall -- a 45-tick scene is too short to judge a steady rate at
  all, by either figure.
- *Whole-run `tick_rate` 38.5-39.2 under DOSBox-X for the 1000-tick
  arms* (~0.65 s pre-loop + settle): noted. It is the same arithmetic
  as Gate 1's whole-run problem -- 1000 ticks at 40 Hz leave ~0.5 s for
  everything else. Whether to judge on a longer window is the
  operator's call.

**P2.0 -- the bandwidth probe, MEASURED on HW-486-66 (2026-09-17;
`tests/harness/results/bandwidth-probe/`, raw output
`HW-486-66-2026-09-17-bwprobe-PRBOUT.TXT`; every copy verified -- the
control by memcmp, each LFB by readback).** This is the ceiling every
later P2 prediction is checked against.

| route | MB/s | 64,000 B | 76,800 B | 196,608 B | 307,200 B | 460,800 B | 614,400 B |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CONTROL: system RAM -> system RAM | **17.0** | 3.61 ms | 4.32 | -- | 17.22 | 25.83 | 34.43 |
| LFB, near pointer (0x101 / 0x111) | **27.3** | 2.24 | 2.68 | -- | **10.66** | **16.10** | **21.46** |
| banked A000h + VBE 4F05h switches | 25.0 | 2.43 | 3.07 | -- | 11.64 | 17.64 | 23.47 |
| 512x384x8 (0x01F3, UniVBE), LFB | 27.4 | 2.16 | 2.69 | 6.84 | -- | -- | -- |
| 512x384x8, banked | 25.2 | 2.50 | 3.08 | 7.44 | -- | -- | -- |
| Mode 13h, A000h (dosmemput = near ptr) | **9.3** | **6.54** | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |

`rep movsl` and libc `memcpy` are the same to three figures on every
route (DJGPP's memcpy IS a `rep movsl`), so the copy loop is not a
lever. What the table says:
- **Writing to this card is FASTER than copying within system RAM**
  (27.3 vs 17.0 MB/s): a RAM-to-RAM copy pays a DRAM read and a DRAM
  write, a VRAM write pays one DRAM read and a bus write. So the
  retracted "~7 MB/s ceiling" was off by 4x, and the expensive thing in
  a present is every EXTRA pass over system RAM, not the push.
- **Today's 640x480x8 present spends 41.9 ms in
  `SDL_UpdateWindowSurface` on a push that costs 10.7 ms.** The other
  ~31 ms is the backend's normal path: a whole-surface copy at the
  17 MB/s RAM rate (18 ms) plus its cursor/vblank work -- exactly what
  the direct-framebuffer hint removes (zero-code probe, running next).
  Add the 2x scale blit (34 ms) and a real 8-bit present is ~76 ms for
  10.7 ms of bus.
- **Unscaled is the prize: a 320x200 or 320x240 frame is 2.2-2.7 ms**
  into the LFB of either 640x480 or 512x384 -- per byte the two modes
  are identical, so (b) vs (c) in the bake-off will be decided by the
  picture, not the numbers.
- **Mode 13h is the SLOWEST route per byte (9.3 MB/s, the legacy VGA
  aperture)**, but its frame is small: 6.5 ms, against 2.2 ms for the
  same 64,000 bytes centred in a VESA mode. It stays in the bake-off
  for the full-screen picture, not for speed.
- **16-bit:** AGS Quest's own 640x360 rectangle is 16.1 ms per push,
  the full 640x480 21.5 ms -- so full-frame 16-bit at 40 fps (25 ms) is
  NOT out of reach on bandwidth alone, which is what the retracted note
  claimed; it is out of reach today because a frame costs ~85 ms of
  blit + fill + double copy around that push.
- Banked costs ~8% more than the LFB, bank switches included -- so
  `SDL_DOS_PREFER_LFB=1` is worth ~1 ms per 307,200-byte present, no
  more.

**Diagnosis of the AGS Quest miss (same session, before the operator's
next round): the unchanged-frame skip should never have been allowed
to engage on a 460,800-byte 16-bit frame.** `present_dirty_check` on
`AQ100B1` was 36.8 ms/call x 1233 calls -- a full byte-compare plus,
on every CHANGED frame, a full copy into the cache, at the 486's
measured 17 MB/s RAM rate (P2.0). AGS Quest is mostly moving content
(only 528-527 of 1234 render passes were unchanged), so most calls paid
36.8 ms to save nothing, and outright LOST time against not checking at
all (previously: no check ran on a bordered frame, `present_blit`
26.5 ms was the only per-present cost beyond the ~34 ms fixed fill,
which 0100 also removed). Fixed by **patch 0102**: the skip check now
only runs on frames <= 100,000 bytes (76,800 covers every 8-bit
320x200/240 fixture with headroom; 460,800/614,400 for AGS Quest do
not qualify). DOSBox-X gate on `9279767270b5`: BENCH8 idle/Trilby's
Notes window screenshots identical, AGS Quest AutoPilot 18/18 with
capture hashes PASS, all seven BENCH8 arms PASS.

**Why BENCH8's `walk` jumped so much more than `anim12` (+31 vs +5
fps): the skip DOES engage on 8-bit frames (they are under the 0102
gate) and `walk` has far more identical consecutive frames than
`anim12` by construction** -- `B8WKB1`: 768 of 966 render passes
skipped (79%); `B8ANB1`: only 33 of 329 (10%, the 12-object animation
keeps almost every frame different). Both are still real wins over A
(which took none of the fast blit, none of the skip): `walk`'s few
real presents are ~26.8 ms of fast 2x blit instead of ~82.6 ms of
generic scaled blit; `anim12`, mostly un-skippable, gets the same
per-present win on nearly every frame, which is the more representative
number for genuinely busy 8-bit content.

**Lesson applied, not just described:** this is the ABBA doing its
job -- a plausible, source-grounded prediction (bordered-frame skip
"just works" once the geometry check is relaxed) was WRONG in one of
three fixtures, caught immediately because the pre-registered threshold
was a real number and AGS Quest's B cells both landed clearly below it,
not scattered around it. Fixed with a size gate keyed to the actual
cost (measured MB/s x frame bytes vs the present it replaces), not a
revert of the feature -- BENCH8's win is real and stands.

**Investigation: why candidate (b) 512x384 fell back to 640x400 under
DOSBox-X's oversized conf -- a conf/emulator limitation, NOT a bug in
`DOSAGS_MAX_SCALE` or AGS's mode selection (checked from source/logs
before building anything on it further, per the coordinator's
instruction).** The leftover staging dir from that run
(`LOGS/SDLDBG.LOG`) shows DOSBox-X's own S3 Trio64 VESA BIOS emulation
(`[dosbox] machine = svga_s3` in the oversized conf) enumerating **36
modes, none of them 512x384 at any depth** -- the full list is 640x400,
640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1280x960/1024, 1152x864 at various depths,
plus text modes; nothing between 640x400 and 800x600. `DOSVESA-MODESET`
picked `0x0100 640x400 8bpp` because AGS's own `find_nearest_supported_
mode()` correctly found the closest match to a requested 512x384 in a
list that simply does not contain it -- the same code path that, given
`DOSAGS_MAX_SCALE=1` in candidate (c)'s test, DID correctly render at
exactly 320x200 centred in 640x480 (candidate (c) is proof the
mode-selection and scale-cap logic both work; only the specific mode is
absent here). **Real hardware has the mode**: TNP81A's SDL log (this
session, 2026-09-16) lists `mode 0x01F3: 512x384 bpp=8 ... lfb=1` via
UniVBE, which the oversized conf's synthetic S3 BIOS does not provide
and has no config knob to add (`[vesa] modelist = compatible` selects
DOSBox-X's own canned list, not an arbitrary one). **Conclusion:**
candidate (b) is untestable under this DOSBox-X conf by construction,
not because of anything wrong in this port; its real bring-up and
correctness check happens directly on HW-486-66, where the mode exists,
as part of the bake-off below -- not pre-validated under DOSBox-X first

**Verdict, stated against the number written down in advance:
`+1.45` is a REAL, PERFECTLY REPRODUCIBLE gain (spread 0.00 within
each arm, no A/B overlap) that is nevertheless BELOW the pre-registered
`+2.0` WIN threshold.** By the rule set before the data, that is "real
but the model over-predicted", not a win. It is recorded as such. What
the model got wrong, specifically: the prediction assumed the ~15 ms
per-present margin fill would come off the top of a ~85 ms frame while
everything else held, giving ~70 ms. The fill did go and the fast
unscaled blit did engage -- `blit_path` proves both -- but at 1x the
row-memcpy path costs essentially what the generic 1:1 scaled blit
cost (26.8 vs 26.5 ms measured), exactly as P2.0's 17 MB/s RAM rate
said it would, so the only real saving was the fill. `presents_real`
rising 1233 -> 1374 is the honest shape of the gain: ~11% more frames
delivered in the same wall time.

**The full arc of this slice, for the record:** patch 0100 predicted
+2.0 on AGS Quest and delivered **-2.20** (a regression); the cause was
diagnosed to the byte (a 36.8 ms skip-check on a 460,800-byte frame at
the measured 17 MB/s), fixed as patch 0102 with a size gate rather than
a revert, and the corrected mechanism delivers **+1.45** -- positive,
reproducible, and smaller than predicted. Two wrong predictions in one
slice, both caught by pre-registered thresholds rather than by
inspection of the result.

  a straight line through the origin. This is the research note's

  ignores the rect list and copies the whole surface every present**, so
  the scoped `SDL_UpdateWindowSurfaceRects` that patch 0100 issues buys
  nothing yet. P2.3's direct-framebuffer hint is the lever that would

**Operator correction 2026-09-18 -- THE S3 ViRGE AND CIRRUS LOGIC CARDS
ARE ALSO IN SCOPE, and the presentation design so far is over-fitted to
the Mach64.** "Remember we will also be testing and using the S3 ViRGE
and Cirrus Logic video cards too." Everything P2.1 measured is a
Mach64 result and is labelled as such above. Two consequences, both
checked against the logs and shared sources before being written here:

- **There is a rung ZERO above the whole ladder: a card that HAS a real
  low-res mode should simply SET it.** doskutsu's own logs on other
  cards enumerate `0x01F9 320x200 bpp=8 ... pitch=320 lfb=1` and
  `0x01F8 320x240 bpp=8 ... pitch=320 lfb=1` (verified directly in
  `~/git/doskutsu/qa-results/2026-08-11-DX266-full/602SDL.LOG` and
  `2026-08-13-r2-POD83/GE3SDL.LOG`). Full screen, 64,000-76,800 bytes a
  frame, no scale, no centring, no margins -- strictly better than any
  of (a)-(d). **The Mach64's lack of any mode below 512x384 is what
  forces the centred/scaled discussion at all, and that does not
  generalise.** Our Mach64 enumerates 19 modes whose smallest 8-bit
  entries are 512x384 (`0x01F3`) and 640x400 (`0x0100`) -- TNP81A's own
  SDL log.
- **So the default must be chosen PER CARD, from what that card
  actually enumerates at runtime**, never once globally. Selection
  order to implement (reads the live mode list, assumes no card's
  shape): **(0)** a native mode matching the game's own resolution ->
  **(a)** Mode 13h for a true 320x200 8-bit game -> **(b)** centred 1x
  in the smallest mode that contains the picture -> **(c)** centred 1x
  in 640x480 -> **(d)** integer-scaled, as the last resort. Today's
  2x path stays available in every case, per the standing constraint.
  NOT built yet -- this is the design the next P2 slice implements.

**P2.3 -- card-awareness of the direct-framebuffer path, checked in the
shared backend's source rather than assumed (2026-09-18).**
- **On Cirrus the direct path will land on BANKED, and patch 0103 does
  not fight that.** `SDL/0019` auto-disables LFB on the Cirrus
  CL-GD5430 (a genuine hardware defect: the LFB aperture and the VRAM
  the display generator reads are decoupled under UniVBE 6.7;
  HARDWARE.md row 52 -- and note the chip is a **5430**, mislabelled
  "5434" through most of `shared/`'s patch history). Read at
  `SDL_dosmodes.c:988-1012`: `use_lfb` is gated on `!force_banked`,
  where `force_banked` is that auto-detect OR the manual
  `SDL_HINT_DOS_DISABLE_LFB`; **`PREFER_LFB` does NOT clear it -- only
  `SDL_HINT_DOS_FORCE_LFB` (patch 0030) does.** So 0103's
  `PREFER_LFB=1` is simply ignored on that chip and the banked direct
  path is taken, which the research already established IS per-rect
  aware. 0103 is therefore card-safe as written; what it is NOT is
  card-TUNED, and the two open banked hazards below are why that
  matters.
- **Two open hazards live on the banked path** (HARDWARE.md rows 54 and
  59, both read in full): the unfixed bank-select settle-delay/readback
  gap (all cards, banked; found on a real S3 ViRGE 86C375), and a
  reproduced multi-hundred-ms flush stall on Cirrus + dossage
  (`SDL_UpdateWindowSurfaceRects` spiking 2.2 ms -> 243-326 ms, 3-4
  times a run, at reproducible frame positions).
- **A cross-project finding worth flagging: dosags is the port that can
  settle HARDWARE.md row 59's open question.** That row narrows the
  stall to `WaitForVBlank()`, called when `vsync_interval > 0 ||
  dac_needs_update`, and rules the `dac_needs_update` leg out *for
  dossage specifically* because dossage is 16bpp and never presents
  INDEX8 -- while saying it "is still real and worth checking for any
  future *paletted* port on this backend -- a scripted fade/palette-
  cycle at fixed narrative beats would explain a reproducible-position-
  independent-of-input stall exactly this way." **dosags is that
  paletted port**, and this plan has already measured exactly that
  shape: Trilby's Notes' 1132 ms tick-1 stall is a 13-step palette
  fade, every step changing the palette (P1's fade analysis,
  `docs/design/p2-dirtyrect-and-idle-design.md` section 5).
- **And that predicts a second, unlooked-for effect of patch 0103.**
  All three `WaitForVBlank()` call sites (`SDL_dosframebuffer.c:2710,
  2867, 2907`) are in the NORMAL path; the direct path
  (`~1880-2100`) programs the palette on a version change but **never
  waits for vblank**. So moving to the direct path should remove the
  per-palette-step vblank wait that makes those fade stalls as
  expensive as they are -- on the Mach64 too, not only on Cirrus.
  Stated as a prediction to be measured, not a claim; the fade stall is
  a Gate 1 item and this is a hypothesis for it.

**P2.3 -- PRE-REGISTERED four-way re-run under the direct-framebuffer
path (written 2026-09-18 before any 0103 cell; Mach64).** Same
discriminating cell as the bake-off, BENCH8 `anim12`, one cell per
candidate, binary `97709fd0a103` (0103, direct path default ON),
sound-off, RTC on. The reference column is the bake-off's own normal-
path cell for the same candidate.

*Mechanism being tested:* the direct path copies only the rect it is
given, so each candidate should pay for its PICTURE (320x200 = 64,000
bytes for a/b/c; 640x400 = 256,000 for d) instead of its WINDOW SURFACE
(64,000 / 196,608 / 307,200 / 307,200). Prediction is anchored on two
measurements, not on the raw bus rate: P2.0's LFB figures (64,000 B in
2.24 ms, 307,200 B in 10.66 ms = 27 MB/s linear) AND this port's own
zero-code probe on candidate (d) geometry, which measured
`present_update_window` 22.6 -> 13.8 ms for a 256,000-byte rect --
i.e. about **17-18 MB/s effective** once the per-row stride work is
paid. Narrower rects (320-byte rows for a/b/c, against d's 640) should
be somewhat worse per byte again, so the estimates below use 12-18
MB/s rather than 27.

| candidate | window surface | rect actually pushed | `present_update_window` now | **predicted** | `fps_p50` now | **predicted** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Mode 13h | 64,000 B | 64,000 (full-surface shortcut) | 7.84 ms | **2.5-4 ms** | 40.00 | **40.00** (already at the pacer cap) |
| (b) 512x384 ctr | 196,608 B | 64,000 | 15.95 ms | **4-6 ms** | 26.89 | **38-40** |
| (c) 640x480 ctr | 307,200 B | 64,000 | 21.60 ms | **4-6 ms** | 19.72 | **33-40** |
| (d) 640x480 2x | 307,200 B | 256,000 | 24.31 ms | **13-15 ms** (probe measured 13.8) | 11.83 | **15-18** |

*The call this round exists to make, stated in advance:* if those hold,
**(a), (b) and (c) all converge at or near the 40 fps pacer cap and the
speed ordering between them COLLAPSES** -- they already deliver the same
~13.5 real frames/s, and the bake-off gap between them was headroom
created by the whole-surface copy. In that case the choice stops being
about speed and becomes about picture size and deployment
(Mode 13h: biggest picture, 8-bit 320x200 only; 512x384: needs UniVBE;
640x480 centred: smallest picture, no dependency), which is precisely
why the operator deferred. **(d) should remain clearly last** -- its
28.2 ms scale blit is untouched by this patch. If instead b and c stay
well below a, the whole-surface copy was not the binding constraint and
I will say so.

*Also to be checked in the same cells, with a CAMERA photo rather than
a citation -- these are the documented trade-offs of the path:*
**(i) the cursor** (the direct path does no cursor compositing; AGS is
believed to draw its own sprite -- the bake-off's normal-path photos
show a cursor on screen, so its absence under the direct path would be
a visible regression), and **(ii) tearing** (the direct path never
waits for vblank -- all three `WaitForVBlank()` call sites are in the
normal path). A still photo can only catch a tear if one is happening
when the shutter opens, so several shots are taken and the result is
reported as what was seen, not as proof of absence.

| candidate | `present_update_window` normal -> **DIRECT** | predicted | `fps_p50` normal -> **DIRECT** | predicted | render passes | real frames/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Mode 13h | 7.84 -> **7.58 ms** | 2.5-4 -- **MISS** | 40.00 -> **40.00** | 40.00 -- HIT | 1023 -> 1022 | 13.5 -> 13.5 |

**The call this round existed to make, and it lands on the side the

*The two prediction misses, both instructive:*
- **(a) barely moved (7.84 -> 7.58) where I predicted 2.5-4 ms.** The

  **9.3 MB/s** -- not the LFB's 27. 64,000 B / 7.58 ms = 8.4 MB/s,
  matching that figure almost exactly. There was also nothing to scope:
  in Mode 13h the picture IS the whole window, so the rect list is a
  full-screen flush and the direct path takes its full-surface
  shortcut. (a) was already as fast as its aperture allows.
- **(d) beat its prediction (9.93 vs 13-15 ms).** 256,000 B / 9.93 ms =
  25.8 MB/s, close to P2.0's raw 27 MB/s LFB rate -- so the per-row
  stride penalty I extrapolated from the earlier zero-code probe
  (which measured 13.8 ms for the same geometry on the pre-0100 binary)
  has largely gone. Patch 0100's clear-margins-once is the plausible
  reason the probe's figure was higher; not chased further.

*Trade-off (i), the cursor: CONFIRMED PRESENT, on the monitor.* The
direct path does no cursor compositing, and AGS's own cursor sprite is
plainly visible in every photo of all four candidates (clearest on the
pillar in `P3AAN-a-2.jpg`). No regression; the belief is now a
measurement.

*Trade-off (ii), tearing: NO TEAR CAUGHT in 16 photos across the four
candidates -- reported as that, not as proof of absence.* Zoomed on the
pillar's vertical edges and the mortar lines, which is where a
mid-scan write would show as a horizontal step: they are continuous in
every shot. **The method has limited power and I will not overstate
it** -- a webcam exposure integrates over roughly a CRT refresh, so a
transient tear tends to blur rather than freeze, and a still can only
catch one that is happening as the shutter opens. What can be said:
tearing is not gross or continuous. Whether it is visible in motion is
a judgement for someone watching the screen, and worth the operator's
own look before this default is considered settled.

*And the palette-fade prediction, MEASURED in the same session
(`TNFADE1`, Trilby's Notes, direct path, default 640x480 2x -- the same
config as the normal-path cell `BKDTN` it is compared against, single
lever the binary; raw `tests/harness/results/TNFADE1-2026-09-18/`):*
**CONFIRMED, and the arithmetic identifies the mechanism.**

| | BKDTN (0102, normal) | **TNFADE1 (0103, direct)** | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| tick-1 stall (the fade-in) | 1135 ms | **739 ms** | **-396 (-35%)** |
| tick-2 stall | 620 ms | **403 ms** | **-217 (-35%)** |
| total stall time | 1756 ms | **1142 ms** | **-614 (-35%)** |
| whole-run `tick_rate` | 33.71 | **34.48** | **+0.77** |
| `tick_rate_steady` | 40.57 | 40.63 | unchanged, as expected |
| `fps_p50` | 40.00 | 40.00 | both at the cap (idle screen) |

Both stalls fell by the same 35%, which is the signature of a fixed
per-step cost leaving a fade of a fixed number of steps. The size fits
the named mechanism: 396 ms over the fade's **13 steps is ~30 ms a
step**, and `WaitForVBlank()` is **two** back-to-back spins on the VGA
status port (HARDWARE.md row 59), i.e. ~2 refresh periods -- ~28 ms at
70 Hz. So the direct path's not waiting for vblank is what went, and
the `dac_needs_update` leg that HARDWARE.md could only hypothesise for
"a future paletted port" is real and now measured on one.

*What it does and does not do for Gate 1:* it is worth **+0.77** on
whole-run `tick_rate` (33.71 -> 34.48), real but far from the 39.2 the
gate needs. The remaining ~740 ms of fade-in is the 13 full presents
themselves, which is what the palette-only present (skip the pixel push
when only the palette changed) would address -- still not built.

Also: every real-hardware cell to date ran the 640x480 2x-scaled path.
The 1:1 Mode 13h path (`--windowed --gfxfilter stdscale 1`, 64,000
bytes/frame, no scaling) was confirmed on DOSBox-X on 2026-09-10 and
never on the rig with a real game.

**P1 -- palette-only present (patch 0104): DESIGN + PREDICTION, written
before coding (2026-09-18).**

*Premise VERIFIED in source, not taken from the design note:*

- `ScreenFadeSoftware` at `game.color_depth == 1` renders the scene to the
  back buffer exactly ONCE, in `Begin()` (`ac/screen.cpp:245-251`:
  `ClearDrawLists` + `construct_game_scene` + `construct_game_screen_overlay`
  + `RenderToBackBuffer`). `RunImpl()` (`:305-315`) then only interpolates
  the palette and calls `set_palette_range()`; `Draw()` (`:292-295`) only
  calls `render_to_screen()`. **No pixel of the virtual screen changes
  between steps.**
- The transition's own loop (`ScreenTransition::Run()`, `:114-125`) is
  `RunImpl -> Draw -> sys_evt_process_pending -> update_polled_stuff ->
  WaitForNextFrame`. It does NOT re-run `construct_game_scene` or
  `RenderToBackBuffer` either, so nothing else can dirty the buffer
  mid-fade.
- Default `_speed` 5, `_alpha` 0->64 (`:309-313`) => **13 steps**.
- In `Present()`, `SyncPaletteIfNeeded()` (`gfx/ali3dsw.cpp:647-706`)
  returns true on every step, and `unchanged` requires `!palette_changed`
  (`:1129`), so all 13 steps take the full path: cache memcpy + full blit
  + full window push.
- **The DAC update does NOT depend on the rect list.**
  `DOSVESA_UpdateWindowFramebuffer` computes `dac_needs_update` purely
  from `dac_palette->version != vdata->palette_version`
  (`SDL_dosframebuffer.c:2597-2625`) and the direct path likewise
  (`:1901-1906`), each calling `ProgramVGADAC()` independently of what
  rects were passed. So a minimal-rect flush still reprograms the DAC --
  which is what makes this optimization possible at all.

*The change:* in `Present()`'s `clean_case` block, split the current
single `unchanged` test into `pixels_same` and `palette_changed`:

- `pixels_same && !palette_changed` -> skip entirely (today's behaviour).
- **`pixels_same && palette_changed` -> palette-only present: skip the
  cache memcpy (pixels already cached and identical), skip the blit (the
  window surface already holds exactly these pixels from the previous
  present), and push a 1x1 rect inside `dst` so the backend's flush runs
  and reprograms the DAC.** Everything else -> unchanged full path.

Correctness notes: gated inside `clean_case`, so it already requires
`margins_clean`, `dst_inside`, matching formats, no flip and a frame
<= 100,000 bytes; on a `!margins_clean` present the margin fill changes
pixels and `full_update` must stand, which that gate excludes. 8-bit
only in practice, since `palette_changed` can only be true for INDEX8.

*PREDICTION, derived from TNFADE1's own measured constants (stated before
running anything):*

- Per fade step today: `present_blit` 33.72 + `present_update_window`
  22.74 = 56.5 ms, and stall tick 1 is 739 ms = **13 x 56.8 ms** -- the
  step count from source and the per-step cost from the log agree to
  within 1%, which is what makes this prediction worth writing down.
- After: each step costs the compare (~6 ms) plus a 1x1 push, so the
  fade becomes pacing-bound at `WaitForNextFrame`'s 25 ms period.
  **Stall 1: 739 -> ~325 ms** (13 x 25). **Stall 2 (403 ms, ~7 steps):
  -> ~175 ms.** Total stall 1142 -> ~500 ms.
- **Whole-run `tick_rate`: 34.48 -> ~35.3.** `tick_rate_steady`
  unchanged (~40.6), `fps_p50` unchanged at the 40.00 cap.
- **Stated in advance: this does NOT close Gate 1's whole-run half, and
  no achievable version of it can.** The arithmetic: the gate needs
  <= 1000/39.2 = 25.51 s of total runtime; TNFADE1's steady loop alone is
  24.56 s and its pre-loop is 3.10 s. Even with every stall at ZERO the
  run is 27.86 s = 35.9. **The binding term is the pre-loop, not the
  fades** -- and per the startup block that 3.1 s is dominated by
  `first_room_load_ms=2528`, i.e. real room-loading work, not waste.
  Closing the whole-run half over a 1000-tick window therefore needs an
  operator decision (window length, or the catch-up repay policy), not
  another optimization -- exactly the tension the KPI note below already
  flagged. This slice is still worth landing on its own merits: it is
  real, it is the mechanism P2.4 will reuse, and the same fade cost is
  paid on every room transition in Gates 2/3.

**Operator decisions, 2026-09-18 (recorded here as received; the
presentation ones are the design for the NEXT P2 slice, not this one):**

- **Tearing is accepted for this port.** "Tearing is fine, these are
  adventure games." The direct-framebuffer path's no-vsync trade-off is
  therefore closed as a question: patch 0103 stays default-ON with its
  env kill-switch, and no future slice needs to revisit tearing as a
  blocker. The reasoning is genre-based and does NOT transfer: an
  adventure game has mostly-static screens, no scrolling and no camera
  motion, so a tear is rarely visible and never mid-action. **A port
  with scrolling or fast motion must not inherit this decision
  unexamined.** With the cursor question already settled by measurement
  (AGS's own sprite visible in every bake-off photo), both of P2.3's
  documented trade-offs are now closed -- one measured, one accepted by
  operator judgement.
- **Governing principle for presentation: "I want the fastest options
  available by default, with tunable features that could reduce
  fps/ticks as options."**
  - Mode 13h IS the default where it fits (true 320x200 8-bit).
  - UniVBE is acceptable on our own machines, but the audience is a
    public release for real DOS users, so it must not be REQUIRED:
    detect what is actually present at runtime and use the fastest
    available. The provider is already logged (`oem_string`), so this is
    automatic -- no user config, no support burden.
  - Software 2x scaling is never a default anywhere; it stays an opt-in
    for someone who wants a bigger picture and accepts the cost.
  - **Selection policy, fastest first, decided per card from the LIVE
    enumerated mode list:** (1) a native mode matching the game's own
    resolution/depth -> set it; (2) a true 320x200x8 game -> Mode 13h
    (the backend always synthesises it, so this works on any card
    including the Mach64); (3) otherwise centred unscaled in the
    smallest mode that contains the picture (512x384 if enumerated, else
    640x480); (4) software 2x by opt-in only.
  - *Correction recorded with the decision:* the ViRGE/Cirrus fill the
    screen by setting a NATIVE low-res mode whose display hardware
    double-scans for free (doskutsu sets `0x01F8 320x240 8bpp`,
    `fb_size=76800` -- `qa-results/2026-08-11-DX266-full/602SDL.LOG`),
    NOT by software 2x. On a card with a native mode, software 2x would
    be choosing the slow path (a 28 ms CPU blit, the most expensive
    single thing in the 8-bit path) on the fast card.
  - **OPEN QUESTION, to be answered when a card is next in the machine,
    not guessed:** in doskutsu's logs those low-res modes sit in
    UniVBE's own OEM `0x01Fx` series with UniVBE resident, exactly like
    the Mach64's 512x384. So it is NOT established whether the
    ViRGE/Cirrus ROMs offer low-res modes WITHOUT UniVBE -- which is
    what matters for the public-release audience. One-line check:
    enumerate with and without UniVBE resident on that card.
- **Campaign shape: "continue and push performance as far as we can with
  the mach64, laying a solid foundation and then we will test the virge
  and cirrus cards."** Stay on the Mach64 until the performance work is
  genuinely done. It is the worst case, so what works here works
  everywhere, and a fix tuned on an easier card might never have been
  forced to find the real mechanism. Consequences: do not defer a hard
  problem to "the other cards will be better" -- if something is slow
  here, find out why here; keep every finding card-labelled anyway so
  the later ViRGE/Cirrus work is a comparison rather than a
  re-derivation; and prefer mechanisms that generalise over ones that
  only pay off on this card (a card-specific win is worth having, but
  flag it as such).

**Every presentation number in this plan is a Mach64 number.** Rung 1 of
the policy above, and ViRGE/Cirrus behaviour generally, are unproven
until measured on those cards.

**Operator decision 2026-09-18 -- LENGTHEN THE MEASUREMENT WINDOW.**
"Both must pass" is unchanged; what changes is the window the whole-run
figure is judged over (1000 ticks was never a deliberate choice, it was
inherited from the S7-era recipe). Direction was 4000-5000 ticks, with
5000 the safer of the two, and an instruction to derive it from a real
cell rather than an estimate, and to report rather than nudge if 5000
landed short.

**MEASURED, and 5000 DOES land short -- reported, not nudged.**
Two 5000-tick Trilby idle cells on the current binary (`a874798824e6`,
patches through 0104), sound-off, raw in
`tests/harness/results/TNW5K{1,2}-2026-09-18/`:

| | TNW5K1 | TNW5K2 |
|---|---|---|
| whole-run `tick_rate` | **38.96** | **38.90** |
| `tick_rate_steady` | 40.05 | 40.05 |
| `fps_p50` | 40.00 | 40.00 |
| stalls / preloop (ms) | 411 / 2882 | 411 / 3094 |
| `clock_crosscheck` | 0.99997 | 0.99997 |

Mean **38.93**, spread 0.06 -- repeatable, and short of the 39.2 band
edge. Note `stall_ms` is unchanged from the 1000-tick cells (411 vs 413)
and `presents_palette_only` is still 20: the fade is a ONE-TIME startup
cost, which is exactly why a longer window dilutes it.

*Why the estimate said 39.2 and the machine says 38.93:* the estimate
used ~2.5 s of fixed cost (room load only). The real fixed term inside
`tick_rate`'s denominator is **3.60 s** -- preloop 2.99 + stalls 0.41 +
shutdown ~0.2. The other half is that steady settles to **40.05** over a
long window, not the 40.24 seen at 1000 ticks (at 1000 ticks the
catch-up loop is still repaying the fade backlog; over 5000 it is not).
Both corrections push the same way.

*The model, now validated at two window lengths:*
`tick_rate(N) = N / (3.60 + N/40.05)` gives 35.00 at N=1000 (measured
35.25) and 38.93 at N=5000 (measured 38.93).

| N ticks | whole-run ceiling | engine time |
|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 35.00 | ~28 s |
| 4000 | 38.66 | ~103 s |
| **5000** | **38.93** (measured) | ~128 s |
| 6000 | 39.11 | ~153 s |
| **6650** | **39.20 -- break-even** | ~170 s |
| 8000 | 39.34 | ~203 s |
| 10000 | 39.48 | ~253 s |

**What this actually means, stated plainly: the whole-run gate is a
DILUTION test on fixed startup cost, and the window length is the dial.**
Whole-run `tick_rate` approaches steady (40.05) from below as N grows and
can never exceed it, so the question is only how many ticks it takes for
3.60 s of startup to fall under the 2% allowance. Today that is **~6650
ticks**. No window shorter than that can pass on this binary, however the
number is chosen.

**Two dials, and they trade off -- an operator decision, not mine:**

1. **Lengthen further.** 8000 ticks (39.34) has real margin over the
   6650 break-even; 6650 itself is break-even to two decimals and would
   fail on any bad day. Cost: ~3.4 min of engine time per cell, so a
   four-cell ABBA is ~14 min of engine time plus transfer/boot overhead.
2. **Cut the fixed cost instead.** It is dominated by the ~2.9-3.1 s
   pre-loop, itself mostly `first_room_load_ms` (~2.5 s). **If the
   pre-loop came down to 1.0 s the break-even drops to ~2975 ticks** --
   i.e. pre-loop work buys back window length at better than 1:1, and a
   3000-tick window would then pass where 6650 is needed today.

I have NOT adopted a window unilaterally, because 5000 landing short
makes this a genuine fork rather than a parameter. **Re-baseline for
whichever is chosen is already in hand at 5000** (the table above is the
current binary's clean before-number at that length).

**Window labelling, so history stays readable:** every whole-run figure
recorded before 2026-09-18 is a **1000-tick** number and stays as
written -- they are not restated in the new units. Every new one is
labelled with its window. The two are different measurements of the same
machine, not a jump in performance: the same binary reads 35.25 at 1000
ticks and 38.93 at 5000. `tick_rate_steady` and `fps_p50` are unaffected
by window length (40.24->40.05 is the catch-up-repay effect above, not a
unit change). Whatever window is adopted applies equally to BENCH8's and
AGS Quest's gate cells when their turn comes, so all three gates are
judged consistently.

**Gate 1 on the current binary at a 5000-tick window:**

| measure | value | gate | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fps_p50` | 40.00 | >= 40 | **PASS** (static screen, 4994 of 5017 presents skipped) |
| `tick_rate_steady` | 40.05 | 39.2-40.8 | **PASS** |
| whole-run `tick_rate` | 38.93 | 39.2-40.8 | **FAIL by 0.27** |

**Operator decision 2026-09-18 -- ATTACK THE FIXED STARTUP COST, do NOT
lengthen the window to dilute it.** Cutting the pre-loop buys window
length at better than 1:1, and unlike lengthening it makes the game
genuinely faster to start for a real player rather than only moving a
measurement. Gate 1 stays open until it closes on merit. The window is
NOT to be re-tuned as a way of reaching the number; if a shorter window
later becomes justified BECAUSE the fixed cost fell, that is a different
and legitimate thing and must be stated as such.

**P1 -- pre-loop instrumented (patch 0105) and MEASURED on the machine.**
Measurement only, no behaviour change. `start_game()`
(`main/game_start.cpp`) makes the pre-loop's composition plain: between
`set_runtime_start()` and the first `GameTick()` there are exactly five
things, and each is now bracketed at its call site.

**HW-486-66, current binary + 0105, Trilby's Notes idle, sound-off
(`tests/harness/results/TNPRE1-2026-09-18/`):**

| pre-loop item | ms | share |
|---|---|---|
| `game_start` script | 13 | 0.4% |
| **`SetRestartPoint()`** | **690** | **22%** |
| **placeholder-room fade-out** | **611** | **20%** |
| **`load_new_room()`** | **1779** | **57%** |
| `first_room_initialization()` | 0 | 0% |
| **sum** | **3093** | vs `preloop_ms=3098` measured independently |

**The five brackets account for 3093 of 3098 ms -- essentially 100%, no
unexplained remainder.** (Contrast the per-tick investigation earlier in
this campaign, which took four rounds to get from 62% to accounted-for.)

*Two of the three real costs look like work no player benefits from, and
the source says why:*

- **`SetRestartPoint()`, 690 ms -- a save game written to disk at every
  startup.** It runs only for `loaded_game_file_version <
  kGameVersion_361_10`; Trilby's Notes (DataVersion 27, editor 2.62)
  qualifies, as will most of the compatibility-sweep library. This is
  the disk activity the operator noticed early in this campaign, now
  measured: it is I/O, and it is 22% of everything the whole-run gate
  can see.
- **The placeholder-room fade-out, 611 ms -- fading out a 1x1 bitmap.**
  `set_room_placeholder()` (`ac/room.cpp:1107-1119`) installs a
  `Bitmap(1, 1, 8)` dummy as the background and every mask; the call
  sits inside `if (displayed_room < 0)`, so by construction no real room
  has ever been displayed when it runs. There is provably nothing on
  screen to fade. Patch 0104 already made its steps cheap-per-step; what
  is left is mostly the fade's own 13-step pacing.
- **`load_new_room()`, 1779 ms** is the genuinely necessary half: CLIB
  read, decompression, sprite-cache population, room parse. Real work,
  and the hardest to attack.

*What removing them would be worth, at the CURRENT 5000-tick window
(steady 40.05, stalls 0.411 s, shutdown ~0.2 s):*

| | pre-loop | whole-run at N=5000 | break-even N |
|---|---|---|---|
| today | 3.098 s | 38.89 | 6851 |
| minus `SetRestartPoint` | 2.408 s | 39.10 | 5576 |
| minus placeholder fade | 2.487 s | 39.08 | 5722 |
| **minus both** | **1.797 s** | **39.29** | **4448** |

**Removing both would close Gate 1's whole-run half at the window we
already have -- 39.29 against the 39.2 the band needs -- with no window
change at all.** Reported with its own caveat: that is a **0.09 margin**
against a measured A-to-A spread of 0.06 at this window, i.e. passing but
only ~1.5 spreads clear of the edge. It would want confirming twice, and
`load_new_room` (57%, untouched by either) is where any comfortable
margin would have to come from.

**Both fixes are behaviour changes, so both are operator decisions, not
mine** -- and the plan's own design note already flagged the fade one as
such:

1. **Skip/short-circuit the placeholder fade-out when nothing has been
   displayed.** Visible effect: none that a player can observe (a 1x1
   dummy). The end state `play.screen_is_faded_out` must still be set so
   the following fade-in behaves identically. Lowest risk of the two.
2. **Skip or defer `SetRestartPoint()`.** Higher risk and genuinely
   semantic: the auto restart point is what makes `RestartGame` work on
   a pre-3.6.1 game that never sets one in script. Deferring it to first
   use would snapshot a LATER game state, which is not the same thing --
   so this is "accept slower startup" vs "change restart behaviour for
   old games", not a free win. Worth noting the sweep library is exactly
   those old games.

**Both generalise -- neither is Mach64-specific.** They are engine-level
startup work with no card involvement, so every port and every card
inherits the saving. Per the operator's stay-on-the-Mach64 direction
that makes them worth more than a card-specific win, and the benefit is
not confined to this gate: Shards of God's first-room load was measured
at ~3.7 s and its asset load ~2.5 s, and AGS Quest faces the same
dilution arithmetic when Gate 3's turn comes.

**Operator decisions 2026-09-18 (pre-loop):** (1) **Placeholder
fade-out: SKIP IT** -- approved, with the correctness requirement stated
as the test: the faded-out end state must still be established so the
first REAL room's fade-in is identical, proven through the fade rather
than at the settled frame. (2) **`SetRestartPoint()`: investigate a
semantics-preserving fix FIRST and report before implementing** -- a skip
was explicitly NOT approved, because `RestartGame` on a pre-3.6.1 game
that never calls it in script is exactly the sweep library (Trilby's
Notes, 5 Days, 7 Days, MMD) and this is heading for public release; a
functional regression there is not worth 690 ms.

**P1 -- patch 0106: the placeholder fade-out is skipped. Equivalence
PROVEN, and the win is real but marginal.**

*The correctness proof (DOSBox-X, one binary, the only difference the
call site, via a temporary no-skip arm that was reverted afterwards).*
Patch 0106 also adds a fade trace (`DOSAGS_FADE_TRACE=1`, off by
default): an FNV-1a hash of the 256-entry palette at each transition
step. A fade's visible output is fully determined by its palette
sequence, since `ScreenFadeSoftware` renders the scene to the back
buffer once in `Begin()` and never touches those pixels again -- so
matching per-step palettes mean the identical animation, which is a
stronger check than screenshots sampled at a few ticks.

- **The first real room's fade-in is IDENTICAL step-for-step** -- all 13
  palette hashes equal between arms. That is the requirement, met.
- **The placeholder fade-out's own 13 steps produce exactly ONE distinct
  palette hash.** It was fading black to black: the animation provably
  changed nothing on screen. Worth stating because it was *measured*,
  not merely argued from the 1x1 dummy.
- Trace count 33 -> 20: exactly the 13 placeholder steps removed and
  nothing else.
- Gate: Trilby's Notes validate PASS, BENCH8 all seven arms PASS with
  unchanged capture hashes, AGS Quest AutoPilot 18/18 with PH01-PH03
  matching the committed baseline.

| TNFB2 | **B** | **39.00** | 40.04 | **2472** | **1** | 710 |

**A mean 38.930, B mean 39.030, delta +0.100 against a pre-registered

throughout; clock cross-check 0.99997; all cells dated today with

*Prediction vs measurement, and the miss matters more than the hit:*

| | predicted | measured |
|---|---|---|
| placeholder fade | 611 -> 0 ms | **610 -> 1 ms** (hit) |
| preloop | 3098 -> ~2490 | **~2473** (hit) |
| whole-run | 38.93 -> ~39.08 | **39.03** (low by 0.05) |

**The unpredicted stall increase is what ate a third of the expected
gain, and it is flagged rather than smoothed over.** The 620 ms pre-loop
saving is unambiguous and tightly reproducible (3095/2888 -> 2475/2472).
But the B arm's stall tick -- the first real room's fade-IN, which this
patch does not touch -- rose from a rock-steady 411 ms in both A cells to

larger than the entire A-vs-B difference in means**, so the safest
reading is that removing the preceding fade-out changes where the
fade-in lands against tick/pacing boundaries, and that stall timing is
simply noisier than this campaign had assumed. It is NOT extra rendering:
`presents_real` is 23 and `presents_palette_only` 20 in every cell of

exactly the 13 placeholder presents no longer happening.

**Consequence worth acting on: a +0.10 delta measured on top of a term
that can move 213 ms is at the edge of what this window can resolve.**
Before leaning on small whole-run deltas again, stall variance should be
characterised (several repeats of one arm), or deltas should be taken on

(688 ms, unchanged and untouched by decision) and `load_new_room`
(~1775 ms).

**P1 -- `SetRestartPoint()` investigated (patch 0107, measurement only).
REPORTING BEFORE IMPLEMENTING, as instructed. The suggested in-memory
design does NOT work; a different, semantics-preserving fix does.**

*Where the slot is consumed -- every reader of
`RESTART_POINT_SAVE_GAME_NUMBER` (999):*

1. `restart_game()` (`ac/global_game.cpp:112`) -- `try_restore_save(999)`.
   The main consumer, and the behaviour that must not regress.
2. **`SetSaveGameDirectory()` (`ac/game.cpp:455-460`) -- copies the
   restart save as a FILE on disk** into the new directory if it exists.
   **This is the constraint that rules out an in-memory-only design:**
   something outside the save/restore path expects the file to be real.
3. `FillSaveList(saves, 0, 998, ...)` (`:352`) -- deliberately EXCLUDES
   999, so the save-slot UI never lists it. No dependency there.

*What the 690 ms actually is (HW-486-66, Trilby's Notes, TNRP1):*

| | ms |
|---|---|
| `GetDiskFreeSpaceMB()` (a statfs on DOS) | **0** |
| `create_savegame_screenshot()` | **0** (this game has OPT_SAVESCREENSHOT off) |
| **`SaveGame()` -- serialise + compress + write** | **686** |
| whole call | 688 |

**It is not I/O.** The restart save is **9,397 bytes**. Even at a
pessimistic 100 KB/s that is ~94 ms; at the 751 KB/s this machine's own
FTP transfer achieved, ~13 ms. So at least ~86% of the 686 ms is CPU,
and **the "serialise to memory now, flush to disk later" design saves
almost nothing -- the flush is already the cheap part.** The operator
anticipated exactly this possibility ("if it turns out to be mostly
CPU-side serialisation, an in-memory approach saves little and the
answer changes"), and it is what happened.

*What the CPU time IS, found with a zero-patch experiment using an
existing supported config key (`[misc] compress_saves`, `config.cpp:457`;
default true, `gamesetup.h:151`), TNRP2:*

| | restart point | of which `SaveGame` | pre-loop |
|---|---|---|---|
| compression ON (default) | 688 ms | 686 | 2476 ms |
| **compression OFF** | **194 ms** | **192** | **2050 ms** |

**Compression is 494 ms -- 72% of the restart point's cost.** And what it
buys, measured on the same game: the save is **9,397 bytes compressed vs
9,396 uncompressed**. **One byte.** AGS still runs the full compressor
pass over the state and achieves essentially nothing on a save whose
content is already dense binary structures and which carries no
screenshot.

*Proposed design -- semantics-preserving, and the narrowest form of it:*

**Do not compress the restart-point save.** Pass `false` rather than
`usetup.CompressSaves` in `save_game()` (`ac/game.cpp:1313-1315`) when
`slotn == RESTART_POINT_SAVE_GAME_NUMBER`. Everything the operator's
constraint list requires is preserved:

- The file still exists on disk, so consumer 2's directory copy is
  unaffected.
- `RestartGame` still works: the save format records its own compression
  and the loader handles either, so consumer 1 restores identically.
- The snapshot is still taken eagerly, at the same point, capturing the
  same pre-room state -- the thing that made deferral semantically wrong
  is untouched.
- Expected saving ~494 ms of the pre-loop; whole-run at the 5000-tick
  window would go ~39.03 -> ~39.15. **Still short of 39.2 on its own**
  -- `load_new_room` (~1775 ms) remains the last big term.

*Caveats I would want on record before this is approved:*

- **The "compression buys one byte" result is measured on ONE game with
  no save screenshot.** A game with `OPT_SAVESCREENSHOT` on puts a bitmap
  in the save, which IS compressible -- there the trade-off is real.
  Scoping the change to slot 999 keeps player saves compressed and
  confines the risk, which is why that narrow form is proposed over
  flipping the global default.
- A wider question this raises, NOT proposed here: if compression costs
  ~500 ms and saves ~nothing for screenshot-less saves, the DOS default
  for *player* saves may be wrong too -- but that is a user-visible
  disk-space trade and belongs to the operator, on evidence from more
  than one game.
- Both this and the change are engine-level and **generalise -- no card
  involvement**, so every port and every card inherits the saving.

**Not implemented. Awaiting the operator's decision.**

**Tooling trap, hit TWICE in one session and worth the line:
`git format-patch` run from the WRONG directory silently produces a
patch containing the wrong commit.** The vendor workflow is: edit
`vendor/<name>/`, commit THERE, then `git format-patch` THERE. Chaining
`cd <repo> && git format-patch` puts the repo's own last commit into
`patches/<vendor>/` under a plausible filename. It does not fail loudly
-- `git am` later reports a conflict in a patch whose subject is a
PLAN.md commit, which is the first visible symptom, and `git am --abort`
then resets the vendor tree to the pin and takes any uncommitted or
freshly-committed vendor work with it (recoverable from the reflog by
cherry-pick, but only if you look). Check `grep '^+++ b/'` on a new patch
file before trusting it: a vendor patch touches `Engine/...`, never
`PLAN.md` or `tests/`.

## Fixed timestep in benchmarking -- review, 2026-09-16

(Date note: this session's entries, records, and manifest dates say
2026-09-16, the UTC date; its git commits are stamped the evening of
2026-09-15 -0700. Same session either way -- read the two as one.)

Operator ask: "review the fixed timestep and make sure it is included
when we begin doing benchmarking." Reviewed the patches, every real-
hardware record since S0, and both tool paths (DOSBox-X and rig).
Findings first, then what changed.

**What exists.** `patches/ags/0047` implements the catch-up loop behind
`DOSAGS_FIXED_TIMESTEP=1` (env var, read once, default OFF -- unset/0 is
byte-for-byte the upstream 1:1 logic/render path), logs one line
`DOS-PORT fixed-timestep: ENABLED (logic decoupled from render)` /
`DISABLED (1:1 logic/render)` via `Debug::Printf` (so it lands in
`STDOUT.TXT` under `--log-stdout=+mgs:all`), and clamps catch-up at
`MAX_CATCHUP=5` (doskutsu's 0153 value). `0048` emits `DOS-PORT
tick_rate=<r> frames_skipped=<n>` right after the RUNMANIFEST block.
`0046` is the RenderCounter/LoopCounter decoupling both rest on.

**Consistency of the record so far.** Every KPI cell since S0 set the
flag by hand: the S7 OPL3/WB ABBA (2026-09-13), all S7 diagnostics, the
S7-GUS ABBA (SGA1/SGB1/SGB2/SGA2), and the 8/16/32-bit comparison
(TN8A1/TN8A2, S32B7, all DOSBox-X depth cells). Two kinds of record
deliberately do NOT have it and must never be compared against post-S0
fps numbers: the S2 PCM cell (a correctness cell, flag off on purpose,
noted in its own writeup) and every AGS Quest baseline before S0
(HW1/HW8/HW10, 9.62 fps -- 1:1 runs where low fps meant slow gameplay).

**Gaps found, and what was done about each (2026-09-16):**

1. `tools/port-game/port_game.py validate` never set the flag -- a
   manifest-driven run would have benchmarked slow gameplay. FIXED:
   `validate` sets `DOSAGS_FIXED_TIMESTEP=1` for every arm by default
   (`validate: fixed_timestep: false` is the explicit opt-out) and
   checks patch 0047's own log line in `STDOUT.TXT`
   (`checks.fixed_timestep`), so the record shows what ran, not what
   was requested. Confirmed under DOSBox-X: Trilby's Notes sound_off
   (witness ENABLED, tick_rate 31.95, frames_skipped 91) and both
   32-bit manifests from their own new `validate:` blocks (tick_rate
   37.94/37.47 for Shards' 32/16-bit arms, 33.79/30.26 for IOAWN4T's --
   mechanism only, never a performance number).
2. `tick_rate`/`frames_skipped` were never parsed by the tool; every
   manifest's `tick_rate` had been typed by hand from the log. FIXED:
   parsed from the `DOS-PORT` lines (plus `memory_min_free_kb`) and
   written by `record` into the `validated:` entry alongside `fps_p95`
   and `binary_sha12`.
3. `run-rig.sh` only ever passed the flag through `--env`; nothing
   defaulted it. CHANGED (bash -n checked only -- its real validation
   is the first rig run, which must show the `ENABLED` witness in
   `STDOUT.TXT`): `SET DOSAGS_FIXED_TIMESTEP=1` is emitted into RUN.BAT
   by default, `--no-fixed-timestep` opts out, an explicit `--env
   DOSAGS_FIXED_TIMESTEP=...` still wins (emitted later; DOS `SET` is
   last-writer-wins).
4. No tool checked the game-speed KPI itself. ADDED: a non-gating
   `game_speed_40hz` check (tick_rate within 40 +/- 2%) on every
   `validate`/`check` result -- informational on DOSBox-X, a real-
   hardware campaign's own acceptance line.
5. The RUNMANIFEST `env_block_sha` allowlist (patch 0038: `BLASTER`,
   `DOS_PORT_ENVIRONMENT`, `SDL_DOS_AUDIO_SB_SKIP_DETECTION`,
   `SDL_INVALID_PARAM_CHECKS`) predates 0047 and does not include
   `DOSAGS_FIXED_TIMESTEP`, `DOSAGS_FORCE_COLOR_DEPTH`,
   `DOSAGS_TAS_AUTO_EXIT_TICK`, or `SDL_HINT_DOS_AUDIO_BACKEND` -- two
   runs differing in game-speed semantics, depth, or MIDI backend hash
   to the same config fingerprint. FIXED the same day: `patches/ags/
   0077` extends the allowlist with all six (kept alphabetical per
   `runmanifest.h`'s contract; strings verified against the exact
   names `SDL_GetHint`/`gus_hint_is_one` read), `/sdldos:review`ed,
   and confirmed under DOSBox-X -- two otherwise-identical Trilby's
   Notes runs on the same build (`binary_sha12=c9ee2b121d04`) hash to
   `env_block_sha=098a64e57eea` with `DOSAGS_FIXED_TIMESTEP=1` and
   `5ebc5417d476` without, each with the matching ENABLED/DISABLED
   witness line. A run that sets none of the new names hashes exactly
   as before, so earlier records stay comparable to each other.
6. A real-hardware `record` path did not exist (only DOSBox-X
   `validate` fed `record`). ADDED: `port_game.py check --run-dir`
   applies the identical checks to a `run-rig.sh` collected dir; proven
   against the committed S32B7 logs (every gating check passes,
   tick_rate 0.32 parsed, game speed reported FAIL as it should).

**What the numbers already say for the 40fps push.** With
`MAX_CATCHUP=5`, one rendered frame can carry at most 6 logic ticks, so
game speed can only hold 40 ticks/s when rendered fps >= 40/6 = 6.67.
Every real 486-tier workload measured so far is below that floor
(Trilby's Notes idle 4.99 fps -> tick_rate 23.8; Shards 32-bit 0.05 fps
-> 0.32; AGS Quest stress 12.3 at HW11B). So on HW-486-66 the game-speed
KPI currently FAILS for every workload, and the fps target decomposes
into two: reach ~6.7 fps (game speed becomes correct, fps becomes purely
smoothness), then push toward 40. Raising `MAX_CATCHUP` trades input
latency and burstiness for a lower floor -- a legitimate, separate knob
to A/B on the rig, not something to change blind.

**Standing rule for every future benchmark cell (DOSBox-X or rig):** the
record must contain the `ENABLED` witness, `tick_rate`, and
`frames_skipped`; a cell without them is not a benchmark record.
`validate`, `check`, and `run-rig.sh` now produce that by default.

## Compatibility sweep -- design and first pass, 2026-09-15

**Scope of this pass (operator decision):** exactly six games -- the five
Game porting framework golden references (trilbysnotes, 5days, mmd,
shards, iowna) plus King's Quest III (Infamous Adventures, 2006, AGS
database page 734), already flagged in "Requested titles" above as
in-profile and testable now. The broader/commercial candidates that
survey also lists are explicitly out of scope for this pass.

**Why this milestone needed design before running anything:** the
Milestones list's own wording ("recording boots/title/first-room/
playable/complete/failure-reason per game") was written for games with
an AutoPilot module (AGS Quest's own shape). None of these six games
have source -- they are closed binaries -- so there is no scripted TAS
driver possible, and a passive boot-and-wait run cannot honestly claim
the later rungs. Each rung below is defined against something actually
observable through this harness's existing tooling, source-verified
against the pinned engine, not assumed:

- **boots**: `exit_code=0`, no crash, RUNMANIFEST present -- the same
  signal `port_game.py validate` already checks for these five games.
  Reused, not re-derived.
- **title**: a real screenshot, taken mid-run via
  `tests/harness/run-dosbox.sh --interactive` (private Xvfb,
  `DOSBOX_DISPLAY`) + `import -window root`, the same mechanism already
  precedented for AGS Quest's own title-screen capture (2026-09-10, see
  the tooling-findings table). Visually inspected this session, not
  hashed into a committed regression baseline (no source access means no
  `SaveScreenShot` call to pin the moment reliably the way AGS Quest's
  AutoPilot does) -- recorded as a one-time visual confirmation, with the
  screenshot's own file noted per game.
- **first-room**: `Engine/ac/room.cpp:573`'s `debug_script_log("Loading
  room %d", newnum)` is unconditional engine behavior (kDbgGroup_Game,
  kDbgMsg_Debug) -- not gated on AutoPilot -- and is already captured by
  every run because `run-dosbox.sh` unconditionally passes
  `--log-stdout=+mgs:all` (`kDbgMsg_All` == `kDbgMsg_Debug` per
  `Common/debug/out.h`, confirmed by reading the enum, not assumed from
  the flag's name). Every game logs at least one "Loading room" line for
  its own first room (title or otherwise) -- that alone is redundant
  with "boots". **first-room is defined as a SECOND, DIFFERENT room
  number appearing in that log before auto-exit fires** -- genuine
  evidence the engine advanced past its initial room into another one,
  which is the meaningful new fact this rung is supposed to add over
  "title".
- **playable / complete**: **NOT ATTEMPTED for any of the six games this
  pass.** No scripted input exists for a closed binary, and this harness
  has no generic, proven DOSBox-X input-injection layer for driving an
  unfamiliar game's GUI/menus blind (the one precedent, AGS Quest's own
  `xdotool` PLAY-button click, used coordinates and timing specific to
  that one game's own known layout). A passive run that merely waits at
  a title screen for `auto_exit_tick` to fire proves nothing about
  playability and would be a check that cannot distinguish success from
  failure -- recording a false "playable" this way is exactly the
  harness-invariants trap the dos-hardware-validation skill warns
  against. `failure_reason` for both rungs, every game: "no input-
  injection automation exists for binary-only games this pass; would
  need either per-game manual driving or a generic DOSBox-X input
  harness, neither built yet."

**Where results live:** each game's own `tests/games/<id>/manifest.yaml`
gets a `compat_sweep:` block (new, alongside the existing `validate:`/
`validated:` keys) recording per-rung results, the screenshot path, and
the auto_exit_tick/timeout used. `STATUS.md`'s milestone table gets the
six-game summary, consistent with how "Game porting framework" is
already tracked there. DOSBox-X only, no real hardware needed for this
rung set.

| Game | boots | title | first-room | playable | complete |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Trilby's Notes | PASS | PASS (room 1) | not reached | not attempted | not attempted |
| 5 Days a Stranger | PASS | PASS (room 1) | not reached | not attempted | not attempted |
| Maniac Mansion Deluxe | PASS | PASS (room 50) | not reached | not attempted | not attempted |
| Shards of God | PASS | PASS (room 0) | not reached | not attempted | not attempted |
| IOAWN4T | PASS | PASS (room 15) | not reached | not attempted | not attempted |
| 7 Days a Skeptic | PASS | PASS (room 0) | not reached | not attempted | not attempted |

Every game reaches exactly one room (its own title/start room, per
`STDOUT.TXT`'s `(room:N) Now in room N` line) and idles there,
`exit_code=0`, for the entire drive window -- consistent across all
five, and consistent with the honest expectation the design above set:
none of these games auto-advances its title screen without player
input, and this pass injects none. Full per-game detail (auto_exit_tick,
evidence line, failure_reason) in each game's own `manifest.yaml`
`compat_sweep:` block.

**A real methodology finding, not just a result:** the plan above left
open whether "title" should be a screenshot or a log signal. Screenshot
capture was attempted for Trilby's Notes (the fastest game to complete)
via `run-dosbox.sh --interactive` + `import -window root`, three tries
at t=5s, t=11s, and t=3s into the run. All three missed -- the entire
run (DOS boot, engine init, the 200-tick logic window, clean shutdown)
completes in **~7s of wall-clock time** under the fast conf, too narrow
a window for blind-timed screenshot sampling to reliably hit. Not
repeated for the other four games once the pattern was clear; "title"
for all five is grounded in the `STDOUT.TXT` room-line evidence instead,
which proved deterministic where screenshot timing did not. A real
per-game visual title check, if ever wanted, needs either a much longer
`auto_exit_tick` reserved just for this check or a tighter polling loop,
not a fixed sleep-then-shoot.
