**Decisions (operator, 2026-09-16):** build it with a Linux-native
headless pipeline from AGS's own tools, with the proven Wine Editor
`/compile` path as the cross-check (no Windows VM); license CC0 1.0 for
art/backgrounds/WAV/MIDI, this repo's MIT for scripts/project/tooling,
the already-verified OFL font (Press Start 2P). The spec is unchanged
from "What we need" above (320x200, 8-bit, one room/character/hotspot/
inventory object, one TTF slot actually used, MIDI + WAV, save/load via
GUI, nothing else, well under 1 MB) plus the additions below that make
it a benchmark fixture rather than only a milestone gate.

**Why it is now feasible without the Editor -- verified this session.**
AGS 3.6.3.13 ships a headless toolchain that builds natively on this
host from the pinned `vendor/ags` tree (`cmake -DAGS_BUILD_ENGINE=OFF
-DAGS_BUILD_TOOLS=ON -DAGS_BUILD_COMPILER=ON`; one gap: `Common/util/
stdio_compat.c` needs `-D_GNU_SOURCE` under `-std=c11` for `truncate()`,
passed via `CMAKE_C_FLAGS`, no source change): `agscc` (script
compiler, `Compiler/main.cpp`), `agf2dta` (`Game.agf` XML -> `game28.
dta`, `Tools/agf2dta`), `spritepak` (a directory of PNGs -> `acsprset.
spr` + index, with 8-bit palette storage and the Editor's compression
options), `crmpak` (create/import/export room files: backgrounds, the
four masks, compiled script), `agspak` (the CLIB packer). Smoke-tested
2026-09-16: `agscc --tell-api-versions` runs; `crmpak -l` lists the
Sierra template's `room1.crm` correctly (1 background 320x200x32, four
masks, 50 hotspots, compiled script); `crmpak -c` creates a minimal
room; `agf2dta` compiled the Empty Game project's `Game.agf` into a
7.8 KB `game28.dta`. What the toolchain does NOT cover: room DATA beyond
images and script -- hotspot names/event-handler bindings, object
placements/sprites, walkable-area properties, edges/starting positions.
Those live in the room file's main block, which only `Common/game/
room_file.cpp`'s `WriteRoomData()` writes, so the plan includes one
small tool of our own (`mkroom`, ~150 lines of C++ linked against the
same `libtools` the AGS tools use, reading a JSON room description)
rather than a Python reimplementation of the room format. Everything
else is AGS's own code.

**Package layout (`tests/fixtures/bench/`, committed):**

```
tests/fixtures/bench/
  README.md              spec as built, licenses, tool versions, verification log
  Game.agf               hand-authored XML (Editor 3.6.3 schema; no template content)
  GlobalScript.asc/.ash  our own minimal global script (GUI wiring, save/load)
  AutoPilot.asc/.ash     the TAS module (below)
  rooms/room1.json       mkroom input: hotspots, objects, walkables, edges, handlers
  rooms/room1.asc        room script
  assets/                CC0 PNG background + masks, sprites, WAV, MIDI, the OFL TTF,
                         generate_assets.py (generated/self-drawn, reproducible)
  tools/mkroom.cpp       JSON -> room1.crm via WriteRoomData (MIT)
  build.sh               host tools -> agscc/spritepak/mkroom/crmpak/agf2dta/agspak
                         -> BENCH8.ags, BENCH16.ags, BENCH32.ags
  BENCH8.ags BENCH16.ags BENCH32.ags   committed outputs (our content, < 1 MB each)
```

Three depth builds of the SAME content are deliberate: they give the
40fps push its same-content 8/16/32-bit curve (step 2 of the push) on a
package light enough to reach the rig in one transfer, instead of
sizing depth decisions off two different games (Trilby's Notes vs
Shards). `Game.agf`'s `<ColorDepth>` (Palette/HighColor/TrueColor) is
the only difference between builds; sprites are authored once as 32-bit
PNG with alpha plus an 8-bit paletted export against a fixed, committed
palette.

**TAS design (the benchmark contract).** AutoPilot is built in from day
one -- reuse the AGS Quest module's phase machine and its `AUTOPILOT
phase=<name> status=<begin|ok|fail> tick=<n> room=<n>` grammar so
`parse-results.py` and the RUNMANIFEST tooling work unchanged -- armed
by `--test`. AGS script cannot read the environment, so scene selection
comes from a small text file the harness stages next to the package
(`BENCH.CFG`, read with `File.Open` from `$APPDATADIR$` at boot):
`scene=<name>`, `hold_ticks=<n>`, `objects=<n>`. Scenes, each a fixed-
tick window with its own scene label in the log:

| Scene | What runs | What it isolates |
|---|---|---|
| `idle` | static room, cursor still, nothing animating | the present-path floor (full-frame blit/palette cost per depth) |
| `walk` | player walks a fixed path across the walkable area, crossing a walk-behind | character blit + walk-behind + dirty-rect coverage |
| `anim` | N always-animating objects (N from BENCH.CFG) | per-sprite cost scaling, the dirty-rectangle question |
| `text` | `Display`/`Say` with the TTF font, auto-advancing | alfont/FreeType rasterization + text overlay |
| `gui` | open/close the save/load GUI repeatedly | GUI redraw path |
| `audio` | MIDI clip + WAV on a loop | sound-on cost with a known melody (the Sound gate's pitch-track check applies) |
| `full` | look/interact hotspot (WAV), pick up, use inventory, save, restore, quit | the FULL_GAME functional gate; also the glitch regression capture |

Every scene ends with `SaveScreenShot("PHnn.BMP")` at a fixed tick so
DOSBox-X hashes gate correctness and real hardware compares pixel-for-
pixel (the AGS Quest harness proved Mach64 and DOSBox-X render
identically). `quit` emits RUNMANIFEST with the fixed timestep on
(default), so every cell yields `fps_p50/p95`, `tick_rate`,
`frames_skipped`, `memory_min_free_kb`, and the scene label.

**Glitch regression built in:** room 1 carries one 32-bit sprite with a
real alpha channel and one with the magenta mask color, both over a
light background, in the 16-bit build. Our pipeline (`spritepak`) keeps
the alpha in the package, so this exercises the ENGINE's load-time
alpha-to-mask conversion (`ReplaceHalfAlphaWithRGBMask` + Allegro
`KEEP_TRANS`) -- the path the 2026-09-16 investigation proved correct on
DJGPP (see "Black-box sprite glitch -- root cause, fix plan, test plan"
below; the AGS Quest boxes turned out to be Editor-import data, not
engine behaviour). Its `PH` capture is the standing regression for that
engine path.

**Verification ladder (the "known-working on a desktop AGS runtime
first" rule, all on Linux):** (1) the package built by our pipeline runs
on AGS's official Linux engine build (`/tmp/ags-linux-ref`, downloaded
from the same release in the seventh session; re-fetch and hash if
gone) through the AutoPilot `full` scene with a clean quit -- the
desktop-runtime check, no Windows needed; (2) the same source project
compiled by the Wine Editor `/compile` path (`tests/harness/setup-wine.
sh` already provides it) also runs `full` cleanly and its `inspect`
report matches ours on DataVersion/assets/fonts/clips -- the cross-check
that our hand-authored `Game.agf` is what the Editor would have
produced; (3) dosags under DOSBox-X, all scenes, hashes committed to
`tests/harness/expected/bench/`; (4) the rig.

**Work order (each slice buildable and committed on its own; no real
hardware until T6):**

- [ ] **T0 -- host tools.** `make host-tools`: builds `agscc`,
      `agf2dta`, `spritepak`, `crmpak`, `agspak` from `vendor/ags` into
      `build/host-tools/` with the `_GNU_SOURCE` flag (documented in the
      Makefile, not a source patch), plus `mkroom` from `tests/fixtures/
      bench/tools/`. Record the exact CMake invocation in the README.
- [ ] **T1 -- skeleton that boots.** Hand-authored `Game.agf` (320x200,
      Palette, one character with a 1-frame view, one font slot = the
      OFL TTF, empty GUI list), `GlobalScript`, `room1` from `mkroom`
      with a flat background and one walkable area, compiled with
      `agscc`, packed with `agspak`. Gate: `ags.exe` under DOSBox-X
      reaches `Initialize path finder` and renders the background -- the
      bar the Wine-compiled Empty Game reached in the seventh session.
- [ ] **T2 -- content to spec.** Background art, walk view, hotspot +
      interaction message, inventory item + pickup, save/load GUI, MIDI
      + WAV clips, all CC0 and generated/self-drawn under
      `assets/generate_assets.py` (extend the harness's generator, which
      already synthesizes the WAV chime and the MIDI tune). Gate: the
      milestone checklist's spec, every item exercised by hand under
      DOSBox-X once.
- [ ] **T3 -- AutoPilot + BENCH.CFG scenes.** Port the AGS Quest
      module's machinery, add the scene table, the PH captures per
      scene, the glitch sprites. Gate: all scenes `ok` on DOSBox-X,
      hashes committed.
- [ ] **T4 -- verification ladder (1) and (2)**, recorded in the README
      with engine version, command lines, and results. Gate: both
      reference runs quit cleanly through `full`.
- [ ] **T5 -- harness + framework wiring.** `tests/harness/packages/
      bench/PIN` (points at the in-repo source and its build), `tests/
      games/bench/manifest.yaml` with arms `depth8/depth16/depth32` x
      `sound_on/sound_off` and per-scene `validate:` recipes (`BENCH.CFG`
      staged via `--include-extra`), `expected/bench/dosbox-x.json`.
      Gate: `port_game.py validate --arm all` green from the manifest
      alone.
- [ ] **T6 -- first rig cells** (rig session): `idle`/`walk`/`anim` at
      8-bit, then 16 and 32, single cells, through `run-rig.sh` ->
      `check` -> `record`. These are the pre-registered baselines the
      40fps push optimizes against; the depth curve they produce is the
      input to the push's step 3 decision.
- [ ] **T7 -- milestone bookkeeping.** "Game package parses" / "First
      room renders" / PLAYABLE were claimed on AGS Quest; FULL_GAME is
      defined against THIS game -- claim it when `full` runs start-to-
      finish on real hardware. Update `LICENSE-REVIEW.md`'s test-game
      entry with the as-built licenses.

**Risks, named:** `agf2dta` may not write every field the pinned
engine's `game28.dta` reader expects for a 3.6.3 DataVersion (it is an
"AGS Team" v0.1.0 tool) -- the Wine cross-check in T4 is precisely the
detector; if it diverges, prefer fixing our `Game.agf` over patching
the tool. `mkroom` is the one piece of format code we own; keep it to
what `WriteRoomData` needs and cite `room_file.cpp` per field.
Template-derived content is the licensing trap the checklist already
names: nothing from `ags-template-source` goes into the package,
including default GUI sprites and cursors -- generate ours.

## Black-box sprite glitch -- root cause, fix plan, test plan, 2026-09-16

**Reproduced and root-caused on DOSBox-X (no rig needed), and it is NOT
a DOS port bug.** Full evidence trail: a read-only investigation this
session captured the AGS Quest harness's own `PH01-PH03.BMP` (room 3,
room 4, balcony) and found black rectangles around the player, the NPC
wizard, the chest, the frog, both tree-house door objects, the
chandelier, and the balcony objects -- GUI buttons and backgrounds
clean, every boxed pixel exactly `(0,0,0)` (16-bit `0x0000`), never the
`MASK_COLOR_16` magenta `0xF81F` a failed transparency test would
leave. Then the decisive control: AGS's official Linux 3.6.3.13 engine
(`ags64 --gfxdriver software`, the same package, the same AutoPilot)
produced `PH01-PH03` **sha256-identical** to the DOS captures -- zero
pixels differ -- and its OpenGL driver shows the same boxes. The DOS
engine renders this data exactly as upstream does. (The committed
baselines in `tests/harness/expected/agsquest/` enshrine the defect,
and the 2026-09-10 title-screen shots already showed the cursor boxed
on both engines -- present from the very first package build.)

**Mechanism, every link read in source:** upstream `ags-demo-game`
authors AGS Quest at `TrueColor` with 64 of 67 sprites
`AlphaChannel="True"`, `ImportMethod=LeaveAsIs` (no colour key).
`tests/harness/packages/agsquest/overlay/Game.agf.patch` flips the game
to `HighColor` (this port's 16-bit profile). Upstream gitignores
`acsprset.spr`, so the Wine `AGSEditor.exe /compile` step recreates
every sprite from its source PNG (`Editor/AGS.Editor/Tasks.cs:196-252`,
`RecreateSpriteFileFromSources`) -- and the Editor's import rule
(`Editor/AGS.Editor/Utils/SpriteTools.cs:369-375`, `AdjustImportParams`)
keeps a PNG's alpha channel ONLY for a TrueColor game. The source PNGs
have RGB-black under their alpha-0 pixels (e.g. `TreehouseBackDoor
Closed.png`: 3209 of 4620 pixels alpha 0, all black; the character
sheets mix alpha-0-black with genuine magenta). With alpha discarded and
no colour key, those pixels land in the package as opaque `0xFF000000`
(confirmed by decoding the package's `acsprset.spr` per
`Common/ac/spritefile.cpp`: door/chandelier slots `alpha0=0/N`, corners
`0xFF000000`; the sheets' magenta pixels are correctly `0x00FF00FF`).
Every engine then draws them, correctly.

**What this rules out (the section above this one, "Known graphical
glitch", carried the wrong lead):** doskutsu's `SDL_ConvertSurface`
colorkey-to-alpha trap cannot apply -- no `SDL_ConvertSurface` or
`SDL_SetSurfaceColorKey` call exists in `patches/ags/`, `vendor/ags/`,
or the SDL3-DOS backend's present path (patch 0029's `Present()` wraps
the finished virtual screen with `SDL_CreateSurfaceFrom` and does one
`SDL_BlitSurfaceScaled`; the backend's single colorkey use is its own
hardware-cursor emulation, which AGS never exercises since it hides the
SDL cursor and draws its own as a sprite). The engine's 32->16 sprite
preparation is also correct on DJGPP: `PrepareSpriteForUseImpl`
(`Engine/ac/draw.cpp:491-548`) -> `ReplaceHalfAlphaWithRGBMask` ->
`GfxUtil::ConvertBitmap` with `COLORCONV_KEEP_TRANS` (`Engine/gfx/
gfx_util.cpp:29-41`) -> Allegro `CONVERT_BLIT_EX` mapping
`bitmap_mask_color(src)` to `bitmap_mask_color(dest)` (`libsrc/allegro/
src/blit.c:137-160`) -> `masked_blit` via `vtable16` (all depth vtables
compiled, `libsrc/allegro/cmake/FileList.cmake`) -- and the same
sheets' magenta pixels ARE drawn transparent on DOS, so that path
demonstrably works. A DOS-side change that made the boxes disappear
would be masking a data defect and must be rejected.

**Fix plan (harness side, not the port):**

1. **Flatten alpha to the mask colour before the Editor compiles**
   (`tests/harness/build-package.sh`, after the overlay is applied):
   for every sprite source PNG the project references, rewrite alpha-0
   pixels (and alpha 1..127, matching the engine's own
   `ReplaceHalfAlphaWithRGBMask` threshold so the package equals what a
   TrueColor game would produce at load) to opaque `(255,0,255)`, the
   rest to opaque RGB. Header comment cites the Editor rule and the
   PNG facts above. Keeps the 16-bit profile every harness and real-HW
   number rests on. No sprite in the package uses soft alpha edges
   (`semi-alpha=0` on every PNG checked), so nothing is lost. **In
   progress this session** -- see the harness README once it lands.
2. Do NOT "fix" it by building AGS Quest at TrueColor: that changes the
   profile every recorded number was taken under. Building TrueColor
   and running with `DOSAGS_FORCE_COLOR_DEPTH=16` (patch 0076) is a
   valid one-off CONFIRMATION of the diagnosis (the engine's own
   load-time alpha handling then produces clean sprites), not the fix.
3. Retire the "Known graphical glitch" section's SDL-colorkey lead
   (done below in that section) and note in `tests/harness/README.md`'s
   slice-5 baseline rule that the pre-fix baselines contained this
   defect -- the "look at the actual image before trusting it" step was
   done, and the boxes were mistaken for content.

**Test plan:**

- DOSBox-X (the correctness gate): rebuild the package, run the harness,
  convert `PH01-PH03` and LOOK: no boxes around any of the sprites
  listed above, no magenta fringes, no hard edges that were soft before
  (none expected). All three `expected/agsquest/dosbox-x.json` hashes
  WILL change; re-baseline only after that inspection, in the same
  commit as the build-script change, with the before/after PNG
  comparison described in the commit message (images themselves are
  never committed -- NC-ND art).
- Reference cross-check: the official Linux engine on the rebuilt
  package must again be byte-identical to the DOS `PH0n.BMP` -- this
  is the proof the fix changed data, not engine behaviour.
- Regression: the DOS harness's 18 phases stay green and tick-for-tick
  identical (the fix touches pixels, not logic); `parse-results.py`
  reports the three hashes as changed and nothing else.
- Real hardware (rig session, queued): `expected/agsquest/realhw.json`
  goes stale with the DOSBox-X hashes; one `run-rig.sh agsquest` cell
  re-establishes it. The AGS Quest fps baselines are unaffected in
  meaning (same sprite count and sizes; opaque black vs transparent
  pixels cost the same in `masked_blit` only if the mask test is
  per-pixel either way -- it is), but record the re-baselined cell's
  fps next to HW10/HW11 rather than assuming.
- Standing regression for the class of bug: the self-authored test game
  (plan above) ships one 32-bit alpha sprite and one magenta-keyed
  sprite in its 16-bit build, packed by OUR pipeline (which keeps alpha
  in the package, so the ENGINE's load-time conversion is what gets
  exercised -- the path proven correct here). If a future engine or
  Allegro change breaks `ReplaceHalfAlphaWithRGBMask`/`KEEP_TRANS`, that
  capture's hash catches it; the AGS Quest fix above guards the OTHER
  failure mode (data authored without alpha), which the Editor-built
  harness package is the right fixture for.

## Game porting framework -- decided 2026-09-11

**Purpose**: turn "make AGS game X run on dosags" from hand work into a
repeatable pipeline -- a per-game manifest in, a DOS-runnable package
plus a validation record out -- so adding a title is a manifest and a
run, not a session. The five golden references above are its first
inputs and its standing regression fixtures. Lives in this repo
(`tools/port-game/`, Python, the `build_fixture.py` precedent) because
every stage is AGS-format-specific; nothing here belongs in `shared/`.

**Stages** (each a subcommand; `all` chains them):

1. `inspect` -- parse the game's data (from a `.ags`, or the CLIB
   appended to a Windows `.exe`, per the engine's own game-data search):
   `DataVersion` (must be >= `kGameVersion_250` = 18, else stop with
   "needs an Editor re-save"), resolution and color depth (against the
   v0.1 8/16-bit profile; 32-bit games are flagged, not converted), the
   full `ScriptAudioClip` table with each clip's `fileType` and size,
   fonts (TTF/WFN), and the presence of `audio.vox`/`speech.vox`. Emits
   a report; this is also the survey tool for the "verify locally" gaps
   above.
2. `convert` -- audio per the manifest's policy: OGG/MP3 -> WAV at the
   device tier (11025 Hz mono, 8- or 16-bit per the manifest, `ffmpeg`
   on the host); tracker -> native or pre-rendered per decision 5 once
   made; MIDI and WAV/VOC pass through (WAV/VOC resampled to the tier
   only if above it). Speech packs (`speech.vox`) follow the same rule.
3. `repack` -- rewrite the CLIB v30 pack with the converted assets and
   patch each converted clip's `fileType` byte (anchored on its 15-byte
   `fileName`; names never change, so `v361_objnames` stays valid).
4. `layout` -- the DOS directory: `<NAME8>.AGS`, `acsetup.cfg` with the
   DOS defaults (tier, backend hint, `--user-data-dir`-equivalent), a
   `RUN.BAT` matching `run-rig.sh`'s shape (tags, log redirection, the
   `C:\VGACAP\MODE12` restore), all 8.3-safe.
5. `validate` -- DOSBox-X boot-to-title + `DOSAGS_TAS_AUTO_EXIT_TICK`
   (patch 0044) + RUNMANIFEST + a title-screen capture hash; then the
   same on the rig via `run-rig.sh`. Binary-only games have no autopilot
   module, so driving is limited to: the auto-exit tick, optionally a
   short per-game input script in the manifest (DOSBox-X `xdotool` /
   rig `vcctrl` keys -- the one place the harness's "no OS-level input"
   rule is relaxed, because there is no script hook to use instead), and
   `--loadsavedgame` where a save is available. Title-screen music +
   idle fps is enough for the Sound gate's audio verdict and the
   sound-on/off ABBA.
6. `record` -- `tests/games/<id>/manifest.yaml` (id, verified source URL,
   license as read, pinned file hash, expected `DataVersion`/res/depth,
   audio policy, driving recipe, expected capture hashes) plus a
   `results/` record per run. Game data never enters git.

**Milestone**: added to the Milestones list as "Game porting framework"
between Sound and the Compatibility sweep, since the sweep consumes it.
Gate: all five golden references run `inspect` -> `validate` on DOSBox-X
end to end from their manifests alone, and the three in-profile ones
have a real-hardware `results/` record.

## Fixed timestep and the fps KPI -- decided 2026-09-11

**Operator decision**: AGS's native rate is 40 fps (`GetGameSpeed()`
default; the harness already scales its waits by it). The rendered-fps
KPI targets 40 and tracks how close each hardware tier gets, like
doskutsu -- but **games must run at the correct speed even when fps is
below target**: a fixed-timestep mode like doskutsu's, so a game plays
and feels right at 20 rendered fps instead of running at half speed.

**Why this changes the KPI**: AGS ties one script tick to one render pass
at the `SetGameSpeed()` rate (recorded when the KPIs were pre-registered),
so today low fps IS slow gameplay. The HW10 run proved it with numbers:
tick-counted phase durations matched DOSBox-X exactly while wall-clock
metrics diverged ~10x -- the 486 was running game logic at whatever rate
it could render, not at 40 ticks/s. Under a fixed timestep the logic rate
is pinned at 40 ticks/s wall-clock and rendering skips frames to keep
up, so the fps number becomes purely a smoothness measure and game speed
becomes a separate, hard PASS/FAIL.

**KPI amendment (supersedes the "primary KPI" framing of 2026-09-10)**:
- *Game speed* (new, hard requirement): measured logic ticks per wall-
  second on the in-profile package on HW-486-66 = 40 within a
  pre-registered tolerance (+/- 2%), from a new RUNMANIFEST-adjacent
  `DOS-PORT tick_rate` line; FAIL below that regardless of fps.
- *Rendered fps* (the tracked KPI): target 40 = native; p50/p95 from the
  existing sampler, per tier; the PASS band for HW-486-66 is still set
  from the first in-profile datum, as before. A `frames_skipped` count
  goes next to `tick_rate` so a run at 40 ticks/s and 12 fps is visible
  as exactly that.
- The secondary KPIs (room-transition latency, memory, audio glitch-
  freeness, input latency) are unchanged.

**Design constraints, read from the engine (not yet designed)**: every
blocking wait already runs `GameTick()` -> `UpdateGameOnce(true)` and
the single frame wait `WaitForNextFrame()` (see the Sound section's
pump facts), so the catch-up loop has one place to live; `render_
graphics()` is called from inside `UpdateGameOnce`, so "skip render" has
to be threaded through it rather than bolted on outside; `Game.
TickCounter` must keep advancing once per logic tick (the harness and
save games depend on it); a catch-up cap (doskutsu's value, once read)
keeps a stall from turning into a burst. **First step of the slice is to
read doskutsu's own fixed-timestep patches and `UpdateGameOnce`/`render_
graphics`/`WaitForNextFrame` in full, not to design from this summary.**

- [x] **S0** -- fixed timestep + `tick_rate`/`frames_skipped`
      instrumentation (one vendor patch each, `/sdldos:review`ed);
      confirmed on DOSBox-X (ticks stay at their un-stalled baseline
      under an artificial render stall) and then on HW-486-66 against
      AGS Quest, where the existing HW1/HW8/HW10 records gave the
      before-numbers. Lands before any Sound fps measurement. **Done
      (thirteenth session)**: `patches/ags/0046` (RenderCounter/
      LoopCounter decoupling, a prerequisite refactor), `0047` (the
      catch-up loop itself -- `DOSAGS_FIXED_TIMESTEP=1`, default off),
      `0048` (the RUNMANIFEST `tick_rate`/`frames_skipped` line).
      DOSBox-X: a temporary, never-committed artificial-render-stall
      diagnostic showed tick rate held at its un-stalled baseline
      (~32-33/s) while rendered fps correctly dropped to ~18 under a
      50ms-per-render stall, vs. the flag-off path where the whole run
      took ~2x as long under the identical stall. HW-486-66 (tags
      HW11A/HW11B, real numbers, no artificial stall needed -- this
      hardware is already too slow for the 40Hz target): `tick_rate`
      rose 6.54->12.32 (+88%) and the same AutoPilot sequence completed
      in `duration_s` 486->266 (~45% less real time) with all
      phases/screenshots/`dialog` `chosen=14` unchanged. See "Current
      state (2026-09-11, thirteenth session)" above for the full
      write-up, including a real accumulator-design bug (a private
      wall-clock delta double-counting a nested dialog-options loop's own
      ticks) caught and fixed before landing.

## First test game selection criteria

Not popularity -- the smallest thing that actually exercises the engine:
320x200 preferred, older AGS-version game format, simple scripts, few
plugins, no Theora video, no OGG if avoidable, small package, one room /
one character / one hotspot / one inventory object, MIDI + WAV sound,
save/load, freely redistributable or legally obtainable, known-working on
a desktop AGS runtime first (rules out a game that's already broken
upstream).

**Font: TrueType via the vendored alfont/FreeType wrapper, decided
2026-09-10** -- chosen over AGS's legacy bitmap (WFN) fonts despite the
extra unmeasured perf variable it adds to the very first KPI datum (see
"Performance KPIs" above). TTF-via-alfont is the path most real-world AGS
games actually ship with, so measuring the DOS port's real target
workload from the start outweighs isolating the very first fps datum to
a zero-rasterization-cost text path. This also makes alfont's default
(non-`ALFONT_DOS`) charset-rendering correctness -- already an open
test-game question, see "Open questions" below -- load-bearing for the
chosen game specifically, not just a hypothetical: confirm it renders
correctly once the test game exists, not merely that it compiles.

**Scoping research done 2026-09-10 (sixth session, not yet built) --
reaffirms self-authoring, with a concrete tooling path.** A subagent
survey of real existing candidates and of headless/non-Editor tooling
options, reported here rather than re-derived later:

- **No existing game fits.** Checked the official
  `adventuregamestudio/ags-demo-game` ("AGSQuest", 2024): 4 rooms not 1,
  OGG audio not MIDI+WAV, no TTF font anywhere in the repo (WFN only),
  and its own `LICENSE.md` splits script (0BSD) from art (**CC BY-NC-ND
  4.0** -- non-commercial, no-derivatives, verified by reading the file
  directly). Checked `adventuregamestudio/ags-demo-quest-old` ("Demo
  Quest", early-2000s): actually matches the MIDI+WAV criterion (5 MIDI +
  24 WAV) but has **no LICENSE file anywhere in the repo** -- unverifiable,
  disqualifying per this project's own never-guess-a-license policy --
  and is 20 rooms of deprecated-API-era content regardless. The official
  starter templates (`ags-template-source`) are empty shells with no
  license file either; using one still means authoring everything
  ourselves with no real head start. No itch.io/indiedb game was found
  with an explicit, verifiable permissive license and matching scope.
- **No headless/CI compiler independent of the Windows Editor exists.**
  The Editor does have a real CLI flag, `AGSEditor.exe /compile
  path\to\Game.agf` (documented, CI-oriented, real exit codes), and a
  third-party wrapper (`ericoporto/agstoolbox`, `atbx build`) automates
  it -- but both `ags-demo-game` and `ags-template-source`'s own
  currently-working CI (`build.yml`) run this on `windows-latest` GitHub
  Actions runners, not Linux. Upstream GitHub issues #872 and #1100
  (decoupling a standalone compiler from the Editor) exist but were never
  implemented. Wine LITERATURE (old forum threads, the AGS wiki's own
  Linux page: "WINE does not work very well") is real but not
  encouraging -- see below for what an actual first-hand attempt found,
  which is a materially different, more encouraging picture.
- **Update, seventh session (2026-09-10): a real, first-hand Wine attempt
  got substantially further than the literature above predicted.** Not
  just re-citing old forum reports -- a subagent actually ran it, in a
  strictly time-boxed session, in this environment (`wine-10.0` (Debian),
  a fresh `WINEPREFIX`, `winetricks`'s `dotnet46` verb chain -- needed
  `cabextract` via `apt`, not preinstalled -- then the portable
  `AGS-3.6.3.13-RC2.zip` build against `ags-template-source`'s "Empty
  Game" template): under a bare Wine invocation with no `DISPLAY`,
  `/compile` silently no-ops (exit 0, empty log, no output -- a false
  negative from the missing display, not a real signal; don't mistake
  this for "Wine works" or "Wine fails" on its own). Under `xvfb-run`,
  **the Editor genuinely launches, initializes WinForms/.NET, loads the
  project, and runs the real AGS compiler** -- it fails with
  `AGS: The player character cCharacter has StartingRoom set to room -1
  which does not exist` / "There were compilation errors.", exit code 1
  -- a real, semantically-meaningful AGS game-data validation error (the
  Empty Game template needs a starting room assigned, a genuine project-
  setup gap), not a Wine crash, not a .NET failure, not a silent no-op.
  This is well past what the 2010-era forum report and the wiki's "does
  not work very well" line described. **Not yet proof of a working
  compile path** -- no `.ags` was produced this run, and this project's
  own "known-working on a desktop AGS runtime first" rule means even a
  future successful Wine compile still needs its output verified against
  a real/known-good AGS runtime before being trusted for anything. Worth
  a real follow-up (assign a starting room, retry) before either
  accepting or discarding Wine as a viable path -- genuinely open again,
  not settled either way. See PATCH-SEQUENCE.md-style discipline: this
  updates a documented conclusion with first-hand verification rather
  than leaving the older, now-superseded literature-only claim standing
  unchallenged.
- **Follow-up, same session: a real compile actually succeeded.** Root
  cause of the StartingRoom error above: the official "Empty Game"
  template genuinely ships ZERO rooms (`<Rooms>` empty, `StartingRoom`
  -1, no `.crm` files anywhere in the template) -- the interactive
  Editor's own "New Game" wizard normally scaffolds a default `room1.crm`
  on project creation, a step the raw checked-in template + `/compile`
  CLI path skips entirely. Fix: copied `room1.crm`/`room1.asc` from
  `ags-template-source`'s OTHER official template ("Sierra-style", which
  does ship a real room) into the Empty Game project, hand-patched
  `Game.agf`'s `<UnloadedRooms>`/`StartingRoom` to reference it -- both
  trivial text edits (`.agf` is XML), no binary authoring needed.
  Recompiling under the same `wine-10.0` + `winetricks dotnet46` +
  `xvfb-run` setup (no new environment setup needed) produced
  `AGS: Compilation successful!`, exit 0, and a REAL, non-empty `.ags`
  file (111,459 bytes, real `CLIB` header + asset filename table --
  confirmed by reading the header bytes directly, not just the file's
  existence). **This materially changes the "no credible Wine compile
  path" conclusion above**: a real AGS project (official template +
  a trivial hand-patched room reference) compiles end-to-end under Wine,
  non-interactively, on this Linux host -- contrary to the literature
  survey's "no successful modern (2020s) report" finding. Two things this
  does NOT yet establish, both genuinely open: (1) whether the compiled
  package is actually valid/playable -- nothing has run it on any AGS
  runtime yet, real or emulated, per this project's own "verify, don't
  trust the file existing" rule; (2) whether the INTERACTIVE Editor GUI
  (room designer, sprite/font/audio import, the actual authoring surface
  the real first test game needs) is usable under Wine at all -- only the
  non-interactive `/compile` CLI path was exercised here. If GUI
  automation under Wine+Xvfb turns out viable too, this could remove the
  Windows-VM dependency for authoring the real first test game entirely,
  not just for compiling an already-authored one -- a decision for a
  future session, not assumed here. Everything for this finding lives
  under `/tmp/wine-ags-test` (not committed anywhere) -- nothing in this
  repo or the hub changed as a result of it.
- **Follow-up: ran the Wine-compiled package under dosags's real `ags.exe`
  in DOSBox-X (still not committed -- local verification only).** Real,
  clean, informative result: the engine correctly parses this genuine
  Windows-Editor-produced package (`Game data version: 3060310`,
  `Compiled with: 3.6.3.13`, real GUID `{8e93a1f9-...}`, `Game title:
  'Empty Game'`) all the way past `engine_init_gamedata()` and into
  graphics-mode setup -- the first time any REAL (non-synthetic) package
  has reached that point on this port -- then fails cleanly and exactly
  as this port's own v0.1 compatibility profile predicts:
  `Game native resolution: 320 x 200 (32 bit)`, `Failed to init gfx
  mode. Error: Display colour depth not supported: 32`. The Empty Game
  template defaults to `<ColorDepth>TrueColor</ColorDepth>`; this port's
  `ali3dsw.cpp` window-surface driver only supports 8-bit/16-bit by
  design (32-bit is explicitly deferred, program-doc section 17 /
  `PLATFORM-SURFACE.md`'s tl;dr). **This is the compatibility-profile
  boundary working as intended, not an engine bug** -- confirms this
  port's own scope decision against a real, externally-produced package
  for the first time, not just its own synthetic fixtures. An 8-bit
  recompile attempt of the same template is a natural, tightly-scoped
  next step (in progress/deferred depending when this session ends) --
  see whether it changes this row.
- **Follow-up: an 8-bit recompile worked cleanly, and running it reached
  deep into real room-loading logic for the first time ever, with an
  independent reference-engine cross-check.** The real project-level enum
  (`AGS.Types.GameColorDepth`, read from the Editor's own source, not
  guessed: `Palette=1` = 8-bit, `HighColor=2` = 16-bit, `TrueColor=4` =
  32-bit) has no XML override, so `Game.agf`'s `<ColorDepth>TrueColor
  </ColorDepth>` -> `<ColorDepth>Palette</ColorDepth>` was a one-line
  edit; recompiling under the same working Wine pipeline produced a real
  8-bit `.ags` with only a benign driver-suitability warning -- the
  template's own default 32-bit-alpha GUI/cursor sprites did NOT block
  compilation or cause a depth-mismatch error. Running this package
  against `dosags`'s real `ags.exe` under DOSBox-X: `Game native
  resolution: 320 x 200 (8 bit)`, `Window surface pixel format:
  SDL_PIXELFORMAT_INDEX8` -- past every prior blocker -- **`Initialize
  sprites` succeeds silently for the first time ever on any real
  (non-synthetic) package** (patch 0039's 4 MB sprite-cache default
  finally exercised against a real `acsprset.spr` for the first time),
  followed by `Engine initialization complete`, `Starting game`,
  `Initialize path finder` -- deep into real room-setup logic, well past
  every milestone this port has reached before. The process then runs
  continuously (high, sustained CPU, no further log output) rather than
  exiting -- consistent with a real, silent interactive game loop, not a
  hang, confirmed two independent ways: (1) AGS's own official prebuilt
  Linux engine (`ags_3.6.3.13_linux.tar.gz`, downloaded fresh from the
  same GitHub release, a genuine independent reference implementation,
  not Wine and not this DOS port) run against the byte-identical `.ags`
  package reaches the exact same last log line (`Initialize path finder`)
  and then goes equally silent; (2) a real screenshot of each engine's
  actual rendered frame (DOS: DOSBox-X's own internal `Capture ->
  Take screenshot`, bypassing the X11 compositing problems a bare Xvfb-
  without-window-manager display has for a plain X screenshot tool --
  see the tooling note below; reference: `import -window` against the
  reference engine's real GL window) shows the SAME solid flat blue
  color on both, pixel-for-pixel indistinguishable by eye -- proving this
  port's own room rendering is CORRECT, not broken, and that the flat
  color is this minimal, hand-patched test room's own real (if visually
  uninteresting) content, not a rendering bug. **This is real,
  independently-cross-checked evidence this port is at or very near the
  "Game package parses, reaches initial room setup" milestone** against
  a real (if generic, unlicensed, hand-patched-together, not-yet-spec-
  compliant) package -- `dos_status`/the Milestones checkbox is
  deliberately NOT changed this session per this session's own explicit
  instruction; a future session should decide whether this counts or
  whether the milestone still wants the real spec-compliant authored
  game first. Tooling note worth keeping: a bare `Xvfb` with no window
  manager makes `xdotool windowactivate`/`getactivewindow` fail
  (`_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW` unsupported) -- `windowfocus`/`getwindowfocus`
  work fine without a WM (raw `XSetInputFocus`, no EWMH needed), and a
  plain X screenshot tool (`scrot`/`import -window`) can silently return
  stale/blank content for a window whose real content isn't composited
  into the normal X drawable in this setup -- DOSBox-X's OWN internal
  capture (`Capture` menu / `F12+P`) is authoritative for this port's
  windows regardless. Also confirms (accidentally, the hard way): running
  `dosbox-launch.sh` with a bare `--fast` (no `--stage`) mounts the repo
  root itself as `C:\` -- a real save file (`AGSSAVE.999`) and copied
  test binaries leaked into the actual working tree this way and had to
  be cleaned up by hand; a future interactive session should prefer
  `--stage` or stage into a scratch dir outside the repo to avoid this.
  Everything for this finding (the Wine pipeline, the compiled packages,
  the reference-engine download) lives under `/tmp` -- nothing committed
  to this repo or the hub as a result.
- **Recommendation, reaffirming the 2026-09-10 review decision above**:
  author the test game ourselves, on a real Windows environment (a VM is
  enough -- doesn't need to be the DOS dev box), not by fighting Wine on
  this Linux box. Self-authoring also sidesteps the licensing-verification
  problem entirely (the project picks its own license, e.g. matching this
  repo's own MIT license) and is the only path that guarantees a TTF font
  asset exists at all -- no real candidate game found in this research
  ships one. Concrete next action: get access to a Windows VM with .NET,
  install an AGS Editor build compatible with the pinned `v3.6.3.13`
  engine revision (`atbx install editor <version>` can automate fetching
  one, itself Windows-only), and hand-build to spec: 320x200, 8-bit, one
  room/character/hotspot/inventory object, one TTF font assigned to an
  in-game font slot, MIDI + WAV, save/load exercised via the default GUI.
  Commit the compiled game data (and ideally the `.agf` source project) to
  `tests/fixtures/` under a license this project chooses. Time-boxed Wine
  fallback only if Windows access is genuinely unavailable, expecting the
  documented compile-step failure mode may still apply -- treat any Wine
  success as needing desktop-runtime verification before trusting it, per
  this section's own "known-working on a desktop AGS runtime first" rule.

### What we need (concrete checklist, written 2026-09-10 after the research above)

**The Windows environment (one-time, authoring only -- the port itself
stays a Linux/DJGPP/DOSBox-X workflow):**

- Any Windows install that runs the AGS Editor: a .NET Framework WinForms
  app (the Wine recipe found in research installs .NET Framework 4.6 via
  `winetricks dotnet46` -- confirm the exact requirement from the 3.6.3
  Editor's own download page/release notes before provisioning, don't
  assume). A VM is fine; no GPU, no DOS, no DOSBox-X involvement.
- An AGS Editor build from the **same 3.6.3 release line as the pinned
  engine** (`v3.6.3.13`), so the game-data format it emits is exactly what
  the pinned engine expects. An older 3.6.x Editor would also produce
  readable data (the engine reads older formats), but not a 4.x one --
  `ags4` is a separate parallel line the pinned `ags3` engine does not
  target (see the hub's `ports.yaml` pin note). `atbx install editor
  <version>` (ericoporto/agstoolbox, Windows-only) can fetch a pinned
  build; AGS's own release page is the alternative.
- A way to get files out of the VM (shared folder / scp) into this repo.
- The desktop verification comes free: the Editor bundles the matching
  Windows engine, so "Run" (F5) inside the Editor IS the "known-working on
  a desktop AGS runtime first" check -- walk, interact, pick up, hear
  MIDI + WAV, save, load, all working there before the package goes
  anywhere near DOS.

**The game itself (build to this spec and nothing more):**

- 320x200, 8-bit (256-color palette). **The former "known wrinkle" here is
  resolved (seventh session, Measured Constants)**: a synthetic 320x200x8
  fixture confirmed both real paths work cleanly under this DOSBox-X
  setup -- the default fullscreen-desktop path (window sized to the
  640x480 desktop, game's native size applied only as the virtual
  screen) and the exact 1:1 `--windowed --gfxfilter stdscale 1` path
  (which genuinely does render at 320x200x8, via the vendored SDL DOS
  backend's own always-present classic VGA "Mode 13h" entry -- no VESA
  BIOS mode involved at all, so the earlier "no 320x200 VESA mode" record
  doesn't apply to this path the way it reads). No fallback/XRGB8888
  surface was observed on either path. Still worth keeping a 320x240
  variant of the real project as a diagnostic control per this note's
  original reasoning, and worth a real video-capture screenshot once
  320x200 is actually load-bearing (a real room rendering) -- the
  synthetic-fixture confirmation used log evidence only.
- One room: one paletted background, one walkable area.
- One player character with a real (if tiny) walk view -- this is what
  makes `acsprset.spr` a real sprite file, the thing the next milestone
  needs.
- One hotspot with a scripted interaction (look/interact shows a message)
  -- exercises the script VM and room events.
- One inventory object that can be picked up -- exercises inventory.
- One **TrueType** font imported and assigned to a font slot that displayed
  text actually uses (normal text and/or speech), not merely present in
  the package -- this is the alfont/FreeType decision above made real.
  The `.ttf` itself must be freely redistributable (e.g. an OFL font),
  license verified by reading its own license file.
- MIDI background music started on room load, one WAV sound effect on the
  hotspot interaction. MIDI + WAV only -- no OGG, no MP3. (Audio is still
  stubbed in this DOS build, so nothing will be audible under DOSBox-X
  yet; the assets exist so the package parses and so the Sound milestone
  has something real to play later.)
- Save/load reachable through the game's GUI -- the "Sierra-style"
  template's default GUI has it; "Empty Game" does not.
- Nothing else: no plugins, no Theora, no `speech.vox`, no translations,
  no custom dialog system. Total package well under 1 MB.

**Licensing checkpoint before anything is committed:**

- Decide the license up front so every asset is made under it -- e.g.
  MIT matching this repo's own `LICENSE`, or CC0 for the art/audio.
  Record it in `LICENSE-REVIEW.md`.
- **Template-derived content is the trap**: the official templates
  (`ags-template-source`) had no LICENSE file in the research, and a game
  started from "Sierra-style" or even "Empty Game" inherits default GUI
  sprites, cursors, and global-script boilerplate from it. Before
  committing, inventory what template-derived content actually ended up
  in the package and find its real terms (the Editor's own license/docs
  may state them -- read them); if that can't be resolved, replace the
  template-derived assets with hand-made ones. Never guess.
- Same for the font, MIDI, and WAV: self-made, or a verified-free source
  with its license file read and recorded.

**Deliverables into this repo (`tests/fixtures/<game-name>/`):**

- The compiled game package (the single `.ags` CLIB the Editor emits --
  in 3.6.x it contains `game28.dta`, `acsprset.spr`, rooms, fonts, and
  audio; nothing needs staging separately), named 8.3-safe for DOS.
- The source project too (`Game.agf`, `*.asc`/`*.ash`, `*.crm`, the raw
  background/sprite/font/audio assets), so it can be rebuilt.
- A README recording: Editor version used, the exact spec above as
  built, the license(s), and the desktop-runtime verification actually
  performed (what was exercised, in which Editor/engine version).

Not built yet -- this is scoping, not a decision to start building this
session (see "Current state" above).

## Open questions / risks

- **Decisions taken in the 2026-09-10 plan review** -- recorded so they
  are not re-litigated by a later session; the reasoning is in
  `PATCH-SEQUENCE.md`'s tl;dr: (1) the DOS graphics driver presents via
  `SDL_GetWindowSurface`, not `SDL_Renderer`, from the start; (2) v0.1
  targets 8-bit and 16-bit games (32-bit later); (3) the build patches
  AGS's own CMake and drives it from this port's Makefile through the SDL
  DJGPP toolchain file -- the hub `ports.yaml` note that said "DJGPP needs
  its own hand-written Makefile regardless" predates
  `shared/build/sdl3-dos.mk` and has been corrected; (4) the first test
  game is authored by us. Standing policy restated: nothing here is ever
  contributed upstream to AGS (see `CLAUDE.md`).
- **SDL2->SDL3 strategy** -- see above; `SDL-SURFACE.md` recommends
  Strategy A, contingent on the two items directly below. **Settled by
  the 2026-09-10 review** -- see the strategy section.
- **Resolved 2026-09-11 (see "Sound milestone plan", "Architecture"):
  replace, don't port -- a small fixed-voice mixer on an SDL3 audio
  stream implements the `AudioPlayer` contract, mojoAL and SDL2_sound
  both stay gated out, MIDI goes to hardware via the shared `midi_sched`.
  Settled by doskutsu's and dossage's real-hardware measurements, not by
  preference. The original question is kept below for the record.**
  **mojoAL (AGS's vendored OpenAL implementation, `vendor/ags/libsrc/mojoAL/mojoal.c`,
  4923 lines) is a second, large, independent SDL2 audio/threading/atomics
  surface.** AGS's real-time audio mixer (`audio_core.cpp`,
  `openalsource.cpp`) calls OpenAL (`al*`) functions, not raw SDL audio
  directly -- found during `SDL-SURFACE.md`'s research, not previously
  flagged anywhere in this file. Two real options, not yet decided: port
  mojoAL's own SDL2 surface to SDL3 too (more upfront work, keeps AGS's
  OpenAL-based mixer as-is), or replace AGS's `OpenAlSource`/`audio_core`
  usage with a small custom mixer written directly against SDL3's audio
  stream API (less code overall, but a real behavioral rewrite of AGS's
  own mixing path, not a port). See `SDL-SURFACE.md`'s Audio section for
  the full mojoAL symbol inventory either choice needs.
- **~~Whether SDL3's `SDL_Renderer` actually works on the DOS backend~~
  -- moot, resolved by decision (2026-09-10 review).** AGS's "Software"
  driver (`ali3dsw.cpp`) is built on `SDL_CreateRenderer`/`SDL_Texture`,
  and -- found in the review -- **hard-requires a 32-bit display**
  (`ali3dsw.cpp:73` rejects any other depth, `GetDisplayDepthForNativeDepth()`
  returns a constant 32, the streaming texture is ARGB8888). That is
  three full-frame 4-byte-per-pixel passes for an 8-bit game and a VESA
  mode 486-era cards often don't have, directly against program-doc
  section 17, `docs/video.md`'s reduced-color-depth guidance, and
  doskutsu's own measurement (its 8bpp+palette wave was its largest
  single gain, +12.7 fps, on the real-hardware-proven INDEX8
  window-surface path). Decision: the DOS driver presents via
  `SDL_GetWindowSurface` at the game's own depth from the start
  (`PATCH-SEQUENCE.md` 0017 -- the renderer is used only in the present
  step, so the touched surface is about the same size as a rename port
  would have been). Whether `SDL_Renderer` works on the DOS backend no
  longer matters to this port.
- **Ogg/Vorbis have no build-time disable toggle** (unlike Theora's
  `AGS_NO_VIDEO_PLAYER`) -- **confirmed** during `DEPENDENCIES.md`
  research (2026-09-10), with real added precision. Two independent
  layers each want Ogg/Vorbis/Theora, and they decompose differently:
  (a) `Engine/libsrc/apeg-1.2.1/` (video-cutscene decode) is the only
  code in this whole repo that calls real `ogg_`/`vorbis_`/`theora_`
  symbols directly -- `AGS_NO_VIDEO_PLAYER` does correctly drop it from
  the *link*, but the top-level `find_package(Ogg/Vorbis/Theora
  REQUIRED)`/Fetch calls in `CMakeLists.txt` run unconditionally at
  *configure* time regardless of that flag, so configure still fails
  without working copies even when nothing ends up linking them --
  making that configure-time gate conditional on `AGS_NO_VIDEO_PLAYER`
  (or a new DOS-specific flag) is real, undone upstream work. (b)
  Nothing in AGS's own `Engine`/`Common` code calls these codec libs
  directly for *audio* -- `.ogg` music/SFX decode goes entirely through
  SDL2_sound's own `Sound_*` abstraction, so porting SDL2_sound to DJGPP
  (the open item below) is what actually needs libogg/libvorbis for
  audio, not AGS's own engine code.
- **SDL2_sound is a real, separate dependency** (not SDL_mixer) that
  upstream AGS uses for audio decode. Not yet inventoried against DJGPP
  portability. Do not vendor SDL3_mixer as a substitute without confirming
  it's actually the right replacement -- see `vendor/sources.manifest`'s
  note. **New precision (2026-09-10)**: AGS doesn't vendor SDL2_sound at
  all -- `CMake/FetchSDL_Sound.cmake` pulls a pinned commit
  (`3a41c3de5b90355745333041b96e142ba8f5fbdf`) of `icculus/SDL_sound` via
  `FetchContent` and builds it inline at configure time. This port should
  vendor a local pinned copy instead (matching `vendor/sources.manifest`'s
  existing convention for every other upstream here), not rely on
  `FetchContent` producing correct DJGPP-target code during a
  cross-compile. Also found: AGS explicitly force-enables SDL2_sound's
  own *software* MIDI decoder (`SDLSOUND_DECODER_MIDI`, set via CACHE
  variable with a comment citing an upstream SDL_sound issue about it not
  defaulting on) -- a DOS port almost certainly wants hardware MIDI
  passthrough (MPU-401/OPL3/GUS, per this hub's existing audio
  architecture) instead, so porting/enabling that decoder for DJGPP would
  likely be wasted effort unless deliberately kept as a soft-synth
  fallback.
- **Correction (2026-09-10): the "Allegro is not a real dependency" note
  below was wrong on its specific evidence, found while reading
  `CMakeLists.txt` for `DEPENDENCIES.md`.** There IS a real link target:
  `include(FindLocalAllegro)` -> `add_subdirectory(libsrc/allegro
  EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL)` -> `add_library(Allegro::Allegro ALIAS allegro)`,
  and `Allegro::Allegro` is genuinely linked into both `Engine/CMakeLists.txt`
  (line 546) and `Common/CMakeLists.txt` (line 201). The prior claim ("no
  `find_package(Allegro)`, no link target") checked only for
  `find_package`, and missed the vendored `add_subdirectory` + `ALIAS`
  pattern -- a real gap in that research, not a stale fact, worth naming
  plainly rather than quietly overwriting.
  That said, **the practical conclusion mostly survives**: this vendored
  `vendor/ags/libsrc/allegro/` is Allegro **4.4.3**, but AGS's own
  `cmake/FileList.cmake` compiles only a small, headless subset --
  software blit/dither/palette/quantize routines (the per-bpp `vtable*.c`/
  `c/cblit*.c`/`c/cgfx*.c` families), FLI/FLC animation decode, polygon/
  rotate/flood-fill primitives, fixed-point math, BMP loading, Unicode
  string helpers, and a legacy packfile reader (`file.c` +
  `unix/ufile.c`/`win/gdi.c`+`wfile.c` for the two platform-specific file
  helpers only) -- **none of Allegro's own display, audio, input, timer,
  or threading subsystems are compiled at all** (no `system.c`, no
  `gfxdrv`, no sound/joystick/keyboard/mouse/timer sources anywhere in
  `FileList.cmake`). So this is not an OS-integration dependency
  competing with SDL3 -- it's roughly 1500-2500 lines of real vendored C
  that needs to build under DJGPP as part of Engine/Common (its own
  `CMakeLists.txt` does Unix-specific `check_include_files`/`mmap`/
  `mprotect` feature probes, none of which are known yet to break under
  DJGPP -- not verified either way). **New, unresolved item this
  correction surfaces: this vendored Allegro subset ships with no
  license file anywhere in the pinned AGS tree** (`find libsrc/allegro
  -iname '*license*'` returns nothing; neither AGS's own `License.txt`
  nor `Copyright.txt` mentions Allegro) -- `LICENSE-REVIEW.md` needs an
  Allegro entry, currently has none, and per this hub's "never guess a
  license" rule that entry stays unverified until someone actually reads
  Allegro 4.4.3's real upstream license text, not assumed from general
  knowledge that Allegro is customarily zlib/giftware-licensed.
- **Four CMake-level build gaps found during `DEPENDENCIES.md` research
  (2026-09-10), none patched anywhere yet**: `Glad::Glad` (OpenGL loader)
  and `Cda::Cda` (physical CD audio) both link into the `engine` target
  unconditionally, independent of `AGS_HAS_OPENGL`/DOS relevance; the
  `find_package(Ogg/Vorbis/Theora REQUIRED)`/Fetch calls run at CMake
  *configure* time regardless of `AGS_NO_VIDEO_PLAYER` (only the *link*
  is conditional); SDL2_sound is `FetchContent`-pulled and built inline
  rather than vendored+pinned like everything else in
  `vendor/sources.manifest`. See `DEPENDENCIES.md`'s "CMake build-system
  gaps" section -- each needs its own new guard as part of the minimum
  patch sequence, not assumed already handled by existing `#if` guards on
  source files. **Three more found while writing `PATCH-SEQUENCE.md`**:
  the SDL2 acquisition itself (`FetchSDL2`/`find_package(SDL2)` can never
  resolve an SDL3-only sysroot), `FindLocalOpenAL.cmake`'s unconditional
  fall-through to building mojoAL, and the two independent
  `CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME` `FATAL_ERROR` gates (top-level and Allegro's own)
  -- see that document's tl;dr and Phase A.
- **alfont-2.0.9's dormant `ALFONT_DOS` build path is a trap, not a head
  start -- corrected 2026-09-10 (review).** `alfont.c:20` shows
  `#ifdef ALFONT_DOS` selects `<iconv.h>` (its README credits "the
  Libiconv project for DOS version"); the default path selects
  `<locale.h>`/`<wchar.h>` + `setlocale`/`mbstowcs` instead. The DJGPP
  probe (`tests/probes/djgpp-runtime/`) shows `<iconv.h>` is absent and
  the default path's facilities are present. So: **do not define
  `ALFONT_DOS`**; build alfont the way every current AGS platform does.
  Whether the default path renders a real game's non-ASCII text
  correctly is a test-game question, not a build one. `DEPENDENCIES.md`
  carries the same correction.
- **Two DJGPP viability questions -- both answered 2026-09-10 by
  `tests/probes/djgpp-runtime/run.sh`** against the real toolchain (GCC
  12.2.0): (a) `std::mutex`, `std::condition_variable` and `std::thread`
  **do not exist** -- libstdc++ is built without `_GLIBCXX_HAS_GTHREADS`,
  so `<mutex>` defines no `std::mutex` at all. `AGS_DISABLE_THREADS` only
  guards thread *creation*; `audio_core.cpp` keeps a `std::mutex` and a
  `std::condition_variable` as unguarded members (lines 48-49) and locks
  them unguarded (158, 182, 191), and `debugmanager.cpp/.h` does the
  same. This is now a known patch (`PATCH-SEQUENCE.md` 0010: DOS-only
  no-op lock/cv shim -- correct, not just expedient, since the build is
  single-threaded by construction), not a question. `sleep_for`/`chrono`/
  `atomic` all build. (b) `GetDiskFreeSpaceMB()`: `statfs()` from
  `<sys/vfs.h>` compiles and links -- mechanism identified (0020);
  runtime correctness under DOSBox-X still to verify.
- **Memory budget** -- AGS's modern defaults do assume far more RAM than
  a DOS box should dedicate: `Engine/ac/gamesetup.h:86-92` defaults the
  sprite cache to 128 MB (32 MB on Android/iOS), the texture cache to
  128 MB, the sound cache to 32 MB (read 2026-09-10). Conservative
  starting caches (sprite 4-8MB, sound 2-4MB, texture cache irrelevant
  for the software driver) are `PATCH-SEQUENCE.md` 0022 -- a `STARTS`-time
  patch, listed so it isn't forgotten -- and need profiling against a
  16-32MB DOS target once something runs.
- **Compressed music decode cost on a 486** -- if the first test game uses
  MIDI (preferred per selection criteria), hardware MIDI should be the
  recommended 486 configuration; OGG/Vorbis audio is a later-phase risk,
  not a v0.1 requirement.

### Patch 0108 (restart-point compression) -- PRE-REGISTERED, written 2026-09-18 before any cell ran

Binary under test (B arm): `152b3226eeb2`. A arm: the current pinned
binary `7762d0ac915e` (patches 0104-0107). Patch 0108 commit in vendor
tree `658a5a8b6`.

**Which metric carries the threshold, and why.**

The threshold is set on **`setrestart_ms` and `preloop_ms`**, NOT on
whole-run `tick_rate`. Reason, established by the previous slice's own
result: the B arm's stall term moved 213 ms between two cells of the same
binary, which is larger than the entire whole-run delta a pre-loop saving
of this size can produce (~0.15). A +0.15 whole-run delta measured on top
of a 213 ms-noisy term is not resolvable by a 4-cell ABBA, so setting the
threshold there would be scoring a coin flip. `preloop_ms` reproduced to
2475 / 2472 across the two B cells -- a 3 ms spread -- and the patch's
mechanism acts entirely inside the pre-loop, so it is both the
direct-effect metric and the precise one. **Whole-run `tick_rate` is
recorded as a downstream check: it is expected to move in the predicted
direction, but it does not decide PASS/FAIL for this patch.**

**Predictions.**

| metric | A (expected) | B (predicted) | basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| `setrestart_ms` | ~688 | **194 +/- 20** | zero-patch config-key run TNRP2 measured 194 |
| `preloop_ms` | ~2473 | **1979 +/- 70** | 2473 - 494; band covers the 68 ms wobble seen between the 494 and 426 figures in TNRP2 |
| whole-run `tick_rate` | ~39.03 | **~39.18** | 5000/(3.23 - 0.494 + 124.88); downstream only |
| `tick_rate_steady` | 40.04 | **unchanged** | patch touches startup only |
| `fps_p50` | 40.00 | **unchanged** | as above |
| save file size | 9,397 | **9,396** | one byte larger compressed, measured |

**WIN threshold (decides the patch):** `setrestart_ms` below 300 in both
B cells AND `preloop_ms` delta >= 400 ms between arm means.

**Stated in advance so it cannot be spun later: this patch is predicted
to land at ~39.18 and therefore NOT to close Gate 1 on its own.** 39.2 is
the bar; `load_new_room` (~1775 ms) is the remaining term. If B comes
back above 39.2 that is a bonus inside the noise band, not the
milestone -- it would need the noise caveat attached and the operator
decides, not me.

**Invalidity conditions:** any cell not dated 2026-09-18; RTC cross-check
outside 1 +/- 0.5%; `binary_sha12` not matching its arm;
`DOSAGS_CLOCK_CROSSCHECK=1` absent from any cell.

**Correctness gate (must pass before the ABBA is even run):** the claim
is that `RestartGame` still restores from the now-uncompressed slot. That
is proved by exercising the restore path, not by checking the file
appeared: run the game once so it writes an uncompressed `AGSSAVE.999`,
then run again with `--loadsavedgame 999`, which routes through
`start_game_load_savegame_on_startup()` -> `try_restore_save()` -- the
same function `restart_game()` calls, on the same slot. A successful
restore there IS the RestartGame path.

### RETRACTION: "compression buys one byte" was WRONG. It buys ~52 KB.

Found by patch 0108's own DOSBox-X correctness gate, before any ABBA cell
ran. The gate's run 1 wrote an uncompressed `AGSSAVE.999` of **61,199
bytes**. Every pre-0108 binary writes ~9,395-9,399.

**So compression on this save is ~85% effective, not 0%.** The earlier
claim -- "9,397 bytes compressed vs 9,396 uncompressed, one byte" -- was
a bad measurement. Note the spread of *compressed* sizes across 60-odd
retained DOSBox-X stage dirs: 9,395 to 9,399. **My "one byte difference"
sat entirely inside ordinary run-to-run jitter of the compressed size**,
which is exactly what you would expect if I had compared two compressed
saves and never actually measured an uncompressed one. The timing half of
that experiment was sound (the config key really did disable compression,
688 -> 194 ms); the size half was not.

*Corroboration I had already seen and explained away as noise:* the
config-key run showed `setrestart_ms` falling 494 ms but `preloop_ms`
falling only **426 ms**. I attributed the 68 ms gap to noise. It is not
noise -- it is the extra time to write a 61 KB file instead of a 9 KB
one (~52 KB at this machine's ~751 KB/s is ~69 ms). **The discrepancy I
waved off was the evidence for the thing I got wrong.**

*Does the patch still stand? Yes, but the trade is different and the
honest version is:* ~426 ms off every startup, paid for with ~52 KB of
disk on a file that is rewritten from scratch each launch and read only
if the player picks Restart. On a CF card that is a good trade. **The
scoping argument gets STRONGER, not weaker:** the original rationale
("compression achieves nothing here") would have been an argument for
turning it off globally, and that would have been wrong. Compression
works; player saves keep it. Patch header and commit message corrected
accordingly (vendor `a38178a02`).

**Operator note: the compression fix was approved on a rationale that has
now been retracted.** The approval was for a narrow, semantics-preserving
slot-999 change and that is still exactly what the patch is -- but the
cost side moved from "one byte" to "52 KB", so the decision deserves a
second look rather than my assuming the approval carries over.

### Patch 0108 correctness gate -- PASS

Run 1 wrote an uncompressed slot 999. Run 2 restored it with
`--loadsavedgame 999`, which routes to `try_restore_save()` -- the same
function `restart_game()` calls. Log: `Try restore save on start: 999` ->
`Restoring saved game './agssave.999'` -> `Created global script` ->
`Loading room 1` -> `Now in room 1` -> room script ran (`Object 0 turned
on`, `Playing music 1`). No error. **The restore path was exercised, not
inferred from the file's existence.**

### Patch 0108 pre-registration, AMENDED before any cell ran

Amended because the gate above corrected the input, not because of any
result -- no ABBA cell has run. Original prediction stays visible above.

| metric | A (expected) | B, ORIGINAL | B, AMENDED | basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `setrestart_ms` | ~688 | 194 +/- 20 | **194 +/- 20** | unchanged, directly measured |
| `preloop_ms` | ~2473 | 1979 +/- 70 | **2047 +/- 40** | 2473 - 426, using the measured pre-loop delta rather than the SaveGame-only delta; the 68 ms gap is now explained, so the band tightens |
| whole-run `tick_rate` | ~39.03 | ~39.18 | **~39.15** | downstream only |
| save file size | 9,397 -> 9,396 | (wrong) | **~9,396 -> ~61,199** | measured in the gate |

B-arm binary is now **`ad3ab9b148f1`** (the corrected header changed the
build); `152b3226eeb2` in the original pre-registration is superseded and
must not appear in a scored cell. WIN threshold unchanged:
`setrestart_ms` below 300 in both B cells AND `preloop_ms` delta >= 400 ms
between arm means. The prediction that this patch does NOT close Gate 1
on its own also stands.

### Method lessons from the retraction (recorded as method, not just correction)

**1. "X changes nothing" needs X measured in BOTH states, not one state
twice.** The one-byte result compared 9,397 against 9,396 when the
compressed size's own range across ~60 stage dirs is 9,395-9,399. The
control -- an actual uncompressed save -- did not exist until patch
0108's gate produced one. General form: *when a conclusion is "this
setting doesn't matter", first prove the setting was actually in both
states in the two things being compared.* A null result is the easiest
kind to fake accidentally, because failing to apply the treatment
produces exactly the same reading as a treatment with no effect.

**2. An unexplained gap between two brackets that should agree is
evidence, not noise.** `setrestart_ms` fell 494 ms while `preloop_ms`
fell 426 ms. The 68 ms I called noise is ~52 KB at this machine's own
measured ~751 KB/s = ~69 ms. **The bracket arithmetic already contained
the refutation of the conclusion drawn from the same experiment.** This
is the same shape as the child-vs-parent maxima tell from the unit bug:
two measurements that must reconcile, don't, and the residual is the
finding. Reconcile brackets before reporting from them.

### Pre-registration correction #2: the A-arm binary was misidentified

Also caught before any cell ran. The amended pre-registration named the A
arm `7762d0ac915e` "(patches 0104-0107)". **That is wrong: `7762d0ac915e`
is the 0104-0106 binary** -- the fade-skip ABBA's B arm. Patch 0107, the
`SetRestartPoint()` sub-brackets, was written *after* it.

This matters because the threshold in this pre-registration is carried by
`setrestart_ms` / `preloop_ms`, and **those fields only exist in a binary
that has 0107's brackets.** An A arm without them could not produce the
metric the patch is being scored on. The A arm is therefore the
0104-0107 build, rebuilt for this run: **`3ade995daf03`**. Verified as a
genuine 0107 state, not an artefact of reverse-applying 0108:
`git diff HEAD~1` against the 0107 commit is empty, and the engine
contains no `__DATE__`/`__TIME__`, so the differing sha is explained by
its being a different patch level, not a non-reproducible build.

Arms for the ABBA: **A = `3ade995daf03` (0104-0107), B =
`ad3ab9b148f1` (0104-0108)**, each staged from one pinned file so both
cells of a pair are the identical binary.

### Operator decision (2026-09-18): patch 0108 RE-CONFIRMED on corrected facts

Recorded as a *re*-confirmation, not the original approval, so this file
does not carry the retracted "compression buys one byte" reasoning as the
justification for a patch that is still in the tree.

**The trade as it actually stands: ~426 ms off every startup, against
~52 KB written per launch.** Operator's reasoning: 52 KB is negligible
against 72 MB+ game packages; the file is transient, rewritten from
scratch each launch and read only if the player picks Restart; and 426 ms
is a visible improvement on a 486 for a real player.

**Narrow slot-999 scope stands. Player saves keep compression.** Patch
0108 stays.

**REVISED ESTIMATE (after the ABBA, 2026-09-18): quote the benefit as
~350-420 ms, variable -- NOT 426 ms.** The four-cell ABBA missed its
pre-registered threshold because the uncompressed write turns out to
range 202-356 ms where the compressed path is tight to 5 ms. The operator
accepted this trade partly on 426 ms being a visible improvement on a
486; it still is, but it is less predictable than they were told, and the
softer number is the one that should survive in this file.

## Patch 0108 ABBA -- INCOMPLETE (3 of 4 cells), 2026-09-18

**Not scored against the pre-registration.** The closing A cell was
interrupted; a 3-cell run is not the 4-cell design that was
pre-registered, and is not reported as one.

### Void cells, and why

| tag | void because |
|---|---|
| TNCMPA1 | **ambient config contamination.** The rig still had my own `ACSETUP.CFG` with `compress_saves=0` on it, left from the zero-patch experiment, so the A arm ran *uncompressed too*. `restart_savegame_ms=205` where A should be ~690. This is the "two samples of the same state" failure, committed one message after the coordinator warned about it -- the lesson did not transfer on its own, which is why it is written down rather than just fixed. **Every cell now stages an explicit `ACSETUP.CFG`**, so the config is a controlled input, not whatever the previous run left behind. |
| TNCPA1 | superseded: correct config, but built by reverse-applying 0108 to the working tree (see fingerprint hazard below). |
| TNCQA2 | target was powered down mid-cell for operator maintenance. Void, re-run from scratch, **not** salvaged. |

### Instrumentation hazard: `binary_sha12` cannot see an uncommitted change

`Makefile:105` derives `AGS_BUILD_SHA12` from `git -C vendor/ags
rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` -- the **committed** tree. A binary built by
patching the *working* tree therefore compiles one thing and stamps
another. My first A arm compiled 0107 code and stamped the 0108 identity,
and **both arms came back `057854a618a3`** -- so the standing invalidity
condition "arms must differ" would have been silently satisfied by two
identical stamps had I not been reading the brackets.

*Fix applied:* each arm is now built from a genuine checkout of its own
commit. A = **`e21541244bb1`** (0104-0107, commit `8bdade858`),
B = **`057854a618a3`** (0104-0108, commit `a38178a02`).

*Retrospective check of earlier ABBAs in this campaign,* since the
coordinator asked whether any were built this way:

| ABBA | A fingerprint | B fingerprint | distinct? |
|---|---|---|---|
| patch 0091 (TNP3) | 7762d0ac915e | 2baf55f31095 | yes |
| patch 0104 (TNP2) | 8a2d3a032833 | 7762d0ac915e | yes |
| fade skip (TNF) | 63831d4f90be | f8488eea3bbc | yes |

**All earlier arms carry distinct fingerprints, so the specific failure
mode -- two arms sharing a stamp -- did not occur in any of them.** What
that does NOT prove: a distinct stamp cannot show that a given arm's
binary matched its own commit, since an arm built from commit X *plus*
uncommitted edits still stamps X. I have no evidence any arm was built
that way and the results were internally consistent and reproducible, but
**I cannot positively rule it out retrospectively, and I am not claiming
to.**

### `clock_crosscheck` -- I raised an alarm and it was wrong

Flagged because `rtc_s=138 uclock_ms=137995 ratio=0.99997` is *byte
identical* in all three cells here AND in all four cells of the previous
fade-skip ABBA, across binaries whose startup differs by 426 ms.

**Resolved from source (`quit.cpp:556-575`): this is correct, expected
behaviour, not a bug.** The span is measured **RTC second edge to RTC
second edge**, so it reports how much `uclock` time elapses during N real
seconds. That is a property of the machine's two clocks, not of the run,
so a constant ~0.99997 is exactly what a healthy timebase looks like.

**But the operational conclusion stands and matters:** the crosscheck
validates the *timebase*, and it is **not** a per-cell fingerprint. Three
cells reporting 0.99997 are not three independent confirmations that
those cells differ -- it would read 0.99997 for a cell that was wrong in
every other way. It stays an invalidity condition on the clock; it must
never be cited as evidence a cell is distinct.

### The three completed cells (reported, not scored)

| cell | arm | sha12 | tick_rate | steady | fps_p50 | preloop_ms | restart_ms | room_load_ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TNCQA1 | A | e21541244bb1 | 39.05 | 40.04 | 40.00 | 2484 | 696 | 1772 |
| TNCQB1 | **B** | 057854a618a3 | 39.12 | 40.04 | 40.00 | **2058** | **202** | 1839 |
| TNCQB2 | **B** | 057854a618a3 | 39.07 | 40.04 | 40.00 | **2212** | **356** | 1839 |

`exit_code=0`, `critical_count=0`, `warn_count=0`,
`memory_min_free_kb=154944`, `env_block_sha=fc89dca0bc06` in all three.

**Two observations that the fourth cell will not change, and one of them
is a new cost of this patch:**

**1. The uncompressed path is far NOISIER than the compressed one.**
Compressed restart, three runs today: 692 / 694 / 696 -- a 4 ms spread.
Uncompressed: 202 / 356 -- a **154 ms** spread. The likely mechanism is
that the patch writes 61 KB instead of 9.4 KB, and CF-card write time
depends on erase-block state. **So the patch does not simply trade 690 ms
for 194 ms; it trades a very tight ~694 ms for a variable ~200-360 ms.**
Still a large win, but "426 ms saved" is the optimistic end. Two B cells
cannot characterise a variance, so this is flagged, not quantified.

**2. An untouched bracket moved between arms.** `preloop_room_load_ms` is
1772 in A and 1839 in **both** B cells -- a consistent +67 ms in the arm
whose only change is writing a bigger file *before* the room loads. This
patch does not touch room loading. Per the lesson recorded above, an
unexplained gap between brackets that should agree is evidence, not
noise: a plausible mechanism is that the 61 KB write changes disk layout
or cache state for the reads that follow. **This directly concerns the
next slice, which is `load_new_room`** -- it means room-load timings are
not independent of what the pre-loop did before them, and the
`load_new_room` sub-brackets must be measured with the compression state
held fixed.

## Operator decision (2026-09-18): minimise mains power cycles -- STANDING POLICY

**Leave the target powered on between back-to-back rounds.** Power down
only for long gaps (overnight, or when the operator says they are done for
a while), when a maintenance window requires it, or whenever they ask --
and say which applies when doing it. **No reflexive power-off at the end
of a round.**

*Rationale, as it actually stands:*

1. **Thermal cycling of 30-year-old parts** -- motherboard, socketed DIP
   chips, connectors; expansion and contraction working solder joints and
   chips loose. Independent of the PSU.
2. **A recorded, unexplained no-POST on this rig** -- the hub's
   `HARDWARE.md` power-cycle recovery row, hit twice in one session, once
   needing physical intervention, never root-caused.
3. **Time** -- g2k's README, the rig's authority: Ctrl-Alt-Del reaches a
   live prompt in ~43 s versus ~90 s for a mains cycle, and does not cycle
   the PSU. "Prefer it. Mains cycling is the last resort, for a machine
   that has stopped answering."

*Practical rules:* prefer warm reboots wherever a reboot is needed at all,
including the return-chord reboots used for transfers. **`hw_guard`'s
one-power-cycle recovery stays exactly as it is** -- a wedged keyboard
controller cannot be cleared warm, which is the legitimate last-resort
case the README describes. Do not weaken it. **Log mains cycles per round**
so the cumulative count stays visible over the campaign; if the machine
ever starts failing to POST we want the history.

*A mechanism that was cited and is WITHDRAWN:* "PSU inrush on aging
electrolytics" does not apply -- **the machine has a PicoRC, a modern
DC-DC unit, not a 30-year-old AT/ATX supply.** Recorded because the error
is the reusable part:

> **Do not reason from "vintage machine" to "vintage everything".** Check
> what is actually fitted before invoking an age-related failure mode.
> The reasoning was about a component nobody had stated the model of,
> while g2k's README was right there and the operator knew.
