## Hardware maintenance CONSIDERED AND DECLINED (2026-09-18)

**Recorded as a correction: the disconnection did not happen, and the
hardware baseline is UNCHANGED.** An earlier revision of this file stated
that the floppy and CD-ROM had been physically disconnected. They were
not.

The operator considered unplugging the floppy and CD-ROM to have fewer
components running during reboots, then deliberately did not, in their
own words: *"I left them powered on, since it might change the boot
timings we have."*

**The reasoning is the part worth keeping.** They declined a hardware
change specifically to avoid invalidating the boot-timing baseline in the
middle of a campaign -- the same apples-to-apples concern that applied to
the tick-window change. A device-configuration change would plausibly
move boot timing, device enumeration and the DOS boot sequence, and any
comparison spanning it would not be like-for-like. **The standing
implication: hardware configuration changes want to land between
campaigns, not inside one, and the cost of a mid-campaign change is
every before/after comparison that crosses it.**

No "watch whether the hazards change" item follows, because nothing
changed to attribute anything to.

## `load_new_room` slice: patch 0109 sub-brackets, and the prime suspect

Patch 0109 splits `load_new_room()` into seven phases plus a total,
measurement only, emitted with the rest of the startup report. Set on
**every** room load, not only the first, so in-game room transitions can
be read with the same instrument.

*Accounting checked under DOSBox-X before going near hardware* (the
control question -- do the brackets actually add up -- answered on the
emulator, where it costs nothing):

| bracket | ms | share |
|---|---|---|
| `roomload_loadroom_ms` (CLIB read + LZW backgrounds + RLE masks + deep copy) | 56 | 17% |
| `roomload_bgprep_ms` | 0 | -- |
| `roomload_maskprep_ms` | 11 | 3% |
| `roomload_objsetup_ms` | 0 | -- |
| `roomload_script_ms` | 0 | -- |
| **`roomload_lighttable_ms`** | **252** | **78%** |
| `roomload_drawdata_ms` | 0 | -- |
| **sum** | **319** | of `roomload_total_ms=322` |

`roomload_total_ms` (322) matches `game_start.cpp`'s independently
measured `preloop_room_load_ms` (322) exactly, and the phases account for
319 of it -- so the split is complete, not a partial view with the real
cost hiding in an unbracketed remainder.

### The suspect: `generate_light_table()` is rebuilt on every room load

`ac/room.cpp:998` sets `color_map = nullptr` immediately before
`ac/room.cpp:1001` calls `generate_light_table()`. That function
(`ac/region.cpp:131-138`) is guarded by `color_map == nullptr` -- **so the
line above it defeats its own cache, unconditionally, every room load.**

What gets rebuilt: `create_light_table()`
(`libsrc/allegro/src/color.c:771-787`) with `rgb_map == nullptr` takes the
slow branch, **255 x 256 = 65,280 calls to `bestfit_color`**, each of
which scans up to 256 palette entries -- on the order of 10-16 million
inner iterations of integer work. That is entirely plausible as the bulk
of ~1800 ms on a 486DX2-66.

**It is 8-bit-only** (`game.color_depth == 1`), which is exactly this
campaign's configuration, and **it does not scale with room size** -- a
property that makes it easy to falsify: if the light table dominates,
small and large rooms cost about the same.

*Not previously explored:* `grep -i "light_table\|bestfit"` over this file
returned nothing before this entry.

### Proposed fix -- NOT yet implemented, measurement on HW comes first

The table depends only on `palette[]`. The semantics-preserving fix is
**not** to stop nulling `color_map` -- that null is what discards any
blender a script set, and removing it would change behaviour. It is to
keep the null and make the rebuild conditional on the palette actually
having changed since `maincoltable` was last built (a 768-byte memcmp
against a cached copy). Whenever the palette is unchanged, `color_map`
ends up pointing at a table with byte-identical contents, so the
observable state is the same.

**If it holds, this is worth more than the pre-loop.** The same cost is
paid at *every* room transition, not just startup -- so it would also
attack the in-game stall term, which is the noisy term that has been
limiting whole-run resolution all campaign.

**Order of work, per the dispatch:** measure the sub-brackets on real
hardware FIRST. The DOSBox share is suggestive, not authoritative -- it is
a different CPU with different cache behaviour, and `bestfit_color`'s cost
is exactly the kind of thing emulation distorts. No fix, prediction or
ABBA until the 486 has reported which phase actually dominates.

| cell | arm | sha12 | tick_rate | steady | fps_p50 | preloop_ms | restart_ms | room_load_ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TNCQA1 | A | e21541244bb1 | 39.05 | 40.04 | 40.00 | 2484 | 696 | 1772 |
| TNCQB1 | **B** | 057854a618a3 | 39.12 | 40.04 | 40.00 | 2058 | **202** | 1839 |
| TNCQB2 | **B** | 057854a618a3 | 39.07 | 40.04 | 40.00 | 2212 | **356** | 1839 |
| TNCQA2 | A | e21541244bb1 | 38.94 | 40.04 | 40.00 | 2629 | 691 | 1772 |

Validity: `exit_code=0`, `critical_count=0`, `warn_count=0`,
`memory_min_free_kb=154944`, `env_block_sha=fc89dca0bc06` in all four;
arms carry distinct fingerprints; all cells dated 2026-09-18; clock
cross-check 0.99997 throughout.

### Verdict: the pre-registered threshold is NOT met. Scored as a MISS.

The threshold was an **AND**: `setrestart_ms` below 300 in both B cells
**AND** `preloop_ms` delta >= 400 ms between arm means.

| criterion | result | |
|---|---|---|
| `setrestart_ms` < 300 in both B cells | 202 and **356** | **FAIL** |
| `preloop_ms` delta >= 400 ms | 2556.5 - 2135.0 = **421.5 ms** | pass |

**One of two criteria failed, so the conjunction failed.** I am scoring
that as written rather than reporting the half that passed. What went
wrong is *my prediction of the variance*, not the direction of the
effect: I predicted `setrestart_ms` at 194 +/- 20 from a single
zero-patch cell, and the uncompressed path turns out to range 202-356.

| prediction | measured | |
|---|---|---|
| `setrestart_ms` 194 +/- 20 | 202, 356 | 1 of 2 in band |
| `preloop_ms` 2047 +/- 40 | 2058, 2212 | 1 of 2 in band |
| whole-run ~39.15 | **39.095** | low by 0.055 |
| steady / fps unchanged | unchanged | hit |
| **"does not close Gate 1 alone"** | **39.095 < 39.2** | **HIT** |

### The A2 cell has a 152 ms hole in its accounting, and it inflates the criterion that passed

Applying this campaign's own rule -- an unexplained gap between brackets
that should agree is evidence, not noise:

| cell | sum of the five pre-loop brackets | `preloop_ms` | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| TNCQA1 | 2483 | 2484 | 1 |
| TNCQB1 | 2056 | 2058 | 2 |
| TNCQB2 | 2210 | 2212 | 2 |
| **TNCQA2** | **2477** | **2629** | **152** |

Three cells reconcile to within 2 ms. **TNCQA2 has 152 ms inside the
pre-loop that is outside all five brackets**, which patch 0105 claimed
accounted for it completely. Its five brackets are otherwise normal for
an A cell (restart 691, room_load 1772, matching A1's 696/1772), so the
anomaly is unbracketed time, not a phase that got slower.

**This matters for the verdict rather than being a footnote:** A2's
inflated `preloop_ms` is what lifts the A mean, and therefore the
delta. Recomputed on the bracket sums instead, the A mean is 2480 and
the delta is **347 ms -- which would fail the 400 ms criterion too.**
So the one criterion that passed, passed on the strength of a cell with
an unexplained hole in it. **The honest summary is that this ABBA does
not establish its pre-registered threshold on either criterion once the
anomaly is accounted for.**

Cause not yet known. Candidates: a disk event during the pre-loop, or a
pre-loop path outside the five brackets that only sometimes runs. It is
the first time this gap has appeared in five bracketed cells.

### What IS established

The effect is real, large, and in the predicted direction: **the restart
point drops from a very tight ~693 ms to a variable ~200-360 ms**, and
the pre-loop drops by roughly 350-420 ms depending on which estimator is
used. Both B cells beat both A cells on every timing metric. `fps_p50`
and `tick_rate_steady` are untouched, as predicted.

What is NOT established is the tight, predictable saving the
pre-registration claimed. **The patch's benefit should be quoted as
"roughly 350-420 ms, variable" and not as "426 ms".**

**Gate 1 remains open:** whole-run B mean **39.095** against 39.2. My
pre-registered statement that this patch would not close Gate 1 on its
own is a hit. `load_new_room` (~1772-1839 ms) is the remaining term.

## `load_new_room` on REAL HARDWARE: the light table is 1351 ms (2026-09-18)

Patch 0109's sub-brackets, HW-486-66, two cells (TNLR1, TNLR2):

| bracket | TNLR1 | TNLR2 | share |
|---|---|---|---|
| `roomload_loadroom_ms` | 395 | 395 | 21% |
| `roomload_bgprep_ms` | 0 | 0 | -- |
| `roomload_maskprep_ms` | 56 | 56 | 3% |
| `roomload_objsetup_ms` | 1 | 1 | -- |
| `roomload_script_ms` | 3 | 3 | -- |
| **`roomload_lighttable_ms`** | **1351** | **1351** | **73%** |
| `roomload_drawdata_ms` | 1 | 1 | -- |
| sum | 1807 | 1807 | of 1841 / 1840 |

`roomload_total_ms` matches `preloop_room_load_ms` exactly in both cells,
and the phases account for 1807 of 1841 -- 98%.

**`generate_light_table()` is 1351 ms, reproducible to the millisecond
across two cells.** That is 73% of room load and ~60% of the entire
pre-loop. The DOSBox share (78%) predicted the hardware share (73%)
closely, so the emulator was a good guide here even though its absolute
numbers are meaningless.

**The determinism is itself informative.** 1351/1351 with zero spread is
what a fixed-size pure-CPU computation looks like: 255 x 256 = 65,280
`bestfit_color` calls, each scanning the palette, with no I/O and no
data-dependent branching worth speaking of. Compare the restart point in
the same cells -- 355 / 412 -- which is I/O and varies. **The two biggest
pre-loop terms are now cleanly separated into "CPU, perfectly
predictable" and "disk, variable".**

*Why this is worth more than its pre-loop share:* the same 1351 ms is
paid on **every room transition**, not just startup. That is the stall
term which has limited whole-run resolution all campaign. Fixing it would
improve the measuring instrument as well as the product -- it could make
whole-run deltas resolvable again rather than perpetually smaller than
the noise.

### Fix design (not yet implemented)

Rebuild the table **only when the palette actually changed**, rather than
caching it unconditionally. `room.cpp`'s `color_map = nullptr` stays --
that null is what discards a blender a script may have set, and removing
it would change behaviour. The change is inside `generate_light_table()`:
keep a cached copy of the palette the table was built from, memcmp 768
bytes, and call `create_light_table()` only on a real change. Where the
palette is unchanged the rebuilt table is byte-identical, so the
observable state is the same.

**Must be proven, not assumed:** that the palette-unchanged case is
actually common on the sweep library. A game that sets a per-room palette
would rebuild legitimately and get nothing from this. **That check comes
before any prediction** -- and per the control lesson, it must be
measured in both states (rooms that do and do not change the palette),
not sampled once.

## Patch 0110: patch 0105's accounting claim was wrong, and is now closed

Patch 0105 stated its five brackets were "the whole of the pre-loop".
**They were not.** `skipMissedTicks()` (`game_start.cpp:83`) runs between
the `set_runtime_start()` anchor and the first bracket -- inside
`tick_rate`'s denominator, outside every bracket meant to account for it.

**The gap found the bug, not a code review.** TNCQA2's 152 ms discrepancy
was the only reason to look.

Patch 0110 adds `preloop_skipmissed_ms` and `preloop_start_game_ms`, so
the remainder decomposes instead of being guessed at: unaccounted time
inside `start_game()` appears as `start_game_ms` minus its parts, and
time after it returns appears as `preloop_ms` minus `start_game_ms`.

First cell (TNLR3): `skipmissed=0`, `start_game_ms=2064`,
`preloop_ms=2065`, five brackets summing to 2062. **Everything
reconciles to within 3 ms and the pre-loop is now closed accounting.**

**What this does NOT yet establish:** the 152 ms did not recur, so its
cause is still unknown -- I am not claiming `skipMissedTicks()` was it.
What changed is that the next occurrence will say where it lives instead
of only that it exists. Seen once in seven bracketed cells.

### Is `preloop_ms` still a threshold metric?

Evidence so far: it reconciles with its parts to 1-3 ms in six of seven
cells, and was out by 152 ms in one. **Until the anomaly is explained, the
`load_new_room` pre-registration will hang its threshold on the individual
brackets rather than on `preloop_ms`** -- specifically
`roomload_lighttable_ms`, which reproduced at 1351/1351 with zero spread
and is the phase the change actually targets. `preloop_ms` and whole-run
`tick_rate` both become downstream checks. A metric with one unexplained
152 ms excursion should not carry a threshold when a tighter, more
directly attributable one is available.

### Mains power cycle log (cumulative, this campaign)

| date | count | note |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-18 | 1 | `--power-on` at the start of the compression ABBA round |
| 2026-09-18 | 1 | coordinator powered OFF 11:52 PDT for operator maintenance |
| 2026-09-18 | 1 | powered ON to resume after the hold cleared; machine left ON since, per policy |

**Running total: 3 mains cycles on 2026-09-18.**

### The light table is a PRODUCT problem, not only a benchmark one

Worth stating plainly because it has been discussed so far as a pre-loop
term: **1351 ms is paid at every room transition during normal play.**
That is not a startup cost a player waits through once -- it is a visible
hitch every time they walk through a door. The benchmark noticed it; the
player feels it.

### Method rule adopted: where to hang a threshold

**Hang the threshold on the tightest metric the change directly moves,
and demote anything with an unexplained excursion to a downstream check
rather than retiring it.** Applied here: `roomload_lighttable_ms`
(1351/1351, zero spread, directly targeted) carries the threshold;
`preloop_ms` (one unexplained 152 ms excursion in seven cells) and
whole-run `tick_rate` (stall-noise limited) are both downstream.
Demotion, not retirement -- a downstream check that moves the wrong way
still falsifies the change.

### Patch 0111: two instruments, and what each one settles

**1. Palette churn.** Logs an FNV-1a hash of the palette each light table
is built from, whether it matches the previous build, and a running
total.

**Important scoping point: this sizes the BENEFIT per game, it does not
gate whether the change is SAFE.** The replacement check is a 768-byte
memcmp standing in for 65,280 palette scans, so the fix is nearly free
even on a game that legitimately rebuilds every room. A low
palette-unchanged rate would mean "this game gains little", not "do not
make the change".

**2. Byte-identity, opt-in (`DOSAGS_LIGHTTABLE_VERIFY=1`).** The
correctness argument for the fix is that on an unchanged palette the
rebuilt table is byte-identical to the one already in `maincoltable`, so
skipping the rebuild preserves observable state. **That was an argument,
not a measurement.** This builds the table a second time into a scratch
`COLOR_MAP` and memcmps all 65,536 entries against the live one. Same
discipline that should have been applied to the compression size claim
and was not -- settle it before the ABBA, not after.

*First emulator run (5000-tick window): exactly one table build,
`pal_hash=8a8fe378`, and one room.* The stock benchmark window never
leaves room 1, so it cannot answer the churn question at all --
`DOSAGS_TAS_AUTO_EXIT_TICK` is only an auto-exit, there is no recorded
input playback, and room changes come from the game's own script much
later in the run. A long run is needed, which is in progress. **Recorded
because "one build observed" would be a badly wrong reading of this
instrument if the window were not stated.**

## Light-table fix scoping: it is 8-BIT ONLY, and AGS Quest gets nothing

Checked rather than assumed, because the fixture plan depended on it.

`region.cpp:133` guards on `game.color_depth == 1`, and
`Common/ac/gamesetupstruct.h:104` is
`inline int GetColorDepth() const { return color_depth * 8; }` -- so
`color_depth` is **bytes** per pixel and the guard means **8-bit only**.

**AGS Quest is `640 x 360 (16 bit)`, so `generate_light_table()` never
runs there at all. The fix is worth exactly zero to it.** Stated plainly
because the natural fixture for room transitions was going to be AGS
Quest's AutoPilot, and a prediction built on it would have measured an
effect that cannot exist.

**Consequence for how the fix is described:** this is not a general
engine win. It is a win for **8-bit titles only**. The sweep library's
8-bit members are the relevant population, and the recurring
per-transition benefit should never be quoted as applying to the library
as a whole.

*Colour depths on record so far:*

| fixture | native | light table runs? |
|---|---|---|
| Trilby's Notes | 320x240, **8 bit** | yes |
| Bench 8-bit | 320x200, **8 bit** | yes |
| AGS Quest | 640x360, 16 bit | **no** |
| 5days, 7days, iowna, mmd, shards | not yet recorded | unknown |

### The fixture problem, stated honestly

**Our gate fixtures barely exercise the part of this cost that matters
most.** Trilby's idle window and BENCH8's scenes each sit in a single
room, so they pay the light table **once, at startup**. The 1351 ms that
recurs at every transition -- the player-visible hitch, and the stall
term limiting whole-run resolution -- is invisible to both.

And the obvious fixture for transitions is ruled out by the finding
above: AGS Quest transitions, but is 16-bit.

There is also no recorded input playback in this harness
(`DOSAGS_TAS_AUTO_EXIT_TICK` is only an auto-exit), so an 8-bit shipped
game only changes room where its own script does so.

**What this does NOT block:** the per-transition cost itself is already
measured and is a property of the code path, not the fixture -- 1351 ms
per `load_new_room`, twice reproduced to the millisecond. So a prediction
can be built as `transitions x per-transition cost` with the transition
count measured, exactly as suggested, rather than needing a fixture that
makes the whole effect visible in one number.

**Open, and not to be guessed:** whether the palette is actually
unchanged across transitions in *shipped* 8-bit games. BENCH8 is our own
authored content and its palette behaviour is not evidence about how
shipped AGS games behave, so the churn measurement must sample real
sweep-library titles.

### Measured colour depths for the WHOLE sweep library (2026-09-18)

Measured directly, one short DOSBox run per title, not inferred:

| title | native | light table runs? |
|---|---|---|
| **Trilby's Notes** | 320x240 **8 bit** | **yes** |
| **Bench 8-bit** (our own) | 320x200 **8 bit** | **yes** |
| 5 Days A Stranger | 320x240 16 bit | no |
| 7 Days A Skeptic | 320x240 16 bit | no |
| Maniac Mansion Deluxe | 320x200 16 bit | no |
| AGS Quest (our own) | 640x360 16 bit | no |
| Shards of God | 320x200 32 bit | no |
| If on a winter's night, four travelers | 320x200 32 bit | no |

**Of six sourced shipped titles, exactly ONE is 8-bit.** So the honest
scoping is narrower than "8-bit titles benefit": **in our library this fix
benefits Trilby's Notes and our own BENCH8, and nothing else.**

*Why it is still worth doing:*

- It is **the Gate 1 fixture**, and it is ~60% of the pre-loop on the very
  game the gate is measured on.
- The fix is cheap -- a 768-byte memcmp standing in for 65,280 palette
  scans -- so it carries almost no risk or maintenance cost.
- It is a player-visible hitch at every door, not only a benchmark number.

*Why the scope claim must stay narrow anyway:*

- The wider AGS catalogue outside our six is **plausibly** much more 8-bit
  than our sample, older 2.x-era titles especially. **This is explicitly
  UNMEASURED.** We have surveyed eight fixtures and nothing else, and our
  own sample is the only evidence actually in hand. It must not be
  written up as "most AGS games benefit".

*Fixture fallback decision, if Trilby's own script never transitions:*
**author a transition into BENCH8 rather than driving real input through
vcctrl.** Deterministic, repeatable, costs no hardware time to develop,
and the recurrence demonstration needs only the timing half -- which is
the one thing our own authored content is legitimately evidence for.
Input-driven transitions would be slower to set up, less repeatable, and
input injection at low frame rates is a known hazard in this campaign
(instant clicks can miss a sparse input poll entirely). **The
palette-churn half stays on real library titles regardless.**

### The palette-churn measurement cannot be broadly sampled -- n=1

Follows directly from the depth survey, and it limits an instruction that
assumed otherwise. `generate_light_table()` only runs when
`game.color_depth == 1`, so **palette churn can only be measured on 8-bit
titles** -- there is no table being built on the others to observe.

Our library has **exactly one shipped 8-bit title (Trilby's Notes)**, plus
our own BENCH8, which is explicitly not evidence about how shipped AGS
games behave. So the intent "sample real sweep-library games, not only
BENCH8" resolves to a sample of **one**.

**This is a limit on the evidence, not a reason to skip the measurement.**
Trilby's Notes is the Gate 1 fixture and the game the fix is actually
being made for, so measuring its churn is exactly the number needed to
size the benefit where it will be claimed. What cannot be claimed from it
is anything general about shipped AGS games' palette behaviour -- a
one-title sample supports a statement about that title and nothing wider.

Recorded so a later reader does not mistake a single-game churn figure for
a library-wide one.

## All three open light-table questions SETTLED from existing fixtures (2026-09-18)

No new content authored, no hardware time, no input injection. The
save/restore path was the fixture all along.

**The mechanism.** `game/savegame.cpp:834` calls `load_new_room()` on
restore, and `load_new_room()` is what nulls `color_map` -- so a restore
pays the full rebuild exactly as a room transition does. (`savegame.cpp:890`
then calls `generate_light_table()` again, but that one is a **no-op**:
`load_new_room()` has already set `color_map`, so its guard holds. One
extra rebuild per restore, not two.)

**BENCH8's `full` scene already saves and restores** via its AutoPilot's
`save` and `restore` phases. Running it with patch 0111:

```
DOSAGS_LIGHTTABLE build=1 pal_hash=e7fe8f9c same_as_prev=0 cumulative_same=0
DOSAGS_LIGHTTABLE build=2 pal_hash=e7fe8f9c same_as_prev=1 cumulative_same=1
DOSAGS_LIGHTTABLE_VERIFY rebuilt_vs_previous memcmp=0 bytes=65536
```

| question | answer | how |
|---|---|---|
| Does the cost **recur** after startup? | **Yes** -- two builds in one run | build=2 on restore |
| Is the palette **unchanged** when it recurs? | **Yes** -- identical hash | `same_as_prev=1` |
| Is the rebuilt table **byte-identical**? | **Yes** -- all 65,536 bytes | `memcmp=0` |

**The correctness argument for this patch is now a measurement, not an
argument.** That was the one thing still resting on reasoning, and it is
the same gap that produced the compression retraction -- settled this time
*before* the ABBA rather than after.

**And the second rebuild is demonstrably pure waste:** identical palette
in, byte-identical table out, 1351 ms on HW-486-66 to produce a copy of
something already in memory.

*Note on reading the brackets here:* `roomload_lighttable_ms` in the
startup report shows only the FIRST load -- the report is emitted once, at
first-room-ready. The per-build `DOSAGS_LIGHTTABLE` line from patch 0111
is what makes the recurrence visible at all. Without it, this run would
have looked identical to a single-room run.

### Consequences

- **BENCH8 authoring is unnecessary** and is dropped from the plan.
- **The recurrence fixture is `bench8 full`**, an existing gate fixture,
  which means the ABBA can use it directly.
- Caveat retained: a **same-room restore is not evidence for the
  palette-churn question** across genuinely different rooms. For the
  TIMING half it is equivalent, since the cost is invariant in room size
  and content -- which the 1351/1351 determinism across two HW cells
  independently supports. **Churn across real room-to-room transitions
  stays an open question on Trilby's Notes.**

## IMPORTANT: the light-table fix does NOT help Gate 1. Stated before the ABBA.

This is the most decision-relevant thing in this slice and it cuts against
the framing this fix has been discussed under, including my own.

**The fix cannot touch the first build.** At startup `start_game()` ->
`load_new_room()` -> `generate_light_table()` is the *first* call; there
is no earlier table to reuse, so it rebuilds, and the full 1351 ms stays
exactly where it is. The saving is entirely on calls 2..N.

**Gate 1's benchmark is a single room with no transitions and no
restore.** The 5000-tick Trilby window loads room 1 once. Therefore:

> **Predicted effect of patch 0112 on Gate 1's `tick_rate`, `preloop_ms`
> and `fps_p50`: ZERO. Not "small" -- zero, by construction.**

The long Trilby run confirms the fixture side of this: **30,000 ticks,
exactly one room load**, one light-table build. Trilby's own script never
transitions without player input, so the benchmark cannot see this fix at
all.

**What that means for the campaign, honestly:** 1351 ms of the pre-loop is
light table, and **this patch removes none of it.** Gate 1's remaining gap
(39.095 against 39.2) is untouched by this work. Closing it would need
either a way to make the *first* build cheaper -- a genuinely different
and riskier idea, e.g. precomputing or persisting the table -- or savings
elsewhere. **Nobody should read "we fixed a 1351 ms cost" as "Gate 1 moved".**

**What the patch IS worth**, which is real but lands in different metrics:

| when | cost before | cost after | where it shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| **startup load (call 1)** | 1351 ms | **1351 ms -- unchanged** | `preloop_ms`, whole-run `tick_rate` |
| **each later load** (room transition, restore) | 1351 ms | **~0 ms** | stall ticks, player-felt hitch |

So the benefit is a **player-experience and stall-term** improvement, not
a startup or Gate 1 improvement. It may still matter to measurement
indirectly -- the stall term is what has limited whole-run resolution --
but that is a downstream hope, not a prediction.

### Conditional benefit: the cost is unconditional, the SAVING is not

Care with the "hitch at every door" framing, mine included:

- **The 1351 ms COST is paid at every door, unconditionally.** That claim
  is measured and stands.
- **The SAVING only materialises where the palette is unchanged.** A room
  with a genuinely different palette rebuilds legitimately and saves
  nothing.

**And whether rooms in real 8-bit games share a palette is UNMEASURED.**
The long Trilby run produced no transitions at all, so the only
same-palette evidence is a *same-room restore* (bench8 full), which is not
evidence about door-to-door transitions. **This stays open, and the
per-transition benefit must not be quoted as if it were established.**

## Operator decisions (2026-09-18) on the light table

**1. Run patch 0112's ABBA, framed as a PLAYER-EXPERIENCE fix, not Gate 1
work.** Threshold on the corrected per-call metric; downstream on the
stall term. The pre-registration must state explicitly that the predicted
effect on `tick_rate` / `preloop_ms` / `fps_p50` is **ZERO, and that a
null result there is a HIT, not a miss.** The palette-churn dependency
stays flagged as unmeasured in the same document: **the ABBA validates
the mechanism; it does not establish the per-transition benefit on real
room-to-room transitions.**

**2. Gate 1's target becomes the FIRST light-table build.** The
arithmetic makes it the obvious candidate: 5000 ticks at 39.095 is
127.89 s, at 39.2 is 127.55 s, so Gate 1 needs about **343 ms** of fixed
overhead removed -- and there is **1351 ms sitting in one function at
startup**. Even a partial win closes it comfortably.

Two directions to evaluate from source before proposing anything, neither
asserted to work:

- **Lazy build.** Does anything in a run actually need `color_map` before
  the first frame? It exists for the blender used by tinted/light
  regions. A game with no tinted region and no blended draw may never
  need the table at all, so building on first use could remove it
  entirely for such games. Requires finding every consumer of `color_map`
  and what forces it.
- **Persist it.** The table is a pure function of the palette and
  `rgb_map`'s state. A 64 KB file keyed on that hash, written once and
  loaded thereafter, trades disk for 1351 ms of CPU -- and this machine
  reads far faster than it computes (the restart-point measurement found
  the bottleneck was serialisation, not I/O: 9.4 KB took 686 ms of CPU
  and ~13 ms of disk).

**Correctness bar for either: prove byte-identity rather than argue it,
and key any cache on everything `create_light_table()` actually branches
on, not just the palette.**

**If both turn out infeasible, say so plainly** -- the operator holds
"several smaller terms" and "revisit the gate definition" as live
alternatives. **Do not stretch a marginal fix to reach 343 ms.**

*Shared error worth recording, since both of us made it:* the coordinator
named the light-table work as the candidate to close Gate 1, and I
carried the same implicit "1351 ms found = Gate 1 moves". Neither of us
checked that the fix could reach the *first* build until the
pre-registration forced the question. **That is pre-registration working
as intended -- the error surfaced before the ABBA, not after it.**

## Patch 0112 ABBA -- PRE-REGISTERED, written 2026-09-18 before any cell ran

**Framing, per the operator: this is a PLAYER-EXPERIENCE fix, not Gate 1
work.**

Arms, each built from a genuine checkout of its own commit:
**A = `086131cad092`** (0111, instrumentation only),
**B = `23b26cfffdd0`** (0112, the fix).

*Build-identity note:* the first B binary was built before 0112 was
committed and therefore carried the **0111** stamp -- `binary_sha12`
derives from the committed tree, so both arms briefly shared
`086131cad092`. Caught by checking, not assumed. My own rule from this
morning ("build each arm from a genuine checkout of its own commit") had
been applied to A but not to B. **The rule only works if applied to every
arm.**

**Fixture: `bench8 full`**, whose AutoPilot saves and restores, so
`generate_light_table()` is called twice in one run. This is the only
fixture available that exercises a second call -- Trilby's script never
transitions (30,000 ticks, one room load).

### Which metric carries the threshold, and why

**`DOSAGS_LIGHTTABLE call=2 ms`** -- the cost of the second call. It is
the only thing this patch changes, it is reported per call in both arms,
and it is measured directly rather than inferred.

**Deliberately NOT `roomload_lighttable_ms`**, which I proposed earlier
and which would have shown **nothing**: the startup report is emitted once
at first-room-ready, so it reports only the FIRST load -- the one call
this patch does not touch.

### Predictions

| metric | A (0111) | B (0112) | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `call=1 action` | rebuilt | **rebuilt** | the fix cannot touch the first build |
| `call=1 ms` | X | **X, unchanged** | same work, both arms |
| `call=2 action` | rebuilt | **reused** | |
| `call=2 ms` | X (>= 300) | **0-1** | |
| `lighttable_reused` | 0 | **1** | |
| PH01.BMP hash | 33d19e90cb9af406 | **identical** | correctness |

`X` is deliberately left unbound: the per-call cost is **not** a constant
across games. `bestfit_color()` exits early on an exact palette match, so
the cost depends on palette content -- under DOSBox it was 252 ms for
Trilby's and 628 ms for BENCH8. Predicting an absolute I have never
measured on this fixture would be the one-sample overconfidence that
produced the compression retraction. **The threshold is set on the
relationship, not on an absolute.**

**WIN threshold:** `call=2 ms` <= 5 in both B cells **AND** `call=2 ms`
>= 300 in both A cells (proving there was a real cost to remove) **AND**
PH01.BMP identical across all four cells.

### Downstream checks -- and where a NULL result is a HIT

**These differ by fixture and must not be conflated:**

- **On `bench8 full`** the restore happens *inside* the measured window,
  so the saving lands in it: **stall term expected to fall, and
  `tick_rate` may rise.** A real effect here is expected.
- **On Gate 1's Trilby fixture** the predicted effect on `tick_rate`,
  `preloop_ms` and `fps_p50` is **ZERO, by construction** -- single room,
  one light-table call, which this patch does not change. **A null result
  there is a HIT, not a miss.** It will be recorded as a confirmation
  that the patch does what it claims and nothing more.

### What this ABBA does NOT establish

**It validates the mechanism. It does not establish the per-transition
benefit on real room-to-room transitions.** The only second call
available is a *same-room restore*, so the palette is trivially unchanged.
**Whether genuinely different rooms in shipped 8-bit games share a
palette is UNMEASURED**, and the per-transition benefit must not be
quoted as established on the strength of this result.

**Invalidity conditions:** any cell not dated 2026-09-18; `binary_sha12`
not matching its arm or not differing between arms; `DOSAGS_CLOCK_CROSSCHECK=1`
absent; RTC cross-check outside 1 +/- 0.5%; non-zero critical/warn counts.

### Pre-registration AMENDED: the patch had to be SPLIT, and cell TNLTA1 is void

**Caught by running cell A1 and reading it, before scoring anything.**

TNLTA1 came back with `build=` lines but **no `ms=` line at all**. Cause:
the per-call timing had been written *inside the fix*, so the A arm --
which by definition does not have the fix -- could not emit the metric the
threshold was set on. **A threshold cannot be set on a number only one arm
emits.** That is the same control rule as measuring in both states, and I
broke it one slice after recording it.

*Fix:* split into two patches, which is also what the repo's own
one-concern-per-patch convention required and the first draft violated:

- **0112 -- time every `generate_light_table()` call.** Measurement only,
  table still rebuilt unconditionally. **This is the A arm.**
- **0113 -- rebuild only when the inputs changed.** The fix. **This is the
  B arm.**

Both arms therefore emit `call=N action=... ms=...`, and the A arm reports
`action=rebuilt` with its real cost where B reports `action=reused`.

**TNLTA1 is void.** Arms rebuilt from genuine checkouts of their own
commits: **A = `d6f44251d55a`** (0112), **B = `dc64ee2e08da`** (0113).
Everything else in the pre-registration above stands unchanged -- fixture
`bench8 full`, threshold on `call=2 ms`, absolute cost left unbound, zero
effect on Gate 1's Trilby fixture being a HIT, and the per-transition
benefit remaining unestablished.

## Gate 1 direction: can the FIRST light-table build be avoided? Source analysis

The operator's two candidates were lazy build and persistence. The source
says **lazy build is the stronger one**, and the reason is that
`color_map` has a remarkably small consumer surface.

### Every read of `color_map` in the whole tree

`color_map` is **8-bit only**. It is dereferenced nowhere in AGS itself --
AGS's single reference is the null *test* at `ac/region.cpp:137`. Every
real deref is inside vendored Allegro's 8-bit blender macro header
`libsrc/allegro/src/c/cdefs8.h` (`:41`, `:46`, `:51`, `:57`); the 15/16/24/32-bit
headers use `_blender_func*` instead.

Those macros are instantiated in exactly four routines --
`_linear_putpixel8`, `_linear_hline8`, `_linear_draw_trans_sprite8`,
`_linear_draw_lit_sprite8` -- and **AGS can reach them through exactly two
lines**:

- `Common/gfx/allegrobitmap.cpp:370` -- `TransBlendBlt` -> `draw_trans_sprite`
- `Common/gfx/allegrobitmap.cpp:376` -- `LitBlendBlt` -> `draw_lit_sprite`

**That choke point is what makes a lazy scheme a two-line hook rather than
a scattered audit.**

### What actually reaches it in an 8-bit game

Almost nothing. Checked caller by caller: `tint_image` bails out below 9
bpp; the screen-tint path is queued only when `_srcColorDepth > 8`
(`gfx/ali3dsw.cpp:466`); sprite alpha blending requires 32-bit
(`gfx/gfx_util.cpp:94`); **object/character/GUI transparency in 8-bit
falls through to a plain masked blit** (`gfx_util.cpp:127`); 8-bit fades
go through `set_palette_range` instead (`ac/screen.cpp:333`); AA text
needs >= 16 bpp. `draw.cpp:1747` explicitly zeroes `tint_level` at
`color_depth == 1`.

**The one realistically reachable path is `apply_tint_or_light` ->
`LitBlendBlt` (`ac/draw.cpp:1844`), and in 8-bit only for NEGATIVE light
levels -- region darkening.** `draw.cpp:1798-1801` drops tints and
brightening in 8-bit; darkening falls through.

`_linear_putpixel8` / `_linear_hline8` need `DRAW_MODE_TRANS`, and AGS
never calls `drawing_mode()`/`solid_mode()`/`xor_mode()` anywhere, so
those two are unreachable.

### The finding that matters for Gate 1

> **A plain 8-bit room render with no light regions never dereferences
> `color_map` at all.** For such a game the 1351 ms build is pure waste --
> established by following the code paths, not inferred.

**So if Trilby's Notes uses no region darkening, lazy construction removes
the entire 1351 ms, and Gate 1 needs only ~343 ms.** That is the
hypothesis to test next -- **and it must be MEASURED, not assumed**, which
is a counter on those two choke-point methods.

### Risks, recorded before any implementation

1. **Layering.** `allegrobitmap.cpp` is in `Common/`; `generate_light_table()`
   and the palette live in `Engine/`. A hook needs a callback installed at
   startup, or the layering breaks. This is the main structural cost.
2. **The null sentinel is overloaded.** `region.cpp:137` uses
   `color_map == nullptr` to mean "needs building", while `room.cpp:1035`
   sets null to mean "discard blender". Under lazy build the pointer stays
   null indefinitely, so patch 0113's cache must key off its own `bool`
   rather than the pointer. `savegame.cpp:890` needs the same treatment.
3. **No graceful degradation.** `cspr.h:545` dereferences `color_map`
   *before* the pixel loop and after the clip early-outs, so a missed hook
   is a **hard fault on real hardware, not a visual glitch**. Any lazy
   scheme should also harden `cdefs8.h` with a null guard, or keep a small
   static identity `COLOR_MAP` as a non-null fallback, so a missed path
   degrades instead of crashing.
4. **One unguarded path.** `ac/draw.cpp:1447` tests `src_has_alpha &&
   alpha == 0xFF` with **no colour-depth check**, so an 8-bit game with
   `SPF_ALPHACHANNEL` set on a sprite could reach
   `_linear_draw_trans_sprite8`. Pathological but possible -- **hook both
   methods, not just `LitBlendBlt`.**
5. **Moving the hitch.** For a game that DOES darken, lazy build moves
   1351 ms from room load into the first frame the character steps on the
   region -- arguably worse-feeling. **The hybrid is better: keep 0113's
   cache AND make the initial build lazy**, so a game with no light
   regions never pays it and a game that uses them pays once.

## CRITICAL for the Gate 1 half: deferring the build is WORTHLESS. Only eliminating it counts.

Whole-run `tick_rate` is ticks over **total elapsed wall time**. So 1351 ms
moved out of the pre-loop and into the first lit frame leaves total
elapsed **unchanged** and the gate exactly where it was.

**And it would look like progress**: `preloop_ms` would fall by 1351 ms
while the gate metric did not move at all. That is precisely the shape of
a partial result being misread as a win, so the criterion is written
before the work rather than after:

> **Gate 1 success condition: the light table is NEVER BUILT at any point
> during the 5000-tick window.** Not deferred past first frame -- never
> built. Patch 0114's choke-point counters answer exactly this
> (`colormap_consumers transblend=0 litblend=0` means it was never
> needed).

### The two halves have DIFFERENT success conditions

| half | fixture | what counts as success |
|---|---|---|
| **Player experience** | any game, any room | **Deferral IS valuable.** A hitch never paid beats one paid at startup, and for a game that never darkens it disappears entirely. |
| **Gate 1** | Trilby, 5000 ticks, room 1 | **Only elimination over the whole window.** Deferral scores zero. |

### Design consequence: the safe fallback is the DEFAULT, not a guard

`libsrc/allegro/src/c/cspr.h:545` dereferences `color_map` *before* the
pixel loop and after the clip early-outs, so a missed hook is a **hard
fault on the operator's machine**. And our correctness gate is DOSBox-X,
where **a path that never executes cannot be caught** -- the gate is
structurally unable to find this class of miss.

So the design must make a miss degrade rather than fault: **install a
non-null identity `COLOR_MAP` up front.** 64 KB of static data turns "we
forgot a hook" into "that one blend renders wrong" instead of a crash.
That is the default shape of the design, not a guard bolted on afterwards.
Both `TransBlendBlt` and `LitBlendBlt` get hooked, per the
`ac/draw.cpp:1447` path that has no colour-depth check.

## Standing rule: "probably doesn't matter" is how a pre-registration gets quietly relaxed

Recorded as a rule, not as a note on one cell.

When a cell is voided mid-sequence, the remaining cells no longer form the
pre-registered design. The temptation is to finish with what is left --
here, holding two B cells and running A,A to get four cells in the
file -- and to justify it on the grounds that the confound the design
guards against is implausible for this particular metric.

**That reasoning is almost always available, and it is exactly how a
pre-registration stops constraining anything.** The rule: **if the
executed sequence is not the pre-registered one, either re-run it or
report the deviation explicitly as a deviation.** Do not argue that the
design was unnecessary in this instance. Applied here: TNLTA1 was voided,
and rather than run B,B,A,A a clean A,B,B,A was re-run from scratch.

## Patch 0114 first result: Trilby's Gate 1 window NEVER uses the light table

Emulator, Trilby's Notes, `DOSAGS_TAS_AUTO_EXIT_TICK=5000` -- the exact
Gate 1 window:

```
DOS-PORT colormap_consumers transblend=0 litblend=0
DOSAGS_LIGHTTABLE call=1 action=rebuilt ms=225 rebuilt_total=1
```

**Zero. Across the whole benchmark window, `color_map` is never
dereferenced once.** The table is built, at a cost of 1351 ms on real
hardware, and then never read.

**This meets the Gate 1 success condition as written** -- not "deferred
past first frame" but *never needed at all*, so a lazy build would
**eliminate** the 1351 ms rather than move it. Gate 1 needs ~343 ms and
this is 1351 ms.

*Status and caveats, before this gets treated as a result:*

- **This is DOSBox, and real hardware is the authority in this campaign.**
  It is a deterministic code-path count rather than a timing measurement,
  and the benchmark has no input, so it should hold on hardware -- but
  "should" is not "does". **To be confirmed on HW-486-66 before any
  prediction rests on it.**
- **Scope is the benchmark window, not the game.** Trilby's Notes may well
  use region darkening in rooms the benchmark never visits. This says the
  *Gate 1 fixture* never needs the table; it does not say the game never
  does. For the player-experience half a game that does darken would pay
  the build once, lazily, which is the hybrid's intended behaviour.
- It also does not license removing the build for other games. **BENCH8,
  5days and the rest are unmeasured on this counter.**

### BENCH8 also never dereferences `color_map`

Same counter, `bench8 full` under the emulator:

```
DOS-PORT colormap_consumers transblend=0 litblend=0
```

**Both 8-bit fixtures build the light table and never read it.** On
BENCH8 that build costs **4699 ms** on HW-486-66 -- measured, and paid
*twice* per run of the `full` scene (startup plus the restore), so
**~9.4 seconds of a benchmark run is spent computing a table nothing
reads.**

That is now two fixtures out of two. It does not generalise to shipped
8-bit games -- **BENCH8 is our own authored content, and Trilby's is one
title** -- but it does mean the lazy approach is not a corner case: the
fixtures this campaign actually measures on would both drop the cost
entirely.

*Note the two costs are very different and both are real:* 1351 ms on
Trilby's, 4699 ms on BENCH8, same code and same 65,280 `bestfit_color()`
calls. The spread is palette content -- `bestfit_color()` exits early on
an exact match. **A per-game figure must never be quoted as the engine's
figure.**

## Evaluating the "declared darkening" design (source only, not implemented)

The concern behind it: **pure lazy has a player-experience regression.**
For a game that DOES darken, it moves a 1351-4699 ms cost out of room
load -- where a pause is expected and forgiven -- into the first lit
frame, an unexplained mid-game freeze. Every benchmark number would
improve while the game got worse to play.

### What "declares darkening" has to mean, from source

**8-bit can only darken, and the engine says so itself** --
`ac/draw.cpp:1737-1741`:

> `// In a 256-colour game, we cannot do tinting or lightening`
> `// (but we can do darkening, if light_level < 0)`
> `if (game.color_depth == 1) { if ((light_level > 0) || (tint_amount != 0)) return; }`

and `draw.cpp:1746-1748` zeroes `tint_level` outright when
`game.color_depth == 1`. **So in 8-bit, tint never needs the table and no
separate tint test is required.** Only `light_level < 0` matters.

`light_level` has exactly two sources (`get_local_tint`, `draw.cpp:1735-1776`):

1. **Region-declared** -- `thisroom.Regions[onRegion].Light`, or
   `Regions[0].Light` when `onRegion <= 0` (`draw.cpp:1795-1802`).
2. **Ambient, script-set** -- when `play.rtint_enabled` and
   `play.rtint_level <= 0`, `light_level = play.rtint_light`
   (`draw.cpp:1758-1774`).

So the test is: **any `Regions[i].Light < 0` over `MAX_ROOM_REGIONS`, OR
ambient darkening enabled.** `Light == 0` means no change, so the `< 0`
test handles an unconfigured room correctly.

### Is the data in hand at the call site? Yes, on both paths

- **Restore path:** `game/savegame.cpp:885-889` copies `RoomLightLevels`
  into `thisroom.Regions[i].Light` *immediately before* calling
  `generate_light_table()`.
- **Normal path:** region parameters are read during `LoadRoom` and the
  region state is set up at `ac/room.cpp:692-808`, both **before**
  `:1001`'s `generate_light_table()`.

Cost of the test: a scan of `MAX_ROOM_REGIONS` ints against 65,280
palette scans -- nothing.

### The residual case that still needs the lazy hook

**Region light IS script-settable at runtime** --
`ac/global_region.cpp:71` (`SetAreaLightLevel`) and `:107`
(`SetRegionTint`'s luminance form) both assign
`thisroom.Regions[area].Light` after room load. `play.rtint_*` likewise.

**So the declared test cannot be the only mechanism**, and the resulting
shape is exactly the three-case one:

| case | behaviour |
|---|---|
| room declares no darkening | **never built** -- Gate 1's case, and both measured fixtures |
| room declares darkening | **built at load, as today** -- no regression, no mid-game hitch |
| script enables darkening later | lazy hook pays once; the only unavoidable mid-game cost |

### Design order, per the safety argument

**The identity-table fallback is designed FIRST and the hooks are the
optimisation on top, not the reverse.** If the common case is that the
table is never built, then every consumer path becomes a path that has
never executed in testing -- and DOSBox cannot catch a missed hook,
because it will not execute there either. A non-null identity
`COLOR_MAP` makes a miss render one blend wrong instead of hard-faulting
on the operator's machine. That is the load-bearing safety property of
the whole change.

**Still unverified and not to be assumed:** that `Regions[]` is fully
populated at `room.cpp:1001` on *every* entry path (not just the two
traced), and the semantics of `Light` for a room with no regions at all.
**If the declared test proves unreliable, pure lazy plus the identity
fallback is still a better trade than today** -- it only costs the
mid-game hitch in the darkening case.

### Independent reachability check on the zero -- and what it does NOT close

The zero rests on the counters at `Common/gfx/allegrobitmap.cpp:370/376`
being the only route to a `color_map` dereference. The structural worry:
the routines that actually dereference it are wired into Allegro's own
8-bit graphics **vtable** (`libsrc/allegro/src/vtable8.c:54,56` ->
`_linear_draw_trans_sprite8` / `_linear_draw_lit_sprite8`). **A vtable
entry is reachable by anything that dispatches through it**, not only by
the callers anyone traced -- so another path would leave the counters
reading zero while the table was genuinely being read, and the whole
elimination would rest on a false premise.

*Checked, and it holds:* across `Engine` and `Common` the only callers of
the vtable-dispatched API are `allegrobitmap.cpp:390` (`draw_trans_sprite`)
and `:399` (`draw_lit_sprite`) -- the same two functions the counters
bracket. `color_map` appears in exactly two files in the vendored Allegro
tree: its definition at `color.c:82` and the four blender macros in
`c/cdefs8.h`.

**What this does not close, stated deliberately:** it is a *static
reachability argument over the AGS-side tree*, which has **the same
epistemic status as the caller analysis that was deliberately distrusted**
when the counters were placed at the choke point rather than at the
callers. It says nothing about Allegro-internal paths nobody enumerated,
nor about anything reached through a function pointer rather than a named
call. **It raises confidence; it is not a substitute for failing safe, and
the identity-table fallback stays the load-bearing property regardless.**

*What it does genuinely strengthen:* since the vtable entries are the real
dereference sites and they are reached only through those two wrappers, a
hook placed **at the wrappers is complete for this build by
construction** -- resting on a two-element vtable surface with two known
callers rather than on having enumerated every caller correctly. That is a
stronger position than the original caller analysis, and it is a different
*kind* of argument, not just more of the same one.

## Note for the patch 0115 pre-registration: its shape INVERTS 0113's

Recorded now so the two are not conflated in the record later. They are
opposite in what counts as success, and writing 0115 by analogy to 0113
would get it exactly backwards.

| | patch 0113 (cache / reuse) | patch 0115 (lazy / eager-if-declared) |
|---|---|---|
| gate metrics (`tick_rate`, `preloop_ms`, `fps_p50`) | **ZERO movement predicted; a null is a HIT** | **movement IS the point** |
| threshold lives on | the per-call metric (`call=2 ms`) | **whole-run `tick_rate` crossing 39.2** |
| supporting evidence | stall term, downstream | consumer counters and `preloop_ms` |

**0115's success condition is a CONJUNCTION, and either half alone is
insufficient:**

> **(a) the light table is never built at any point in the 5000-tick
> window, AND (b) whole-run `tick_rate` crosses the band.**

*Why both:* a never-built table that somehow does **not** move the gate
would mean the time went somewhere unaccounted for -- the model would be
wrong even though the patch "worked". A crossing **without** the counters
at zero would mean we do not know why it moved, and an unexplained
crossing is not a closed gate. **Each half checks a different failure,
and this campaign has now been bitten by both kinds** -- unaccounted time
(TNCQA2's 152 ms) and an effect credited to the wrong cause (the
compression size claim).

*Also required of 0115, from the safety analysis:* the identity-table
fallback is designed first and the hooks are the optimisation on top,
because if the table is normally never built then every consumer path is
one that has never executed in testing and the DOSBox gate cannot catch a
missed hook.

**Prerequisite, not yet satisfied:** the zero is currently DOSBox-only.
**A standalone HW-486-66 cell with the 0114 build must confirm
`transblend=0 litblend=0` before 0115 is designed**, since the whole
approach rests on it. The 0113 ABBA arms predate 0114 and cannot carry
that counter, and a clean ABBA must not be contaminated to piggyback it.

Validity: `exit_code=0`, `critical_count=0`, `warn_count=0`,

### Verdict: PASS. All three threshold conditions met.

| condition | result | |
|---|---|---|
| `call=2 ms` <= 5 in both B cells | 0, 0 | **pass** |
| `call=2 ms` >= 300 in both A cells | 4699, 4699 | **pass** |

*Every prediction hit:*

| predicted | measured |
|---|---|
| `call=1` rebuilt in BOTH arms | rebuilt in all four |
| `call=1 ms` unchanged between arms | **4699 in all four cells** |
| `call=2` A rebuilt / B reused | exactly that |
| `call=2 ms` A >= 300 / B 0-1 | 4699 / 0 |
| PH01 identical | identical |

### The downstream signature is the part worth keeping

**`preloop_ms` is UNCHANGED across arms** -- 5313/5526 in A against
5313/5529 in B. **The saving lands entirely in the stall term**:
`stall_ms` mean **10,680 (A) -> 5,881 (B)**, a drop of **4,799 ms**,
against a single skipped build of 4,699 ms.

That is the predicted signature, and it is worth more than the threshold
pass: **the patch removed exactly the cost it claimed to remove, in
exactly the metric it should have landed in, and did not move the metric
it should not have moved.** A saving that had shown up in `preloop_ms`
would have meant the first build was being skipped, which would be a
correctness problem, not a win.

*(`tick_rate` on this fixture is ~2-3, not ~40, because `full` is a
43-tick correctness scene dominated by stalls, not a rate benchmark. It
rose 2.38 -> 3.24, consistent with the stall drop, but the absolute is
not a frame-rate figure and must not be quoted as one.)*

**Gate 1 is untouched, as pre-registered.** This fixture is not the gate
fixture, and on the gate fixture the predicted effect remains zero.

### The build-stamp trap has now bitten THREE times. It needs a fix, not another note.

Occurrences: (1) the 0108 A arm built by reverse-applying a patch to the
working tree; (2) the first 0113 B binary built before its commit; (3)
cell **TNCM1**, the first attempt at the above, which carried
`binary_sha12=dc64ee2e08da` -- **0113's stamp on a 0114 binary**, colliding
with the ABBA's B arm.

*Root cause, same every time:* `Makefile:105` derives `AGS_BUILD_SHA12`
from `git -C vendor/ags rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` -- **the committed tree.**
A binary built from a working tree that differs from HEAD, whether by an
uncommitted edit or by being built before the commit, is stamped with a
tree it was not built from. The stamp is silently wrong, and it is wrong
in the direction that *passes* the "arms must differ" check.

*Handling this time:* TNCM1 was discarded and re-run as TNCM2 after
rebuilding post-commit, rather than accepted on the grounds that its
conclusion was obviously unaffected. The conclusion **was** unaffected --
which is exactly the argument that would retire the check if taken.

**Proposed fix (port-local, not `shared/`): fold the working tree's dirty
state into `AGS_BUILD_SHA12`** -- e.g. append `git -C vendor/ags status
--porcelain` or a `git stash create` tree hash to the hashed inputs. Then
a working-tree build gets its own distinct stamp instead of impersonating
the last commit, and the failure becomes visible rather than silent. **Not
implemented yet; recorded as the next instrumentation fix.**

## Patch 0115 -- DRAFT pre-registration (not yet implemented, not yet run)

**Shape INVERTS 0113's.** 0113 predicted zero movement in the gate
metrics and treated a null as a hit. **Here, movement in the gate metric
IS the point.**

### Design (to build): eager-if-declared, lazy otherwise, identity fallback first

Built in this order deliberately -- **the fallback is the load-bearing
safety property, the hooks are the optimisation on top:**

1. **Install a non-null identity `COLOR_MAP` at startup.** If the table is
   normally never built, then every consumer path becomes one that has
   **never executed in testing**, and the DOSBox gate cannot catch a
   missed hook because it will not execute there either.
   `libsrc/allegro/src/c/cspr.h:545` dereferences `color_map` *before* the
   pixel loop, so a miss is a **hard fault on the operator's machine**.
   The identity table makes a miss render one blend wrong instead.
2. **Skip the eager build when the room declares no darkening.** 8-bit can
   only darken (`ac/draw.cpp:1737-1748`), so the test is
   `Regions[i].Light < 0` over `MAX_ROOM_REGIONS`, plus ambient darkening
   (`play.rtint_enabled && play.rtint_level <= 0 && play.rtint_light < 0`).
3. **Build eagerly at load when it does declare darkening** -- no
   regression, no mid-game freeze, exactly today's behaviour.
4. **Lazy hook at `Bitmap::TransBlendBlt` and `Bitmap::LitBlendBlt`**
   (`Common/gfx/allegrobitmap.cpp:370/376`) for the script-enables-it-later
   case. **Both**, not just the lit one --
   `ac/draw.cpp:1447` has no colour-depth check.

### Threshold: whole-run `tick_rate`, and the success condition is a CONJUNCTION

> **(a) `colormap_consumers transblend=0 litblend=0` AND no light table
> built at any point in the 5000-tick window, AND**
> **(b) whole-run `tick_rate` crosses 39.2.**

**Either alone is insufficient, and each half catches a failure this
campaign has already suffered:**

- **(a) without (b)** -- the build vanished but the gate did not move --
  means the time went somewhere unaccounted for. That is TNCQA2's 152 ms
  hole, which was real.
- **(b) without (a)** -- it crossed, but the counters say the table was
  still built -- means we do not know why it moved. That is the
  compression size claim, credited to the wrong cause. **An unexplained
  crossing is not a closed gate.**

### Predictions

| metric | A (0114) | B (0115) | basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| light table builds in window | 1, at 1351 ms | **0** | TNCM2 measured zero consumers |
| `colormap_consumers` | 0 / 0 | **0 / 0, unchanged** | it was already never read |
| `preloop_ms` | ~2060 | **~709** | 2060 - 1351 |
| whole-run `tick_rate` | ~39.12 | **~39.53** | 5000/(127.85 - 1.351) |
| `tick_rate_steady` | 40.04 | **unchanged** | startup only |
| `fps_p50` | 40.00 | **unchanged** | startup only |
| PH01 / screenshot hash | -- | **identical** | correctness |

Gate 1 needs ~343 ms; this removes 1351 ms, so the predicted crossing has
margin rather than landing on the line. **That margin is itself a claim to
be checked** -- if it crosses by far less than predicted, the model is
wrong even though the gate passed, and that must be reported rather than
banked.

**Supporting, NOT threshold-carrying:** `preloop_ms` and the consumer
counters. **Downstream:** the stall term.

### Stated limits, before any result

- **Scope is the Gate 1 fixture.** Trilby's may darken in rooms the
  benchmark never enters; a game that does darken pays the build once,
  which is the design working as intended, not a regression.
- **The player-experience half has a different success condition** and is
  not scored here.
- **Unverified:** that `Regions[]` is fully populated at `room.cpp:1001`
  on every entry path, and `Light` semantics for a room with no regions.
  **If the declared test proves unreliable, fall back to pure lazy plus
  the identity table** rather than stretching the declared test.

**Invalidity:** any cell not dated on its run date; `binary_sha12` not
matching its arm or not differing between arms (**and built AFTER its own
commit** -- see the three-time stamp trap); `DOSAGS_CLOCK_CROSSCHECK=1`
absent; ratio outside 1 +/- 0.5%; non-zero critical/warn.

## Build-stamp trap FIXED and proven (2026-09-18)

The instrument, not a workaround. Three occurrences in one day made it a
pattern rather than bad luck, and **patch 0116's invalidity conditions
depend on the stamp being trustworthy**, so it was fixed before that work
rather than after.

### What was wrong

`Makefile:105` derived `AGS_BUILD_SHA12` from
`git -C vendor/ags rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` -- the **committed** tree. A
binary built from a working tree differing from HEAD was stamped with a
tree it was not built from. **Silently, and in the direction that PASSES
the "the two arms must differ" check**, since two working-tree builds off
one commit share a stamp.

### The fix

**1. Content-sensitive dirt folded into the hash.** `git diff HEAD` per
vendor tree, plus `sha256sum` of every untracked file.

**`git diff HEAD` rather than `git status --porcelain`, and the difference
is real, not theoretical:** porcelain lists changed *paths*, so two
different edits to the same file produce the same string and would
collide with each other. Demonstrated on the actual tree:

| tree state | `build_dirty` | `sha12` |
|---|---|---|
| clean | 0 | `49513e71bebd` |
| one edit to `region.cpp` | 1 | `6e8a3e324187` |
| **a different edit to the SAME file** | 1 | **`c4e779a6d7a9`** |
| edit reverted | 0 | `49513e71bebd` (returns to the clean value) |

Untracked files are hashed because `git diff HEAD` cannot see them. Engine
sources are listed explicitly rather than globbed (only `RESOURCE_FILES`
uses `file(GLOB)`), so an untracked `.cpp` would not be compiled -- but an
untracked `.h` can be included by one that is. No git objects are created,
unlike `git stash create`, so it is safe on every `make`.

**2. Dirtiness made VISIBLE, not merely different** (patch 0115). A
changed hash tells a later reader that two builds differ, not that either
was built from uncommitted source. The manifest now carries its own line:

```
binary_sha12=cf8fea42640a
DOS-PORT build_dirty=1
```

Its own line rather than a `-dirty` suffix, because `binary_sha12` is
**fixed-width in the manifest struct**. Absent the compile flag it reports
**-1 (unknown), not 0** -- a build stage that omits the flag must not be
readable as a clean build.

**3. `make build-dirty`** reports `build_dirty` and the stamp *before* an
arm is built, rather than leaving it to be discovered in a cell's manifest
afterwards.

### Proven end to end

Dirty tree -> `build_dirty=1`, stamp `cf8fea42640a`. After committing ->
`build_dirty=0`, stamp `e5f43b022a08`. Both read back from a real
`RUNMANI.LOG`.

**The lazy light-table patch is renumbered 0116** (0115 is this fix); its
draft pre-registration above stands unchanged apart from the number.

## The darkening fallback is TESTED. All three states, emulator AND hardware. (2026-09-18)

The condition Gate 1's sign-off was withheld on.

### Getting the path to execute at all took finding TWO gates, not one

An earlier attempt (`DOSAGS_FORCE_DARKEN`, patch 0116) set ambient
darkening and still produced `colormap_consumers 0/0` on both fixtures.
**The reason is not that darkening was off -- it is that the character was
exempt from it.**

- BENCH8's character is generated with **`UseRoomAreaLighting=False`**
  (`tests/fixtures/bench/gen_agf.py:208`), which sets `CHF_NOLIGHTING` ->
  clears `OBJF_USEREGIONTINTS`, and `ac/draw.cpp:1970` passes that as
  `use_region_tint`.
- **Everything** in `get_local_tint` sits inside `if (use_region_tint)`
  (`ac/draw.cpp:1717`) -- **including the ambient `play.rtint_*` branch.**

**So the env-var approach could never have worked, on any fixture whose
character has that flag set.** Both levers are required: the character
must be subject to room lighting AND something must darken.

The new `dark` scene sets both from script, so it needs no change to the
generated game and no region mask:

```
player.IgnoreLighting = false;   // Character_SetIgnoreLighting
region[0].LightLevel = -100;     // region 0 is get_local_tint's fallback
```

Region 0 works because `ac/draw.cpp:1799-1802` falls back to
`Regions[0].Light` when the character stands on no region -- **no region
mask had to be authored.** The light level is negative because 8-bit can
only darken.

### The three states

| state | light table | `litblend` | PH01 | exit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1. eager build, used** (arm 0116) | rebuilt at load | **1** | `7e0a277e3d4758c8` | 0 |
| **2. skipped, lazy hook fires** (0117) | skipped, then rebuilt on the blend | **1** | **`7e0a277e3d4758c8`** | 0 |
| **3. skipped, hook MISSING** (0118 test) | skipped, never built | **1** | `94b0d885d8ebca78` | **0** |

**Identical results on DOSBox-X and on HW-486-66** (cells TNDK1, TNDK2;
`binary_sha12=ccdc4269a903`, `build_dirty=0`, `critical_count=0`,
`warn_count=0`).

**`colormap_consumers` reports non-zero for the first time in this
campaign** -- the counter built to prove the table was unused is now the
instrument proving the consumer path runs.

### What each state establishes

**State 2 is the correctness proof for the lazy hook:** its render is
**byte-identical** to the eager build. Deferring the build to the first
blend changes nothing observable.

**State 3 is the one that had never run, and it is the reason sign-off was
withheld.** With the hook deliberately absent, a blend reaches Allegro
with `color_map` pointing at the identity table. On real hardware it
**renders and exits cleanly** -- `exit_code=0`, no criticals, no warnings.
Without the identity table this is a hard fault: `cspr.h:545` dereferences
before the pixel loop.

**The degradation is cosmetic and localised, confirmed visually rather
than inferred from a hash:** the character draws **unblended at full
colour** instead of darkened to near-black. **Everything else in the scene
is pixel-identical.** A missed hook costs one sprite's shading, not
corruption and not a crash.

### Scope, unchanged

BENCH8 is **our own authored content**. This is evidence for the **code
path and the safety property**, and is **not** evidence about how shipped
games use darkening.

and matching within pairs, **`build_dirty=0` verified before building each
arm**, and `exit_code=0` / `critical_count=0` / `warn_count=0` /
