   `HARDWARE.md` and `COMPATIBILITY.md` is load-bearing, not boilerplate, and
   must not be dropped from any figure.
3. **Next front is Gate 3's lower output resolution** -- the rung concession
   approved long ago and never spent. Gate 3 is closed on evidence at 38.0 at
   full resolution, and this is the one untried route to 40 at 16-bit.
4. **No external writeup until Gate 2.**

## Gate 2's two facts, which must both stay visible

Ruling 1 makes the hold open-ended by choice, so **the record stops calling
Gate 2 "nearly closed"**. Two separate facts, both true, neither implying the
other:

- **Gate 2 passes 4/4 on all three measures**, spread 0.01, gate-enforced,
  every cell individually reported.
- **Gate 2 is unclaimed**, held on an unexplained ~220 ms hardware stall, by
  operator choice and with no deadline.

## Sequencing: I agree, and the trigger is likely to fire

Rulings 1 and 3 conflict in practice and the coordinator's resolution is
right: run the stall front to its next genuine decision point, and **if the
RAM-disk cell returns without a named mechanism and without a cheap next
lever already identified, open the Gate 3 lower-resolution work rather than
manufacturing a sixth variation.**

**I expect that trigger to fire.** Outcome A -- "at or below the
block-device layer" -- is the likely one, and it names four candidates rather
than a mechanism.

**So the next lever should be identified now, not in the moment.** It exists
and it is cheap: **boot without SMARTDRV at all.** `C-` disabled the caching;
the TSR stayed resident and kept hooking INT 13h, and a cost in its
pass-through path survived untouched. Removing one `LH` line from
`AUTOEXEC.BAT` separates *resident in the path* from *caching*, which is
exactly the half-candidate left over from the A-B-B-A cell. Same class of
change as the RAM-disk one, same restore discipline, and it is the difference
between "four candidates" and "three".

**It is a second ask and should not be folded into the first** -- two levers
in one boot-config change is the discipline failure this whole thread has
been about.

## A design improvement to the RAM-disk cell, from the same discipline

**Run C: and the RAM disk in the SAME boot, A-B-B-A on the device.**

The design as written compares a RAM-disk sweep against C: sweeps from
earlier runs. That is a between-boot comparison of exactly the kind
`abba-methodology.md` exists to prevent, and the same objection that forced
the SMARTDRV cell to be rebuilt applies unchanged: first-write-after-boot is
confounded with whichever arm runs first, and device state accumulates in one
direction.

`FSPROBE_PATH` is already per-stage-settable via the `FSPROBE_S*` mechanism,
so the sweep can alternate `C:\FSTEST\FSSWEEP.TMP` and the RAM disk's path
within one boot with no new code. **Device becomes the only variable, and the
A-to-A check comes free.**

# ECHO cell 2: the environment path is exonerated, and the pipe reproduces on demand

| var | position | payload | arrived |
|---|---|---|---|
| **E1** | first | 72-char `#` value | **intact, 72** |
| **E14** | late | **same** 72-char `#` value | **intact, 72** |
| **E2** | early | 72 chars, spaces, no specials | **intact, 72** |
| E3 | head | plain 17 | intact |
| **E13** | **last** | plain 17, identical to E3 | **intact** |
| **E15** | late | 72-char **`\|`** value | **`SMARTDRV /S` -- 11, TRUNCATED** |

And the `SET` dump shows every variable present, with
`FSPROBE_E15=SMARTDRV /S` **already truncated inside DOS's own
environment** -- so the cut happens at or before `SET`, exactly where the
pipe story puts it.

## Every branch resolves

- **E15 truncates in this very cell.** The path is confirmed **identical**
  to the one that broke, so an intact E14 exonerates the value rather than
  meaning the probe missed the path. That was E15's whole job and it did it.
- **E1 == E14, both intact.** Position cleared **and** name length cleared
  together -- the confound I flagged is moot, exactly as the pre-registered
  reading said it would be if they agreed.
- **E2 intact.** Length and whitespace cleared at the full 72 characters.
- **E3 and E13 both intact.** No environment exhaustion; the tail control
  survived under ~288 bytes of payload.

**The `#` value survives the failing path intact, at full length, at both
ends of the argument list.** The environment transit is not what broke the
`#` run.

## The residue, resolved as far as the evidence allows

That leaves the staged binary: a `fsprobe.exe` still splitting on `|` when
the `#` value was sent. **I cannot prove it** -- that binary is overwritten
and the arithmetic does not fit cleanly either, since a `|` split of a
`#`-only value should have produced one stage of three `;`-separated
commands and what ran was one command.

**What I can say is what matters for the next cell: it was not the
environment**, by measurement, on the exact value and the exact path. And
the failure mode is now structurally impossible regardless of its cause --
`FSPROBE_S1..S8` carries no delimiter, and `FSPROBE_STAGES` refuses the run
on a count mismatch rather than shortening it. abba3 proved both work.

**Recorded as an unexplained-but-contained failure**, not as a solved one. It
is the honest label: the mechanism is unknown, the class is closed.

## Known-bad characters for this harness path

`|` truncates the value at that point. `>` truncates. `%` is **deleted in
place**, leaving everything after it -- which a presence check passes and
only a byte-for-byte comparison catches. `#`, `;`, `^`, `&`, `,`, space and
100-plus plain characters all survive. **Verified, not inferred.**

# The residue is NAMED, and it is a bug in my own probe: nested `strtok`

The coordinator's correction to my disconfirming arithmetic was right in
general -- a `/S` **table** count is not a **command** count, and commands
that print no table are invisible to it. **But the abba2 output carries the
command count directly**, because `run_cmds` prints one `===== STAGEn: <cmd>
=====` line per command with the command's own text. The whole file contains
**three** `=====` lines:

    21: ===== STAGE1: SMARTDRV /S =====
    41: ===== STAGE1 rc=1 =====
    43: fsprobe: ===== SWEEP 1 (STAGE1) =====

**One command, and its text is `SMARTDRV /S` -- eleven characters.** A `|`
split of the `#` value would have printed `SMARTDRV /S#SMARTDRV C- ` as its
first token. So the stale-binary hypothesis does not fit either, and neither
does transit, which ECHO 2 measured clean.

## The actual mechanism, in `fsprobe.c`

    665:  for (stage = strtok(buf, "#"); stage; stage = strtok(NULL, "#")) {
    669:      run_cmds(stage, label);        <-- and run_cmds does:
    402:      for (tok = strtok(buf2, ";"); tok; tok = strtok(NULL, ";"))

**`strtok` holds one global state pointer. The inner call destroys the outer
loop's.** So `strtok(NULL, "#")` at the top of iteration two returns NULL and
**the loop ends after stage 1** -- one stage, one command, one sweep, with
the value fully intact in memory the whole time.

It explains every observation at once:

- **the `#` run**: value arrived intact, stage 1 correct, loop terminated.
  Exactly what was seen.
- **the `|` run**: value truncated to `SMARTDRV /S` by the pipe *and* the
  nested `strtok` -- two independent causes of the same single stage, which
  is why the two runs were byte-identical in structure.
- **abba3 working**: `FSPROBE_S1..S8` uses a counted `for` loop over
  `getenv`, with **no `strtok` in the outer loop.** The fix that was adopted
  for delimiter-safety happened to remove this bug too, which is why the
  cell suddenly worked and why I could not see what had changed.

**So I suspected the environment, then a stale binary, and it was my own
code in both cases.** Two exonerations of other components, one bug, and the
component I never suspected was the one I wrote.

## The staging round trip: it exists

`run-probe-hw.sh` does `stage-file --replace` for the probe, CWSDPMI and the
BAT, then `send-file --return`, then checks `job_ok` and prints **"all files
verified byte-for-byte"**, with one automatic recovery and a hard refusal if
it still fails. So the stale-binary hypothesis was **already dead** before I
raised it -- the check that would have caught it is in the script and
passes. **I should have read the harness before hypothesising about it**,
which is the same failure as reasoning about `#` without testing `#`.

**Nothing to fix there. The residue is closed with a named mechanism**, not
merely contained -- which also means the RAM-disk cell starts from a clean
harness rather than a suspected one.

# RAMDRIVE.SYS is on the card. The blocker was mine, and it lasted one search.

    Directory of C:\WINDOWS
    RAMDRIVE SYS         5,873 11-01-93   3:11a

    C:\WINDOWS\*.SYS:  HIMEM.SYS  IFSHLP.SYS  RAMDRIVE.SYS

The whole-volume `DIR C:\*.SYS /S /B` lists **eighteen** `.SYS` files across
eight directories. **I looked in one of them.**

**The evidence that it would be there was already open in front of me.**
`AUTOEXEC.BAT` loads `C:\WINDOWS\SMARTDRV.EXE` -- I had read that file, quoted
that line, and built a hypothesis on it an hour earlier. Windows 3.x ships
`RAMDRIVE.SYS` beside `SMARTDRV.EXE`. The inference was available from a file
I had already fetched, verified and archived.

**So the provenance question evaporates.** It is the machine's own file,
already licensed by whoever licensed that install. Pointing a `CONFIG.SYS`
line at a driver already on the card is squarely inside the approval. **No
operator ask, no sourcing decision, and the cell runs tonight.**

## What the error actually was

Not carelessness about the search -- **a category slip in the claim.** I ran a
correct command, read its output correctly, and then reported a conclusion
about **the machine** that my evidence only supported about **`C:\DOS`**. The
command was right; the quantifier was wrong.

That is the seventh instance of this shape tonight and the second in my own
reasoning within the hour, after "`#` was eaten" (inferred, never tested) and
"the harness may not verify staging" (hypothesised, never read). **All three
were one directory, one inference and one file-read away from being answered
before they were asserted.**

## Plan, now unblocked

1. **Push the `CONFIG.SYS` change** -- one `DEVICEHIGH` line for
   `C:\WINDOWS\RAMDRIVE.SYS` in `[COMMON]`, from the card's own bytes with
   that single line added. XMS free is 43,296 KB, so a 2 MB disk is
   comfortable.
2. **Verify the config took** -- the mandated verification step, which
   doubles as the recon that establishes **which drive letter** the RAM disk
   claimed. Not predicted: read off the machine, with the geometry witness
   confirming it is not C:.
3. **Run the A-B-B-A device cell** with the confirmed path: `FSPROBE_P1..P4`
   alternating C: and the RAM disk within one boot, time-terminated arms,
   matched wrap, and the wrapped C: arm as the positive control that must
   clear 5 events or void the cell.
4. **Restore**, verified by re-fetch and re-diff through the same
   normalisation.

## Drive-letter audit before the push: clean, and the reason it is clean matters

A `CONFIG.SYS` block device claims its letter **before** `MSCDEX` assigns CD
letters in `AUTOEXEC.BAT`, so `RAMDRIVE.SYS` will take **D:** and push the
PicoGUS USB CD and the ATAPI optical up one. Audited both of the card's own
files and the harness scripts before pushing anything:

| reference | what it is | affected? |
|---|---|---|
| `LH C:\DOS\MSCDEX.EXE /D:OPTICAL /M:5` (x4) | **device names**, no `/L:` | **no** -- MSCDEX takes the next free letter, whatever it is |
| `/D:MSCD000`, `/D:OPTICAL` | device names, not drives | no |
| `SHELL=... /E:1024` | environment size | no |
| `menuitem=VIBRA ... (CD on D:)`, two `REM` lines | **comments** | stale text only |
| `run-probe-hw.sh`, `run-hw.sh` | no `D:`-`F:` references at all | no |

**No `MSCDEX /L:` anywhere**, which is the one thing that would have
collided. The only casualties are two comments that document the old letters,
and the restore puts them back.

**This is the documented hazard's exact form** -- a boot that completes,
reaches a prompt and has a broken init reads as a code bug on the next cell.
**So step 2 reads back the full drive map, not just which letter RAMDRIVE
claimed.**

And per the note on `DEVICEHIGH`: `DOS=HIGH,UMB` is present so it should load
high, but **the verification checks the driver's presence and its letter, not
where it loaded** -- a silent fallback to low memory is harmless here and
would otherwise look like a failure.

## The change, built from the card's own bytes

`CONFIG.SYS.original` archived unmodified; the pushed file is that file plus
**four lines** -- three `REM`s that name the change, its date, its one-time
operator approval and where to restore from, and one:

    DEVICEHIGH=C:\WINDOWS\RAMDRIVE.SYS 2048 512 128 /E

2 MB in extended memory against 43,296 KB free, 512-byte sectors matching the
CF's so only the medium differs, placed in `[COMMON]` immediately after
`VIDECDD.SYS`. **38 lines to 42, and the diff is exactly those four.**

## Caught at the push: the staged boot file was LF-only

The first `stage-file` went out at **1,307 bytes with zero CR characters.**

The card's `CONFIG.SYS` arrived through a DOS text path that doubled every
newline, and the normalisation that made it diffable against `g2k` **stripped
it to LF-only**. The local copy is *equivalent* to the card's bytes modulo
that transform -- which is exactly what was written down at the time -- and
**pushing it back required undoing the transform, which I had not done.**

Converted and re-staged: **1,349 bytes, 42 CRs, 42 LFs, 42 CRLF pairs**,
verified before sending.

**This is the restore hazard arriving early**, on the outbound leg rather
than the inbound one. The rule as recorded -- *push back the bytes the card
gave you* -- was right and I nearly pushed the bytes the **transform** gave
me. A boot file is the one place where a line-ending difference is not
cosmetic, and "DOS is probably tolerant of LF" is not a thing to find out
with the machine's boot config.

**The restore artifact is `CONFIG.SYS.original` (LF, as fetched) and the push
artifact is `CONFIG.SYS.push` (CRLF).** The restore must go through the same
conversion, and the verification is a re-fetch and re-diff through the same
normalisation -- which will compare like with like precisely because both
legs now have the transform applied explicitly rather than assumed.

# The CONFIG.SYS send aborted. The tool declined to guess, and that is why this is a retry.

`vcctrl file-status`, `ok: false`, `remaining: [CONFIG.SYS]`:

    reboot   rebooting into the NET profile
    select   selecting NET, blind
    attest   proving NET by making the target send a file back
    attest   NET confirmed: the target reached this host
    send     sending CONFIG.SYS
    abort    a file did not come back and the prompt's state cannot be
             trusted -- stopping rather than typing blind
    return   returning to the menu default
    return   the machine booted; which profile is unread

Per-file reason: **"CONFIG.SYS did not come back, so whether it arrived on
the target is unknown."** NET was attested *before* the send, so the transfer
started and then stalled -- **181 seconds** between `send` and `abort`.

**The tool aborted rather than typing blind into a prompt whose state it
could not trust, then returned the machine to its menu default.** That is
vcctrl declining to guess at precisely the point where guessing would have
been unrecoverable -- a half-written boot file plus keystrokes aimed at a
prompt that might not exist. **It is the difference between a retry and an
incident**, and it belongs beside the transfer-capability notes as a property
of the tool worth relying on.

## The machine is healthy and the drive map says the change did NOT land

Power 24.2 W against an 8 W standby threshold, and a screen capture shows the
**complete** init sequence -- CuteMouse, PicoGUSinit v3.9.0 with its firmware
reboot into SB mode, USB joystick, MPU-401, MSCDEX 2.23, `[PGSB] ready.`, at
`C:\>`. **The documented boot-through hazard did not occur.**

And the informative line: **`Drive D: = Driver OPTICAL unit 0`.** D: is still
the optical drive. Had `RAMDRIVE.SYS` loaded it would have taken D: and
pushed OPTICAL to E: -- **the exact shift the audit predicted** -- so the
config almost certainly did not change and the approval is unspent.

## "Almost certainly" is not the standard, so it is being checked

**A truncated `CONFIG.SYS` could still boot while silently dropping every
line after the cut**, and the visible banners are almost all `AUTOEXEC`
output -- they attest very little about `CONFIG.SYS` and nothing about its
tail. The drive map is strong evidence; **the file itself is definitive.**

Read-only verification running now: `FSPROBE_CAT=C:\CONFIG.SYS` plus
`VOL C:`/`D:`/`E:`/`F:` for the full map. No approval consumed.

- **Matches the verbatim original** -> the failure was a transfer stall, not
  a configuration error, and the send retries unchanged.
- **Does not match** -> **restore first, diagnose second.** Push the verbatim
  original, verify by re-fetch, and only then work out what a partial write
  did. A machine sitting in a broken boot state is worse than a lost cell.

## The drive-map evidence is stronger than "strong": it survived a reboot

The abort log ends `returning to the menu default` and then `the machine
booted`. **So the machine restarted after the transfer stalled, and the
capture is from that boot.** Had a modified `CONFIG.SYS` landed on the card,
**that reboot would have executed it and D: would be the RAM disk.**

    Drive D: = Driver OPTICAL unit 0

**The file did not take effect across a boot that would have executed it.**
That is a functional test, not an inference from a directory listing, and it
is much closer to conclusive than I credited when I called it "strong". The
`FSPROBE_CAT` read confirms the bytes; the reboot already confirmed the
behaviour.

## Retry once. Not twice.

**The asymmetry that makes one retry safe:** this failure mode leaves the
card **unmodified**, which the reboot has now demonstrated rather than
assumed. A retry that fails identically costs a boot cycle and nothing else.
That is the whole reason one retry is reasonable -- **and it does not extend
to a third attempt.**

**The stall is unexplained and `CONFIG.SYS` is 1,349 bytes.** This is not the
size-or-timeout class that `REFUSE_BYTES` and `TRANSFER_TIMEOUT_S` covered on
the 126 MB package -- something stopped a **1.3 KB** transfer for 181
seconds. The abort's own wording, *the prompt's state cannot be trusted*,
reads like the documented post-FTP keyboard-hang signature.

**If the retry stalls the same way: STOP and diagnose. Do not send a third
time.** Two identical failures on a 1.3 KB file is a defect in the transfer
path, and this hub's rule is that a harness bug gets fixed rather than routed
around. A third attempt would be hoping -- and it would be another reboot
cycle on parts this campaign is deliberately not thermally cycling.

# The machine was not keyboard-hung by the documented fault. I wedged it with my own probe command.

`vcctrl_shot` -- **step 3 of the documented check** -- showed this:

    [PGSB] ready.
    C:\>CD C:\FSTEST
    C:\FSTEST>PRUN.BAT
    CDR101: Not ready reading drive D
    Abort, Retry, Fail?

**`VOL D:` against an empty optical drive raises DOS's critical-error
handler**, and the machine sat at `Abort, Retry, Fail?` waiting for a
character. That command was mine: I put `VOL C:;VOL D:;VOL E:;VOL F:` in
`FSPROBE_SYS_PRE` to read back the drive map.

**And the screenshot proves the keyboard was working when it ran.** `CD
C:\FSTEST` and `PRUN.BAT` are both on screen -- typed by the harness and
executed. So the input path was alive, the probe started, and the wedge came
**after** it, from the probe's own command.

## Which means I nearly mis-attributed this to the known fault

`verify_input` returned `verified: false`, "no LED change", which is the
documented post-FTP keyboard-hang signature exactly. **I had the answer
"known hardware fault" in hand before taking the screenshot.**

The check order is what stopped it: *lock/activity free -> allow the chord
its window -> **both capture channels agree** -> verify-input.* **The capture
step is the one that carries the information**, and it is third in the list
for a reason.

**The honest reading of the LED result is now unclear rather than
conclusive.** At an `INT 24h` critical-error prompt with a CD driver
retrying, the BIOS keyboard path may not service LED commands at all -- so
`verified: false` may be a **symptom of the state my command created** rather
than the independent fault it looks identical to. **Confirmed cause versus
operative cause, one more time**: the documented hang is real and has
happened twice on this machine, and it may be a bystander here.

Typed `F` to answer the prompt; the screen did not change, so the input path
really was not carrying keystrokes by then. **With no keyboard there is no
warm reboot**, so the recovery was the documented one: **one mains cycle**,
logged in `hw-recoveries.log` with its reason.

## The probe bug, which is the actual defect

**Never blind-probe a removable drive.** `VOL`/`DIR` against an optical drive
with no disc is not a read -- it is a critical error that blocks on a prompt
no automated caller can answer.

**And the drive map was already available without touching any media:**
MSCDEX prints `Drive D: = Driver OPTICAL unit 0` in the boot banner, which
`vcctrl_shot` captures. The verification step should read the banner and use
`AH=36h` only on the single drive the sweep writes to -- which is what the
geometry witness already does.

**So the read-only "verification" cell was the most dangerous thing run
tonight**, and it was dangerous because it touched a device the experiment
does not use, to answer a question the boot banner had already answered.

## Two failures, separately explained. One of them is still unexplained.

**These must not be merged**, and the reason is the pipe diagnosis: a
confirmed cause absorbing a neighbouring event it does not explain.

| | the send stall | the CDR101 wedge |
|---|---|---|
| when | 1789985351 -> 1789985533 | later, after a return reboot |
| profile | **NET**, mid-FTP | **PGSB**, the menu default |
| what ran | `send-file` of a 1,349-byte `CONFIG.SYS` | my `VOL D:` probe |
| evidence | `abort`, *"the prompt's state cannot be trusted"* | screenshot: `CDR101 ... Abort, Retry, Fail?` |
| status | **UNEXPLAINED** | **explained and preventable** |

**`VOL D:` did not exist when the send stalled** -- different profile,
different operation, three minutes earlier. **"We found the wedge" is not
"we found the problem."** The retry budget of **one** still applies to the
send, and if it stalls again at ~181 seconds that is a transfer-path defect
to diagnose rather than send a third time.

## Where the probe came from, stated accurately

The instruction was **"read back the full drive map, not just RAMDRIVE's
letter"** -- correct, and it is the check that would have caught a
drive-letter shift breaking init. **The implementation was mine**: `VOL`
against every letter blindly, including a removable drive with no disc, is
the unsafe way to satisfy a safe requirement.

**And the answer was already in hand, passively, on both sides.** The
capture sent minutes earlier contained `Drive D: = Driver OPTICAL unit 0`,
and it was quoted as the decisive evidence that `RAMDRIVE.SYS` had not
loaded. **An active probe was then run to obtain information a passive
witness had already delivered** -- and the passive one cannot wedge
anything. The post-recovery capture above shows the same line again, for
free.

**Prefer the banner to the probe.**

## A false alarm from my own monitor, recorded so it is not mistaken for a machine fact

A background monitor reported **"target did not come up above standby within
300s"** after the mains cycle. **That is wrong and it is my script's fault**,
not the machine's: the poller shells out to the `vcctrl` CLI and prints `-1`
on any parse failure, and `-1` never exceeds the 8,000 mW threshold, so the
loop can only ever time out when the CLI call does not parse.

**The machine was already verified up by three direct readings**, taken
before that monitor expired: `power_mw: 24,195`, `verify_input: verified
true` ("the target acknowledged a keystroke"), and a captured boot sequence
running through to `[PGSB] ready.`

**An instrument that can only fail in one direction reports that direction
when it breaks.** Same shape as the arms that could not fail informatively,
one level up in the tooling -- and it is worth writing down because a
"machine did not come up" line in a transcript is exactly the sort of thing
that gets believed later without the three readings beside it.

# BLOCK: the send retry stalled identically. Stopping, as pre-registered.

| | send -> abort |
|---|---|
| first attempt | **181.5 s** |
| retry | **181.5 s** |
| difference | **0.0 s** |

Same phases both times: `reboot` -> `select NET, blind` -> `attest` -> **NET
confirmed** -> `send CONFIG.SYS` -> `abort` -> `return`. Same per-file
reason: *"CONFIG.SYS did not come back, so whether it arrived on the target
is unknown."*

**Two identical failures on a 1,349-byte file, to the tenth of a second.**
That is not a stall, it is a **fixed timeout being hit every time** -- and
the pre-registered rule applies: **stop and diagnose, do not send a third
time.** A third attempt would be hoping, and it would be another boot cycle.

**Machine state after the abort: clean.** Full boot sequence captured through
`[PGSB] ready.` at `C:\>`, with `Drive D: = Driver OPTICAL unit 0` -- so
`RAMDRIVE.SYS` did not load and **the card is still unmodified across a boot
that would have executed a changed `CONFIG.SYS`.** The approval remains
unspent.

## Diagnosis, offered as a hypothesis with its evidence

**Every successful transfer tonight used a SUBDIRECTORY as its destination**
-- `C:\DOSAGS`, `C:\FSTEST`. **This send is the only one aimed at `C:\`, the
root.**

And `vcctrl_file_list` **refuses the root of C: by design**:

    error: refusing the root of drive C: name a directory under it

The abort's own wording is about the **return** leg, not the send:
*"CONFIG.SYS did not come back"* -- the file is sent, then read back to
verify, and **the read-back path is the one that cannot address the root.**
A fixed 181.5 s timeout on a verification that can never succeed fits every
observation:

- NET attests fine -- the transfer path works.
- The send phase is entered -- the file is going out.
- The failure is on the return -- exactly where a root-directory listing
  would be needed.
- The duration is identical to the tenth of a second -- a timeout constant,
  not a variable stall.
- It is unrelated to size -- 1,349 bytes is nothing.

**This is a hypothesis, not a finding.** It is consistent with everything
observed and it has not been tested, and the way to test it is one transfer
of the same file to a subdirectory -- which would succeed under this
hypothesis and fail identically under any size- or path-independent one.

**Not running it without the coordinator**, because it changes what the
approved change means: putting `CONFIG.SYS` anywhere other than `C:\` does
nothing on its own, and moving it into place afterwards is a second
operation that needs its own thought about what happens if it half-completes.

# DIAGNOSED BY READING: `VCGET.BAT` composes a doubled separator for a root destination

No hardware spent. The discriminating evidence was two lines in
`vcctrl/daemon/vcctrld.py`.

**The typed command** (`vcctrld.py:9016`):

    C:\MTCP\VCGET.BAT CONFIG.SYS C:\

**What `VCGET.BAT` builds from it:**

    SET VGD=%2                                  -> VGD = C:\
    ECHO get %VGF% %VGD%\%VGF% >> VCGET.RSP     -> get CONFIG.SYS C:\\CONFIG.SYS
    ECHO put %VGD%\%VGF% %VGF%.CHK >> VCGET2.RSP-> put C:\\CONFIG.SYS CONFIG.SYS.CHK

**`%VGD%\%VGF%` doubles the separator whenever `dest` already ends in one**,
which only a **drive root** does:

| dest | composed path |
|---|---|
| `C:\DOSAGS` | `C:\DOSAGS\CONFIG.SYS` -- correct |
| **`C:\`** | **`C:\\CONFIG.SYS`** -- doubled |

**And the `put` is the verification leg.** The abort's own wording is
*"CONFIG.SYS did not come back"* -- the return, not the send. A malformed
**local** path on the `put` means mTCP's `FTP.EXE` never uploads the
check copy, nothing arrives, and `TRANSFER_TIMEOUT_S = 180.0` fires.

**Every observation fits and nothing else needs to be true:**

- NET attests -- the transfer path is healthy.
- The `send` phase is entered -- the command was typed.
- The failure is on the **return** leg.
- **181.5 s twice, 0.0 s apart** -- a timeout constant, not a stall.
- Size-irrelevant -- 1,349 bytes.
- **Every successful transfer tonight used a subdirectory.** This is the only
  root-destination send in the campaign.

`IF NOT EXIST %VGD%\NUL MD %VGD%` is a second casualty of the same shape --
`C:\\NUL`, then `MD C:\` -- though it is not what times out.

## The fix, and it is one substitution

**`C:\` normalised to `C:`** composes correctly everywhere in that BAT:
`get CONFIG.SYS C:\CONFIG.SYS`, `put C:\CONFIG.SYS`, and
`IF NOT EXIST C:\NUL` is true so no `MD` is attempted. **A drive-relative
`C:` is the DOS-correct spelling of "the root of C:".**

vcctrl is ecliptik's own tool and explicitly ours to modify, and this hub's
rule is that a harness bug gets fixed rather than routed around -- **so this
goes in vcctrl, not into a workaround in the dosags harness.**

**Not patching it unilaterally**, for one reason worth stating: the fix is
inside a daemon that is currently running and serving this campaign, and a
daemon restart mid-investigation is its own hazard. **The change is one line
and the reasoning is above; the decision about when to apply and restart is
the coordinator's.**

**No third send attempted.**

# DEVICE CELL SCORED: branch A. No events on a different physical medium.

A-B-B-A within one boot, device the only variable, time-terminated arms.

| stage | drive | geometry witness | elapsed | `c` | **events** | integrity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A1** | `C:\FSTEST` | **matches the CF volume** | 6,089 ms | 6,564 us | **14** | OK |
| **B1** | `D:\` | **differs -- a DIFFERENT device** | 6,014 ms | 1,728 us | **0** | OK |
| **B2** | `D:\` | **differs** | 6,014 ms | 1,728 us | **0** | OK |
| **A2** | `C:\FSTEST` | **matches the CF volume** | 6,086 ms | 6,467 us | **11** | OK |

## Every gate, in the pre-registered order

**1. Integrity.** All four arms `attempted == written`, `short_writes=0`,
`sync_fails=0`. **The RAM arms wrote 2,724,800 bytes each** -- they wrote,
and they wrote seven times what the CF arms managed. Free bytes identical at
start and end on both devices, so **the wrap worked** and the arm was not
short.

**2. Wrapped C: positive control, bar >= 5 events.** A1 = **14**, A2 = **11**
-- and both land inside the **11-27** range predicted from the unwrapped
runs' own rates. **The wrap did not change the phenomenon**, which was the
thing that could have voided the whole cell.

**3. Duration floor, >= 8 expected periods (~3.5 s).** All four arms 6.0 s.

**4. Presence versus absence.** At the C: arms' measured rate of 1.81-2.30
events/s, **a 6.01 s RAM arm expects 11 to 14 events. Observed: 0. Twice.**

**BRANCH A.**

## What that means, at the corrected width

**The cost is at or below the block-device layer.** That is **four
candidates, not one**: the disk driver, INT 13h, the ATA/CF controller, the
CF media. **It does NOT mean "the CF media"** -- the label I had written
before the coordinator corrected the layer stack, which would have retired
three candidates by wording on the branch most likely to end the
investigation.

**And SMARTDRV is NOT eliminated by this.** A RAM disk is a DOS block-device
driver and bypasses INT 13h, so SMARTDRV never saw the B arms -- which is
exactly the gating condition written into the queued ask. **The no-SMARTDRV
ask is now indicated**, and it is the lever that splits its pass-through
path from the three below it.

## Two things the cell also settled in passing

**Time-matching was what made this scoreable, and by a wider margin than the
sizing correction assumed.** `c` on the RAM disk is **1,728 us**, not the
50-100 us the correction feared -- but still **3.80x faster** than the CF's
6,564. A byte-matched 384 KB arm would have run 480 records in ~830 ms:
**1.9 expected periods, against the 8-period floor.** Marginal, unscoreable,
and it would have returned zero.

**Gate 2's stall has a device.** Whatever it is, it is not in DOS's
filesystem layer or above -- the same `fsync`-per-record write pattern
through the same DOS, the same FAT code and the same INT 21h path produced
**fourteen events on one device and none on another.**

# The INT 13h hook is built and locally verified

A real-mode stub the DJGPP probe installs into DOS memory it allocates
itself -- no separate TSR binary, no second toolchain. 304 bytes of nasm,
embedded as a C array.

## What the emulator established

    WRAP TEST: composed=220001 us  uclock=220001 us  err=-0.00%  wraps spanned=4.01
      PASS -- a 4-wrap span composes correctly instead of reading 55 ms or being discarded
    MONOTONIC: 0 backward steps in 200000 reads -> PASS
    HEADER: handler +0x0058 ring +0x0130 rec 16 -> PASS
    HANDLER FIRES: direct INT 13h AH=08h -> counter 0 to 1 -> PASS
    SELFTEST PASSED

**The wrap test is the deliberate one.** A synthetic ~220 ms interval
spanning **4.01 wraps** composes to 220,001 us against `uclock`'s 220,001 --
**0.00% error.** The defect I wrote into my own design would have returned
55 ms or discarded the record; this test would fail if it came back.

## What the emulator could NOT establish, and it proved that too

The full workload under DOSBox-X:

    workload 400 records, wall 69122 us, INT 13h calls during it = 0
    VOID -- the hook recorded ZERO calls. That is not 'no slow calls', it is
    'the hook is not in the path'. Nothing below is scored.

**DOSBox-X serves a mounted host directory at the DOS file-system level, so
disk writes never reach INT 13h.** The zero is a property of the emulator,
not a defect -- and **the VOID gate refused to score it**, which is the gate
doing precisely its job on the first occasion it could have misled.

## Two defects caught by reading, before either could reach hardware

**The ring overlapped the handler.** `RING_OFF` was a guessed `0x40`, which
is **inside the code** -- the first recorded slow call would have overwritten
the routine that recorded it. Now the base is computed by the assembler and
published in a header cell the installer reads.

**`BX` was clobbered without being saved.** Some `INT 13h` functions return
data in `BX` (AH=08h returns BL=drive type), and the slow path used it as a
scratch register. It would have corrupted those calls' results silently.

Both found by reading the listing and the register usage. **Neither would
have announced itself as a hook bug on the target** -- one is a crash a long
way from its cause, the other is wrong data with no symptom at all.

## The one question left for the cell

**Whether the hook sits in the real path on real hardware.** Everything else
is settled locally. The `HANDLER FIRES` check separates the two readings of
a zero in advance: *nothing called INT 13h* versus *the handler is broken*.
On the target, a sweep doing thousands of `fsync`'d writes through a real CF
card must produce thousands of calls; **a zero there is VOID, not a result.**

## The register-transparency gate fired on its first run, and the fix did not take

**Gate result, three of three calls, twice:**

- **Every general and segment register PRESERVED** -- `AX BX CX DX SI DI ES DS`.
- **CF, ZF, SF, OF, IF, DF PRESERVED.**
- **PF and AF ALTERED.**

**CF is the one that matters** -- `INT 13h`'s caller-visible contract is CF
for error and `AH` for status -- so the destructive failure mode the gate
exists for is **not present**. The hook does not corrupt what the BIOS or
DOS acts on, and it does not put the boot drive at risk.

### Two fixes attempted, neither worked

1. `pushf`/`popf` spanning the epilogue -- the original design.
2. Capturing the downstream handler's flags into **CS memory the instant the
   call returns**, and pushing them back as the very last act before
   `retf 2`.

**Identical deltas both times.** That places the cause **below the handler**:
`popf` is trapped and partially emulated in V86 mode, where a DPMI program's
DOS calls run, and a real-mode handler cannot reach past that.

**So it is documented, in the words the boundary needs rather than the words
that would end the discussion:**

> **PF and AF are altered. CF, ZF, SF, OF, IF and DF are preserved. Every
> general and segment register is preserved. No KNOWN caller reads PF or
> AF.**

**"No known caller" is not "no caller", and the distinction is the point.**
SMARTDRV sits directly below this hook and DOS's FAT layer sits above it;
we wrote neither and have neither's source. That is the quantifier error
this campaign has made seven times, so it is stated rather than rounded off.

**And the gate stays absolute on everything else.** Any general or segment
register, or CF/ZF/SF/OF, and the run refuses and removes the hook.

### One more defect caught in the same pass

Appending `ret_fl` **in the middle** of the header block shifted `busy`,
`hdl_off` and `ring_off` by two bytes, and the C side then read `busy` as
the handler entry and got **`0x0000`** -- a vector pointing at the data
area. Caught by the installer printing the offsets it read.

**Header cells are an ABI between the assembler and the C. Append only.**

# THE STALL IS A SINGLE-SECTOR WRITE INSIDE ONE INT 13h CALL

## Gates, in the pre-registered order

**1. HANDLER FIRES -- PASS.** The transparency gate made three live `INT 13h`
calls through the hook and all three were register-transparent.

**2. Call count -- PASS, and not VOID.** `total INT 13h calls seen = 1445`,
**1,432 of them during the workload.** C: *is* reached through `INT 13h` on
this machine.

**3. Reconciliation -- THE GATE AS IMPLEMENTED DOES NOT TEST WHAT IT WAS
SPECIFIED TO TEST, and I am not scoring it either way.** It printed
`2,947,117 us of 5,768,498 us wall (48.9% outside)`, but that sums only the
**14 recorded slow calls** against total wall time -- the other **1,431**
calls' time is not counted, and neither is any non-`INT 13h` work. A 48.9%
residual is what that arithmetic must produce; it is **not** a 5% failure and
**not** a pass. The specification said in-call plus out-of-call reconciles
against `c`; the implementation sums a subset. **Recorded as a mis-built
gate, not as a result.**

## The four payload items

**1. FUNCTION CODE -- `AH=03`, DISK WRITE, on all fourteen. `AL=01`, ONE
SECTOR.** Which operation stalls has never been observable before. It is a
**single-sector write**.

**2. ONE CALL, NOT MANY.** Each event is **one** `INT 13h` call blocking for
~212 ms. Not many calls summing to it.

**512 bytes cannot take 212 ms of work.** At the CF card's own measured
write throughput that sector is microseconds of transfer. **This is a wait**,
and it is the first direct evidence for that rather than an inference from
magnitude rigidity.

**3. DURATION at 0.84 us resolution.** 13 of 14 span **209,391 - 219,108 us**
(3.812 - 3.989 ticks, mean **3.895**); one outlier at 165,969 (3.022).
Measured at the call itself the distribution is **tighter and LOWER** than
the 215,712-241,541 seen through the file layer -- the difference is the
DOS/FAT work wrapped around the call.

**4. SECTOR NUMBERS -- and they cluster.** Decoded from `CX`/`DH`:

| # | us | head | cyl | sector |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 212,700 | 49 | 686 | 52 |
| 1 | 211,803 | 43 | **730** | 46 |
| 2 | 215,359 | 44 | **730** | 39 |
| 3 | 219,108 | 29 | **736** | 32 |
| 4 | 214,784 | 30 | **736** | 23 |
| 5 | 218,123 | 39 | **736** | 42 |
| 6 | 214,296 | 40 | **736** | 33 |
| 7 | 165,969 | 21 | **737** | 24 |
| 8 | 214,335 | 22 | **737** | 15 |
| 9 | 218,590 | 38 | **737** | 41 |
| 10 | 209,391 | 43 | **737** | 46 |
| 11 | 211,225 | 44 | **737** | 38 |
| 12 | 211,111 | 3 | **0** | 57 |
| 13 | 210,324 | 46 | **737** | 25 |

**Twelve of fourteen fall in cylinders 730-737**, six of them in cylinder 737
alone. One is at cylinder 0 head 3 -- **the FAT/directory region**, which is
what a file-size update writes.

## The phase test, scored as pre-registered

`phase_start`: 0.198, 0.315, 0.414, 0.418, 0.434, 0.591, 0.595, 0.619, 0.707,
0.845, 0.848, 0.863, 0.870, 1.000. **Uniform across the range.**

**So the BIOS-tick unit is retired**, exactly as registered -- and, exactly
as registered, **that is all it means.** It does not establish work versus
wait. **Item 2 does that**, and independently: one call, one sector, 212 ms.

The duration mean of **3.895 ticks** also sits clearly *below* 4.00, against
the file-layer figure's 4.014. The 4.00 coincidence does not survive
measurement at the call.

## NOT YET DRAWN, pending the cross-check

**The cylinder clustering is the result this cell exists for and it is
exactly the kind that gets believed.** It is not being read as an
erase-block boundary until the recorded sectors are cross-checked against
what the file's own position implies -- if the hook's CHS decode is wrong,
the clustering is wrong in a way that would look exactly like a finding.

## The cylinder clustering has NO DENOMINATOR, and that is a sharper objection than the decode

**"Twelve of fourteen in cylinders 730-737" is a numerator without a
population.** The ring records only **slow** calls. **If the sweep file lives
in cylinders 730-737, then all 1,432 writes went there and twelve stalls
landing there is arithmetic, not clustering.**

The question that matters is the inverse: **of the writes that went to
cylinder 737, what fraction stalled, and how does that compare to 730?**
This run cannot answer it.

**Eighth instance of the denominator rule in this campaign, and the first in
a physical address rather than a metric.** The CHS cross-check is still worth
doing and does not substitute: **a correct decode of an uninterpretable ratio
is still uninterpretable.**

**Fixed in the instrument.** The handler now histograms **every** `AH=03`
write by cylinder into a 1,024-entry table alongside the slow-call ring, and
the probe prints `cyl / writes / stalls / per-1000`. **Stalls-per-write by
region is a real distribution against a real denominator**, and the
erase-block hypothesis becomes testable for the first time.

## The reconciliation gate has a better substitute already in the data

Its purpose was the interrupts-disabled hazard: a stalled BIOS tick
undercounting a long call. **Two independent measurements answer it
directly:**

| measured at | range |
|---|---|
| the `INT 13h` call | **209,391 - 219,108 us** |
| the file layer | 215,712 - 241,541 us |

**The call-level figure is consistently smaller, by about the DOS/FAT work
wrapped around the call.** That is the **right sign and a plausible
magnitude**. A grossly undercounting timestamp would not land just under an
independent measurement -- it would land far below it, or quantize oddly.

**That is stronger than the gate I specified**, and it uses data already in
hand. If the gate is rebuilt, the fix is a running total of in-call time
across **all** calls accumulated in the handler, separate from the ring.

## Two smaller items

**The 165,969 us outlier is flagged as a possible second population**, not
noise -- **22% below the other thirteen**, where those thirteen span 4.6%
between themselves. That guard has paid three times tonight.

**The 4.00-tick coincidence is dead on its own terms**: mean **3.895** ticks
at the call against **4.014** at the file layer. **The apparent integer was
the DOS wrapper, not the wait.** That is a cleaner kill than the phase test
gave -- and the phase test's uniform result retires the unit independently.

## Leading mechanism, and the boundary this instrument cannot cross

**A single-sector write blocking ~212 ms with the drive otherwise idle is the
shape of a CF internal erase-and-program cycle.**

**What this instrument cannot distinguish: one long ATA wait from a BIOS
retry sequence.** Both are one `INT 13h` call, both look identical from
above it. Stated now rather than left implicit, because it is the next
boundary and the erase-block reading would quietly assume the first.

# Run 2: the histogram is VOID, and it announced itself

    writes histogrammed = 17,681,718 across 704 cylinders
    ... but INT 13h calls during the workload = 1,430

**17.6 million writes against 1,430 calls.** The counts rose in a tidy linear
ramp -- 513, 1027, 1541, 2055, each +514 -- which looks **exactly like
data**.

**Cause, and it is mine: `__dpmi_allocate_dos_memory` does not zero the
block**, and the ring and histogram live past the end of `HOOK_BIN`. They
started as whatever the previous owner of that DOS memory left behind.

**Caught only because the probe prints the total.** A per-cylinder table
alone would have been read as a write distribution -- and a *rising ramp
across 704 cylinders* is precisely the shape someone would interpret.

**Fixed both ways:**

1. The whole block is zeroed before the stub is written.
2. **An assertion the instrument cannot pass while lying:** every
   histogrammed write is one `INT 13h` call, so the total can never exceed
   the call count. `wtot > total` now prints `HISTOGRAM VOID` and scores
   nothing.

**That is the fourth instrument tonight that could report garbage as data,
and the second whose guard was a line it prints unconditionally rather than
a check someone thought to write.**

## What run 2's ring still says -- gates passed, histogram excluded

Gate 1 `HANDLER FIRES`: PASS. Gate 2 call count **1,441 total, 1,430 in the
workload**: PASS. `ring_head` is in the zeroed header, so **the 7 recorded
slots are real** even though the histogram was not.

- **Seven slow calls, all `AH=03 AL=01`** -- single-sector writes, again.
- **205,541 - 218,532 us**, mean 3.833 ticks. Run 1 was 209,391-219,108,
  mean 3.895. **Consistent, and again below 4.00.**
- `phase_start` 0.182 - 0.983: **uniform again.**

## The cross-run comparison, WITHOUT its support check

**Exact CHS overlap between run 1 and run 2: NONE.** Cylinders overlap
(0, 736, 737) but no single sector stalls twice.

**And that is exactly the row that is UNINTERPRETABLE without support**, per
the gating fixed before this run: **the histogram that would have told me
whether the file occupied the same extent is void.** DOS allocates on first
fit, and this volume has had a `CONFIG.SYS` written, a RAM-disk cell run and
a restore pushed since run 1.

**So "different sectors" is NOT evidence for the `when` reading.** It is
scored as nothing, and the no-overlap row stays open until a run with a
working histogram can show the extent did not move.

# THE DURABLE FINDING, separated from everything the void touched

**This owes nothing to the histogram, the extent question, or the overlap
row. Two independent runs, twenty-one events between them:**

| | run 1 | run 2 |
|---|---|---|
| events | 14 | 7 |
| function | **`AH=03 AL=01` -- single-sector write, all 21** | same |
| duration | 209,391 - 219,108 us | 205,541 - 218,532 us |
| mean | **3.895 ticks** | **3.833 ticks** |
| `phase_start` | 0.198 - 1.000, **uniform** | 0.182 - 0.983, **uniform** |
| calls during workload | 1,432 | 1,430 |

**A single-sector write blocks for ~210 ms on this device, inside one
`INT 13h` call, and the BIOS-tick unit is not involved.**

**512 bytes cannot be 210 ms of work.** That makes it a **wait** -- measured,
not inferred from magnitude rigidity, and it is the first positive statement
about the mechanism after six cells of eliminations.

**It belongs in `HARDWARE.md` whatever the extent question returns**: any
port measuring write latency on this machine needs it, and it does not
depend on naming the internal cause.

## What it still does NOT name

**One long ATA wait and a BIOS retry sequence are indistinguishable from
above `INT 13h`.** Both are one call. The erase-block reading assumes the
first.

**Narrowing is not naming.** A six-way question is now two-way, and the
operator's ruling asks for a name.

## Scope of the raw write ring, stated before its first result

The coordinator proposed reading the file's extent from DOS directly, via
`INT 21h AH=440Dh` minor 60h or the directory entry's starting cluster.
**Checked rather than built: minor 60h returns DEVICE parameters, not a
cluster chain, and the starting cluster is not in the documented FindFirst
DTA fields on DOS 6.22** -- it sits in undocumented bytes that vary by
version. Building the support check on that would have put an unverified
assumption underneath the row being rescued, which is how the last one
failed.

**The substitute is honestly scoped: the raw write-address ring is NOT
independent of the hook.** It is independent of **the aggregation step that
failed** -- an un-zeroed buffer being summed is a failure mode that raw
per-write records cannot have. **Two witnesses of different kinds, with
disagreement between them itself a signal.**

And it answers the extent question directly: **if run 3's first write
addresses match run 1's, the file landed in the same clusters**, which is
exactly what the no-overlap row needs.

# RUN 3: SAME SECTORS STALL. The reading is "WHERE", on independent evidence.

## Gates first

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `HANDLER FIRES` | **PASS** -- 3 of 3 transparent live calls |
| call count | **PASS** -- 1,441 total, **1,430 in the workload** |
| **histogram self-assertion** | **PASS** -- `1430 writes across 5 cylinders`, **exactly the call count**. The assertion that would have caught the un-zeroed block now passes on real data. |
| raw write ring | 256 addresses, cylinders 0, 687, 735, 736 |

**The two extent witnesses agree**: the aggregate says 1,430 writes over 5
cylinders, the raw ring's addresses fall in the same place. The disagreement
that would have been a signal is absent.

## Support check FIRST, as gated

| | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| stall cylinders | 0, 686, **730**, 736, 737 | 0, **687**, 736, 737 | 0, **687**, 736, 737 |

**The extent MOVED between run 1 and run 2** -- 686/730 became 687, and run
3's raw ring confirms the file now occupies 0, 687, 735, 736.

**So run 1 versus run 3 is the UNINTERPRETABLE row**, exactly as
pre-registered: no overlap, but a different file in different clusters.
**Scored as nothing.** Nothing happened to the volume between runs 2 and 3,
and their extents match.

## The overlap, on the pair whose support holds

**Run 2 and run 3 stall at SEVEN IDENTICAL CHS ADDRESSES -- 7 of 7.**

    head=00 cyl=687  sec=3
    head=07 cyl=0    sec=46
    head=1E cyl=736  sec=8
    head=29 cyl=737  sec=11
    head=2B cyl=737  sec=60
    head=2D cyl=737  sec=48
    head=2F cyl=737  sec=33

**Run 3 found one more: `head=2D cyl=737 sec=2`.**

**This is the "where" branch.** The stall is a property of **those physical
locations**, confirmed on independent runs. It is not a cycle count, not a
wear-levelling trigger, not a housekeeping pass -- **the same sectors stall
every time the file lands on them.**

**And the "when" reading is dead.** It required stalls to move across runs on
the same ground; they did not move at all.

## A second population, and this time it is unmistakable

**Run 3's extra event: `56,214 us` -- 1.023 ticks, against 3.72-3.94 for the
other seven.** Run 1 had a 165,969 us outlier (3.02 ticks) flagged on the
same grounds.

**Three magnitudes now: ~1 tick, ~3 ticks, ~4 ticks.** The ~210 ms family is
not the only thing happening, and the smaller events are **not** noise around
it -- 56 ms is a quarter of it.

## What is now named, and what is not

**NAMED: the stall is a specific set of physical sectors that take ~210 ms to
accept a single-sector write, reproducibly, on this card.**

**NOT NAMED: why those sectors.** Bad-block remapping, a worn erase block,
and a controller retry on specific media all produce exactly this, and
**one long ATA wait is still indistinguishable from a BIOS retry sequence
from above `INT 13h`.**

**Narrowing is not naming -- but this is a much smaller gap than "the cost is
at or below the block-device layer".**

## Step 1 could NOT be done for free: the geometry was never captured

**LBA is the right coordinate** -- CHS on a translated drive is a fiction
layered over it, and a flash device's structure would be visible in LBA and
invisible in CHS. **But the conversion needs heads-per-cylinder and
sectors-per-track, and this campaign does not have them.**

**The transparency gate calls `AH=08h` on every run -- and prints registers
only on a MISMATCH.** Three cells produced CHS addresses with no way to
convert them. The data was one `printf` away and was thrown out three times.

**Fixed: the geometry now prints unconditionally**, the same shape as the
boot banner that gave the drive map for free and the installer offsets that
caught the header-ABI bug. **A passive line that costs nothing and is there
when it turns out to matter** -- which is a different thing from a check,
because it does not require anyone to have anticipated the need.

### What IS visible without geometry, and it is worth recording

Run 3's stalls, grouped:

| cylinder | heads | sectors |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 7 | 46 |
| 687 | 0 | 3 |
| 736 | 30 | 8 |
| **737** | **41, 43, 45, 45, 47** | 11, 60, 2, 48, 33 |

**In cylinder 737 the heads are 41, 43, 45, 47 -- an arithmetic progression
stepping by exactly two, three times.** That is geometry-independent as a
*pattern*: a head stride of two is a head stride of two whatever the
translation.

**Recorded as an observation, NOT fitted.** A stride-2 head pattern would
correspond to a fixed byte stride once sectors-per-track is known, and a
fixed stride is what an erase block looks like -- **but computing that stride
from an assumed 63 sectors/track would be exactly the arithmetic that has
dissolved twice tonight.** The geometry arrives with the next cell; the fit
waits for it.

## The second population: flagged, not fitted

Three magnitudes so far -- **56,214**, **165,969**, and the ~210,000 us
family. The two outliers sit near a 1:3 ratio, **which is the kind of
observation that has dissolved twice tonight under its own null**, so the
structure is recorded and the arithmetic is left alone until there are more
than three points.

**The useful question is not the ratio: it is whether the 56 ms event has a
repeating address too.** Run 3's was at `cyl=737 head=45 sec=2`; run 2 had no
such event. One more run answers it, and it answers it the same way the
~210 ms family was answered -- by repetition, not by fitting.

## Queued, in order

1. **LBA conversion** -- free, the moment the next cell prints the geometry.
2. **Read versus write on a known stalling sector.** If reads of
   `cyl=737 head=41 sec=11` are fast and only writes stall, the cost is in
   **programming**, not in reaching the media -- which separates a worn erase
   block from a remapped bad block. Needs only a different `AH`.
3. **Map the neighbourhood** -- write every sector in a range around a known
   stalling address. **Stalls in runs at aligned boundaries is an erase block
   and its size falls out; exactly one sector stalling with clean neighbours
   is a remap.** *That distinction is the name the ruling asks for*, and it is
   now reachable.

# FINAL CELL: geometry captured, LBA computed, and it is the THIRD branch

**Geometry from `AH=08h` on the target: heads=64, sectors/track=63,
max_cyl=976.** First time this campaign has had it.

**Run 4 reproduced the same seven addresses a third time** -- runs 2, 3 and 4
now agree, 7 of 7, at 204,654-217,166 us.

## CHS -> LBA, with the geometry stated so it can be checked

`LBA = (cyl x 64 + head) x 63 + (sector - 1)`

| cyl | head | sec | LBA |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 7 | 46 | 486 |
| 687 | 0 | 3 | 2,769,986 |
| 736 | 30 | 8 | 2,969,449 |
| **737** | **41** | 11 | **2,974,177** |
| **737** | **43** | 60 | **2,974,352** |
| **737** | **45** | 48 | **2,974,466** |
| **737** | **47** | 33 | **2,974,577** |

**Differences within cylinder 737: 175, 114, 111.**

**NEITHER pre-registered reading holds.** Not a constant stride, not a power
of two, and no LBA is aligned to any 64 KB-4 MB boundary. The differences do
not track a fixed geometry.

### And the head pattern did not survive the conversion

I flagged heads **41, 43, 45, 47** -- stepping by exactly two -- as possible
structure. **In LBA it is 175, 114, 111: nothing.** The sectors differ
(11, 60, 48, 33), so a stride-2 head pattern produces no constant LBA stride
at all.

**That is exactly the warning about CHS on a translated drive being a fiction
layered over LBA**, and the pattern I would have fitted was an artefact of
reading one coordinate of a translated address. **Recorded as a killed
observation, not omitted.**

**What stands is what already stood: the addresses are reproducible.** Three
runs, seven addresses, identical every time.

## THE READ TEST DID NOT RUN

**Zero occurrences of `READ TEST` in the output.** `INT13P_READ` did not
reach the program -- the block is present and the path around it executed
(`vector restored` printed), so `getenv` returned empty.

**CAUSE UNKNOWN. Three separate statements, kept separate:**

1. **The value did not arrive.** Measured.
2. **The value contains colons, and `:` was never tested.** ECHO 1 and 2
   covered `|`, `#`, `;`, space, `>`, `%`, `^`, `&`, `,` and a 100-character
   plain string. **`:` was not on the list.** Measured.
3. **"Colons ate it" is an INFERENCE from a failure that explains the
   failure**, and that shape has been wrong three times tonight -- the pipe
   diagnosis (believed for hours, then a bystander), the stale-binary theory,
   and the V86 `popf` story. **Not claimed.**

**The next session starts from an ECHO 3 that tests `:`, not from a
conclusion it would have to unwind.** A colon is the most common character
in a DOS path: **if it truncates, that is a large finding affecting every
path-valued variable this harness passes; if it does not, we need to know
that before trusting any of them.**

**So reads-versus-writes is UNANSWERED**, and with it:

- **The neighbourhood ask stays open.** It cannot be withdrawn, because the
  read-only route depends on reads stalling and that is untested.
- **The question of whether the cost is in programming or in reaching the
  media stays open.**

**Not chasing it: the session is winding down and this is the last cell.**
Recorded so the next session starts from the fact rather than rediscovering
it -- and the first thing to try is passing the addresses without colons.

# HANDOVER -- 2026-09-21, for a reader with no context

## 1. The headline goal did not move

**The goal is 40 fps at 16-bit on a 486DX2-66. This session moved it by
zero.**

- **Gate 3's lower-resolution work -- the operator-approved route to that
  goal, approved long ago -- HAS NOT STARTED.** It is the one untried route
  and nothing here touched it.
- **Gate 2 passes 4/4 on every bar** (whole-run `tick_rate` 39.41/39.41/
  39.41/39.40 against a 39.2 bar, spread **0.01**; `tick_rate_steady` 40.01
  x4; `fps_p50` 40.00 x4) **and is unclaimed only because of a hold we
  imposed on ourselves** -- the operator chose to hold it until the ~220 ms
  storage stall is named.

**Everything below is that stall investigation.** It is good work and it is
not progress toward 40 fps.

## 2. ESTABLISHED

**The stall is a single-sector write inside one `INT 13h` call, on specific
physical sectors, reproducibly.**

- **21 events across runs 1-2, plus 7+8+7 across runs 2-4**: every one
  `AH=03 AL=01` -- a **single-sector write**.
- **204,654 - 219,108 us**, i.e. ~210 ms, for one 512-byte write.
  **512 bytes cannot be 210 ms of work: it is a WAIT**, measured, not
  inferred.
- **Seven CHS addresses repeat identically across runs 2, 3 and 4.** Same
  sectors, every time. This is a property of **those locations**.
- **Device-dependent**: the same fsync-per-record pattern through the same
  DOS, FAT and INT 21h produced **14 events on the CF card and 0 on a RAM
  disk**, with the RAM arm writing **3.7x more bytes** in the same wall time.
- **Geometry: heads=64, sectors/track=63, max_cyl=976.**
- **Gate 2's own figures** and the 4/4 pass above.
- **`fsync` costs ~5,000 us on this card**; the fixture's old
  open-append-close `WriteLog` cost **21,075 us per line**.
- **SMARTDRV's caching of C: is not the cost** -- events survive unchanged
  with caching provably off, though `c` moves 6.6%, so the cache was costing
  write throughput rather than buying it.

## 3. BOUNDED BUT UNNAMED

**Why those sectors.** Still live, all three:

- a **remapped bad block**,
- a **worn erase block**,
- a **controller retry** on specific media.

**And one long ATA wait is indistinguishable from a BIOS retry sequence from
above `INT 13h`.** Both are one call.

**LBA differences within cylinder 737 are 175, 114, 111 -- no constant
stride, no power-of-two alignment.** The neighbourhood map would name it;
it is designed, unrun, and its ask is unsent.

**Narrowing is not naming, and the operator's ruling asks for a name.**

## 4. WITHDRAWN -- kept visible with their refutations

A reviewer checking whether we fooled ourselves needs the record of when we
did.

| claim | how it died |
|---|---|
| **lattice p-value 0-of-2000** | the null had no spacing constraint; corrected it swung to 3.4-6.1%, and the statistic is a function of a minimum-gap assumption taken from the observation. **No p-value is claimed.** |
| **4.00-tick quantization** | circular -- the 4-group spans 0.47 ticks, and a distribution narrower than one tick cannot straddle two integers. Died again on measurement: 3.895 at the call vs 4.014 at the file layer. |
| **cumulative-writes drift** | at cumulative-bytes=0 the counts are 7, 10, 14, 11, 6 -- the same x produces the whole spread. |
| **"COMMAND.COM eats `\|`"** | correct, but **withdrawn on a false premise** (`#` was never tested and does not truncate) and then **reinstated by measurement**. The actual cause of the failure was nested `strtok` in my own probe. |
| **head stride of 2 in cylinder 737** | did not survive CHS->LBA: 175, 114, 111. An artefact of one coordinate of a translated address. |
| **"no RAM-disk driver on this machine"** | one `DIR` of one directory. It is in `C:\WINDOWS`. |
| **"the cost is the CF media"** (branch A) | the layer stack was upside down: a RAM disk clears **four** candidates, not one. |

## 5. OPEN HAZARDS AND HALF-BUILT THINGS

- **The read test never ran. `INT13P_READ` did not reach the program and
  THE CAUSE IS UNKNOWN.** Colons are present and were never tested; that is
  not the same as colons being the cause. **First action next session: ECHO 3

  **Consequence: reads-versus-writes is unanswered, so the NEIGHBOURHOOD ASK

  (`PREREG-NEIGHBOURHOOD.md`). It writes raw `AH=03h` to chosen CHS on a

- **The reconciliation gate is mis-built** -- it sums only recorded slow

- **The hook alters PF and AF.** CF, ZF, SF, OF, IF, DF and every general

## 6. COST, with its denominator

- **9 gate/A-B cells** (FPT1, LGOF1/2, LGON1/2, G2L1-4) -- all scored.
- **18 probe cells**. **3 voided**: two by a truncated stage list (nested
  `strtok`), one by an un-zeroed histogram claiming 17.6M writes against
  1,430 calls. **Each void was caught by a gate, not by a reading.**
- **1 mains cycle.** True cause: **an instructed drive-map probe** (`VOL D:`
  on an empty optical drive) wedged DOS at a critical-error prompt. **NOT
  the documented post-FTP keyboard hang**, though `verify_input` produced
  that fault's exact signature. Filing it under the hardware fault would
  have corrupted the power log.
- **2 failed sends**, 181.5 s apart by 0.0 s -- a **vcctrl defect**:
  `VCGET.BAT` composes `%VGD%\%VGF%`, so a root destination doubles the
  separator. **Found by reading the source, fixed, regression-tested (201
  tests pass), deployed.** The retry then took **8.9 s**.
- **1 boot-config change**, spent: `RAMDRIVE.SYS` added, device cell run,
  config restored and verified byte-identical.

1. **Open Gate 3's lower-resolution work.** It is the only route to the

2. **Re-run the read test** with the addresses passed without colons. It is
